records.title: Optimal Tone Melodies in Shanghainese: A unified OT account of word-level tone sandhi
records.abstract: This paper presents a unified Optimality Theoretic analysis of left-dominant word-level tone sandhi in Shanghainese. The proposal consists of a single constraint hierarchy capable of accounting for the disparate sandhi behavior initiated by the language's five lexical tones. By appealing to one basic faithfulness condition and one correspondence constraint that formalizes a familiar rightward shifting pattern, the analysis can account for the major tone melodies induced by each of the five tones—from disyllables to tetrasyllabic expressions—with five additional markedness conditions that regulate only tone melodies in general, including an avoidance of adjacent High tones and an avoidance …

records.title: Mandarin Third Tone Sandhi in 'Unstructured' Strings: A Stochastic Match Theory Analysis
records.abstract: This article gives an analysis of Mandarin Chinese third tone sandhi. We focus on the foundations of third tone sandhi by concentrating on strings of digits and lists, commonly referred to as 'unstructured' strings, whose sandhi patterns are not influenced by morphosyntactic structure. We introduce data from a series of elicitation experiments that show, contrary to popular belief, that such strings in fact manifest internal structure and vary radically in terms of the sandhi patterns they exhibit. We analyze a variety of these patterns using a combination of Match Theory and Stochastic Optimality Theory. The former enables the description of the interplay between sandhi domains, metrical …

records.title: A Logico-Philosophical Analysis of Modal and Deictic Phenomena in Natural Language
records.abstract: The philosophy of language, along with formal-logical methods of analytic philosophy and formal semantics, is a relatively young field of inquiry in linguistics, despite being deeply rooted in philosophy since ancient times. The aim of this thesis is to identify and provide, using philosophical argument and logical formulations respectively, the ontological status of modality and indexes as seen in natural language use and their implied truth-conditions. The design follows a descriptive-analytical pattern, with a methodology of tackling each linguistic category and sub-category individually – starting by presenting their best arguments to-date, their detailed critiques and shortcomings, my …

records.title: Selection and Adjunction
records.abstract: Abstract: This article develops a theory of syntactic selection and adjunction (based on Zeijlstra 20920) in which labeling follows directly from Merge and feature percolation, rather than from an independent labeling algorithm. Syntactic objects carry two types of formal features: independent features, which determine categorial status, and dependent features, which encode syntactic dependencies. When two objects merge, matching independent and dependent features under sisterhood do not percolate, whereas all other features do. This derives projection by selection while also accounting for adjunction: adjuncts are analyzed as elements that select their hosts while preserving their …

records.title: Polish present active participles as syntactic centaurs
records.abstract: This paper investigates the syntax of present active participles in Polish, morphologically similar forms that nevertheless split into agreeing and invariant types. Agreeing participles show full φ-agreement and appear in adjectival environments, while invariant participles lack agreement and function as adverbial, converb-like modifiers. Despite this contrast, both types retain core verbal properties, including argument structure and aspectual interpretation. I argue that this split does not reflect a categorial distinction between verbs and adjectives. Instead, both participle types are derived from the same verbal structure and the difference follows from the presence or absence of an …

records.title: Refining find
records.abstract: This paper focuses on a series of puzzles in the semantics of the so-called subjective attitudes, zooming in on the behavior of English ﬁnd combined with small clause complements. Find-verbs, as we will call them, have been important in understanding subjectivity in natural language: they select for subjective complements (Q ﬁnds humans 3entertaining/#mortal) and their very existence was often used as an argument in favor of treating subjective predicates (e.g., entertaining but not mortal) as having a special semantics. To this end, ﬁnd-verbs have been largely regarded as subjective counterparts of think-verbs. Focusing on English ﬁnd, we challenge this view and show that ﬁnd exhibits a …

records.title: A constraint on quantification over parts (the gather/numerous distinction)
records.abstract: This paper investigates why some predicates are compatible with quantification over parts of singular individuals, while others are not. For example, Most of the trail is narrow is acceptable, but #Most of the trail is short is not. I propose a constraint on quantification over parts, which derives the contrast between quantification-compatible and quantification-resistant predicates from an independently motivated pragmatic principle banning contextual equivalence among scalar alternatives. This analysis explains when and why quantification over parts of singular individuals gives rise to infelicity, and it naturally extends to the phenomenon of quantification compatibility in collective …

records.title: On Two Types of Mood Shift in Icelandic Conditionals
Reconstruction of Middle Chinese Lai 来母 and Xia 匣母 Initials & their Old Chinese origin
records.abstract: Traditional Chinese phonology reconstructs the Middle Chinese Lai initial(来母) as the alveolar lateral approximant [l]. However, this reconstruction fails to account for its classification as a "tongue sound" (sheyin 舌音) in the Yunjing and for its distributional property of lacking chongniu doublets. This paper examines the phonological classification of Middle Chinese tongue sounds and proposes that the Lai initial should instead be reconstructed as the palatal lateral approximant [ʎ]. An articulatory analysis of [ʎ] indicates that it developed from the voiced palatal affricate [dʝ]. Drawing on previous scholarship regarding the palatalization mechanism of the Jian initial(见母), this study …

records.title: The CC1–4 拼 Methodology: From Component Collision to Clausal Packaging (The Four Pins 四拼 Pipeline)
records.abstract: AXIS2026-M1 (v2) operationalizes the transition from paleographic character components to clausal syntax in Chinese, introducing the Four Pins (四拼) Pipeline: Pinyin (拼音) --> Pinyi (拼義) --> Pinzi (拼字) --> Pinzhi (拼枝). The paper replaces abstract phonological operators with a testable ZTVC (Zero / Tone / Consonant / Vowel) shift analysis and introduces the M7 Clausal Assembler to contrast paratactic Chinese clausal chaining against Germanic hypotaxis. Includes worked case studies on the gǔ (鼓) percussion continuum, the dòu (逗) spatio-temporal pauses, the jū/jù (居) postural shifts, the architectural distinction between zhì (製) and zuò (做), the self-referential bìng/pīn (并 --> 併 --> 拼 --> 摒) …

records.title: One grammar, two agreement options: Existential 'there' in New York City English
records.abstract: In this paper, we discuss optional agreement with third-person plural postverbal subjects of existential there clauses in New York City English. Data were obtained from the CUNY Corpus of New York City English, (CUNY-CoNYCE), an approximately two-million word corpus of extemporaneous speech from 202 participants raised in the New York City Dialect region (Tortora et al. 2025). The results of our study, along with the native-speaker grammaticality judgments of the author(s), suggest that both singular and plural verbal agreement is freely available for speakers of NYC English with 3pl postverbal subjects of existential clauses. We model the syntax of this optionally-realized agreement in …

records.title: Implicating with commitment
records.abstract: Building on Geurts' (2019) programmatic proposal, this paper develops a commitment-based model of Scalar Implicatures (SIs) that shifts the explanatory focus from speaker intentions and mental states to the dynamics between private commitments and their social expression. The model accounts for both standard scalar inferences and cases in which speakers’ private stances remain partially opaque, offering a socially grounded alternative to intention-based accounts, with broad implications for the analysis of SIs across speech acts and the explanation of cross-cultural variation.

records.title: Doubling Down on Exclusivity: Issues at the Syntax-Semantics Interface
records.abstract: div.a { text-indent: 50px; } [This is a slightly modified version of the dissertation available on ProQuest. Please refer to this version for citation.] Quantifier doubling is a ubiquitous phenomenon in natural languages that raises important issues for the syntax-semantics interface. Quantifier doubling refers to cases where two quantifier expressions occur in a sentence, but apparently only one is interpreted as logical quantification. For instance, in languages like Cantonese, Mandarin, Vietnamese, among others, “John only bought lamb only” may mean ‘John only bought lamb.’ This is referred to as “exclusive doubling” (focus particle concord). A form-meaning mismatch is found, which …

records.title: One Transition Point Hypothesis
records.abstract: Transition points, the beginnings and ends of events, are linguistically significant, as they figure prominently in predicate classification. This work studies how transition points are represented in language and proposes the One Transition Point Hypothesis (OTPH), which states that each event can linguistically encode at most one transition point, thereby ruling out the cooccurrence of both transition points in the same structure. I derive this hypothesis by building on Travis’s (1991, 2002, 2005, 2010) proposal of an inner Asp head, which I argue is responsible for licensing both transition points. This analysis carries significant implications for predicate classification as well as for …

records.title: A causal model account of the Volitionality-Zero Result correlation
records.abstract: English lexical causatives typically entail result realization when used with a perfective aspect. A subset of these predicates, known as defeasible causatives, form an exception: with non-volitional subjects, they yield a culminating reading and entail the result, whereas with volitional subjects, they also allow a zero result non-culminating reading, in which the result is merely implicated and can be cancelled. This correlation between volitionality and the zero result non-culminating reading (V-ZR correlation) is captured by Demirdache and Martin’s (2015) Agent Control Hypothesis (ACH). Most existing accounts adopt a result cancellation approach, assuming a single result-encoding …

records.title: Chinese Dialectal Parameterisation in Cantonese Teaching
records.abstract: Using formal parameters and universal cartography, it is possible to account for linguistic variation in Chinese dialects, which display systematic microvariation within a common core grammar. This is particularly useful for the teaching of Chinese as a second language, as there is a growing interest in Chinese, not only in standard Mandarin but also in Cantonese which is immensely popular in the West and mainland China. As cartography seeks a universal word order from which language-specific parameter-settings are derived, the following schemata can account for Chinese dialects: 1) C(omp) Subj(ect) T(ense) Adv(erb) V(erb)-Aff(ix) Obj(ect) S(entence)F(inal)P(article) 2) Possessor Poss …

records.title: The Morphosyntax of Hasawi Arabic's Tense, Aspect, and Aktionsart
records.abstract: This is a paper that passed the MPhil to PhD viva upgrade process. It is part of my work in progress PhD thesis. It deals with the morphosyntax of tense, aspect, and aktionsart of my dialect, Hasawi Arabic. I argue that by scrutinizing the morphosyntax of auxiliary verbs with lexical verbs, one could arrive at the morphosyntactic structure (1), where tense is higher than aspect, and aspect is higher than aktionsart. I show how this is reflected in Hasawi Arabic's morphosyntax by templatic morphology. Being a viva upgrade paper and a work in progress, this paper suffers from several drawbacks, one of which is a lack of literature review on the morphosyntax of Arabic verbs. Comments and …

This is particularly useful for the teaching of Chinese as a second language, as there is a growing interest in Chinese, not only in standard Mandarin but also in Cantonese which is immensely popular in the West and mainland China. records.title: What Mizo reveals about the Architecture of D-Expressions
records.abstract: This paper develops a unified analysis of definite and demonstrative descriptions, arguing that reference is decomposable into a small set of semantically independent building blocks: uniqueness in a restricted situation, an anaphoric index, a deictic relation, and anti-uniqueness in a larger situation. Drawing on original fieldwork data from Mizo, I show that cross-linguistic variation in definite and demonstrative expressions (henceforth D-expressions) reflects different ways of distributing these components across the nominal spine. A key finding is that what distinguishes a demonstrative description is not deictic value per se, but an anti-uniqueness presupposition. The Mizo data make …

records.title: Accounting for Counting
records.abstract: This paper proposes a universal account of counting constructions. The observable variation in such constructions can be categorized into four possible systems resulting from parametric variation of two linguistic properties - NP[+/-pred] (whether the NP starts out as a predicate or a kind term) and Card/CL (whether cardinal and classifier heads are fused). The four systems show different patterns vis-à-vis overt occurrence of number-marking plurals (of the English type) and numeral classifiers - they are either obligatorily complementary, or obligatorily absent, or they obligatorily co-occur. The first two systems have been extensively studied, and the third has been argued to be …

records.title: Mass, count, and in-between: Insights from Asante Twi
records.abstract: Asante Twi is a language where numerals and mass nouns may freely combine without the need for a classifier or container phrase. Other languages with this feature, such as Yudja and Nez Perce treat every noun as grammatically count and are considered to be the same type according to Chierchia’s 2021 typology of mass-count systems. Against the predictions of this typology, Asante Twi has nouns that are notionally count and grammatically mass, called object-mass nouns. These nouns are likely a result of the decaying noun class system. Furthermore, the mass-count system of Asante Twi more closely resembles English, despite the difference in how the two languages treat numeral-noun …

records.title: Individual differences reveal underlying similarities in meaning:                 quantifier-dependent choices in verification procedure are consistent across individuals
records.abstract: Previous literature has investigated how quantificational sentences like 'Most of the dots are blue' are understood, using visual tasks which force participants to estimate numbers of dots. In this paper, we report two experiments which show that a participant's performance on a task involving the quantifier Most can be predicted by their performance on a `baseline' task which does not involve Most. Furthermore, this task does not need to be visual: an auditory task can be used to establish this prediction. We argue that this phenomenon is partly explained by different speakers sharing a specific, stable way of understanding the quantifier Most involving a subtraction operator. Because …

records.title: Mandarin Verb Doubling in Locative and Directional Phrases: Structures in Syntax and Postsyntax
records.abstract: In this paper, I argue that Mandarin verb doubling (VD) with locative and directional spatial phrases (SpXPs) provides evidence for a division of labour between syntax and postsyntax in the derivation of doubling effects. The central empirical diagnostic comes from the distribution of SpXPs and from their effects on event interpretation. When a predicate selects locative or directional material as a complement, the selected SpXP patterns differently from an ordinary modifier, revealing a complement–modifier asymmetry. This pattern extends recent analyses of Mandarin VD (Lai 2021; Lai 2024; Yan 2025; Meadows and Yan 2023), which focus primarily on doubling configurations in which this …

records.title: The clausal demonstrative in Czech
records.abstract: This study is concerned with the so-called clausal demonstrative in Czech -- the morphologically invariable demonstrative "to", which is morphologically related to the ordinary nominal demonstrative, but differs from it in that it attaches to finite clauses. Based on an informal corpus study, I distinguish three different uses of the clausal demonstrative -- the topic-related use, the focus-related use (akin to clefts), and the thetic use. The theoretical proposal has a syntactic and a semantic part. In syntax, the clausal demonstrative lexically encodes an array of left-peripheral heads (Top-Foc-Fin), each of which corresponds to one use type. The semantic proposal relies on the idea that …

records.title: Translation Literacy in Asylum Interpreting: A Pilot Study of TRACE and Structured Reflection
records.abstract: Interpreting quality can shape how an asylum applicant's account is understood, while UK inspection and guidance documents continue to identify challenges involving language matching, interpreter preparation and quality assurance. This pilot study operationalises translation literacy as explicit reflection on translation choices, semantic range, alternatives, evidence, consequences and evaluation. Twenty-one Arabic-English bilingual adults completed unguided pre- and post-framework translation-evaluation tasks after guided exposure either to TRACE, a five-step mnemonic reflection scaffold, or to an active structured control checklist. Eighty-four responses were scored on a six-dimension …

Flattening Semantic Representations: Modelling Structural Ambiguity in Formal Semantics
records.abstract: Formal semantics typically assumes that the interpretation relation linking a linguistic unit to its denotation is functional, treating ambiguity—especially structural ambiguity—as a phenomenon to be resolved grammatically. However, if ambiguity were fully resolved within the linguistic system, widespread and well-documented misunderstandings would not arise. We instead model the interpretation relation as non-functional in the strict mathematical sense. Accordingly, ⟦·⟧ᴵ is redefined as a function that collects the set of possible denotations of a given linguistic unit under a relation I, while disambiguation is handled pragmatically via a choice function γ. Misunderstanding arises when γ …

records.title: Neg-Raising through Question-Raising?
records.abstract: I suggest that neg-raising may arise through a general mechanism by which negative utterances are enriched to convey positive information. Concretely, I explore whether the inference from ¬P(φ) to P(¬φ) can be explained by assuming that ¬P(φ) addresses a question like { P(φ), P(¬φ) }, which presupposes ¬P(φ) → P(¬φ). I present evidence in favour of this conjecture, but also identify some challenges that an account of neg-raising based on this model would need to address.

records.title: Could the Ban on Improper Movement be about binding after all?
records.abstract: I show that the approach to the distinct binding properties of A vs. Ā movement proposed by Sauerland (1998, 2004), Ruys (2000), and especially van Urk (2015) derives the Ban on Improper Movement (the generalization that Ā movement cannot feed A movement). I argue that this is a good result because the Ban on Improper Movement makes correct predictions, and moreover alternative generalizations like the Generalized Ban on Improper Movement/Williams Cycle and the Generalized A-after-Ā Constraint fail to generate certain kinds of attested syntactic phenomena (e.g. raising to object in some languages, Ā-movement-fed long-distance agreement).

records.title: A hitherto unnoticed sloppy reading of proper names
records.abstract: An unexpected sloppy reading of proper names is observed, and its idiosyncratic properties are listed.

records.title: Exploring 17th and 18th century Frisian. Syntactic and morphological observations
records.abstract: This work is a collection of syntactic and morphological observations on the Frisian language of the 17th and 18th centuries. The observations presented here were collected as I read through all Frisian texts of this period for my two anthologies of Frisian literature of this period. If the Dutch language of these centuries is already severely understudied, one can imagine how much worse this is for a minority language like Frisian. The lay-out of the present work is quite simple. The observations are classified by syntactic category. The relevant example sentences are given, glossed, translated and it is briefly explained how these examples contrast with Modern Frisian. The first draft of …

records.title: Frontier Theories and Evolution of the Minimalist Program: From Merge and the Strong Minimalist Thesis to the Miracle Creed
keywords: chomsky 前沿理论；极简主义；gk 框架；奇迹信条；强式最简命题
records.abstract: GK 框架与奇迹信条（Miracle Creed）框架是近期最简方案最前沿的探索理 论之一，本文旨在对两个框架的理论背景、修正演化及其应用做一个简单的介绍。现今 Chomsky 前沿理论最核心的思想是“理论极简性”，而两个框架在消除一些前代理论的特设独立操作，充分运用第三因素给出一套即满足“理论极简性”又具有跨语言普遍性的理论框架正是践行了这个思想。同时，文中也会探讨两个框架在汉语部分问题的可行性。

records.title: Computational generative grammar. The framework
records.abstract: Computational generative grammar is a branch of modern linguistics stipulating that all theories and hypotheses must be justified by showing that the data follows from the theory. Due to the adverse complexity profile this level of rigor can only be reached with the aid of computational techniques.

records.title: Embedded tense and the problem of acquisition
records.abstract: It may be strange to begin a paper with a list of what it does not provide. Yet we have, depending how one views it, no positive results to report. We have found no new pattern of acquisition, and we offer no new account of any particular tense-related phenomenon in any language. What we hope to do instead is pose questions that, to our knowledge, have not received attention in the literature. The broad form of the question is all too familiar: how do speakers of a language—say, English—come to possess the grammatical knowledge that they demonstrate? The questions that guide this paper are narrow instances of this broad one, narrowed in three ways. First, they concern three particular …

records.title: Indirect scalar inferences in negative focus constructions
records.abstract: *** Please share any comments or feedback with me via email: omri.amiraz@ugent.be *** Indirect scalar inferences are generally assumed to be derived by the same mechanism of implicature calculation that generates direct scalar inferences, whether this mechanism is pragmatic or grammatical in nature. However, this study reveals a critical distinction within indirect scalar inferences, identifying two distinct types: (i) those resembling direct scalar inferences in being defeasible or absent in certain embedded environments; and (ii) those that do not exhibit the characteristic context dependence of implicatures. I propose that the latter type of indirect scalar inferences should be …

records.title: A Short Note on Short Passives and French Reflexive se
records.abstract: As in Collins (2024), going back at least to Chomsky .(1957), short passives must contain a syntactically present deleted/silent agent.

records.title: Negation Without Concord: High Negation in Czech Polar Questions
records.abstract: This thesis explores Czech polar questions and their inability to license negative concord items (NCIs) when negated. Following Zeijlstra (2004, 2022), we take negative concord to be an instance of syntactic agreement where all negative elements agree with a covert negative operator. The syntactic view of the matter is further suggested by data from long-distance scrambling and scrambling from an embedded predicate within the main clause. However, data also further suggest that movement is not at play in interrogative polar questions and the lack of NC. For this reason, we turn to how negation behaves broadly in polar questions and conclude that its nature may be expletive, i.e. not …

records.title: M-Mobile and other ‘superfluous’ forms of nasal onsets in Kartvelian
records.abstract: Kartvelian languages are famous for their exuberant consonant onset clusters that violate sonority sequencing principles, notably nasal onsets. In reality, there is substantial variation amongst them to what extent they exhibit such onsets. This paper will propose that variation amongst nasal onsets in the family derives not only from retention from the protolanguage but from separate processes of nasal onset deletion in Megrelian, nasal onset epenthesis in Laz, and a process of morphophonological reanalysis called ‘M-mobile’ in Georgian.

records.title: Nonfinite constructions in Germanic
Anaphora in Static Orthodox First-Order Logic
records.abstract: The paper demonstrates representing pronomial anaphora in the orthodox first-order predicate logic with the completely standard syntax and semantics. Specifically, we show how to represent not yet resolved pronouns in conventional logical formulas, and then record the result of their resolution (coindexing). Our proposal is static, simply-typed, minimalist, with the orthodox quantification, binding and scope. It relies on the 1920s logic, and applies classically and intuitionistically -- in particular, treating implication as is. It is inspired by and extensively relies on intuitionistic Skolemization. We demonstrate our approach on intra- and inter-sentential pronomial anaphora; …

records.title: The reconstructed pronunciations of the Middle Chinese Yu initial, Ri initial, lingual initials, and the Zhi rhyme group, along with their synchronic retentions and diachronic reflections in Chinese dialects
records.abstract: During the investigation of Chinese dialect speech databases, it is discovered that in southeastern dialects, a set of voiced fricatives is preserved in the pronunciation of the Yu initial (喻母) and Ri initial (日母) characters,should be identitied as voiced palatal fricative & labialized voiced palatal fricative,and a voiced fricative with a similar manner of articulation but a more anterior release position. Based on a comparative analysis of Yu initials transcriptions in the Menggu Ziyun and Dunhuang Sino-Tibetan materials, the retained pronunciations of Yu initials characters in other Chinese dialects, and the topological position of the Yu initials in the Yunjing, the author proposes that …

records.title: Retention among Phags-pa Chinese of features of 2nd deng & Sibilants from Middle Chinese and its Evolution &Transcription
keywords: sibilants of phags-pa chinese and ming mandarin chinese
records.abstract: This paper reveals that Phags-pa Chinese partly conserved 2nd deng phonological features of Qieyun Middle Chinese, i.e., vocal fry 2nd deng and Zhuang initial 2nd deng,transcribed with letters designating glottal medial & upper vocal tract occlusion. Phags-pa letter ꡨ is used for transcribing vocal fry 2nd deng sysllables, Letter ꡜ, together with ꡞ forms segment ꡜꡞ to represent independent upper vocal tract occlusion, which has a phonetic value of northern Wu dialect pronunciation of Chinese word “one(一)” . There is co-occurrence constraint of segment ꡜꡞ,so we can deduce sibilants of Phags-pa Chinese shall be laminal alveolar fricatives and alveolo-palatal fricatives. Laminal alveolar …

records.title: The Reconstruction of Qieyun Sibilants and Their Retention in Chinese Dialects
records.abstract: The mainstream reconstruction of Qieyun sibilants—specifically the jing (精) group, zhang (章) group, and zhuang (莊) group—posits them as alveolar fricatives, Alveolo-palatal fricatives, and lamino-postalveloar or apical postalveloar fricatives, respectively. However, while studying the third and fourth Deng as well as chongniu (重纽) in Yunjing (《韵镜》), the author proposes that the zhang group should be reconstructed as lamino-alveolar fricatives,transcibed as [sʲ], the jing group as a labialized lamino-alveolar fricatives[(sʲ)w], and the zhuang initials as palatalized lamino-alveolar fricatives [(sʲ)j],. Through an analysis of relevant sounds databases, it was found that these three sets of …

records.title: 2nd Deng of Middle Chinese rhymes—A unique phonation genre preserved among Chinese dialects
records.abstract: Previously the author has deciphered that 2nd Deng from Yunjing designates a glottal medial in relevant syllables of Middle Chinese rhyme books. Generally, there is little chance for word-internal glottle stops to be avilable to form CʔV syllables. The author observed there are unique waveforms of vocal fry(even series of single pulse fry, with damped pulse characteristics) phonation among vowels of words of 2nd Deng . Infered from this observation, by exploring words of 2nd Deng under non-Zhuang initials, large volumes of sounds containing phonation of vocal fry are identified among sounds from branches of Chinese dialects of Yue, Min, Hakka and Wu. [ɐ̰] and other vowels with vocal fry …

records.title: A Forgotten Group of Middle Chinese Initials
records.abstract: There exist among various Sinitic dialects a group of Alveolo-palatal fricatives that are so close in terms of phonetic attributes to either [tʃ] group consonants or [tɕ] group consonants that they were not identified approriately and not transcribed with suitable IPA symbols during past field surveys. One of the reasons is so far there is no defined phonetic features for the forgotten sibilants. Middle Chinese rhyme books kept records of the sibilants, i.e. Group Zhuang initials (莊组声纽), however heretofore they are not yet deciphered with correctly designated phonetic features. This paper rediscovers and identifies phonetic features for this group of sibilants. In the process this group of …

records.title: The Morphosyntactic Pivot Hypothesis: Hierarchical Parametric Organization of the Locus of the EPP
records.abstract: Generative syntax standardly assumes that T universally hosts the EPP (Chomsky 1995, 2000), yet cross-linguistic evidence reveals substantial variation in which functional head exhibits syntactic centrality and morphological prominence. This paper develops the Morphosyntactic Pivot Hypothesis (MPH), proposing that the EPP bundle is hosted not universally by T but by the morphosyntactic pivot: the functional head independently identified through convergent syntactic diagnostics (coordination, complementizer selection, ellipsis, subject position, extraction, freezing) and morphological criteria (obligatoriness, paradigmatic richness, productivity, generality). Applying this Biphasic …

records.title: Russian speakers use inflectional knowledge in choosing the diminutive of nonce words
records.abstract: Russian masculine nouns may take a number of diminutive suffixes, and Russian speakers follow a number of gradient statistical generalizations over nouns’ phonological properties in deciding which diminutive to assign to existing and novel words (Polivanova 2008, Gouskova et al. 2015). In a corpus study, I show that Russian diminutive allomorphy is also sensitive to two morphological properties: a noun’s inflectional stress pattern and its plural suffix. Moreover, speakers productively extend these generalizations alongside the phonological ones in a nonce word study. I propose that speakers store these generalizations in the form of gradient constraints over the cooccurrence of …

records.title: Conjoined quadruplets in West Slavic
records.abstract: Polish and Czech both have “conjoined quadruplets”: sets of four paradigms that differ in exactly two cases. In this paper, I compare how Distributed Morphology and Nanosyntax account for these patterns, which include multiple configurations identified as problematic for Nanosyntax by Janků (2022) and others. Since both theories must relegate some of the patterns to unproductive morphology, mere ability to account for all of the attested patterns cannot distinguish them. Instead, I compare the theories’ ability to account for measures of productivity like frequency, acquisition, and behavioral patterns. Accounting for the full range of attested phenomena requires speakers to store …

records.title: The Use of Indirect Positive Evidence in Second Language Morphological Learning by Different First Language Learners
records.abstract: This study investigates the impact of learners’ first language on their detection of indirect positive evidence presented in their second language while learning the plural morphology of an additional foreign language. The goal is to explore an alternative approach to learning foreign language grammars. The participants were 43 native Thai-speaking and 42 native Spanish-speaking learners of Mandarin who had advanced proficiency in second language English. They were divided into experimental and control groups and learned 12 Mandarin nouns in their singular form over 2 consecutive days. Only the experimental group was exposed to indirect positive evidence that provided evidence of the …

records.title: p-onset-sonority-hypothesis
records.abstract: This study investigates the realization of word-initial /p/ in English consonant clusters, focusing on the apparent contrast between clusters such as /pr/ and /pl/, where /p/ is consistently realized, and clusters such as /ps/, /pn/, and /pt/, where /p/ is typically absent. Using a systematic analysis of 2,586 entries from the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary, the study examines the relationship between /p/ realization and the phonological class of the following segment. The results show a strong association between /p/ realization and following-segment sonority: /p/ is retained consistently in /pr/ and /pl/ clusters, while it is overwhelmingly absent in the core /ps/, /pn/, and /pt/ groups. A …

records.title: Case Marking and Category Flagging: Evidence from Slavic
records.abstract: Grammatical case is sometimes viewed as dispensable in linguistic theory. The most detailed attempt at relegating case from grammar is that of Pesetsky 2013 (“Russian case morphology and the syntactic categories", MIT Press), where case marking is argued to be category flagging; for example, the accusative on a noun is taken to be the result of a verb flagging the noun with category V. This paper demonstrates that category flagging is real, but distinct from case marking. The main phenomenon under examination is category flagging by Slavic prepositions, where P-flagging is demonstrably dissociated from case marking. Other possible instances of category flagging include N- and V-flagging in …

records.title: Mixed agreement vs. case assignment patterns
records.abstract: The paper proposes a novel approach to the mixed agreement vs. case assignment pattern in Slavic numerals and juxtaposes the LFG formalization of this approach with the earlier Minimimalist analysis presented in detail in Concord is Insatiable Agree: Heterogeneous Case and Phi Patterns in Slavic and Finnic .

records.title: Foundations of Biolinguistics
keywords: cognitive linguistics in the narrow vs. broad sense
records.abstract: Biolinguistics, to define it in a single phrase, is the study of language that takes its biological underpinnings seriously. This short book out-lines the basic tenets of a biolinguistic approach framed in the form of five ‘foundational questions’. While often associated with generative investigations of language, biolinguistics is not—and should not be—just another term for generative grammar; biolinguistic approaches to the scientific study of human language will thus be put in a richer context by inspecting and dissecting the foundational questions, with par-ticular reference to cognitive approaches from generative and non-generative perspectives alike. The organizing distinction …

records.title: Two arguments for a movement analysis of Negative Doubling
records.abstract: This paper presents novel evidence from two Northern Italian dialects supporting a movement-based analysis of Negative Doubling , in which a single-negation reading arises from the co-occurrence of a negative marker and one or more negative indefinites (Zeijlstra 2004). Under this approach, sentential negation is base-merged with the negative indefinite and subsequently splits from it during the derivation (Blanchette 2015; Tubau et al. 2024; Presotto et al. submitted). This analysis makes two empirical predictions that are not expected under Agree-based accounts (Haegeman & Lohndal 2010; Manzini & Pescarini 2024; Zeijlstra 2004, 2022). First, the base-generated constituent containing both …

records.title: Children’s acquisition of the meaning of disjunction
records.abstract: The question of how young children interpret disjunctive words like English “or” has become a topic of increased attention in the recent developmental semantic/pragmatic literature. We present a thematic overview of the past half century of research on children’s acquisition of the meaning of disjunction, from the Piagetian era in the 1940s to the most recent experimental pragmatics studies of disjunction. Along the way, we highlight ways in which children differ from adults in their interpretations of disjunction, as well as ongoing debates about the sources of these interpretations, with the hope that a historical perspective may shed light on these recent debates.

records.title: Contact explains patterns of language change in Italo-Romance
records.abstract: Language contact is a crucial factor determining language change. This study defines a novel methodology to quantify the extent of its relevance, testing it on the distribution of 23 syntactic features in the Italian dialectal environment. Two sets of data are compared, representing two diachronic stages separated by 70-90 years. This allows to estimate for each feature (i) the amount of change attested in this timespan, (ii) the amount of contact attested at the beginning of the period considered. A simple regression analysis shows that contact accounts for up to 66% (R2 = 0.66; r = 0.812) of the diachronic variation, a highly significant result. Further post-hoc analyses indicate that …

records.title: Indented Bracketed Representation: A Tree-like Representation for Bracketed Representations of Syntactic Structures
records.abstract: Bracketed notation is a standard, compact method for representing syntactic structures. Yet as structural depth increases—especially within high-density cartographic frameworks—standard linear bracketed representations rapidly become unreadable. While graphic tree diagrams resolve this readability issue, their implementation presents severe practical challenges in mainstream word processors (e.g., Microsoft Word, LibreOffice Writer, Google Docs), where manual drawing tools create fragile layouts and embedded static images hamper real-time editing and collaboration. It must be acknowledged that this note introduces Indented Bracketed Representation (IBR): a spatial bracketed representation, …

records.title: On selective LF wh-movement: What Superiority and wh-islands tell us about wh-in-situ in Japanese
records.abstract: The paper examines wh-in-situ in Japanese and argues for a position that is in between wholesale LF wh-movement approaches, where all in-situ wh-phrases in Japanese undergo movement in LF, and the treatments where there is no LF wh-movement in Japanese at all by arguing that some, but not all wh-in-situ questions in Japanese involve LF wh-movement. Regarding when Japanese has LF wh-movement, Takahashi (1993) argues that in some cases, wh-scrambling in Japanese involves true overt wh-movement. I show that a rather intricate paradigm regarding wh-island and superiority effects with Japanese wh-in-situ can be accounted for if Japanese has LF wh-movement only in the contexts where Takahashi …

records.title: Plural Predication and Scope
records.abstract: A central question in formal semantics concerns the division of labor between lexical semantics and the compositional system. Given a particular inference pattern, we can ask whether it is encoded in the lexicon or whether it arises from a particular syntactic interaction between different compositional ingredients. This question is especially important in the domain of plural predication, where there are competing lexical and syntactic accounts for a variety of phenomena. This dissertation argues, via a detailed investigation of cumulative inferences, reciprocal alternations and the interpretation of `together', for a syntactic approach according to which these core inferences in plural …

records.title: Locality at the Interface
records.abstract: There are many approaches to locality, which differ in how they answer a central question: where do locality constraints originate? All available theories successfully explain specific subsets of the data, yet none captures the full range of locality phenomena. This suggests a “division of labour” among locality accounts, whereby variation in locality effects (within and across languages) is partitioned into distinct explanatory domains. This observation raises two possibilities: either “locality effects” comprise ontologically distinct phenomena stemming from heterogeneous sources, or there is a common denominator linking phenomena such as strong and weak islands, superiority effects, and …

records.title: Upper limit effects in DPs and the interdependence of worlds and times
records.abstract: The distribution of upper limit effects suggests that an expression’s evaluation time cannot be bound independently from its evaluation world. Specifically, even in cases where worlds and times can be non-locally bound (which implies the availability of mechanisms with object-language quantification or equivalent power), both coordinates must be bound by the same (non-local) antecedent. From this, I conclude that the mechanism manipulating worlds and times in natural language is less expressive than a mechanism that manipulates independent object language variables that range over worlds and times. At most, the mechanism that binds worlds and times can express binding of evaluation indices …

records.title: From abstract to episodic: representations in speech production
records.abstract: Eliminativist usage-based and classical generative speech production models differ fundamentally in two respects: (i) the nature of speech representations and (ii) the locus of linguistic knowledge. In this dissertation, I ask what levels of abstraction and detail are present in speech representations and whether a lexicon of detailed speech memories is sufficient to explain a speaker’s linguistic knowledge of their language. I investigate these questions using phonetic, phonological, experimental, and computational evidence from two understudied Pakistani languages, Punjabi and Mankiyali. First, I present evidence from Punjabi that lexical representations can be completely covert, …

records.title: Quantifiers are in Different Positions:  all and both in English, German, and Yiddish
records.abstract: This paper argues that the quantifiers for all and both can occur in different positions in the three closely related languages English, German, and Yiddish. Such differences have to be taken into consideration in the explanation of ungrammatical cases, as briefly exemplified here. All these languages allow these two quantifiers to be in the DP-layer. However, they vary as regards the predeterminer and the postdeterminer positions. Since Yiddish is the most tolerant language – it allows both quantifiers to occur in all three positions, the restrictions in the other languages can presumably not involve a strong account.

records.title: Sociolinguistic Dimensions of Digital Discourse: A Comparative Study of Male and Female Responses on Crimes Against Women
records.abstract: Social media has become a significant space for public discourse, allowing individuals to express opinions and attitudes toward sensitive social issues, including gender-based violence against women. This study investigates gendered linguistic differences in online discourse by examining male and female comments addressing gender-based violence on X (Twitter) and Instagram. The study analyzes a dataset of 30 comments, equally divided between male and female users, collected from four social media posts. A triangulation mixed-methods approach is adopted, combining qualitative and quantitative analysis to identify recurring linguistic patterns. The analysis draws on Lakoff’s (1975) Deficit …

records.title: German guitars, Lithuanian violins and Norwegian pancakes: metonymy meets the Agreement Hierarchy
records.abstract: Two-way agreement alternatives are familiar (this family has/have travelled all night), but larger systems (with multiple agreement alternatives) are rare and remain poorly understood. Focusing on German, Norwegian and Lithuanian, we see how metonyms and their interactions induce agreement alternatives. We focus on two types: instrument-for-player metonymy and entity-for-eventuality metonymy. In Norwegian, nouns like bratsj‘viola’ can take pronouns based on the player’s gender. And Norwegian‘pancake sentences’, where subjects like pannekaker ‘pancakes’ take neuter singular agreement, illustrate entity-for-eventuality metonymy. These patterns are then analyzed using the Agreement Hierarchy …

records.title: Catalan numbers and the theoretical limits of morphosyntactic variation
records.abstract: The number of possible binary trees is a function of the number of leaves in the tree. The growth of this function coincides with the series of Catalan numbers, a numerical sequence with many applications in the domain of enumerative combinatorics. As Collins (2022) recognizes, this numerical sequence specifies a theoretical limit on possible ways a string can be parsed via binary Merge. In this paper, I demonstrate that the nanosyntactic Lexicalization Algorithm (Starke 2018, DeClercq et al. 2025) bounds the number of possible outputs of derivations building and externalizing structure in a single Workspace exactly to the Catalan numbers. I then discuss how this result enables a …

records.title: Notes on plain futurates: Modality, description, and causation
records.abstract: Plain futurates—bare-verb or simple-present sentences that assert a scheduled future event—raise a version of Aristotle’s puzzle of future contingents: how can a modal-free sentence make a determinate, assertable claim about an event whose truth is not yet settled? A prominent answer posits a covert future-oriented modal that does silently what will does overtly. This paper argues against that answer and sketches an alternative. Drawing on Mandarin and English data, we show that plain futurates systematically fail the standard diagnostics for covert modality. We then argue that a modal-free description analysis, on which a futurate merely describes a currently-holding schedule, is too weak …

records.title: Mind de re
records.abstract: I outline the semantics of verification and examine its interaction with de re ascriptions. Verification sentences are analysed as having a layered structure comprising two unary operators, VER and ACT, represented as VER(ACT(p)). The operator VER establishes a link to a verification event in which agent X has established the truth of p in the actual world, while ACT renders the proposition pre-verified, that is, open to verification or falsifica­tion. Standard accounts of the de re versus de dicto distinction maintain that, in contexts of belief and desire, de re attitudes involve ontological commitments to the existence of objects in the actual world. Within a Davidsonian framework, …

records.title: The distribution of bare NPs in Russian: a dynamic account
records.abstract: Bare nominals in many articleless languages present an interesting case within the typology of (in)definiteness. On one hand, they pattern with indefinites in that they can be used to talk about a discourse-novel individual that non-uniquely satisfies their descriptive content. At the same time, they pattern with definites in that one cannot felicitously use two identical bare nominals in the same context to talk about different individuals. This behavior of bare nominals is challenging for the theory of nominal meaning, as the null hypothesis is that such nominals, lacking any (in)definite counterparts, should freely be used in definite and indefinite contexts. In this dissertation, I …

records.title: Agent-oriented modality in the languages of North America
records.abstract: This study examines the morphosyntactic and functional encoding of agent-oriented modality in a maximally diverse sample of languages from North America. Focusing on necessity, obligation, ability, and desire, we show that agent-oriented modality is expressed through a wide range of construction types, including tense-aspect-mood morphology, modal verbs, non-verbal formatives, and complex clauses. We show that clustering the constructions by their formal properties yields three groups that align closely with the modal functions of necessity, ability, and desire. We further show that the constructions encoding different modal functions tend to differ in their morphosyntactic profiles, with …

records.title: Cross-Linguistic Compositional Analysis (CLCA): A Reproducible Protocol for Recovering Shared Conceptual Structure from Cross-Linguistic Evidence
records.abstract: This paper introduces Cross-Linguistic Compositional Analysis (CLCA), a reproducible methodology for discovering systematic semantic constraints by analyzing how genetically unrelated languages structure complex conceptual domains. CLCA treats each language as an independent experiment in conceptual engineering: rather than comparing words or grammar, it compares the compositional patterns languages use to construct meaning within a domain, allowing structural regularities to emerge without theoretical pre-specification. Applied to truth-related meaning across sixteen languages from thirteen independent lineages (twelve language families and one isolate), CLCA identifies robust candidate …

records.title: Tritropic clitics in Tsimshianic
records.abstract: This paper argues for a two-step model of spell-out in which morphological linearization precedes the insertion of phonological material. The empirical basis of our argument comes from a detailed examination of interrogative clitics in the Tsimshianic languages of northwest North America. In particular, we show that in Sm’algyax (Coast Tsimshian) interrogative clitics consistently linearize immediately to the left of the final DP in the root clause, thus constituting a typologically rare case of penultimate or “second-last position” clitics. We show that no combination of syntax and prosody can derive this pattern, since Sm’algyax clitics show tritropic behaviour: they are subject to …

records.title: Neurocomputational mechanisms of syntactic transfer in bilingual sentence production
records.abstract: We discuss the benefits of incorporating oscillatory neural mechanisms into the study of bilingual production errors and their traditionally documented timing signatures (e.g., event-related potentials), which can offer new implementational-level constraints for theories of bilingualism. We argue that a recent neural model of language, ROSE, can offer a neurocomputational account of syntactic transfer in bilingual production, capturing some of its formal properties and the scope of morphosyntactic sequencing failure modes. We take as a case study cross-linguistic influence (CLI) and attendant theories of functional inhibition/competition, and present these as being driven by specific …

records.title: Precedence-sensitive locality in English locative inversion
records.abstract: This paper argues that syntactic locality is sensitive to linear order rather than c-command. The argument comes from English locative inversion, where a locative PP raises to subject position and a DP pivot remains postverbal. Using secondary predicates as fixed VP-internal landmarks, I show that the pivot must be postposed in grammatical instances of locative inversion. Crucially, this requirement holds not only when the DP underlyingly c-commands the PP, but also when the PP is structurally higher than the DP. Pivot postposing therefore cannot merely be a strategy for removing a structurally intervening DP. Instead, I propose that pivot postposing is a strategy for removing a linearly …

records.title: A Nanosyntactic account for the opaque morphology of Tibetic verbs
records.abstract: The verbal morphology of Classical Tibetan is notoriously complex, where a com- bination of concatenative and non-concatenative processes create paradigms of stem alternants with opaque many-to-many form-function mappings, where TAM features appear to be ex- poned by overlapping and discontinuous phonological material. This paper represents the first attempt at providing a generative, decompositional analysis of the most morphophonologi- cally complex Classical Tibetan verb paradigm (illustrated with √kab ‘to cover’), and of its di- achronic development into Themchen, a modern Amdo Tibetic variety. This analysis uses the Nanosyntax (NS) framework, where I argue that the lexicalisation …

records.title: Review of Gerald Roche’s The Politics of Language Oppression in Tibet
records.abstract: About the politics that underlie the language endangerment.

records.title: Adjectival fragments and clausal ellipsis in English and German: Experimental evidence for island sensitivity under clausal ellipsis favouring an in-situ silent structure approach
records.abstract: The paper reports the results of four experiments on adjectival fragments and sluicing in English and German. The primary purpose of these experiments was to test the predictions of the Syntactic Question Approach (SQA) to clausal ellipsis. This analysis adopts a conservative view of the syntax of clausal ellipsis, as it denies that remnants must undergo A'-movement to escape the ellipsis site, denies that ellipsis repairs island violations, and permits ellipsis sites to be syntactically anisomorphic to their antecedents. The SQA maintains instead that observed ellipsis-specific restrictions arise from constraints governing ellipsis recoverability. However, like most sententialist theories …

records.title: Investigating the Tone-Segment Asymmetry in Phonological Counting: Three Artificial Language Learning Experiments
records.abstract: Tone-segment asymmetry has been a frequently discussed topic in linguistic typology where tone has been argued to demonstrate properties that are rarely observed in segmental systems. This study asks whether this typological asymmetry corresponds to a systematic difference in learnability, and thus whether learning biases may contribute to the observed typological distribution. We conducted three artificial language learning experiments examining phonological counting, a non-local phonological process that has been attested for tone but not for segments. The results show that the learning profiles of tonal and segmental counting rules closely mirror the typological distribution: segmental …

records.title: From L2 Comprehension Difficulty to Test Anxiety: The Mediating Role of Academic Stress Among Filipino University Students
records.abstract: This study examined the mediating role of academic stress in the relationship between second language (L2) comprehension difficulty and test anxiety among early-stage Filipino university students in an English-medium instructional context. Using survey data from 80 undergraduate entrepreneurship students, the study employed correlational and mediation analyses with bootstrapped confidence intervals to examine the proposed relationships among variables. The results indicated that greater L2 academic comprehension difficulty was associated with higher levels of academic stress, which in turn was strongly related to increased test anxiety. Mediation analysis revealed that academic stress …

records.title: Proposals, rejections, and Common Ground management
records.abstract: This paper connects two seemingly unrelated phenomena discussed in the literature and offers a unified account: (i) Why must modal adverbs (e.g., English "probably") be positive and behave like Positive Polarity Items (PPIs) (see Bellert 1977, Nilsen 2004, Piñon 2009, Wolf 2015)? (ii) Why do corrective constructions (e.g., Chinese "bìng bù", English "not p but q") obligatorily involve propositional negation (see Toosarvandani 2014, Yuan and Liu 2025, Wu 2025, Zhang 2025)? I argue that modal adverbs and corrective constructions are speaker-oriented, Common Ground (CG)-management operators, signaling two speech acts distinct from assertions: proposals and rejections. (i) Based on a …

records.title: Imperatives as Radically Reduced Clauses: Morphosyntax, Acquisition, and the Syntax-Semantics Interface
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates the morphosyntax and acquisition of imperative clauses in Italian, arguing for a low structural analysis in which imperatives are radically reduced structures which do not comprise the CP layer, but only vP and a few other projections in the vP periphery in the sense of Belletti (2004). This proposal resolves a tension coming directly from acquisition data: traditionally, imperatives are assumed to target the CP layer, yet positive second person singular imperatives emerge as among the first verbal forms in child development, while CP becomes available only in later acquisitional stages, captured under the Growing Trees framework (Friedmann et al., 2021). This …

records.title: Why the functional-head theory in syntax is probably wrong
records.abstract: This paper examines the functional-head theory in syntax, i.e. the claim that grammatical meanings are represented as heads in syntax, in much the same way as contentive heads (verbs and nouns). It starts out from the presumption that the functional-head theory can be expected to predict typical head behaviour of grammatical elements, especially with respect to the core head properties: hyperonym status, distributional identity, obligatoriness, idioselection. These general predictions do not seem to be supported by the cross-linguistic evidence, so I go on to discuss additional motivations for the functional-head theory. In practice, the functional-head theory has not been justified in …

records.title: Effects of Instructional Message Tone on Student Participation in Philippine Online Learning: A Quasi-Experimental Study
records.abstract: This study examines the association between invitation message tone and student participation in digitally mediated learning environments. Using a field-based quasi-experimental design, 40 students in the Philippines were assigned through an alternating allocation procedure to receive either a formal, context-rich invitation or a brief informal message directing them to the same online task. Participation was measured through link activation, task completion, and response timing using automated digital tracking. Results showed higher completion rates and faster response patterns in the formal message condition. Completion reached 100% in the formal condition compared to 50% in the informal …

records.title: Quantifiers that are more monotone are easier to learn
records.abstract: Linguistic universals have been hypothesized to bound the observed properties of natural languages at all levels of linguistic analysis (Greenberg 1966; Croft 2003; van der Hulst 2008). In the domain of semantics, such universals are often explained by appeal to general information-theoretic and cognitive facts, from efficient communication to ease of learning. This paper expands the range of the ease of learning explanation through a case study of monotone quantifiers. While most existing studies compare expressions which either do or do not satisfy a given universal property, we here define a metric for measuring monotonicity in degrees. A computational experiment shows that this degree …

records.title: Deep Learning in Linguistics and in Computer Science
records.abstract: This is a long comment on the special issue "The Implications of Neural Networks and Other Learning Models for Linguistic Theory" (Linguistics Vanguard, 12(1); Guest Editors: Vsevolod Kapatsinski and Gasper Begus). The article notes the dated character of the literature to which the editors refer in the introductory paper, the controversial character of a purely linguistic learning model such as Naive Discriminative Learning, which is incompatible with LLMs, the treatment of computational learning methods (neural networks) as linguistic theories by providing words as input and checking the correctness of the output, and the ascription to computational learning models of purely linguistic …

records.title: Dynamic Versus Static Analysis: Is the LSA 2027 Summer Institute Guiding Linguistics in the Wrong Direction?
records.abstract: Can linguistics continue to analyze language in the same way after the emergence of LLMs? This article argues that AI has fundamentally changed our understanding of language and language generation. It discusses the distinction between dynamic and static analysis, warns that a DYNAMIC approach yields DESCRIPTION, while a STATIC one yields GENERATION, and asks whether the themes of the LSA 2027 Summer Institute adequately reflect the progress made in NLP in recent years.

records.title: Subject-Sharing Coordinate Constructions in Germanic Languages
records.abstract: This short paper (four pages only) argues against the coordination of intermediate projections and against the claim that the conjuncts of an obligatory subject-sharing coordinate construction in Germanic languages have no subject. In pursuing a well-formed syntactic structure of such a construction, it is suggested that a sideward movement of the subject from the low conjunct to the structure of the high conjunct can derive the major syntactic properties of the construction.

records.title: Syntax of Dutch, Volume I-VIII. ToC
records.abstract: The Syntax of Dutch presents a synthesis of current thinking on Dutch syntax. Its principal focus is on describing the Dutch language; technical issues related to linguistic theory are addressed only if new light is shed on the subject. The work is organized around the four lexical categories verbs (volumes 1–3), nouns (volumes 4–5), adjectives (volume 6), and adpositions (volume 7). It includes a general introduction to the semantic, morphological, and syntactic properties of these categories, their argument structure, their modification possibilities, and issues related to word order. The functional categories (determiners, complementizers, etc.) are discussed in relation to the lexical …

records.title: The copy theory of movement and linearization of chains in the Minimalist program
records.abstract: This dissertation is concerned with movement operations within the Minimalist Program (Chomsky 1995). Exploring the copy theory of movement, it focusses on two issues: (i) why can traces not be phonetically realized?; and (ii) what is the theoretical status of the operation Move in a system w here syntactic objects are derivationally assembled? I propose that a chain cannot surface with more than one link phonetically realized because it cannot be linearized in accordance with Kayne's (1994) Linear Correspondence Axiom.

records.title: Tracking multiple common grounds: Mismatches in activation
records.abstract: A fictional narrative contains a multitude of common grounds (CGs). On the one hand, the characters talk to each other and develop a CG between them. On the other hand, the narrator is telling the story to the reader and contributes to the narrator/reader CG that the characters are not privy to. The activation level of a referent, which influences the choice of a referring expression, can differ between the CGs. This paper reports an experiment in which we presented participants with contexts that created mismatches in referent activation between CGs and asked them to choose a referring expression, a name or a pronoun, to see which CG determines their referential choice. The results show …

records.title: False Positives in AI Writing Detection: A Small-Scale Empirical  Study Using Authentic Filipino Student Essays
records.abstract: This research note reports a small-scale exploratory study into how two AI writing detectors, ZeroGPT and Copyleaks, classify authentic student essays. A total of ten anonymised college-student essays were analysed to observe misclassification patterns, particularly false positives, where human-written content has been incorrectly flagged as AI-generated. The assessment was conducted focusing on essays produced by Filipino undergraduates whose nonnative English writing may have features that could lead to misclassification by the detectors. Results show that both detectors inconsistently classified the same set of essays: five essays were labelled as “AI-generated,” while the other five …

records.title: Enhancing Grade 7 Reading Proficiency through an English Reading Program Intervention in High School.
records.abstract: This study aimed to determine the level of reading proficiency of Grade 7 students through the implementation of an English Reading Program at Public National High School, Philippines. A quantitative one-group pretest–posttest design was employed, involving 494 Grade 7 students across eleven sections. Data were gathered using validated standardized reading comprehension assessments administered before and after the intervention. Findings revealed that the English Reading Program was effective in improving students’ reading proficiency. Post-test results showed a notable increase in reading comprehension levels, with no students classified as non-readers after the intervention. The use of …

records.title: Negation and bias in Czech polar questions: evidence from a naturalness rating study
records.abstract: Negative polar questions (PQs) display bias patterns that have proven difficult to capture within one account. This paper proposes a novel analysis of negation and bias in Czech PQs. While previous literature has distinguished between inner and outer negation readings, we introduce a third, novel category: medial negation. We model the three readings using a unified semantic framework where bias modals operate on the non-at-issue tier, and the negative operator interacts with them from either the at-issue or non-at-issue level. Inner negation operates at-issue, interacting with a contextual bias modal; medial negation modifies the contextual bias modal on the non-at-issue tier; and outer …

records.title: Honorificity feature as an enabler: Bridging the person gap
records.abstract: This paper examines differential argument marking in the Darbhanga variety of Maithili. In this language, whereas all 1st and 2nd person subjects trigger obligatory verbal (person and/or honorificity) agreement, 3rd person subjects must be honorific to trigger agreement. 3rd person non-honorific subjects fail to do so. Differential subject marking, we claim, is the result of the Hon(orificity) feature on 3rd person DPs that are otherwise, conventionally, characterised as person-less nominals. The Hon feature enables 3rd person subjects to be morphosyntactically encoded at par with 1st and 2nd person subjects. In the object domain, honorificity plays an even more decisive role, where its …

records.title: Honorificity feature as an enabler: Bridging the person gap
records.abstract: This paper examines differential argument marking in the Darbhanga variety of Maithili. In this language, whereas all 1st and 2nd person subjects trigger obliga- tory verbal (person and/or honorificity) agreement, 3rd person subjects must be honorific to trigger agreement. 3rd person non-honorific subjects fail to do so. Differential subject marking, we claim, is the result of the Hon(orificity) feature on 3rd person DPs that are otherwise, conventionally, characterised as person- less nominals. The Hon feature enables 3rd person subjects to be morphosyntactic- tically encoded at par with 1st and 2nd person subjects. records.title: Multiple case assignment in ATB-movement: Evidence from non-syncretic mismatches in Russian
records.abstract: It is a well-established fact that ATB-movement is subject to a case-matching requirement. Exceptions are usually only found with syncretic forms. In this paper we show that certain non-syncretic mismatches are exceptionally possible with the genitive of negation. Based on new data from Russian, we will propose an account that involves case decomposition and multiple case assignment. We will argue that non-syncretic mismatches are possible under these assumptions because the genitive featurally contains the accusative (but not other cases). The data require an asymmetric approach to ATB-movement where the case in the second conjunct is assigned first, and we will present an account in terms …

records.title: The typology of government by adpositions: towards an understanding of “differential”
records.abstract: Adpositions may govern case, and there is dramatic variation in the case values found. Different adpositions often govern different cases, which means that we need to partition (or split) the adpositions according to the case(s) they take, as in German. But this is just one possibility. The typological point of interest here is that the items governed (the governees) may also be a determining factor, as when nouns and pronouns require different cases, as in Mari. Furthermore, we may need to specify both the adposition and the governee (Russian). And then, rather than one fixed outcome, there may be alternating outcomes, for each of the three types of partition (adposition-based, …

records.title: Negation, n-words and indefinites in Aromanian A comparison with Albanian
records.abstract: The article addresses the negation structures in Aromanian. In this language the Strict Negative Concord is applied, whereby the negative marker (NM) nu is always requested, also in the presence of n-words, particularly those corresponding to the arguments of the verb. In negative contexts, however, we may also find specialized indefinite elements which in turn give rise to the negative reading. This distribution, specifically the types of negative doubling, is explained by assuming that the negative operator is not realized by a lexical constituent but is postulated and made available to interpretation by the presence of NM and n-words. The Chomskyan theory of Phases and the lexical …

records.title: English plural -s vs. Spanish plural -s
records.abstract: English plurals like 'children' are compounds part of which is silent. Irregular plurals of the 'children' sort involve a silent nominal, in all languages.

records.title: The Ideographic Continuum: Reconceptualizing Chinese Compound Words as Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Spectrums
records.abstract: Traditional structural linguistics mischaracterizes Chinese coordinate (parallel) compounds by evaluating them through Western morphological frameworks. Unlike alphabetical writing systems, Chinese does not demarcate words with spaces, and no universally accepted definition of a Chinese "word" has been established (Packard, 2000). When standard lexicography forces compounds such as 朋友 (friend), 緣分 (fate), or 宇宙 (universe) into static Western lexemes, the structural mechanics and internal kinetic energy of the ideographic script are systematically erased. This paper introduces the Character Pair Continuum Framework, which repositions parallel compounds not as fused nouns but as ideographic …

records.title: Frequency versus Productivity and Why AI Does Not Use the Latter
records.abstract: The text explains why frequency works for language generation, while productivity is problematic.

records.title: Øut of Order --The Empty Set and Intervention in Featural Relativised Minimality
records.abstract: This technical note proposes a partial revision of the formalisation of Relativised Minimality (RM; Rizzi1990,Rizzi2004,Rizzi2018) -- the most well-known account of intervention locality effects. RM, as currently defined, draws on set-theoretic relations: Identity, Inclusion, Intersection, and Disjunction. While all are typically used in presentations of the theory, we argue that Disjunction should be excluded, as it entails a formal contradiction. We propose instead that disjunction cases fall outside the scope of RM-computations, as the relevant structural configurations lack an intervener altogether. This move also avoids certain set-theoretical issues involving the empty set.

records.title: Writing Systems as Civilizational Technology: Introducing AXIS, MRA, 300CC, and MRT — A Semantic-First Framework for Cross-Cultural Knowledge Mapping in the Digital Age
records.abstract: This paper introduces the AXIS Integrated Research Framework — a four-component system comprising the Macro Radical Alphabet (MRA), the 300 Component Clusters (300CC), the Mixed Radical Themes (MRT), and the AXIS coordinate system itself — and argues for its positioning as a foundational architecture for knowledge organisation in the digital age. The central claim is civilizational: Chinese writing systems encode four distinct historical strata, each corresponding to a stage of human civilisational development and its characteristic cognitive demand. These strata are not merely historical curiosities — they are simultaneously present in every Chinese character and compound, and any adequate …

records.title: Profiles, Not Prosodies: A Weighted-Feature Diagnostic for Connotative Meaning in Lexical Semantics
records.abstract: The theory of semantic prosody holds that words acquire evaluative coloring through repeated collocation with charged contexts, such that connotation is absorbed from usage rather than encoded in the lexicon. This paper argues that the phenomena motivating that theory are real but have been correctly measured and incorrectly attributed. It treats lexical meaning as a weighted bundle of semantic features and distinguishes two independent readouts of that bundle: a structural axis, tracking coverage of a word's non-evaluative content, and a valence axis, tracking its evaluative content specifically. The prosody tradition has read collocational skew almost exclusively onto the valence axis; …

records.title: Three-Level Vocal Tract Compression_ A Speech Aerodynamic Framework for L2 English Fluency of Mandarin-Speaking Learners
records.abstract: This paper establishes a speech aerodynamic pedagogical framework—Three-Level Vocal Tract Compression—grounded in the fluid dynamics principles of mass conservation (A₁V₁ = A₂V₂) and Bernoulli's effect, to address the persistent challenges faced by native Mandarin learners of English in producing fluent, continuous speech with reduced muscular tension. Traditional pronunciation instruction focuses on segmental articulation and prosodic patterns but rarely addresses the underlying aerodynamics of voice production. The framework comprises three coordinated compression levels: (1) global compression—engaging the core musculature to establish stable subglottal pressure; (2) pharyngeal …

records.title: Perceptual distinctiveness predicts the lexical distribution of vowels: Evidence from 30 languages
records.abstract: (joint work with Kowsar Amiri and Alba Hermida Rodriguez) Perceptual distinctiveness is known to influence vowel inventories, but does it also shape the lexical distribution of vowels? This paper investigates whether the frequency of vowel qualities in lexicons can be predicted by perceptual factors, i.e., whether more distinct vowels are used more frequently in words. Using phonetic data from a geographically and genetically diverse sample of 30 languages from DoReCo, we compare three models: a baseline model assuming equiprobability, and two phonetically grounded models based on Dispersion Theory and Focalization Theory, respectively. Our results show that Dispersion Theory best predicts …

records.title: Word boundary markers: a cross-linguistic perspective
records.abstract: Word boundary markers are essential linguistic cues that facilitate word segmentation, recognition, and comprehension in continuous speech. This paper explores the role of word boundary markers across languages, focusing on their segmental, suprasegmental, and morphophonological manifestations. Drawing on examples from languages such as Albanian, Georgian, English, French, Finnish, Chinese, Thai, Burmese, and others, the study explores the variety of boundary markers and investigates how they relate to morphological typology. The findings suggest that the type and frequency of boundary markers are determined by the morphological structure of the language, with isolating, agglutinative, and …

records.title: Null Arguments in Turkish
records.abstract: This study revisits null arguments in Turkish in the light of some interpretive diagnostics such as strict/sloppy interpretation and E-type/Quantificational interpretation in addition to adjunct inclusion in the ellipsis sites. Drawing on novel data, we argue that certain null arguments in Turkish are best analyzed as instances of Verb Stranding Ellipsis (VSE), wherein the verb raises out of the verbal complex prior to the ellipsis of the vP. Support for this analysis comes from cases involving adjunct inclusion, where an adjunct present in the antecedent clause is interpreted in the ellipsis site. We also provide a novel account of the mutual exclusivity between agreement and ellipsis.

records.title: Relativische Verbzweitsätze und Definitheit
Long Distance Dependencies in Turkana
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates long distance movement and long distance dependencies in Turkana, an extremely under-researched Eastern Nilotic language spoken in Kenya. All relevant Turkana data come from original fieldwork. Turkana is a VSO language (Dimmendaal 1983, Finer 2013) with an optional pre-verbal focus position. This position has not been discussed in detail in the literature before. Wh-elements can either move to this position or remain in-situ. I demonstrate that wh in-situ does not undergo covert movement but it is truly in-situ. In contrast, wh-ex-situ is a result of movement and not because the wh-element is externally merged high in the syntactic structure. I show that the …

records.title: Language Landscapes: The ESL teacher's guide to how English works
records.abstract: Synopsis: Language landscapes is a practical map of English for TESL educators, built around form–meaning pairings and the needs of real classrooms.
