Adopting a CGEL-informed framework, it stabilizes the category – function distinction (e.g., determinatives vs determiner function), pares back overloaded labels (especially in the adverb/preposition space), and introduces syntax trees as a teacher’s analytic lens rather than a student exercise. Early chapters address standards and normativity alongside a usable model of grammaticality; the book then moves through phonology (with Southern Ontario reference vowels and connected-speech processes), vocabulary (frequency, distribution, deliberate …

records.title: Japanese contrast sluicing and pair-list interpretation
records.abstract: In this squib, we investigate contrast sluicing in Japanese with multiple wh questions antecedents. Contrast sluicing in such cases presents a puzzling asymmetry, which reflects the differing status of the two wh-phrases in pair-list multiple wh questions (Kuno, 1982; Dayal, 1996; a.o.). We will argue that this asymmetry can be explained through careful consideration of the syntax/semantics of pair-list questions, together with the common movement-and-deletion approach to the derivation of contrast sluicing (see e.g. Merchant, 2001) and the possibility of argument ellipsis in Japanese.

records.title: ‘Incited and Inclined but Not Impelled’: Distinguishing Productivity from Creativity in Artificial Intelligence
records.abstract: Discussions about the encroachment of Large Language Models (LLMs) on the domain of human creativity often conflate productivity with creativity; they conflate the ability to generate new structures according to rules or other systems (productivity) and the ability to use one’s productive capacity without fixed reliance on identifiable stimuli while nevertheless producing structures appropriate to the situation (creativity). For a behavior to be “creative” is to use the productivity of a capacity like language in ways that are stimulus-free, frequently novel, yet appropriate to situations. This paper argues that, because of this conflation, improvements in the productive capacities of LLMs …

records.title: From Motion to Speech Act: The discourse function of luai-khə in Ji’an Gan Chinese
records.abstract: In Ji’an Yunlou Gan Chinese, the fused motion verb combination luai-khə ‘come-go’ presents a paradox. It is syntactically low, at the vP or VP edge, but interpretatively high, affecting speech-act structure. It activates both speaker and hearer roles, shifting second-person subjects to inclusive interpretations in directives and acting as an attention-getter or ‘negotiator’ in commissives. Pursuing analogies to Basque, Japanese, and Jingpo, we propose a movement-free analysis, following Cheng and Sybesma (2003, 2004) and Cheng (2019) for a similar paradox in Chinese: luai-khə carries a bundled feature complex anchored to the Speech Act Phrase (SAP).

records.title: How Does Linguistic Knowledge Enter AI?
records.abstract: The article argues that the relationship between linguistics and AI needs to be reconsidered—and that this opens an important space for future linguistic research.

records.title: From Quotation to Concession: The Case of East Circassian
records.abstract: This paper presents and analyzes a previously undescribed concessive modifier in East Circassian which is headed by an adverbial form of a quotative verb. This adverbial modifier is used, roughly,to express speaker dispreference for a potential action attributed by the speaker to the quoted agent. We show that this concessive modifier is subject to a set of restrictions on what it can modify, the most striking of which is a restriction to modifiands with negative directive sentential force. We outline a semantic analysis of this adverbial that explains the restrictions on its distribution in terms of two kinds of non-at-issue contents that conspire to generate a concessive interpretation. …

records.title: Categorial Features and The Feature Structure of the Present Tense: Perspectives from Variation and Change
keywords: categorial features; tense; copula; language change; arabic
records.abstract: This paper investigates the syntax of verbless sentences in Arabic in the present tense, contending that the key to understanding the syntax of finite verbless sentences resides in an analysis of the nature of the present tense in Arabic varieties and particularly its feature specifications along the lines of Chomsky (1995) and Benmamoun (2000). Many Arabic varieties lack a copula in present tense sentences with non-verbal predicates, while past tense and future sentences require one. According to Benmamoun (2000), this property and a number of other morphosyntactic asymmetries between the present tense and other tenses in Arabic varieties can be explained under a view that they differ in …

records.title: Strengthening and weakening Addressee Compliance by constraining discourse future: the case of Mandarin `ba'
records.abstract: This paper investigates how opposing discourse effects of either weakening or strengthening the sentential force can be derived from constraining projected discourse future, through a case study of the Mandarin discourse particle `ba'. `ba' has a weakening effect in declarative and imperative uses, but a strengthening effect in morphologically marked interrogatives. Previous literature has either treated the two types of uses of `ba' as distinct particles, or fails to provide a unified account across different clause types. This paper argues that `ba' conveys a single conventional meaning: it signals potential or existing addressee non-compliance in discourse. The core idea is that `ba' …

records.title: From L2 Comprehension Difficulty to Test Anxiety: The Mediating Role of Academic Stress Among Filipino University Students
records.abstract: This study examined the mediating role of academic stress in the relationship between second language (L2) comprehension difficulty and test anxiety among early-stage Filipino university students in an English-medium instructional context. Using survey data from 80 undergraduate entrepreneurship students, the study employed correlational and mediation analyses with bootstrapped confidence intervals to examine the proposed relationships among variables. The results indicated that greater L2 academic comprehension difficulty was associated with higher levels of academic stress, which in turn was strongly related to increased test anxiety. Mediation analysis revealed that academic stress …

records.title: Synchronic and diachronic ordering in Chinese character form patterns
records.abstract: This study demonstrates that interactions among patterns in modern Chinese character form cannot be ascribed to the diachronic order in which the patterns arose. In particular, lexically idiosyncratic patterns and articulatorily or perceptually motivated patterns interact in the modern system as if ordered early and late, respectively, regardless of when they arose historically. The results help confirm that, just as with spoken and signed languages, historical change in writing systems involves a sequence of synchronic grammars, each restructured from the previous one in accordance with universal synchronic principles. [also available at: https://www.fluxus-editions.fr/gla12.php]

records.title: Pronominal clitics in West Slavic: An exploratory corpus study of spoken varieties
records.abstract: Clitic phenomena in Slavic have received a great deal of attention since the 1990s. Generally, clitic auxiliaries and pronouns in West and South Slavic are classified as special clitics exhibiting intricate grammatical properties. In contrast, clitics in Polish, which is a West Slavic language, have been assigned a distinct typological status, since they lack recognised traits of special-clitic-hood, with Wackernagel (or second-position) placement, clitic clustering, and fixed word order among clitics being most decisive here. However, phenomena considered prototypical for Polish clitics are attested in other Slavic languages, too, which is why it is argued here that the typological …

records.title: Fonology: Phonological analysis in R
records.abstract: Fonology is an R package for phonological analysis, with tools for grapheme-to-phoneme conversion, syllabification, stress assignment, sonority-based measures, natural-class feature matrices, and maximum entropy modeling. It provides primary support for Portuguese, Spanish, French, and Italian, and English transcription that allows user-correctable overrides and heuristic fallback for out-of-vocabulary forms. Accuracy of grapheme-phoneme conversion ranges from 94% to 99% (using a combination of lookup and regex). Functions are vectorized, which yields fast performance over large texts (fast for R, that is). The package is designed to support reproducible phonological research and teaching …

records.title: Probability in Closed Symbolic Systems: When Classical Probability Proves What Statistics Cannot
records.abstract: This paper develops a framework for using classical probability, rather than frequentist statistics, to assess relatedness and origins in closed symbolic systems: domains characterized by a small finite alphabet, well-defined combinatorial rules, and effective closure against external input. Frequentist statistics is designed for inference from repeated sampling of an open or incompletely specified population; classical probability is designed for reasoning about a single case within a fully specified, finite universe of possibilities. When a domain meets the criteria for closure, classical probability provides a more direct, transparent, and philosophically appropriate tool than …

records.title: Learning modal force: Evidence from French
records.abstract: In English or French, modals express either possibility (e.g., “you can come”) or necessity (e.g., “you must come”). Prior acquisition studies have shown that English-speaking children master possibility modals early, but have difficulties with necessity modals, based on converging evidence from both comprehension experiments and corpus studies of children’s spontaneous productions. However, the underlying cause of this Necessity Gap remains debated. One issue is that prior studies have focused on English, a language in which necessity modals are much rarer than possibility modals in children’s input, which could participate in their later mastery. In this study, we test the hypothesis that …

records.title: Dative Clitics as Arguments and Adjuncts: A Developmental Perspective on Sentence Processing in Italian Children, Adolescents, and Adults
records.abstract: This study investigates the processing of Italian verb constructions containing preverbal dative clitics that function either as arguments or as adjuncts, adopting a developmental perspective across Italian-speaking children, adolescents, and adults. In a self-paced reading experiment, adults and fourteen-year-old adolescents read trivalent verbs selecting a dative argument (‘Martina mi ha prestato una bicicletta.’; Eng.: ‘Martina lent me a bicycle.’) faster than bivalent verbs licensing a benefactive dative (‘Martina mi ha riparato una bicicletta.’; Eng.: ‘Martina repaired me a bicycle), in line with the Argument Structure Hypothesis, which predicts lower processing costs for lexically …

records.title: The interaction of meaning similarity and confusability explains regularity in form–meaning mappings at and below the word level
records.abstract: Languages exhibit striking regularities in how meanings are mapped to word forms, yet analogous patterns at the subword level remain under-explored. This study presents a large-scale cross-linguistic analysis of regularity at and below the word level, drawing on data from over 1,900 languages. Here we find that while the co-expression of meanings at both levels is highly systematic, the meanings recurrently involved in the two levels differ. Nevertheless, regularity at and below the word level is explained by the same underlying principle: a tension between pressure for lexical compression and lexical differentiation. The former favours reusing forms for similar meanings to ease learning …

records.title: LLMs p-hack LMMs
records.abstract: My recent work has shown that current AI systems help users carry out various types of questionable research practices (QRPs). Building upon the past studies, this paper reports a new case study on a QRP that is ecologically plausible in experimental linguistics and neighboring fields: searching across the random-effects structures of linear mixed-effects models (LMMs), in the hope to find a model that provides a significant main effect. In the present experiment, I uploaded a dataset and asked the AI to explore LMM specifications "to see whether I can obtain a significant main effect," which constitutes a clear form of p-hacking. The dataset was constructed so that whereas …

records.title: Fellow Travelers or Worlds Apart? Posing the Galilean Challenge to Usage-Based Linguistics
records.abstract: Generative Linguistics (GL) and Usage-Based Linguistics (UBL) diverge from one another on how to frame the cognitive science of language. GL seeks to characterize the knowledge of language independently of arbitrary instances of its use. UBL, for its part, conceives of the knowledge of language and the use of language as inextricable, co-mingled during acquisition in ways that make their separation unsatisfactory. This paper argues that this divide between GL and UBL neglects a striking fact: GL’s leading expositor, Noam Chomsky, has for decades introduced the foundations of this approach to language with explicit and nearly romantic references to its use. The “Galilean Challenge” that …

records.title: Minimality in pronominal A’-binding? The asymmetrical distribution of Mandarin Chinese resumptive pronouns in relativization
records.abstract: Following from Aoun and Li’s observation of asymmetrical A’-bound pronouns in Mandarin Chinese quantification, this thesis evaluates existing theoretical and experimental research on Chinese relative structures especially resumptive pronouns in relativization, and the pro-object resumptive clitic suo in relativization and the long passives involving A’-binding as well as left-dislocated topicalization. Then, this study focuses on the subject and the direct object resumption to corroborate the corresponding theoretical description in the existing literature of Mandarin Chinese resumption in the two positions against two sentence processing approaches which yield different predictions. The …

records.title: Chuzhditsa: a phonological citation register for Cyrillic
records.abstract: Between ordinary orthography and specialist transcription lies a layer that alphabets fill only patchily: a conventional way to write a foreign word in the native script so that a reader can recover an adequate approximation of its source pronunciation without technical training. No major Slavic Cyrillic orthography occupies that layer -- foreign words enter through ad hoc transcription, with systematic indeterminacy as the result (Bulgarian Вашингтон ~ Уошингтън, Данчев 1982). We present Chuzhditsa (Bulg. чуждица, 'foreignism'), a computable, Cyrillic-based phonological citation register for foreign words, names, and pedagogical transcription. Japanese katakana proves that a visually …

records.title: Exploring AAB patterns in degree morphology: A DM–Nanosyntax comparison
records.abstract: The paper investigates stem morphology in triplets like bad–worse–to worsen (positive – comparative – deadjectival degree-achievement verb). It focuses on Czech, Ukrainian, Bulgarian and Turkish, and complements a previous typologi- cal study by Bobaljik (2012), which focused on root suppletion within this triplet of forms. The study replicates the main result of Bobaljik (2012) for stems, which is that ABA patterns are virtually unattested, confirming the idea that there is a containment relation among the three forms. The study also finds a rela- tive wealth of AAB patterns, which are absent in root suppletion. The empirical record further suggests that AAB patterns correlate with a …

records.title: Beyond concordance: External validation of probabilistic grammar in the English dative alternation
records.abstract: This paper asks how far a corpus-based model of the English dative alternation can be carried beyond the corpus that produced it. If a model learned from the American data analysed by Bresnan et al. (2007) predicts whether speakers choose give Kim the book or give the book to Kim, does it still predict the choice in later British conversation, for instance in the Spoken British National Corpus 2014 (BNC2014)? Earlier studies show that dative models trained on one variety can rank or classify tokens in another. I ask the stricter question: whether the probabilities remain reliable, which parts of the conditioning carry over, and what that production probability can say about grammar. I …

records.title: When are Alternations Learned?
records.abstract: Because the acquisition of phonotactics begins before the acquisition of morphology, it is possible that phonotactic knowledge underlies the acquisition of alternations, at least when the two align. An example is final devoicing. The typical analysis is that alternating obstruents are underlyingly voiced but devoiced in final position, avoiding a phonotactic violation. If phonotactic knowledge underlies alternation learning, acquisition of alternations should follow rapidly after the acquisition of the morphology that produces violations. Yet different languages with voicing alternations show developmental differences: Dutch-learning children’s developing knowledge is more restricted than …

records.title: Levels and Strata in Linguistic Modeling: Cross-Domain Considerations
records.abstract: Linguistic phenomena are complex, and as a result recourse to multiple representations are common, particularly across the classic subdomains of language (phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics). However, there is also a long tradition in linguistics of using multiple representations to analyze phenomena assumed to fall within a single subdomain of language. The positing of ‘deep’ and ‘surface’ structures starting from early Generative Grammar is just one example. These combinations of multiple representations have been variously referred to as ‘levels’ or ‘strata’, often without it being clear what, if anything, was at stake in the choice of terminology. Ladusaw …

records.title: No Free Lunch: Copredication Beyond Predicate Extension
records.abstract: Under Liebesman and Magidor's Property Versatility account, predicates such as 'on the shelf' and 'by Tolstoy' are more versatile than theorists have assumed. I argue that approach turns a genuine problem about how linguistic representations coordinate incompatible conceptual formats into a permissive doctrine about predicate extension, and does not align with reported empirical patterns found in the psycholinguistics literature. I defend an alternative internalist account on which polysemous nominals make available organized combinations of senses, while predicates act as probes that select and reweight dimensions of these representations. Copredication succeeds when multiple senses can be …

records.title: Chapter Three:The Parallel Multi-Dimensional Syntactic Building Hypothesis
records.abstract: This chapter proposes the Parallel Multi-Dimensional Syntactic Building Hypothesis, which seeks to address a foundational yet often underarticulated question within a theory of free Merge: if Merge is free, why does syntactic building not proceed chaotically from arbitrary combinations in the workspace, but instead give rise to stable and interpretable syntactic structures? The chapter first distinguishes generation from building, arguing that traditional syntactic analysis typically presents the final convergent tree while leaving the initiation of syntactic building insufficiently explained. Drawing on the later minimalist conception of free Merge, the chapter argues that syntactic …

records.title: Apparent voice mismatches in K'iche' ellipsis: non-distinctness, argument structure, and syntactic feature composition
records.abstract: This paper investigates apparent voice mismatches in TP ellipsis in the Mayan language K’iche’. Antecedents of TP ellipsis in K’iche’ can contain a verb in the so-called absolutive antipassive (AP) form in contexts where the elided verb must be active transitive. I argue that the K’iche’ AP differs from the active transitive not in Voice specification, but in that it completely lacks the internal argument. The resulting mismatch bears directly on the formulation of the Syntactic Identity Condition on ellipsis and illustrates how ellipsis can be used to probe the feature composition of syntactic structures, including those associated with voice and argument structure. I show that the K’iche’ …

records.title: Restricting allomorphy without spell-out opacity
records.abstract: This short paper argues that restrictions on contextual allomorphy do not require spell-out-induced opacity. Standard approaches derive locality restrictions from cyclic spell-out, supplemented by additional stipulations that render previously spelled-out material inaccessible for later allomorphic interactions. I argue instead that the relevant locality condition is featural adjacency: two elements may interact allomorphically only if no projecting head intervenes between them. This proposal derives the familiar restriction against root-conditioned allomorphy across categorizing heads while eliminating the need for interface-specific opacity conditions. It also accounts for apparent …

records.title: Floating tones
records.abstract: Floating tones are tones that are not associated with any tone-bearing unit (e.g., segmental material), and they have been used widely in the analysis of a variety of tone systems since the second half of the 20th century. Floating tones are inherently abstract and do not constitute an empirical object (one cannot hear a floating tone). Rather they are an analytical device, one that we show is indispensable for tonal analysis. This chapter gives an overview of floating tones, their nature, and the variety of tonal phenomena they have been used to account for (downstep, blocking effects, etc.). While most of our examples come from African languages (primarily from the Niger-Congo stock, or …

records.title: Phonological profile changes in the Macro-Sudan Belt: Antagonism between ATR and interior vowels
records.abstract: Rolle et al. (2020) present a fine-grained areal distribution of two vocalic properties in the Macro-Sudan Belt (MSB – Güldemann 2008): advanced tongue root (ATR) harmony and interior vowels (i.e. non-peripheral vowels [ɨ ɯ ɜ ə ʌ … ]). Their study determined that these two properties are antagonistic at both the level of individual languages (languages in the MSB tend to have either one or the other, rarely both), as well as at the areal level (ATR-harmony languages and interior-vowel languages are largely in complementary geographic distribution). The focus of this paper is examining diachronic phonological profile changes which take place as language families spread into and out of these …

records.title: Decomposing Place Names: Evidence from the Hebrew Construct State
records.abstract: This paper claims that place-denoting proper names (i.e., toponyms) are structurally decomposable. Evidence for this claim comes from Hebrew toponyms displaying noun-noun concatenation (e.g., Tel-Aviv). I show that such toponyms share properties with the Hebrew Construct State construction. Using Borer's (2013) typology of Constructs, I investigate how these toponyms pattern with Construct subclasses using a range of diagnostics. Accordingly, it is demonstrated that such toponyms are decomposable in two distinct ways. Specifically, they instantiate two subclasses: (a) toponymic Modificational-Constructs, a grammatically transparent class, and (b) toponymic Compounds, a grammatically opaque …

records.title: Phonetically Complete Neutralization of Vowel Nasality in Mankiyali
records.abstract: This chapter examines the neutralization of vowel nasality in Mankiyali, an endangered Indo-Aryan language spoken in northern Pakistan. To evaluate the extent of neutralization in the language, I report the results of two production experiments. The first experiment examines the realization of vowel nasality on the target vowels themselves using both airflow and acoustic measures. The second experiment explores whether traces of the underlying contrast persist in anticipatory coarticulatory nasalization on preceding segments. The results indicate that the neutralization of vowel nasality in Mankiyali is phonetically complete. Not only are underlying oral and nasal vowels indistinguishable …

records.title: A new analysis of ‘A-not-A questions’ in Mandarin Chinese
keywords: so-called inner vs outer a-not-a questions
records.abstract: The analysis of the so-called ‘A-not-A’ questions in Mandarin Chinese, where negation occurs between two identical elements at the VP edge, has basically remained the same since C.-T. James Huang (1982). The entire sequence ‘A-not-A’ is presented as the spell-out of an abstract polar question morpheme [Q] to be obtained via a reduplication rule. However, the issue has never been addressed how under this scenario the correct choice can be made between the negation markers bù ‘not’ and méi (yǒu) ‘not have’ both featuring in ‘A-not-A’ questions, given that phonological rules have no access to the syntactic and semantic information required here. A new approach is therefore necessary. …

records.title: On personal articles in Chilean Spanish
records.abstract: This paper investigates personal articles, i.e., definite articles that combine with personal names in referential contexts, in Chilean Spanish. This syntactic pattern has been widely characterized in other Spanish varieties as expressive or pragmatically marked. Drawing on quantitative evidence from previous corpus studies, acceptability judgments, and morphosyntactic diagnostics, the paper argues that personal articles in Chilean Spanish have a fundamentally different grammatical status. Unlike in other varieties, they neither encode discourse anaphora nor convey interpersonal proximity. The paper advances an analysis according to which Chilean Spanish speakers command two alternative …

records.title: Grammaticality de-idealized
records.abstract: This paper introduces the Operator-Value Model of Grammaticality (OVMG), a framework for (un)grammaticality distinct from grammars focused solely on language production or description. The model treats (un)grammaticality as conditioned stability in form–value relations accepted or rejected within communicative situations, integrating mapping viability, operator-value coherence, population licensing, and speaker-level feelings of anomaly. Previous approaches, including generative grammar, Construction Grammar, and psycholinguistic models, have each captured part of the picture but haven’t jointly explained why semantically coherent constructions may nonetheless be deemed ungrammatical, why …

records.title: Incorporation [handbook chapter]
records.abstract: This chapter overviews typological and theoretical investigations of noun incorporation, a grammatical phenomenon whereby a nominal argument of a verb, typically its object, may be morphologically integrated into the verb complex. This chapter considers incorporation also to include 'pseudo' noun incorporation, in which the noun-verb relationship is based on linear adjacency rather than affixation, as well as 'obligatory' noun incorporation, which arises when the incorporation process is required for certain verbs or certain nouns. Though it is an open question whether incorporation is a unified phenomenon to begin with, syntactic research on this topic has generally been guided by a stable …

records.title: The argument structure of Turkish verbal reflexives
records.abstract: We leverage the rich diagnostic possibilities available in Turkish to probe the representation of verbal reflexivity in this language. We show that the sole syntactic argument of Turkish verbal reflexives, the surface subject, shows evidence of a VP-internal origin, but also passes diagnostics otherwise only satisfied by deep subjects. We argue that this mixed behavior reflects a movement derivation: a reflexive flavor of the agent-introducing head Voice attracts the sole argument from its low base position to its specifier and derives the reflexive interpretation through VoiceP-internal binding of a free variable. Phrasal movement --- a bona fide narrow-syntactic operation --- can then be …

records.title: Cross-Linguistic Frame Compatibility
records.abstract: Second language transfer is often described as the carryover of L1 grammar, but persistent idiom transfer, fossilization, and striking asymmetries between learner populations suggest that the transferred unit is neither a rule nor a word. This paper extends Frame Class theory to cross-linguistic acquisition by treating frames—event-anchored sentence patterns with fixed material, variable slots, and membership in frame classes—as the units speakers carry across languages. It proposes frame compatibility: an L1 frame can be redeployed with L2 lexical material when the target community has conventionalized a structurally compatible frame for the same event; where no compatible frame exists, …

records.title: Fluency as Communicative Integration
records.abstract: Standard accounts of fluency face a classification problem. If fluency is defined by speech rate, pausing, repair behavior, automaticity, vocabulary coverage, native-like production, domain knowledge, or interactional ease, a native-speaking child who preserves a story-state despite missed words may be classified as less fluent than an adult second-language listener who recognizes more words but loses the event relation. This paper argues that such measures are local proxies, not the phenomenon itself. Fluency is communicative integration: the preservation of global event-coherence despite local incoherence. Coherence means the minimum event-state required for the next communicative frame …

records.title: Frame Event-Scaled Fluency Assessment: Testing Coherence through Communicative Functions
records.abstract: This paper proposes an event-scaled model of second language fluency assessment. It does not attempt to redefine fluency. It adopts the companion account of fluency as communicative integration: the preservation and carry-forward of event-state across linked communicative frames despite local incoherence. The present paper asks how that construct can be operationalized in second language testing. The proposed model distinguishes three scales of assessment: immediate frame functionality, local inter-frame coherence, and global event-state coherence. Immediate frame functionality tests whether the learner can perform a necessary communicative function in a single frame or bounded response. …

records.title: Frames: A Pattern-Based Method for Second Language Instruction
records.abstract: Second language learners often acquire substantial vocabulary and a working knowledge of grammatical rules without achieving fluent spoken production. This gap has motivated research on how patterned units shape language use. Construction grammar, the lexical approach, and formulaic-language research all emphasize the role of patterned units in fluent production, but they do not, taken together, provide a unified pedagogical method organized around such units. This paper develops the pedagogical application of Frames for second language instruction. Frames treats the frame family, a cluster of patterned expressions sharing a communicative function, as the primary unit of instruction and …

records.title: A Guide to Analysis in MaxEnt Optimality Theory, Chapters 1-5, Supplementary Materials
records.abstract: Our textbook extract, "Guide to Analysis in MaxEnt Optimality Theory, Chapters 1 and 2," just posted on LingBuzz, makes use of Excel spreadsheets to teach and implement MaxEnt analyses. This zip file includes the spreadsheets.

records.title: A Guide to Analysis in MaxEnt Optimality Theory, Chapters 1-5
records.abstract: This document consists of the first five chapters of a projected textbook for Maximum Entropy Optimality Theory, a.k.a. “MaxEnt”. The text is directed to beginners (i.e. to linguists who are new to MaxEnt) and is meant as a “how-to” book, more pedagogical than polemical. The book is rooted in our view that there are many linguists who are in possession of gradient data (e.g. from observations of free variation, corpora, or experiments) and wish to develop a rigorous generative analysis of their findings — but lack an appropriate formal framework for doing so. We feel that MaxEnt is a very useful such framework, and hope to make it more accessible to researchers by making it easy to learn, …

records.title: The Death of Mystery Has Been Greatly Exaggerated: Comments on Sripada et al. (2026)
records.abstract: In response to Futrell & Mahowald’s (2025) paper on the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) in linguistics, Sripada et al. (2026) strikingly argue that LLMs “illuminate” the mechanisms underlying what Chomsky calls the creative aspect of language use (CALU). Such illumination promises, they argue, to bring this once-intractable problem under the heel of scientific inquiry by advancing our understanding of the mechanisms by which individuals select situation-appropriate expressions from an unbounded class of expressions. Sripada et al. draw attention to an important, foundational issue in generative linguistics, but their paper mischaracterizes CALU. The mischaracterization turns …

records.title: Cognitive Indexical Usage of Demonstrative "Ku" in Korean and a Split DP Analysis
records.abstract: This paper takes up a hitherto unnoted phenomenon in Korean in which the distal demonstrative (DEM) “ku” occurs modifying an adjective phrase (AP), seemingly violating the well-established weight-based adjective ordering restriction (AOR), namely, ‘heavy N modifier > light N modifier > N’. I show that such occurrence of “ku”, which I call KU, is not a run-of-the-mill DEM, and I explain its behavior by calling it ‘a cognitive indexical DEM’. The upshot of the analysis will be that KU selects for an AP and locates the property denoted by its complement in the mental domain of the speaker, pointing to it as if it were visible to the speaker, contributing a speaker comment. To implement this …

records.title: Bridge Principles without UG: Projectibility, Crosslinguistic Evidence, and Linguistic Ontology
records.abstract: Reiss (2026) gives Universal Grammar two roles. In its modest role, UG is a background commitment of Chomskyan I-language inquiry: anyone modelling individual internal grammars with universal primitives is committed, explicitly or implicitly, to such a postulate. In its stronger role, UG is the condition under which data from French, Japanese, or Icelandic can bear on English, so that anyone who denies UG lacks grounds for importing analytic categories across languages. I grant the local stipulation for Chomskyan inquiry, but I deny that inquiry into individual internal grammatical knowledge as such requires UG. I accept the evidential burden but reject the exclusivity. Evidence travels by …

records.title: From Roots to Categories: Deriving Nouns, Verbs, and Adjectives in Santali
records.abstract: Formation of lexical categories in the syntactic workspace has been a part of generative investigation since last few decades. This dissertation investigates the syntactic formation of lexical categories like nouns, verbs, and adjectives in Santali, an understudied Austroasiatic Language spoken in India. The central concern of the current research is the extent to which Syntax affects the internal structure of words/categories. This study employs Distributed Morphology as the theoretical framework to analyze the formation of nouns, verbs and adjectives in Santali because it provides an ideal empirical domain due to its fluid categorial system. This dissertation addresses three specific …

records.title: Plurals under quantification: disentangling readings and gradient effects
records.abstract: We investigate the interpretation of plural expressions, starting from the puzzle of the logical gap between their interpretations in affirmative and negative sentences. While bare plurals (e.g. “books”) typically receive an at least two reading in upward-entailing environments (e.g. “The box contains books”), they yield an at least one reading in downward-entailing contexts (e.g. “The box doesn't contain books”). Existing bivalent and trivalent theoretical approaches differ in their predictions about truth conditions of plural indefinites under the scope of a universal quantifier (e.g. “Every box contains books”) in mixed scenarios (some boxes contain one book, others contain several). …

records.title: A metaphysician’s systemic-functional turn: Amie Thomasson’s Rethinking Metaphysics and the architecture of linguistic description
records.abstract: Thomasson’s (2025) Rethinking Metaphysics brings a grammatical debate into metaphysics. Thomasson uses systemic functional linguistics to explain why noun-term recastings such as the property of redness are useful without behaving like observational object talk. This paper accepts the discourse-role insight but detaches it from Halliday’s grammatical architecture. SFL explains why the recast formulations are worth having; easy ontology licenses the inferences. For linguists, the lesson is broader than syntax: some inferences and expectations follow from linguistic description, but not every expectation imported from familiar models of reference, objecthood, or category.

records.title: Phonological and syntactic locality of object clitics in Czech Evidence from external sandhi
records.abstract: This preprint of the chapter (included in the monograph Czech Clitics: New Insights and Perspectives) examines the phonological aspects of cliticisation, focusing on how phonological and syntactic locality influence the phonological integration of second-position object clitics with a preceding host. Integration is assessed through processes affecting voicing at the object–clitic boundary, namely final obstruent devoicing and pre-sonorant voicing. These external sandhi processes are investigated using reading tasks with Czech speakers, whose readings were recorded and analysed in Praat. The experimental results reveal a statistically significant difference between verbal and adverbial …

records.title: Large-Scale Data Collection in Fieldwork Contexts: A Case Study of Clause Embedding in Zulu
records.abstract: Some research questions require large-scale acceptability judgment datasets to answer them. Constructing such datasets can be challenging when the researcher has limited familiarity with the language. We investigate how to optimally design acceptability judgment collection protocols in such contexts. Taking clause embedding in Zulu as a case study, we collect acceptability judgments using protocols that manipulate a combination of setting, modality, prior exposure, and question format and measure how much data collected using these different protocols converges in the acceptability it implies. We find that unguided surveys can recover the same acceptabilities as elicitation, but need …

records.title: Raising alternatives to express dependence: The compositional issues
records.abstract: Dependence utterances can be built with an adverbial adjunct phrase, e.g. "Depending on how the first round goes, I might stop". They express a complex conditional dependence between two sets of alternatives. Contrary to finite "depend", adjunct dependence utterances (ADUs) exhibit diverse syntactic forms and pragmatic purposes that challenge previous approaches. We show how Dynamic Inquisitive Semantics and Free Association with focus solve the compositional issues in English and French. Different dependence types (speech-act level, clause level, and predicate level) are explained by different adjunct attachment sites, with a single uniform entry for "depend" that captures the various …

records.title: Where passives and PPs meet: the case of Udmurt
records.abstract: It is well-known that constructions called “passive” cross-linguistically do not form a homogeneous class. In this paper we argue that some “passives” are not verbal or adjectival but involve a PP predicate instead. The empirical basis of our investigation is the so-called “passive” construction in Udmurt (Uralic).

records.title: Learning Latent Linguistic Representations with Serial Hypothesis Space Expansion
records.abstract: This paper introduces a learning model to address the computational challenges arising from including highly abstract underlying representations (URs) in morphophonemic learning. The proposed learner structures the UR hypothesis space by disparity distance and considers potential URs in batches, beginning with fully concrete URs, only expanding the UR candidate space if the current set of UR candidates fails to meet a predetermined likelihood threshold. When expanding the UR candidate set, the learner uses markedness constraint weights and violation profiles to identify features that are potentially mis-specified underlyingly, limiting the generation of new URs to changes of those feature …

records.title: The EVEZ Reading of the Tetragrammaton: Letter Descent, Root Isomorphism, and the Termination Ambiguity of the Second He
records.abstract: We present a novel reading of the Tetragrammaton (YHWH) based on two established facts of historical linguistics: (1) the Phoenician letters He and Waw are the direct ancestors of Greek Epsilon (E) and Upsilon/V, respectively; and (2) the initial Yod in YHWH functions as a third-person masculine verbal prefix (y-), not as part of the semantic root. Removing the grammatical prefix yields the triconsonantal root H-W-H (to become). Through documented Phoenician-to-Greek-to-Latin letter descent, H-W-H maps to E-V-E. We demonstrate that the second He admits an ambiguity: iteration (Masoretic reading, producing imperfective loop H-H) or termination (producing aorist reading). Under termination, …

records.title: The EVEZ Reading of the Tetragrammaton: Letter Descent, Root Isomorphism, and the Termination Ambiguity of the Second He
records.abstract: We present a novel reading of the Tetragrammaton (YHWH) based on two established facts of historical linguistics: (1) the Phoenician letters He and Waw are the direct ancestors of Greek Epsilon (E) and Upsilon/V, respectively; and (2) the initial Yod in YHWH functions as a third-person masculine verbal prefix (y-), not as part of the semantic root. Removing the grammatical prefix yields the triconsonantal root H-W-H (to become). Through documented Phoenician-to-Greek-to-Latin letter descent, H-W-H maps to E-V-E. We demonstrate that the second He admits an ambiguity: iteration (Masoretic reading, producing imperfective loop H-H) or termination (producing aorist reading). Under termination, …

records.title: Left branch extraction in German fragment answers: Evidence for an in-situ approach
records.abstract: This paper investigates the role of contrastivity in Left Branch Extraction (LBE) under ellipsis, presenting experimental evidence from German to support an in-situ approach to clausal ellipsis. While prior research suggests that ellipsis can mitigate island violations, particularly in non-contrastive contexts (Merchant, 2001, 2004), recent proposals argue that ellipsis sites may be syntactically anisomorphic to their antecedents, allowing for alternative derivations that circumvent island constraints (Barros, 2014; Griffiths, 2019). However, these claims largely rely on informally collected acceptability judgments, leaving their empirical robustness in question. To address this gap, …

records.title: Ordering of clitics: Cartographic evidence for a universal functional sequence
records.abstract: The chapter examines the internal organisation of the functional domain between TP and CP from a cartographic perspective. The chapter treats the rigid ordering of clitics as evidence for which morphosyntactic features are projected there and in what order, bringing clitics into the cartographic investigation of this domain. Drawing on cross- linguistic generalisations from more than thirty languages and varieties, it develops its argument progressively, moving from relatively simple clitic systems to more complex ones. In doing so, it offers a more precise reconstruction of the universal functional sequence between TP and CP and establishes a robust baseline for future research on clitic …

records.title: Differential object marking in Chavacano
records.abstract: This research investigates differential object marking in the Zamboanga dialect of Chavacano (ZChav), a Spanish-based Creole spoken in Zamboanga region in the south of the Philippines. Using various diagnostics, we show that differential object marking in ZChav correlates with epistemic specificity and discourse-linkedness. We ultimately tie both of these phenomena to the notion of the Common Ground and propose that it underlies the distribution of the differential object marker. We further make some notes on the interaction between differential object marking and word order in ZChav. ZChav is a VSO language; however, with non-specific objects the word order VOS is found. For VSO order, we …

records.title: Cognitive Grammar analysis of Compromise Forms in Bilingual Speech at an Idiolectal level
records.abstract: This paper presents evidence of language contact at the level of the idiolect by applying Ronald Langacker’s Cognitive Grammar framework to bilingual pedagogical discourse. Analyzing seven classroom lectures from a multilingual Indian instructor, the study examines non-standard compromise forms, focusing on integration of construction schemas through extension relations at the level of the individual structured inventory. Rather than demonstrating a shift between bounded linguistic systems as separate mental spaces, the data reveals a fluid, integrated structured inventory where constructions are selected based on cognitive economy and conceptual negotiation. The results show that …

records.title: Italian Pronominal Motion Verbs
records.abstract: In Italian, motion verbs (MVs) may combine with the reflexive clitic SI and the clitic NE, yielding what I call pronominal motion verbs (PMVs). Since PMVs freely alternate with their non-pronominal counterparts, the semantic and syntactic contribution of these clitics remains poorly understood. I argue that SI is a syntactic argument merged in the specifier of a high applicative head, which introduces a direct experiencer Theta-role, whereas NE is associated with a low applicative head with locative semantics. Building on and extending Martin & Arunachalam's (2022) analysis of other Romance pronominal verbs, this study develops an analysis of PMVs that accounts for the Italian data. More …

records.title: The role of word order in the diachrony of flagging
records.abstract: This article challenges the widespread idea that case affixes generally evolve from adpositions through increasing “bondedness.” Instead, I propose that word order, not only increasing tightness of attachment, is another primary factor determining whether a marker becomes an affix or remains a clitic. Using a simple and clear definition of clitic, the paper notes that flags are affixes (case markers) when there is no adnominal modifier occurring between them and the noun, but adpositions otherwise. In view of this, it may be that we need to revise our thinking about grammaticalization, because what all grammaticalization changes share is the development of bound markers from free contentful …

records.title: Unchanging Core Syntax: Gender in Heritage Tamil
The domain of phonological processes
records.abstract: In Optimality Theory (Prince & Smolensky 1993), phonological constraints are evaluated with respect to a domain corresponding to the usual notion of grammatical word. I argue here that some common phonological patterns are better analysed by relaxing this restriction. In particular, while a notion of 'phonological' or 'prosodic' word has previously been shown to provide the relevant domain for phonological processes, I argue that productive morphemes can also provide such a domain. The hypothesis is tested with respect to data from Australian and other languages. I show that a model allowing for both intra-and inter-word domains of evaluation provides a more unified analysis of …

records.title: Modality and Aspect
records.abstract: This chapter examines the reality of conceptual and formal distinctions between the semantic categories of modality and (grammatical) aspect, focusing on three broad classes of phenomena in which these categories appear tightly intertwined. I first explore the case for eroding a formal distinction by examining arguments for incorporating modality in the semantic contribution of aspectual operators: I discuss modal solutions to the well-known imperfective (progressive) paradox, as well as apparently modal meaning associated with the core interpretation of (non-culminating) perfectives, perfects, and prospectives. Second, I discuss two phenomena in which modal interpretation appears to either …

records.title: Non-canonical agreement in early grammars
records.abstract: Children acquiring a diverse range of unrelated language go through a stage, typically between the ages of 2 and 3, where they use bare, infinitival or default forms instead of the agreeing forms required in adult grammar. Whether such under agreement errors reflect non-adult syntax for agreement or incomplete morphological knowledge has been a topic of debate for decades (Brown 1973, Radford 1990, Rizzi 1994, Wexler, 1998, a.o.). These errors are interesting developmentally, since children otherwise make few grammatical errors, and theoretically, given the central role of agreement in understanding the combinatorial mechanisms of natural language. In this paper, we approach this classic …

records.title: Resolving Relatedness in a Reconstructed Lexicon:  A Probabilistic Method for Proto-Language Internal Reconstruction
records.abstract: The standard comparative method in historical linguistics relies on written evidence to establish relatedness. In reconstructed proto-languages, where such evidence is unavailable, claims of internal connections are often considered unprovable. This paper introduces a probabilistic method for assessing whether phonemic similarity between two forms in a closed system is likely to be coincidental. Applying the method to Proto-Indo-European, we show that the three-phoneme root h₁és-, shared by the copula and the third-person pronoun paradigm, has a probability of coincidental identity of approximately 1 in 27,000 under uniform assumptions, and roughly 1 in 13,000 under frequency-adjusted …

records.title: Inter-modularity: Some Special Properties of Certain Quantifiers in German,  With Focus on Uninflected Ganz and Halb
records.abstract: This paper focuses on the special properties of ganz ‘whole’ and halb ‘half’ in German. It is observed that they do not have an inflection in the singular when a determiner is absent. Discussing other properties, it is documented that the nominals involving these quantifiers are situated between regular syntactic constructions and regular morphological formations. Given that the head noun must involve a proper name, it is proposed that the proper name incorporates into the quantifier as an instance of N-raising. At the end of the paper, some other exceptional quantifiers are briefly discussed.

records.title: Expert Grammaticality Judges as Evaluators, Not Participants: Grammaticality Judgments, Rater Roles, and Research Ethics Review
records.abstract: A grammaticality judgment is always a human act, but it isn't always participant data. Whether the person who supplies one is a participant or an evaluator should turn on what the judgment is evidence of: a person (reactions, processing, or dialect) or an object (an item's status under a stated standard). The role isn't only an ethical classification; it also fixes the generalization a judgment licenses, over speakers or items. In the object case, the judge resembles an essay scorer or prescriptive annotator more than a survey respondent, and systematic, reliability-checked procedures mark measurement rather than a study of the judges. Canada's Tri-Council Policy Statement (TCPS 2) reaches …

records.title: Difference-in-differences for corpus linguistics: Causal inference, corpus composition, and linguistic change after shocks
records.abstract: A form's frequency may move after a shock (contact with another language, a new medium, a redrawn border, or a government decree), and whether the shock caused the change is a natural question. Difference-in-differences is built for that counterfactual, with the discipline applied economics already brings to constructed aggregates like price indices, where the observed number isn't the quantity of interest either. This paper carries that discipline to corpus frequencies, where it's rarely applied and where composition and coding make it bite harder. A corpus frequency is a population rate plus a composition-and-measurement term, so a causal reading requires separating several things a …

records.title: Aspects of ki-Nominalization in Korean
records.abstract: This paper analyzes -ki nominalizations in Korean. We identify two types of the -ki nominalizations,NOM-ki and GEN-ki, with distinct morphosyntactic properties. We propose an analysis along the lines of Kratzer (1996) in which the nominalizer -ki selects verbal projections of different sizes (TP and vP) to account for the observed patterns. We argue against previous accounts of -ki nominalizations, showing either that important generalizations were missed or that there were flaws in the previous analyses. We propose a novel generalization for the two types of -ki nominalizations and propose an appropriate analysis. Some outstanding issues and implications are briefly discussed.

records.title: To seem or not to seem
records.abstract: This paper examines the semantics and morphosyntax of the Russian verb kazat’sja ‘seem’. Kazat’sja and vygljadet’‘look’ are raising verbs that promote their Stimulus argument and raise an embedded constituent to the matrix clause. I argue that kazat’sja is a hybrid predicate combining properties of putative and perceptual verbs, and discuss Apresjan’s proposal to distinguish two lexemes: putative kazat’sja¹ versus perceptual kazat’sja². Kazat’sja² is an obligatory raising verb, whereas with kazat’sja¹ raising is optional. Both kazat’sja¹ and kazat’sja² project three thematic roles: sentential Stimulus, dative Experiencer; and Observer, which may remain covert. The analysis is based on the …

records.title: Laterals patterning with plosives, a piece of evidence from diminutive formation in Modern Frisian
records.abstract: This squib presents evidence from Frisian diminutive formation that laterals may pattern with plosives and nasals to the exclusion of fricatives.

records.title: Mandarin verb doubling and its implications for the syntactic theory
records.abstract: This thesis is concerned with Mandarin verb doubling and its implications for the syntactic theory. I propose a phrasal movement analysis of verb doubling, namely that the doubling configuration in question is derived from verbal phrasal movement out of an articulated verbal structure. After the overall introduction in chapter 1, chapter 2 lays out the core properties of the verbal phrasal movement involved in verb doubling, that is, the fronted verbal phrase can target two landing sites in the clausal spine. I argue that this two-landing-site analysis has both theoretical and empirical advantages over other hypothetical alternatives. Chapter 3 discusses the role of postverbal adverbials in …

records.title: The Curse of Babel: Language, Structure, and the Promise of Translational AI
records.abstract: When a 98-year-old woman disappeared from Tokyo's welfare system in 2023, every institution followed proper procedures—yet coordination failed completely. Building on the concept of "Babel Syndrome" proposed by Matsuura (2018), which describes conflicts between specialized professions, this paper argues that such systemic failures originate in the structure of language itself. The function of language—to divide and label reality—has been **evolutionarily optimized for efficiency and** the cognitive style of the majority (NeuroTypical), producing invisible barriers between different kinds of minds and the institutions built upon them. At this deeper level, language becomes a hostile …

records.title: Thinking Inside the Box: Genitive Subject Licensing in Uyghur under the Miracle Creed System
records.abstract: This paper revisits the licensing of genitive subjects in Uyghur embedded clauses. Building on Asarina and Hartman’s (2011) D-licensing analysis, we argue that the simplified Miracle Creed system provides a more principled account of the relevant facts. We first show that the D-licensing approach is largely compatible with the MC architecture. Adopting the view that boxed elements created by Internal Merge are accessible to higher phase heads, we propose that phase-head access can be reduced to a target-conditioned application of Minimal Search. Under this approach, the licensing of genitive subjects, the optional omission of genitive morphology, scope asymmetries between genitive and …

records.title: Accommodation, acquisition, attrition? The (un)changing grammars of Standard Southern British English speakers in Belfast
records.abstract: There has been traditionally little communication and consensus between the field of language attrition, and variationist sociolinguists investigating dialect change, despite shared interest in the outcomes of language and dialect contact. In this paper, we aim to bridge this divide, outlining ways in which the fields already converge, and where they can inform each other to build a greater understanding of the mechanisms underlying changes to an adult’s otherwise established grammatical state. We do so by investigating two properties of Belfast English in the grammars of L1a Standard Southern British English speakers who have been living in Belfast for, on average, 25 years, having …

records.title: Subjectless assumption in Japanese -te aru configuration
records.abstract: There are two main types of -te aru configurations in Japanese: the intransitivizing and non-intransitivizing -te aru. For the intransitivizing -te aru, it is essential to further verify and clarify the (non-)existence of the agent and its syntactic nature. This article investigates the argument structure of the intransitivizing -te aru, aiming to determine whether there is a covert agent in the structure through subject-oriented adverbs. By comparing it with similar structures in Japanese, such as the passive structure, nominative object structure, and unaccusative verb structure, the generative mechanism of the intransitivizing -te aru can be confirmed. The results show that there is no …

records.title: Merge as Graph Extension
records.abstract: This paper proposes a graph-theoretic interpretation of Merge inside the Workspace. The Workspace is represented as a directed graph, and syntactic objects are represented as Paths or subgraphs inside that graph. An application of Merge preserves the Paths already present and adds a new accessible Path. The new Path can then participate in later applications of Merge inside the same accumulated Workspace. The proposal is stated inside a seven-Layer architecture, with C-I and A-P as external systems and five internal Layers of the Language Faculty: Semantic Component (Σ), A-Syntax, A-bar Syntax, Distributed Morphology (DM), and Phonological Component (Φ). Each internal Layer applies an …

records.title: Decomposing Portmanteaux: Pronominal Morphology and Prosodic Structure in Kono
records.abstract: In many languages with STAMP (Subject-Tense-Aspect-Mood-Polarity) morphology, subject pronouns and tense-aspect auxiliaries surface as apparent portmanteau morphemes whose forms can vary quite unpredictably across paradigm cells. These patterns have often been treated as suppletive, effectively derived from dedicated morphological operations. This paper examines STAMP forms in Kono (Central Mande, Sierra Leone) and argues that the observed paradigmatic variation does not reflect suppletion. Rather, pronouns and auxiliaries remain distinct morphosyntactic objects throughout the derivation, with surface variation arising from independently motivated phonological processes. The same …

records.title: The repetition ratio r/R measures length and encoding, not linguistic status: a reanalysis of Sproat (2014)
records.abstract: The repetition ratio rule (RRR), based on the ratio r/R of geminate to total repeats, has been proposed as a discriminant between linguistic and non-linguistic symbol systems. We show that for short and moderate-length inscriptions the expected r/R (precisely, the ratio of expectations E[r]/E[R]) under a random control is 2/L, where L is the per-inscription token count. The threshold r/R = 0.10 therefore functions as a test of mean inscription length ≥ 20. We demonstrate that RRR misclassifies in both directions when length is matched: top-100 American and Finnish given names, exchange-traded commodity labels, and 10,749 deciphered Mesopotamian seal legends (r/R ∈ [0.13, 0.53]) are …

records.title: Sources of Variability in the ACC-marked External Possession in Korean
records.abstract: This paper seeks to provide an answer to why there is so much disagreement among authors and speakers regarding data instantiating the ACC-marked external possession construction (EPC) in Korean. Along the way, it also provides answers to when ACC-marked EP sentences in Korean are licensed, and why EP-encoding multiple accusative (MA) sentences and non-EP-encoding MA sentences have the same surface form even though the latter do not have a grammatical internal possession counterpart. By conducting a carefully-constructed grammaticality judgment task, I argue that (i) speakers have variable acceptability judgments for the EPC because of the pragmatically marked nature of the construction; …

records.title: A Sketch of the Sampang Language
records.abstract: This work is a grammatical sketch of the Sampang language, an endangered language belonging to the Kiranti branch of the Trans‑Himalayan (Sino‑Tibetan) language family. It is the first published work to cover all aspects of grammar, including phonology, morphology, syntax and lexicon. Like many Kiranti languages, Sampang has extremely complex verbal morphology, displaying both subject and object agreement as well as intricate morphophonological alternations, and a substantial portion of the sketch is devoted to these issues. Other points of linguistic interest include the syntax of case and agreement, and the natureof linking morphs in the language. Some notes are made on the lexicon of the …

records.title: The Motivated Sign in Arabic: Iconicity across Morphology and Grammar
records.abstract: Abstract This article challenges the Saussurean arbitrariness principle by demonstrating that the Arabic linguistic sign is systematically motivated, and that the relationship between phonological form and meaning in Arabic is non-arbitrary at multiple simultaneous levels. Drawing on evidence from four interconnected domains, we advance a theoretical framework of phonosemantic iconicity in which articulatory properties of sounds iconically pre-figure semantic content. First, we demonstrate that the Arabic root-and-pattern verb form paradigm is diagrammatically iconic — the phonological operations of gemination, vowel extension, prefixation, and infixation enact the semantic operations they …

records.title: How English is like Kiitharaka and Búlí: successive cyclicity and optional wh-complementizer agreement in English
records.abstract: We report seven pairs of production and judgment experiments showing that English speakers are less likely to produce "that" when the relevant complementizer lies on the hierarchical path of an A-bar dependency, although "that" in such environments does not reliably lower acceptability. We argue that this production effect reflects optional wh–complementizer agreement, which is difficult to detect in acceptability judgments due to optionality and syncretism. We also find that the effect is sensitive to the distinction between terminal and non-terminal movement. Specifically, it is absent when the complementizer is the highest C in the second conjunct of across-the-board (ATB) extraction …

records.title: Vietnamese Language in Bilingual and Multilingual Environments: Acquisition, Learning and Unlearning
records.abstract: Bilingualism and second language learning always involve the interaction between two language systems or subsystems. When young children acquire language, often there is more than one. Considering the modern era, as the Vietnamese language has expanded geographically and culturally, coming into contact with other language communities, all of the different combinations of acquisition, learning and unlearning have come into play. These include, today, perhaps for the first time in recent history, language interactions that include first language attrition. This progress report of tentative results from our project compares the bilingual learning circumstances in two studies (in Taiwan and in …

records.title: Unconditional Questions: Semantically Legitimate, Pragmatically Degraded
records.abstract: Unconditional questions such as “Whether or not the party is at Emma's place, will it be fun?” are often judged degraded, despite the acceptability of their declarative counterparts. This paper argues that their degradation is pragmatic rather than semantic. Building on inquisitive semantics and stack-based suppositional semantics, I develop a compositional account in which unconditional questions are interpreted relative to multiple hypothetical contexts corresponding to antecedent alternatives. I then propose two pragmatic constraints on their use. First, extending Theiler's (2021) Epistemic Bridge, I argue that every antecedent alternative must sustain an inquisitive issue with respect …

records.title: QUD-sensitive projection in a dynamic semantics with alternatives
records.abstract: This paper presents a compositional dynamic system (building on Muskens 1996; Stone 1999; Brasoveanu 2006; Farkas and Bruce 2010; AnderBois et al. 2015), in which question alternatives are introduced via the random assignment of propositional discourse referents. This system provides a framework for implementing a mechanism for presupposition projection that is sensitive to the question under discussion (QUD; Ginzburg 1996; Roberts 2012; Büring 2003, Farkas and Bruce 2010). The analysis addresses the triggering problem by treating presuppositions as entailments (Abrusán 2011) and derives projection for not-at-issue entailments, following work linking projection to at-issueness (e.g., Simons …

records.title: Coming to remember
records.abstract: This paper is concerned with change-of-state uses of memory predicates like English remember. Change-of-state ‘remember’ appears to denote a change from not remembering to (stative) remembering – roughly ‘(slowly/suddenly) coming to remember’. It is, therefore, suitable to indicate constructive episodic memory retrieval. I argue that these uses are best captured as regular stative remembering, but with only partial – i.e. sub-atomically quantified – events as their object. I predict that remembering some, but not all, details of an event shows homogeneity effects arising from non-maximality. Speakers’ extra-linguistic projection of motion and change onto the third truth-value leads to the …

records.title: Logophors, person and the typological landscape of shiftiness
records.abstract: Logophoric pronouns of the kind found in West African languages have been extensively studied by typologist and formal linguists alike for more than five decades. However, there has been few attempts to connect this line of work with a formal approach to pronouns and the features they consist of, most notably Person (Silverstein, 1976; Zwicky, 1977; Noyer, 1992; Harbour, 2016). The overarching goal of this contribution is to fill this gap, and provide a formal account of logophoric pronouns grounded in a full-fledged theory of person features. Taking inspiration from Schlenker (2003), we propose that logophoric pronouns are non-indexical first persons, specified with a -ACTUAL feature. Our …

records.title: Statistical physics of language change inferred from time evolving maps
records.abstract: Language change may be studied by tracking linguistic variant frequencies through space and time. Observed frequencies may be viewed as realisations of a statistical field. We first set out an efficient cross validated method for inferring the empirical field — the variant frequency distribution estimated directly from data — in our case, high resolution surveys from 20th century USA. We then derive a model of the statistical field, assuming that individuals diffuse locally, periodically migrate, and copy one another based on a form of replicator dynamics involving both bias and linguistic accommodation. We infer model parameters by comparing changes in model and empirical fields. Our …

records.title: Los verbos acabados en -uir y las desinencias verbales del español
records.abstract: This paper proposes a morphological segmentation of the regular Spanish verbal paradigm that significantly simplifies its analysis. In the proposed model, the thematic vowel (TV) is always present in the underlying representation of all verbal forms of the three conjugations, either as stressed or as pre-accented. This analysis offers several advantages over more traditional approaches, such as those represented by recent grammars by the Royal Spanish Academy, since it allows the morphological structure of the three regular conjugations to be unified, including verbs whose root ends in a vowel, like those ending in -uir, with an /i/ following the root that has usually been analysed as an …

records.title: Distributional and Inflectional Properties of Quantifying Words in German: Abstract Agreement Chains Revisited
records.abstract: Quantificational elements fall into different groups in German. Besides quantificational determiners, there are adjectival quantifiers and indeclinable quantifiers. I demonstrate that (non-numeral) indeclinable quantifiers cannot be preceded by determiners. Rather than proposing that these types of quantifiers (or parts of them) are in the DP-layer, I argue that these cases can be explained by Bayer's (2015) agreement chain. If so, this means that these quantifiers can appear below the DP-layer.

records.title: Serialization as Situation. A Formal-Situational Account of Serial Verb Constructions
records.abstract: This paper examines Serial Verb Constructions (SVCs) from a new interdisciplinary perspective by linking linguistic analysis models with the sociological Theory of the Formal Situation (FS). At its core, by re-evaluating cross-linguistic data through this novel lens, the study offers a critique of established, purely morphosyntactic definitions—specifically Martin Haspelmath’s feature-based approach—arguing that such models often neglect pragmatic context and situational embedding. The paper posits that linguistic structures do not primarily follow an innate grammatical code; instead, they emerge as representations of universal situational dimensions: space, time, and quantity. The …

records.title: Negation, n-words and indefinites in Aromanian A comparison with Albanian
records.abstract: The article addresses the negation structures in Aromanian. In this language the Strict Negative Concord is applied, whereby the negative marker (NM) nu is always requested, also in the presence of n-words, particularly those corresponding to the arguments of the verb. In negative contexts, however, we may also find specialized indefinite elements which in turn give rise to the negative reading. This distribution, specifically the types of negative doubling, is explained by assuming that the negative operator is not realized by a lexical constituent but is postulated and made available to interpretation by the presence of NM and n-words. The Chomskyan theory of Phases and the lexical …

records.title: A unified theory of meta-questions
records.abstract: We propose a unified analysis of “meta questions”, a variety of questions about the intentions behind a speech act, among them “Echo-questions”. We analyze meta questions as run-of-the-mill questions in which a wh-Phrase covertly scopes over silent speech-act-material. The silence of the speech act material and the covertness of the movement are derived from independently motivated constraints in the theory of spell-out. The analysis explains a restriction on recursion of ilent speech acts, more specifically the limited distribution of meta-meta questions (Trinh 2024)

records.title: Altersunterschiede in der Interpretation von Gesichtsemojis
records.abstract: In der Untersuchung habe ich Daten zur Interpretation von ausgewählten Gesichtsemojis entlang den Dimensionen Bekanntheit, Valenz und Ambiguität sowie Beschreibungen für die bislang wenig erforschte Altersgruppe der unter 18-Jährigen erhoben und mittels Lemmatisierung und Varianzanalyse sowie einer Kategorisierung der genannten Bedeutungen analysiert. Diesen Ansatz habe ich vergleichend ebenso für die Altersgruppe der Erwachsenen mithilfe des bereits erhobenen Datensatzes von Scheffler & Nenchev (2024) durchgeführt und grafisch entlang der untersuchten Dimensionen dargestellt. Die Untersuchung hat keine relevanten Unterschiede in der Interpretation von Gesichtsemojis zwischen den …

records.title: Feature-Specific Transition Dynamics in Sperm Whale Codas and the CEJONG Cell-and-Tier Notation Framework
records.abstract: Sperm whale codas have been described from two angles: as combinable timing features (rhythm, tempo, ornament, and a slow inter-coda drift termed rubato), and as recurrent spectral patterns within individual clicks labeled a-vowel and i-vowel. The two have not been analyzed jointly at the level where representational decisions are made, which is the consecutive same-speaker transition. This study aligns the two systems on 1,170 vowel-labeled codas from 13 individually identified Eastern-Caribbean whales and tests whether each pair of features moves together across transitions. The resulting transition structure is feature-specific: rhythm and tempo are tightly coupled, ornament adds no …

records.title: Question under Discussion and question bias: Biased A-not-A questions in Mandarin Chinese
records.abstract: This chapter develops a pragmatic analysis of question bias through a case study of Mandarin shi-bu-shi questions. Building on Ye’s (2021a) QUD-based analysis, it argues that the bias associated with shi-bu-shi questions is QUD-dependent, arising from how possible answers contribute to resolving the current Question under Discussion, rather than being directly encoded as a fixed component of the lexical meaning of shi. This view is supported by the observation that the bias in shi-bu-shi questions varies with the nature of the relevant QUD. This chapter further demonstrates that biased questions need not be monopolar. Evidence from responsive embedding and unconditionals shows that …

records.title: Organic Omission: The Evolution of Pragmatics and Defining the In-Group
records.abstract: Modern digital communication increasingly relies on the systematic abandonment of standard orthographic and syntactic signals, a phenomenon frequently dismissed as casual shorthand or linguistic degradation. This paper challenges that assumption by introducing the concept of Systatic Omission: the deliberate, systemic subtraction of punctuation and capitalization executed as a generative pragmatic act to signal intimacy and enforce in-group boundaries. Drawing on Crystal’s foundational digital linguistics, Androutsopoulos’s heteroglossic registers, Han’s cultural critique of the digital swarm, and Taylor’s constitutive theory of language, we establish a framework showing how structural …

records.title: Morpheme structure phonotactics: a categorical model for morpho-phonological productivity in Russian vowel-zero alternations
records.abstract: Nonce word studies motivate a notion of gradient similarity between nonce words and real words. In morpho-phonological research, similarity is often taken as to be a relationship between a nonce word and the list of morphemes / words that undergo a given morphophonological alternation (Albright and Hayes 2003; Becker et al. 2011 i.a.). This paper challenges this view on the basis of nonce word data on Russian vowel–zero alternations (Gouskova and Becker 2013; Becker and Gouskova 2016). I propose a model where morpho-phonological similarity is a relationship between the available underlying representations and the underlying representation the nonce item must have in order to undergo the …

records.title: What you do is first-rate: MRI articulation movies made accessible
records.abstract: This paper reports a collaborative team effort to create MRI-based articulation movies that are accessible for children with hearing difficulties. While the existing MRI articulation movies are useful for college students and grown-up researchers, they can be scary, off-putting and overwhelming for children. My collaborators and I synched the existing MRI videos with an accessible picture. Not only does this succeed in making the movies generally more accessible, it also has the advantage of being able to show very clearly the teeth, the three larynx cartilages, and the distinction between hard palate and soft palate. Our team also came up with a means to explain manner of articulation in …

records.title: Did Humans Invent Language?
records.abstract: No non-human animal has spontaneously acquired language with open-ended vocabulary and rule-governed syntax. This paper proposes that language was invented by early modern Homo sapiens—a cultural act by cognitively capable individuals. Three clusters of novel hypotheses follow from this invention thesis. First, the language invention cluster: the Evolutionary Barrier to Language Hypothesis posits that no species has evolved language by incremental natural selection alone; the Language Invention Hypothesis proposes that humans invented a Free-Form Protolanguage (FFP) of symbolic words and flexible word combinations without structured syntax—sufficient to convey whole thoughts; and the …

records.title: Don't be so Negative: Towards Negation-Free Syntax and Semantics
records.abstract: Proof theorists in logic and mathematics have long been suspicious of the classical (Boolean) approach to negation. This suspicion began with work by Brouwer and Griss in the foundations of mathematics and extended to Heyting's proof theory for logic.
