Griss, in particular, inveighed against using negation in any form in proof theory. Setting aside questions about proof theory in mathematics and logic, what can we say about classical negation in a proof-theoretic semantics for natural language? Can we dispense with it? I argue that we can and, based on the evidence, we should. This suggests a corollary hypothesis: There is no genuine classical negation in the syntax of natural language. The …

records.title: Big DP & Big PRO: A unified account of reflexive and impersonal se
records.abstract: We argue that, despite the lack of an overt external argument in (most) impersonal/passive se clauses in Spanish, there is a syntactically projected external argument: an empty category PRO necessarily doubled by the pronominal clitic se. We unify all instances of so-called impersonal, passive and generic se as involving the same kind of external argument, whose interpretive qualities are determined by an operator. We further extend the same analysis to internal reflexive arguments that are also necessarily doubled by se, thus capturing the intuitive fact that PRO has anaphoric properties (Manzini 1983; Landau 2000; Kayne 2018; 2025). Our analysis has a major advantage, which is a uniform …

records.title: Measuring form and function in Large Language Models
records.abstract: We introduce quantitative metrics from child language research to evaluate language models. Our focus is on the formal syntactic and functional discourse properties of determiners in English, which young children acquire early and accurately. We propose Contextual Alternative Choice (CAC), a new prompting method which provides targeted tests for both syntactic and discourse knowledge of language. The method enables direct comparison of language models against children, and more importantly, against independently established benchmarks in empirical research. No current model trained on a comparable amount of data simultaneously meet both benchmarks like human children, but some models …

records.title: Self-destructive feeding as allomorph optimisation
records.abstract: This paper re-examines self-destructive feeding, a type of overapplication opacity, and proposes a new analysis based on the commonalities shared by all attested cases. It is found that all the four cases of self-destructive feeding found in Turkish, Javanese and Japanese involve rules with non-derived environment blocking and attempt to resolve consonant clusters by making changes to the suffix. Based on these common characteristics, a unified analysis is provided to account for not only the self-destructive feeding pattern but also its related phenomena simultaneously, with the help of underspecification and positional/contextual faithfulness under Parallel Optimality Theory. Finally, it …

records.title: The Identification of a Second Lunar Calendar on Rongorongo Tablet C (Mamari) (Preprint v1.13)
keywords: rongorongo easter island decipherment lunar calendar
records.abstract: This paper identifies and analyzes a previously unrecognized lunar calendar on the recto of Rongorongo Tablet C (Mamari). By applying a structural analysis to recurring delimiter sequences and "staff and bud" glyphs, the author demonstrates a second calendrical pattern (Lunar Calendar B) that aligns with the known lunar calendar identified by Thomas Barthel (Lunar Calendar A). The study compares the sequence of 29 "buds" in the new calendar with the 31 "nights" in the traditional calendar, proposing that the system may represent an agricultural cycle or an alternating 29/30-day lunar month used by the Rapanui people.

records.title: A Feature-Driven Tensor Semantics for Minimalist Grammars
records.abstract: This paper shows how tensor-based distributional semantics can be incorporated into Minimalist Grammars (MGs). We embed the MG feature calculus with a tensor algebra and give a joint tensor-based representation where compositional semantics is guided by the minimalist syntax. By bridging syntactic and semantic operations in tensor spaces, we aim to contribute to the broader enterprise of neurosymbolic approaches to linguistic cognition.

records.title: Havlík’s Law as a Syllabic Rule: A Structural Reanalysis of the Slavic Jers
records.abstract: Havlík’s Law is the classical description of jer behavior in Common Slavic, but its diachronic counting rule cannot be the synchronic rule modern Slavic speakers apply productively to new lexemes. This paper argues that Havlík’s Law is not a counting rule at all but the surface signature of a syllabification mechanism that operates at both temporal slices. A small ranked-constraint syllabifier decides which orthographic positions function as prosodic nuclei. Jers are not nuclei by default; they are promoted only when no other segment can serve. The central empirical contribution is two strictly sealed held-out tests totalling 60 OCS forms selected to lie outside every earlier corpus, with …

records.title: Swap distance minimization shapes the order of subject, object and verb in languages of the world
records.abstract: Languages of the world vary concerning the order of subject, object and verb. The most frequent dominant orders are SOV and SVO, and researchers have tailored models to this fact. However, there are still languages whose dominant order does not conform to these expectations or even lack a dominant order. Here we show that across linguistic families and macroareas, word order variation within languages is shaped by the principle of swap distance minimization even when the dominant order is not SOV/SVO and even when a dominant order is lacking.

records.title: Pair-list readings of questions: new evidence from specificational pseudoclefts
Split Antecedents Across Conjunctions
records.abstract: This study proposes and defends dependency-building dynamic conjunction, which tracks discourse dependencies established within its conjuncts. The proposal is motivated by novel empirical data from English and Japanese, in which the antecedents of a pronoun are spread across conjuncts. The resolution of the anaphora requires keeping track of the discourse dependencies established in the conjuncts as well as internal and external dynamicity. the dependency-building is a characteristic of the universal quantifier. This study suggests that conjunction should (at least sometimes) model dependencies as the universal quantifier does, and that the conjunction and universal quantifier are closer to …

records.title: Corrigendum to “Extending Flexible Boolean Semantics for the Language of Mathematics”
records.abstract: This note corrects a previous claim about the number of readings generated for the sentence "The integers and the reals are countable" in the flexible Boolean semantics framework. It is shown that only two readings are derivable, since a third reading is ruled out by independent constraints on the relevant semantic operators. This correction does not affect the main result that the framework still overgenerates interpretations due to structural ambiguity in coordination.

records.title: A new view on NAmE high negated questions: Experimental evidence and analysis
records.abstract: The consensus on English High Negated Questions (HNQs) is that they necessarily convey the speaker’s bias for the prejacent. I argue that it is the speaker’s bias for the addressee’s belief in the prejacent that is necessarily conveyed by HNQs. I support this claim with experimental results, which show that HNQs are not deemed felicitous without the speaker’s bias for the addressee’s belief in the prejacent even when there is speaker bias for the prejacent, and that they are felicitous when there is speaker bias for the addressee’s belief in the prejacent but no speaker bias for the prejacent. I propose a theoretical analysis which combines independently motivated elements to predict this …

records.title: A utility-based account of the choice of constituent question polarity
records.abstract: People choose their questions based on their conversational goals. But how do they decide between questions that would yield equivalent information? This study examines the mechanism by which a questioner chooses between constituent(“wh-”) questions of positive vs. negative polarity, e.g., “Who came?” vs. “Who did not come?”. Our Rational Speech Acts (RSA) model predicts the following: First, when a partial answer is expected, the question whose polarity aligns with the questioner’s goal is preferred over its opposite polarity counterpart. Second, this goal alignment effect decreases when the structure of the questioner’s decision problem requires an exhaustive answer. These predictions are …

records.title: Processing standard and expletive negation: An eye-tracking study on Italian temporal and causal clauses
records.abstract: Natural language sometimes expresses negation in rather puzzlingly different forms. Different from Standard Negation (SN), Expletive Negation (EN) involves a negative marker that does not affect the truth conditions of a sentence. The theoretical literature debates whether EN is a semantically empty element or a negative operator. This paper addresses this question by investigating the processing of EN and SN against affirmative sentences through an eye- tracking while reading experiment. EN is presented in Italian temporal clauses (It. Rimarrò qui finché Gianni non.EN verrà alla festa; Eng. ‘I will stay here until Gianni comes to the party.’) and SN in Italian causal clauses (It. Chiara è …

records.title: Event counting and discontinuity of the experiential perfect
records.abstract: This paper investigates counting in the domain of events under the Mandarin expe- riential perfect marker -guo, with particular attention to the contrast between the two counting expressions, ⌜NUM xia⌝ and ⌜NUM ci⌝, for different levels of counting. The central question is why only certain activity verbs are compatible with ⌜NUM xia⌝ under -guo, and more generally what constrains the availability of event counting in this environment. I propose that the observed contrast is grounded in a distinction between two subclasses of activity verbs: those whose denotation is associated with determinate endpoints, and those whose denotation lacks such endpoints. Building on this distinction, I argue …

records.title: Spanish subject-verb agreement as cliticization: A Merge-based approach
records.abstract: In this paper, I evaluate the claim that cliticization and “true” phi-agreement are technologically distinct from one another (Zwicky & Pullum 1983; Kramer 2014; Preminger 2014; Yuan 2021, a.o.) against the argument clitic and subject-verb inflectional paradigms from Spanish, showing that argument clitics and subject-verb agreement morphemes in this language display a striking number of formal and distributional similarities that cast doubt on the idea that these two phenomena are underlyingly distinct. Motivated by these similarities, I unify these phenomena by reducing subject-verb agreement to the technology involved in cliticization (e.g., Taraldsen 1992; 1993; Barbosa 1995; Ordóñez …

records.title: Sentiment-linked quantification among adjectives
records.abstract: Yoon (1996) observed that "The cups are clean" is taken by default to describe all the cups, while "The cups are dirty" might describe only some of them. This paper grounds Yoon’s clean/dirty contrast in the sentiment (valence) of these adjectives: "clean" is desirable, "dirty" undesirable. Sentiment is linked to quantification through the longstanding idea, known as the Anna Karenina Principle, that a good situation must be all good, while any bad element makes it bad. Assuming that “Is the current situation okay?” is a common Question Under Discussion across contexts, positive-sentiment adjectives are easily taken to answer this question affirmatively, conveying that the current situation …

records.title: on the proper use of commutation
records.abstract: Thanks to the foundational work of Saussure and Troubetzkoy, further developed by Hjelmslev and Martinet, linguists today possess a highly effective tool for language description: commutation. However, these great pioneers did not provide clear methodological guidelines for applying this tool to the study of significant linguistic units. In this article, I would like to help young researchers use commutation correctly and avoid some common mistakes.Indeed, deploying this analytical method requires some precautions. Above all, it is essential to begin by carefully preparing the field—identifying and selecting relevant contexts in which commutation can be meaningfully applied and lead to …

records.title: Cognitive Grammar analysis of Compromise Forms in Bilingual Speech at an Idiolectal level
records.abstract: This paper presents evidence against matrix-language approaches to code-switching by applying Ronald Langacker’s Cognitive Grammar framework to bilingual pedagogical discourse. Analyzing seven classroom lectures from a multilingual Indian instructor, the study examines non-standard compromise forms, focusing integration of construction schemas through extension relations at the level of the individual structured inventory. Rather than demonstrating a shift between bounded linguistic systems as separate mental spaces, the data reveals a fluid, integrated structured inventory where constructions are selected based on cognitive economy and conceptual negotiation. The results show that …

records.title: A Note on the Syntax and Semantics of Chinese Classifiers
records.abstract: We examine the structure of classifier constructions in Mandarin Chinese in light of Little et al.’s (2022) proposal on the semantics of two kinds of classifier constructions and Zhang's (2011, 2013) analysis of classifiers in Chinese. Little et al. propose that classifiers either compose first with nouns (classifiers-for-nouns) or compose first with numerals (classifiers-for-numerals). The semantic denotation of numerals is different in both cases. Zhang proposes that Chinese has both structures. Taking both proposals at face valve would require us to assume that numerals are listed twice in the lexicon in Chinese (once for each denotation in Little et al.’s models). We critically examine …

records.title: A Brief Discussion of Free Merge, Markovian Merge, and Non-Markovian Merge
keywords: free merge; markovian merge; non-markovian merge
records.abstract: This paper is principally concerned with the principle of Free Merge, arguably one of the central commitments of the Minimalist Programme. It first traces the relevant theoretical developments, before turning to a more gradual analysis of three notions: Free Merge, Markovian Merge, and Non-Markovian Merge. The discussion will then consider what kinds of problems this theoretical apparatus may be able to address, while also offering an exposition and interpretation of Chomsky’s most recent proposals.

records.title: It May or May Not Be Relevant: Testing the Relationship Between Relevance and Informativeness
records.abstract: The dominant view in cognitive science and formal pragmatics is that relevance is a matter of informativeness: a sentence is relevant if it is informative, and irrelevant otherwise. We provide experimental evidence against this thesis. For polar questions (e.g. ‘Is Mary coming to the party?’), we constructed two kinds of uninformative replies: replies that clearly violate relevance (uninformative-off-topic condition; e.g. ‘Mary lives in an old house’) and replies that are equally uninformative yet do not intuitively incur a relevance violation, such as uncertainty or disagreement reports (target condition; e.g. ‘Her parents disagree about that’). In a within-subject study (N = 100; 12 …

records.title: The temporal semantics of proximate futures in English and Turkish
records.abstract: Proximate futures, like English 'be about to' or Turkish 'üzere', are a type of future expression which entails that an eventuality will hold at a future time that is close to the reference time (RT) from tense. While past work on the semantics of future expressions has primarily focused on contrasts between WOLL, 'be going to', and their cross-linguistic counterparts (e.g., Copley 2002, Klecha 2014), less work has investigated the semantics of proximate futures (for an exception, see Hill 2025). What is the core semantic contribution of proximate future expressions, and to what extent does the meaning of proximate futures vary cross-linguistically? In this paper, I discuss a set of …

records.title: Huautla Mazateco Complex Segments as Single Phonemes: A Multi-layered Subsegmental Structure Approach
records.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to the analysis of consonantal phonetic sequences in Huautla Mazatec. These sequences comprise a large inventory of both simple and complex phonemes, including typologically unexpected contrasts such as pre- vs. post-aspirated consonants like /ht/ vs. /th/ or /hnd/ vs. /nth/. This paper argues that the primary phonological contrast between these phonemes does not reside in temporal anchoring or linearity, but rather in a distinct arrangement within a subsegmental hierarchical binary structure. This approach adapts Pike & Pike's (1947) 'Immediate Constituents' proposal to the representational framework of Q-Theory (Garvin et al. 2018; Inkelas & Shih 2016; …

records.title: Knowledge as Conventionalized Arbitrary Relations: Toward a Theory of Epistemology
records.abstract: This paper proposes that encyclopedic knowledge — what we know about the world, as distinct from what follows from definitions or logical structure — consists fundamentally of conventionalized arbitrary relations. Drawing on Saussurean sign-arbitrariness, Kripkean modal semantics, and the gradient conventionalization framework developed in prior work on lexical meaning, the paper argues that every empirical claim depends on a contingent carving of reality into concepts and a contingent act of reference-fixing that anchors those concepts to worldly entities. Both operations are arbitrary in the Saussurean sense and require intersubjective stabilization before they can function as publicly …

records.title: Back Jer as a Negative Marker: Jer Color in Slavic Liquid Contexts as an Etymological Diagnostic and Evidence for Syllabic-Resonant Coloring
records.abstract: Old Church Slavonic distinguishes two jer letters, ъ (back) and ь (front), whose distribution in liquid contexts (CъrC/CьrC, CъlC/CьlC) has resisted phonolog- ical explanation for over a century. This paper makes a coordinated empirical and theoretical claim. Empirically, on the basis of a 128-word Proto-Slavic corpus together with a reanalysis of Kuryłowicz’s (1956) survey of Trautmann’s (1924) Balto-Slavic dictionary, jer color in these positions is shown to function as an ety- mological diagnostic: front jer ь marks inheritance from a PIE syllabic resonant (*r̥, *l ̥); back jer ъ marks every other source—loanwords, laryngeal sequences, substrate vocabulary, full-grade roots. The …

records.title: The Hand That Measures: Greek δῶρον 2 and the Body-Part-as-Measure Cluster on PIE *de-r-
records.abstract: Frisk's Griechisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch and Beekes's Etymological Dictionary of Greek both treat Greek δῶρον as two entries: δῶρον 1 "gift," with its established derivation from PIE *deh₃-ro-, and δῶρον 2 "palm-of-the-hand, palm-as-measure," marked by Frisk as origin unknown and by Beekes as ◁?▷. This paper supplies the etymology Frisk left open. records.title: The Etymology of Albanian dorë: PIE *de-r- “hand, open palm,” the *ĝhʰesr--side reading, and the ARM → HAND grammaticalization pathway
records.abstract: Albanian dorë "hand" (consonantal plural duar) has been derived in two competing ways since the nineteenth century. The *der-side reading, originating with Gustav Meyer's Albanesische Studien I (1883) and running through La Piana (1937, 1942), Belardi (1948), Pokorny (1959), and Frisk (1960–72), groups dorë with PIE *der- "Spanne der Hand" (Pokorny IEW 203) using only regular Albanian sound changes. The *ǵʰesr-side reading, canonicalized by Demiraj (1990, 1997) and inherited by Orel (1998), Vermeer (2008), and Beekes (2010), groups dorë with PIE *ǵʰesr- "hand" (IEW 447) but requires positing the irregular shift *ǵʰ → d in Albanian, where the regular reflex of PIE *ǵʰ is dh. records.title: LENGUA, DIALECTO Y DESCRIPCIÓN GRAMATICAL: EL CASO DEL ESPAÑOL RIOPLATENSE
records.abstract: This chapter offers an overview of the phonology, the lexicon, the morphology and the syntax of Rioplatense Spanish.

records.title: The Geometry of the Accusative
records.abstract: This paper challenges the existence of structural Case as an independent syntactic primitive within the Minimalist Program, arguing against both the Case-by-Agree mechanism and Dependent Case Theory. Adopting a strictly spatial-relational framework, we argue that unmarked core arguments are inherently caseless roots that saturate the eventive core through topological fusion, or pseudo-incorporation. Consequently, the Case Filter and Burzio's Generalization are revealed to be theoretical artifacts. We propose that marked alignments, such as Differential Object Marking (DOM) and the Ergative case, are not the result of abstract feature valuation or phase-mate competition, but the overt …

records.title: The Learnability of Bridge Effects
records.abstract: The distinction between bridge verbs, which allow long-distance questions out of their CP complement, and non-bridge verbs, which do not, is found in a range of languages. In the previous literature, this distinction has been variably attributed to the lexical semantic/discourse properties of the CP-embedding verbs, or the syntactic positioning of the dependent CP. In this study, we provide evidence for an alternative, learning-based account, whereby positive input evidence is needed for children to acquire the possibility of wh-dependencies across a CP-embedding verb, and to further generalize this property to all such verbs. We examine the bridge/non-bridge distinction in English and …

records.title: Some Notes towards a Dual Model of Language Development—  The Computational System behind   a Non-INFL stage of Child Language Acquisition  Absent Minded: A Reply to Borer and Rohrbacher
keywords: the dual mechanism model of language development
records.abstract: The study of syntactic development in children, for all intents and purposes, is reducible to a single-minded inquiry into how the very young child (implicitly) knows to distinguish between lexical stems and functional affixes. Hence, the overriding question burning in the minds of most developmental linguists is morpho-phonological in nature. It would seem that the child must at least know (a priori) the stem before she can then engage in a dual-track process by which ambient sound separation of the morpho-phonological distinction attributive to past tense is carried out, say, between the paradigmatic representation of the English word play vs. play-ed (a dual processing which provokes …

records.title: The logic of the English auxiliary system
records.abstract: This paper proposes an analysis of English auxiliary verbs in Hybrid Type-Logical Grammar. The proposed analysis integrates the key analytic ideas of both transformational and nontransformational approaches in the literature within a logic-based architecture of grammar in which the notion of (formal) inference plays a central role. We show that the proposed analysis not only provides principled and explicit analyses of major properties of English auxiliary verbs but also has interesting implications for crosslinguistic and diachronic aspects of the auxiliary system.

records.title: The Grammar of Absence
records.abstract: While comitative and instrumental relations have received extensive attention in the typological and generative literature, their negative counterpart—the caritive or abessive construction (e.g., without, sans, senza)—remains structurally under-theorized. Descriptive typologies cross-linguistically observe that expressions of absence are systematically more complex and heavily marked than expressions of presence (Stolz et al. 2007). This paper proposes a formal explanation for this markedness asymmetry based on a Double-Relator Model (DRM) and mereotopology. We argue that while comitative/instrumental markers are primitive relational heads computing simple inverse inclusion (⊇), abessive …

records.title: Atoms, Aggregates, and Elementary Predicates: on Proper Names in Italian and beyond
records.abstract: This article challenges uniform predicativism and covert light noun analyses of proper names. Using Italian and cross- linguistic data, we argue that onomastic morphosyntax relies on a mereosyntactic dichotomy: roots conceptualized as atomic individuals merge in D as referential expressions, whereas aggregates merge in N, requiring functional support. This distinction explains asymmetries in toponyms, temporal names, and plural names. For complex names (e.g., Lago di Garda), we propose they avoid ordinary predication by recruiting the exact mereological relators used for material constitution, directly fusing a sortal noun with a rigid designator into a unified domain. Note: After a series …

records.title: Beyond clausal ellipsis: a relational approach to exceptive constructions
records.abstract: We defend a phrasal, relational analysis of exceptive markers against clausal-ellipsis analyses (Vostrikova 2021; Seguin 2024). Universal Grammar, we argue, makes available one dedicated device for exception: a relational head — an Axial Part in a Double-Relator configuration (Franco 2024) — that subtracts the exception from a nominal restriction and surfaces as a PP. A language either grammaticalises such a head (Italian tranne, English except) or approximates exception with a Boolean coordinator plus negation (Italian ma non, English but not), which fails to enforce containment. Containment is therefore our central diagnostic: a marker that imposes it cannot be the Boolean periphrasis and …

records.title: Hallucination, Formal Reasoning, and the α-Gradient: A Linguistic Framework for AI Architecture
records.abstract: This paper applies the gradient conventionalization framework developed in Mozahid (2025a, 2025b, 2026) to the architecture of artificial intelligence systems, arguing that the persistent divide between statistical and categorical AI is fundamentally a semantic phenomenon rather than an engineering one. The framework operationalizes meaning components through levels of intersubjective agreement (α), providing a principled account of why different AI architectures can process only certain ranges of the α-gradient. Categorical systems operate exclusively at α→1.0; large language models (LLMs) operate across α=0.30–0.95, most reliably in the α=0.70–0.90 zone of default entailment. α-level …

records.title: The Theta Misanalysis Hypothesis: Non-Target Theta Assignment and Passive Unaccusatives in L2 English Acquisition
records.abstract: The distinction between two classes of intransitive verbs, unaccusatives (e.g., fall, appear) and unergatives (e.g., run, cry), has been argued to exist in L2 interlanguage grammar. This claim is supported by evidence that L2 English learners frequently produce and accept unaccusatives in passive constructions, suggesting an underlying association between NP-movement in unaccusative and passive derivations. Specifically, learners appear to misanalyze NP-movement in unaccusative structures as requiring passive morphosyntax (be + en). While this analysis accounts for a range of learner behaviors, it fails to capture two crucial factors: discourse-pragmatic influences and the role of subject …

records.title: Lambek linguistically: Towards a category theoretic semantics
records.abstract: This paper develops a category theoretic framework for natural language semantics grounded in the Curry-Howard-Lambek correspondence, with particular focus on intensional and hyperintensional phenomena. I argue that both classical simple type theories and modern record type theories inherit a fundamentally extensional notion of meaning from functional completeness, forcing intensional distinctions to be encoded through additional parameters, worlds, or type-theoretic complexity. In contrast, the present framework weakens functional completeness from uniqueness to representability within intensional domains, thereby allowing morphisms to differ structurally despite identical extensional …

records.title: ZË-RO Cohort 02 Cross-Model Supplement: Replication, Cleaner-Provisional Support, and Pressure Evidence
records.abstract: This short supplement note documents the post-publication cross-model evidence archive for the ZË-RO Cohort 02 bracket-testing study. The supplement archive contains assistant-assisted, researcher-reviewed evidence for three cases selected from the Cohort 02 result space: French /ø~œ/, Danish /ø/, and Turkish /ı/. The goal is not to upgrade the main Cohort 02 claim, but to record whether a small cross-model curation set preserves the distinction between support, cleaner-provisional support, and unresolved pressure. French /ø~œ/ remains the strongest cross-model support case in this supplement, Danish /ø/ remains a cleaner-provisional support case, and Turkish /ı/ remains an unresolved …

records.title: Manner Modification Across Modalities: Insights from Gesture, Sign, and Spoken Language
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates whether event-related modifiers contribute uniformly to interpretation across modalities, with a focus on contrasts between manner and other modifier types, including path and temporal expressions. It combines morphosyntactic analysis with experimental investigation across three empirical domains: Turkish Sign Language (TİD), English (including co-speech gesture), and Turkish. Across these domains, manner expressions diverge from other event-related modifiers and show a distinct interpretive profile under negation and in contrastive environments. First, I develop a morphosyntactic analysis of classifier constructions in TİD, showing that depictive content is …

records.title: Functional Extensionality and Its Discontents. The Curry–Howard–Lambek Correspondence and Natural Language Semantics
records.abstract: What does it mean for two expressions to have the same meaning? In formal semantics, the standard answer is functionally extensional: two expressions mean the same if their functional outputs are equal on all possible inputs. This answer, we argue, is not merely a methodological choice but a consequence of the formal foundations most semantic theories rely on. The Curry-Howard-Lambek correspondence (CHLC), unifying logic, computation, and category theory, carries an implicit commitment to functional extensionality that propagates into the semantic analysis of natural language. The problem is that language does not play by these rules. Speakers routinely distinguish meanings that extensional …

records.title: A unified analysis of prosodic inversion and infixation
records.abstract: This paper argues that infixation and prosodic inversion are best analyzed using the same formal tool, namely, prosodic subcategorization. We show that second-position clitics that have been analyzed as prosodic inversion can be reanalyzed in Cophonologies by Phase with prosodic subcategorization frames, P, that target prosodic constituents like ω, ϕ, or ι. This is shown to parallel an analysis of infixation, which is formally ident sub-word prosodic constituents such as C, V, or σ. This paper is the first in-depth exploration of the range of data that can be accounted for using the P-specifications in Cophonologies by Phase, including German contrastive coordinators, Serbo-Croatian …

records.title: Fine-tuning (in)definiteness in the absence of articles: Experimental investigation of Russian
records.abstract: Languages vary in the ways they encode (in)definiteness. In languages with articles, determiners like the and a/an in English explicitly mark whether a nominal is definite or indefinite. By contrast, in languages without articles, nouns can appear bare, with no special (in)definiteness marking. This raises a fundamental question: in the absence of articles, do bare nouns have a uniform semantic profile, and if so, is it definite-like, indefinite-like, or something else? Is this semantic profile the same in systems where bare nouns co-exist with overtly (in)definite nouns, like English, vs. in systems that have no articles whatsoever? This dissertation aims to answer these questions, …

records.title: Syntax and semantics interface of English and Igbo elliptical structures
records.abstract: ABSTRACT Nigeria’s linguistic landscape is a pluralistic one. Indigenous languages like Igbo and others coexist with English. With English being the language of education, interferences from these indigenous languages are inevitable. Hence, there is need for examinations of English and these indigenous languages. Such examination will properly characterize the features attested in the languages with their variations and hence, facilitate learning. Existing studies on Igbo, for example, have paid attention to characterize some syntactic features like morphology, morphosyntax, inflection and so on. Exploration into elliptical structures in both languages is lacking even though language users …

records.title: Animacy, intention, and null objects in English
records.abstract: It has long been known that the objects of at least some English verbs that are normally transitive can be omitted in at least some circumstances. In recent work, the animacy of the subject has emerged as a potential factor influencing sentence acceptability. While different theories make different predictions about where and how such effects emerge, little quantitative research exists on the extent and nature of animacy-related effects upon object omission. This paper presents a series of three experiments to elicit acceptability judgements on sentences differing in subject animacy and in the presence or absence of an overt object. It was found that not only are animacy and object presence …

records.title: Seven-Primal-Vowel Bracket Testing: Cohort 02 Support and Pressure Cases Across Six Languages
records.abstract: This paper reports Cohort 02 of the ZË-RO Seven-Primal-Vowel bracket-testing program. Cohort 02 extends prior vowel-bracket battery work by testing six language/vowel cases under researcher-reviewed scoring: Norwegian /ø/, Danish /ø/, French /ø~œ/, Portuguese /â/, Turkish /ı/, and Romanian /ă/. The purpose of Cohort 02 is not to claim that every tested case supports the framework. The purpose is to separate support cases from edge-stressed and pressure cases under a documented candidate/control workflow. French /ø~œ/ is the strongest current support case: V5-V7 candidate runs remained intermediate while V2-V5 controls collapsed high. Norwegian /ø/ and Danish /ø/ provide cautious V1-V3 …

records.title: Korean Honorification as Animacy-Based Gender
records.abstract: When discussing what (morphosyntactic) features syntactic theory should include, there is a tension between empirical adequacy and theoretical simplicity: a unique paradigm might seem to warrant a dedicated feature which does nothing but derive that phenomenon. Such a case is Korean honorification (the grammatical marking of politeness); many approaches make use of a bespoke feature like [HON] (Koopman 2005, Choi & Harley 2019, Ackema & Neeleman 2018, Portner et al. 2019, Jou 2024), while others argue this unique feature class is an undue overcomplication (Kim & Sells 2007, Kim & Findlay 2023, Song et al. 2019, Wang 2023). The latter line of work suggests that cross-linguistically, …

records.title: Expanding the nominal in English ACC- and POSS-ing nominalizations
records.abstract: Clausal nominalizations, like English ACC- and POSS-ing gerunds, exhibit both verbal and nominal properties. A classic observation is that these properties trade-off with one another: as a nominalization exhibits more verbal properties, it has fewer nominal ones (Chomsky 1970). This leads to nominalizations often being analyzed as "mixed extended projections" (Borsley & Kornfilt 2000): single abstract functional sequences whose limited positions are split between a verbal and nominal component (assuming 'parallelism' between domains; Chomsky 1970, Abney 1987, Grimshaw 1990, Szabolcsi 1994). As such a mixed extended projection is "filled up" with more verbal material, there is less room for …

records.title: Echoes Across the Sea: Reassessing Japonic Prehistory through Austronesian Comparanda
records.abstract: Investigations into proto-Japonic and proto-Austronesian etyma reveal a highly systematic set of phonetic and semantic correspondances. Several words are manually compared across the Japonic and Austronesian languages from the Oxford-NINJAL Old Japanese Corpus, Eastern Old Japanese Dictionary, Online Dictionary of Japonic Languages, Nikolay Nevskiy’s Miyakoan dictionary and the Austronesian Comparative Dictionary, including data from Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese Reconstructions. records.title: The optional infinitive stage in Japanese
records.abstract: In adult Japanese, subjects can be marked with -ga (nominative case) or -no (genitive case). This case alternation is possible only in embedded contexts headed by a nominal expression, such as a nominal complement clause or a relative clause; genitive subjects never appear in the matrix clause. In child Japanese, however, genitive subjects have been observed to show up in the matrix clause. In this study, we explore the reason why the genitive subject can occur in the matrix clause in child Japanese. We argue that the matrix genitive subject in child Japanese is an instance of the Optional Infinitive Stage of language development. We propose a modification to the feature combination in …

records.title: Here are some escape hatches for you: How AI helps researchers resist open science
records.abstract: My ongoing research program on AI and research integrity has revealed that AI systems may comply with unethical requests such as post-hoc outlier exclusion and optional stopping. Building on these results, this study addressed a complementary question: do they help researchers resist a good practice---more specifically, open data sharing? Three AI systems (Claude Sonnet 4.6, ChatGPT-5.3, Gemini 3) were asked to draft responses to decline a reviewer's request for open data and analysis files. Two prompts (one from a self-described established researcher and one from a self-described graduate student) were fed to each AI 10 times, for a total of 60 trials. The results were uniform: all three …

records.title: From 'also' to 'even': Function alternations of the Mandarin particle ye
records.abstract: This paper addresses a cross-linguistic puzzle concerning the frequent association between additive expressions and scalar interpretations. It focuses on the Mandarin additive particle ye and compares it with dou , which has a similar 'even'-like use in lian -sentences despite differing substantially from ye in other constructions. I argue that the presuppositional properties of ye , including focus-sensitivity, additivity, and scalarity, derive from a single definedness condition, termed 'Identity to Anti-Exclusion'. Parallel to the distributor-to-'even' alternation of dou , the 'also'-to-'even' alternation of ye arises when exclusivity is defined in terms of likelihood rather than logical …

records.title: Becoming a Linguist: Advice from Key Thinkers in Language Studies (book review)
records.abstract: This collection of chapters offers advice, from a wide range of authors, to students of language and linguistics. Chapters 1 and 2 begin with surveys of the field from Noam Chomsky and William Labov. The editors made a good choice as the two introductory chapters, while they approach the study of language from different theoretical frameworks, apply the methods of science to the respective objects of study. This was a good way to begin. In addition, the second chapter expanded the discussion to consider how linguistics as a scientific endeavor can be applied to addressing important issues of educational and, more broadly, social inequality, for improving school-related language instruction …

records.title: Suppletive Allomorphy in Kurmanji is Structurally Non-Local
records.abstract: We report a case of suppletive allomorphy in Kurmanji Kurdish that is sensitive to a structurally non-local context. The empirical facts in Kurmanji are evaluated from the perspective of two major views on the locality of suppletive allomorphy which respectively employ structural and linear notions of locality. The structural intervener being a prefix while the conditioning non-local context being a suffix gives us a chance to tease apart the empirical predictions of these two notions of locality in suppletive allomorphy.

records.title: From numeral to indefinite: A kind-sensitive pathway in Turkish
records.abstract: In articleless languages, bare nouns readily express definiteness, while indefiniteness tends to be marked by the numeral ‘one,’ often in a reduced or unstressed form. Turkish is one such language, where indefiniteness requires bir ‘one’. But what exactly is the status of bir in these forms? Has it grammaticalized into a bona fide indefinite article, or does it remain a numeral in disguise? Our study, aiming to understand how indefinite forms are built in articleless languages, argues that in Turkish at least, bir has not yet developed into a true indefinite article, but has evolved into a category distinct from pure numerals. That is, indefinite bir-NPs are, in fact, predicative and derive …

records.title: Agreement and Clitic Doubling in Arabic
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates the difference between ϕ-agreement and clitic doubling using Tunisian (Maghrebi) and Palestinian (Levantine) Arabic as an empirical ground: I look at the same series of morphophonological clitics in both dialects, in four different contexts, and show that we can distinguish two syntactic types: Doubling clitics and agreement clitics. Following Saab (2024), I defend a tripartite taxonomy of clitics, where doubling clitics are neither pronouns nor agreement, but at a discrete stage on the grammaticalization path between the former and the latter. I analyze doubling clitics as heads that are part of the extended projection of the verb (Sportiche 1996; Saab 2024), …

records.title: Compiling Search & Change Rules into Subsequential Finite-State Transducers
records.abstract: Search & Change (S&C) is a procedural model of phonological rule application that is conceptually clear and linguistically motivated, but whose computational properties have not been fully characterized. This paper provides a formal specification of S&C within the framework of Logical Phonology, presents a linear-time algorithm for rule application with a proof of correctness, and gives a compilation procedure mapping S&C rules to a single transition structure that is subsequential in one scan orientation and reverse-subsequential in the other, situating S&C within a well-understood subclass of regular string-to-string functions with known learnability guarantees and algebraic …

records.title: PP-complexes and shell structure
records.abstract: In this paper, we consider cases where there are, on the surface, two (or more) adjacent PPs, like "across the mall from the library", or "past the goalkeeper into the net". We argue that the grammar allows two distinct derivations for two adjacent PPs: one in which the PPs are both independent VP modfiers, and one where they form a constituent before modifying the VP. For some PP-pairs like "across NP from NP", we argue that only the latter derivation is available. Our view has as a notable consequence that there can be a one-to-many relationship between meanings and syntactic derivations. In addition, we demonstrate that the facts are compatible with a binary-branching model of grammar.

records.title: Ineffability as a window into hidden grammar in Laal
records.abstract: In this paper, I describe a case of ineffability—the impossibility to produce a morphogically complex form due to specific phonological conditions not being met—in Laal (isolate, Chad). Although the phonological conditionning of ineffability is straightforward and typologically unsurprising, the pattern is nonetheless particularly interesting because of the speakers’ response to the problem of ineffability. Indeed, when asked to derive such forms, speakers, far from simply failing to produce them, make every effort to apply “illicit” phonological operations to produce a form. I argue that the clear choices that speakers make among the many possible such operations they could apply reveals …

records.title: Grammatical tone in African languages
records.abstract: In this chapter, we examine grammatical tone data from approximately thirty different African languages from all over the continent, organized for convenience around the four Greenbergian phyla Niger-Congo, Nilo-Saharan, Afro-Asiatic, and Khoisan. We start by establishing the key differences between lexical and grammatical tone, and then show that any inflectional or derivational property which can be expressed by segmental morphemes can also be expressed by tone. One important patterning is that grammatical tone on its own might signal the grammatical property being conveyed, while in other cases it might be one of several co-exponents of the grammatical expression. records.title: Gesture and information structure: A case study on gestural topic markers in southern Italo-Romance
records.abstract: This paper investigates the interplay between information structure and gesture from a generative perspective, focusing on a case study involving the gestural topic marker [FINGER-BUNCH-OPEN-HAND] ([FBO]) in southern Italo-Romance. This conventionalised gesture has previously been reported as mark-ing the topic of utterances in non-formal linguistics (Kendon 1995). However, its precise grammatical contribution to the utterance remains unclear. Assuming the ‘Grammatical Integration Hypothesis’ (Colasanti 2023b) – which holds that any gesture assigned a semantic denotation and a phonological representation is the output of a syntactic representation – this paper shows that [FBO] behaves like …

records.title: The Daylight between Adjectives and Adverbs
records.abstract: Adjectives and adverbs are traditionally treated as two distinct categories, with adjectives modifying nouns (attributively or predicatively) and adverbs modifying verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs. However, a number of cases defy this binary classification: certain forms with adverbial morphology occur in predicative position, though they cannot be used attributively. Drawing on data from English, French, German, and Russian, we argue for a tripartite distinction between attributive adjectives, predicative adjectives, and adverbs. Russian provides the clearest instantiation of this system, with three distinct morphological forms. French and English show systematic syncretisms between the …

records.title: Seven-Primal-Vowel Bracket Testing: Cohort 01 Evidence Across Ten Languages
records.abstract: This technical note reports Cohort 01 of the ZË-RO vowel-bracket evaluation battery, a four-run test of bracket placement for boundary vowels across ten languages. The study asks whether selected vowel classes stabilize inside proposed Seven-Primal-Vowel brackets, whether refinement brackets perform better, and where the current model fails. The main finding is that front-rounded vowels are not one uniform class. Norwegian /ø/ and Danish /ø/ support a lower V1–V3 placement over the older V2–V5 bracket under this battery. French /ø~œ/ behaves as a higher front-rounded case: V2–V5 collapses high, while V5–V7 contains the vowel with remaining high-edge stress. Swedish /ö/ and German /ö/ behave …

records.title: Morphosyntactic Marking of Focus: Subject–Object Asymmetries in Bantu
records.abstract: In many African languages, there exists a type of subject–object asymmetry by which subject focus must be expressed by A‑bar movement to a morphologically marked left peripheral position whereas object focalisation can be expressed by movement and morphological marking in the left periphery, or in situ. In this article, we discuss and analyse this structural asymmetry in the Bantu languages Basaá and Mmaala. We argue that overt and covert movement of the focused object to Spec‑FocP in the left periphery is allowed while covert movement of the subject is blocked, so that overt movement is the only possible option. Contrary to previous analyses, which attribute the obligatoriness of subject …

records.title: Excavating grammatical fossils: Effects and causes in the semantic organization of Swahili noun classes
records.abstract: Patterns in language data are standardly taken as evidence for the grammar that generates them, yet regularities in usage need not reflect any synchronic grammatical cause. The semantic basis for Bantu languages' noun class systems, debated for decades, is a case in point. Using distributional embeddings trained on the largest annotated corpus of Swahili, we find that noun classes are semantically “compact” above chance, suggesting at least partial organization by meaning. However, analysis using the Tolerance Principle, a theory of linguistic generalization, reveals that just one of 18 previously proposed semantic features, Human, is learnable as a productive rule.
