records.title: “Interrogative operator” or bias marker? Nemde in Old and Middle Hungarian questions
records.abstract: Proto-Hungarian is assumed to have been a head-final language, with SOV as basic word order (É. Kiss 2014). The polar interrogative marker -e was cliticized to the sentence-final V, so it had sentence-final position (Kenesei 1992: 692). This characteristic changed during the period of Old Hungarian (896–1526). According to the theory of É. Kiss (2014), the V-head moved to the beginning of the VP. As a consequence, the -e interrogative particle lost its peripheral position. This latter change is taken to have had two effects: (i) double marking with the -e particle: both on the V head and sentence finally, and (ii) the sentence-initial occurrence of “interrogative operators”, such as nemde, …

records.title: Prosodic smothering is idiosyncratic and lexical
records.abstract: Prosodic units, such as the phonological phrase 𝜙, typically correspond to morphosyntactic units, such as XPs. However, prosodic effects associated with individual morphemes may idiosyncratically disrupt these correspondences. In particular, some morphemes may condition ‘prosodic smothering’, a pattern in which outer morphemes trigger restructuring of inner prosodic domains. Most analyses of smothering assume that prosodically exceptional elements (i) have regular, unremarkable syntax; and (ii) are lexically specified for their unique prosodic effects. An alternative is to assume that (i) the syntax of smothering triggers is special; and (ii) their prosodic behavior follows directly from …

records.title: What can LLMs tell us about the mechanisms behind polarity illusions in humans? Experiments across model scales and training steps
records.abstract: I use the Pythia scaling suite (Biderman et al. 2023) to investigate if and how two well-known polarity illusions, the NPI illusion and the depth charge illusion, arise in LLMs. The NPI illusion becomes weaker and ultimately disappears as model size increases, while the depth charge illusion becomes stronger in larger models. The results have implications for human sentence processing: it may not be necessary to assume "rational inference" mechanisms that convert ill-formed sentences into well-formed ones to explain polarity illusions, given that LLMs cannot plausibly engage in this kind of reasoning, especially at the implicit level of next-token prediction. On the other hand, shallow, …

records.title: Deconstructing sentence disambiguation by joint latent modeling of reading paradigms: LLM surprisal is not enough
records.abstract: Using temporarily ambiguous garden-path sentences ("While the team trained the striker wondered ...") as a test case, we present a latent-process mixture model of human reading behavior across four different reading paradigms (eye tracking, uni- and bidirectional self-paced reading, Maze). The model distinguishes between garden-path probability, garden-path cost, and reanalysis cost, and yields more realistic processing cost estimates by taking into account trials with inattentive reading. We show that the model is able to reproduce empirical patterns with regard to rereading behavior, comprehension question responses, and grammaticality judgments. Cross-validation reveals that the mixture …

records.title: Monsters aren't enough: (Non-)indexical shift in indirect discourse
records.abstract: Since Kaplan’s (1989) prohibition of so-called monsters, it has been widely assumed that indexical expressions, such as “I”, “here”, or “tomorrow”, can receive shifted interpretations, i.e., non-speaker-oriented interpretations, only in direct discourse, but not in indirect discourse. However, subsequent work has challenged this view by showing certain perspective-dependent expressions can take their reference from the reported rather than the reporting context (Schlenker 2003; Anand & Nevins 2004; Deal 2017; Saure 2025), which has led to a surge in monstrous analyses of indexical shift. Building on this line of research, the present paper extends the empirical domain of perspective shift …

records.title: Adding to the expressive typology: Emblematic gestures as visual expressives
records.abstract: This paper investigates whether emblematic gestures should be analyzed as expressive meaning contributions in the visual modality of spoken language. While formal-semantic work on gesture has primarily focused on iconic co-speech gestures, emblematic gestures have received comparatively little attention, despite their high degree of conventionalization and their ability to express speaker attitudes and entire communicative acts. Building on Cornelia Ebert and Walter (2025), we first argue that emblematic gestures, unlike iconic gestures in general, satisfy the central diagnostics for expressive meaning proposed by Potts (2007): they are nondisplaceable, perspectivedependent, descriptively …

records.title: The superiority of a movement approach to Greenberg’s Universal 20 (a reply to Dryer 2018)
records.abstract: This article is a reply to Matthew Dryer’s critique (2018, “On the order of demonstrative, numeral, adjective, and noun,” Language 94.4.798–833) of the derivation of Joseph Greenberg’s Universal 20 (1963, “Some universals of grammar with particular reference to the order of meaningful elements”) that I proposed in 2005 (“Deriving Greenberg’s Universal 20 and its exceptions,” Linguistic Inquiry 36.3.315–332). My claim is that Dryer’s approach compares unfavorably with the movement approach I advocated then (and in subsequent work). Dryer’s iconic principles are tailored to apply just to the nominal elements demonstrative, numeral, adjective, and noun (not to mention the fact that they …

records.title: The Hand That Takes: Hittite dā- as pre-PIE *de + postposed -a, with iconographic evidence from Anatolian hieroglyph CAPERE
records.abstract: The first three papers of this project reconstructed pre-PIE *de- "hand, open palm" and decomposed both the body-part noun *der- and the give-verb *deh₃- into the same bare hand-element extended by different morphemes. The present paper carries the framework into Anatolian. We argue that Hittite dā- "to take" preserves a fossilized univerbation of pre-PIE *de- with a postposed directional element *a "toward (the speaker)," contracted by hiatus to long *ā in pre-Anatolian, at a stage before the verbal extension *-h₃- had been added. The argument's centerpiece is the Anatolian X+a parallel: *de + a > dā- fits a documented Anatolian morphological type rather than constituting an isolated …

records.title: Animal semantics [Encyclopedia entry]
records.abstract: Semantics, the study of meaning, plays a central role in research on animal communication, with the goal of uncovering and understanding homologies or analogies to the way that meaning is communicated in human language. One challenge is that, unlike human language (which can be studied with direct introspective judgments), animal meaning can only be investigated with indirect measures. Recent work has shown that concepts and tools from formal semantics—built for human language—can nevertheless be successfully applied to the study of animal meaning. In this chapter, we use a formal semantic approach to define meaning, semantic denotation and pragmatic inferences in animal communication, lay …

records.title: Fünetik Alfübet: "Keep It Simple" Phonetic Alphabet
records.abstract: The Fünetik Alfübet is a simplified phonetic writing system designed to make English pronunciation more accessible to beginning and intermediate learners. The system follows a One Sound, One Character principle, employing primarily Latin letters with a small set of intuitive diacritics. It removes schwa as an independent phoneme, instead representing the underlying vowel, and introduces straightforward representations of rhotic vowels using ʊr or vowel+r. Diphthongs are not treated as phonemic sequences but as natural transitions, allowing the system to maintain a primarily monophthongal inventory. The draft presented here (Version 0.9) is based on Canadian English (Southwestern/Southern …

records.title: Deixis in motion: Addressee surfacing and the politeness path.
records.abstract: AUTHORS: Iarina Albu, Gabriel Carlin Coleman, Idan Caspi, Laia Colina Fortuny and Roberta D'Alessandro In this paper, we provide a formal analysis of the development of polite address during conversation. Starting from the analysis of two very distinct strategies of polite address, we show that they follow a common path towards reinstating deixis throughout the conversation. More specifically, we show that within a couple of conversation turns, those forms that start out as expressing maximal distance between the speaker and the addressee gradually become less marked, and ultimately end up expressing only the addressee feature. In general, we observe a progressive switch from minimal and …

records.title: The Bare Hand: Pre-PIE *de- as a free morpheme, the compositional decomposition of *-tero-, and the bimorphemic structure of *deh₃-
records.abstract: The first two papers of this project argued that pre-PIE *de- "hand, open palm" underlies the lexical cluster Greek δῶρον / Hesychian δάρις / Celtic *durno- / Latvian dūre (Paper 1) and the contrastive suffix *-tero- together with the numeral *du̯o-/du̯i- "two" as derivational siblings on the same root (Paper 2). The present paper completes the framework's verbal and particle branches by going one step deeper: *der- itself decomposes into two independently attested morphemes — a bare hand-element *de- and a locative/spatial extension *-r- — and the same bare *de- underlies the give-verb *deh₃- via a verbal extension *-h₃-. The bare *de- is independently attested as the directional particle …

records.title: Bedeutungen, Assoziationen, Sprachgebrauch: Epistemische Kämpfe in der fachwissenschaftlichen Debatte um geschlechtersensible Sprache
records.abstract: Wenige sprachbezogene Themen werden in der Öffentlichkeit so kontrovers diskutiert wie gendersensible Sprache. Doch auch in der Linguistik gibt es sehr kontroverse Positionen zum sogenannten Gendern. Dies liegt nicht zuletzt daran, dass sich grundlegende Annahmen darüber, wie Sprache im Allgemeinen und Bedeutung im Besonderen funktionieren, in unterschiedlichen Bereichen und Traditionen der Sprachwissenschaft fundamental unterscheiden. Wenn nun aber ein Thema, das verschiedene Bereiche der Linguistik berührt, zu einem der prominentesten gesellschaftlichen “Triggerpunkte” avanciert, so kommen auch die Impulse, die die öffentliche Debatte aus der Linguistik erhält, aus all ihren …

records.title: NP comparatives and ellipsis
records.abstract: A new argument is provided for prenominal NP comparatives requiring extraction of the comparative -er morpheme out of the DP, accompanied by the late merge of the than -clause (cf. Bhatt and Pancheva 2004). We propose that this extraction is driven by the requirements of ellipsis resolution within the than -clause. Whenever these requirements are obviated, NP comparatives can instead be interpreted within the DP.

records.title: A Better Hand: The PIE contrastive *-tero- and the pre-PIE hand-noun
records.abstract: The PIE contrastive suffix *-tero- is, in its oldest documented function, the systematic morpheme for spatial-direction marking across the Indo-European family. Almost every PIE local particle has a *-tero- derivative naming its spatial contrastive — Latin citra/ultra/intra/extra/contra, Sanskrit ádhara-/uttara-/ápara-/ántara-, Avestan and Old Persian fratara-/apatara-/upatara-, Hittite kattera-, Greek próteros/hústeros. The Handbook of Comparative and Historical Indo-European Linguistics states explicitly that outside Greek and Indo-Iranian this spatial-particle function is the original PIE function; the gradational "more X" comparative is a Greek and Indo-Iranian innovation. This paper …

records.title: Recursive embedding in productive causatives: The view from Turkish
records.abstract: This monograph investigates the morphosyntax and semantics of causative constructions, focusing on productive causatives in Turkish. The study advances the claim that Turkish allows genuine syntactic recursion in productive causatives and that the interpretation of these structures is determined by the size and internal composition of the embedded event structure. Adopting a decompositional approach to event structure, the analysis examines how causative heads interact with verbal roots, argument structure, and Voice. The study engages with the ongoing debate on causative recursion, arguing against accounts that deny structural recursion or reduce it to non-structural factors. It …

records.title: What do we mean by language? A pluralist map for the language sciences
records.abstract: The word language names several distinct objects across the language sciences: capacity, idiolect, communicative practice, population convention, named sociohistorical object, and formal system. Pluralist accounts (especially Santana's distinction among psychological, social, and abstract ontologies) show why monism fails but don't say when a proposed sense licenses inference or when evidence about one sense can travel to another. This paper adds a homeostatic property cluster (HPC) discipline: a sense earns realist standing where its properties are stabilized by identifiable mechanisms and project for a field's purposes; where the mechanisms diverge, the shared label doesn't license …

records.title: Tag questions
records.abstract: This chapter consolidates and augments what is known about tag questions (TQs) of both the 'invariant' type (e.g. Kima is graduating, right?) and the 'dependent' type (e.g. Kima is graduating, isn't she?), focusing almost exclusively on their morphosyntax and crosslinguistic distribution. Progress is made in two major areas: (i) expounding the empirical and theoretical status of TQs as ellipsis phenomena, and (ii) confirming the status of tag clauses as polar questions based on the Q-marking strategies they involve crosslinguistically. Concerning (i): after reviewing and strengthening the arguments that dependent TQs involve predicate ellipsis, I sketch a novel analysis of invariant TQs as …

records.title: Condition C, Pronoun Strength, and the Raising Analysis of Relative Clauses
records.abstract: This paper uses Condition C reconstruction to argue that a raising analysis must be available for relative clauses, and suggests that pronoun strength and focus may be responsible for variability in Condition C reconstruction judgements. First we provide some experimental evidence that there is reconstruction for Condition C in English finite relative clauses. Then we present introspective judgements on English and French infinitival relative clauses, which fit a general pattern whereby Condition C reconstruction effects are clearer with silent pronouns. We suggest that the differing strength of reconstruction effects is related to pronoun strength, in that overt pronouns have the potential …

records.title: A simple threshold captures the social learning of conventions
records.abstract: The Tolerance Principle is a domain general learning and decision making mechanism that effectively captures learning behavior at the individual and social setting.

records.title: Sublexical modality
records.abstract: This chapter focuses on sublexical modal verbs, in particular lexical causatives such as teach, send, or offer that covertly encode a modal layer, rendering them defeasible: they imply a result without entailing it. I first outline the various treatments of low verbal modality (in the VP) and propose that modality is introduced by the verbalizing head. A central puzzle addressed is the agent requirement for failed attempt readings: cancelling the result is felicitous with agentive subjects but typically yields a contradiction with non-agentive (causer) subjects. After examining some limitations of previous approaches, I develop an account of this requirement in an anchor-based semantics …

records.title: A Systematic Statistical-Neural Architecture for Multilingual Terminology Recognition and Cross-Lingual Processing
records.abstract: This paper introduces LexiQ, an integrated Natural Language Processing (NLP) architecture designed to optimize Linguistic Quality Assurance (LQA) across divergent language families. While traditional LQA workflows rely on manual intervention or rigid heuristics, LexiQ proposes a hybrid engine that combines Bayesian MAP estimation with multimodal vector space models. We delineate a two-phase optimization initiative: first, establishing a robust statistical foundation for systematic term recognition; and second, implementing a compile-time internationalization framework for global scalability. Key to the architecture is the GATV (Glossary-Anchored Terminology Validation) system, which …

records.title: The Hand That Gives: PIE *der- and the give/take root: an alternative reconstruction proposed for consideration
records.abstract: This paper develops three derivational outputs of a Pre-PIE arm-extension element *de- in the post-Anatolian Indo-European tradition. The first is the directional/allative particle *de/do, preserved as a productive morpheme in Mycenaean Greek by 1400–1200 BCE, in Old Church Slavonic do, Proto-Germanic *tō, and Celtiberian DV at the Bronze of Novallas. The second is the body-part heteroclite arm-noun *de-r-, formed by the addition of the locative case-ending *-r to the bare element; its daughter-language reflexes — Albanian dorë, Old Irish derna, Hesychian δάρις — display the ARM → HAND grammaticalization attested within Sanskrit and articulated for Proto-Celtic by Matasović (2009). A sister …

records.title: Determinatives as nouns in English
records.abstract: English determinatives have been treated as pronouns, as a category apart, and as heads of a functional projection; this paper argues that they are a fourth sub-category of noun, alongside common, proper, and pronoun. The categorial claim doesn't depend on settling the fusion question. CGEL's own treatment of independent genitives (mine, Kim's) shows that fused Det–Head is compatible with noun heads, and the same reasoning extends to the determinative category. Partitive constructions (some of the wine, many of the students) establish determinatives as head-like pivots in matrix NPs where no covert common-noun head is available. Three discriminators (paradigm productivity, structural …

records.title: Grammaticality needs more than locality
records.abstract: Gibson (2026) argues that dependency grammar is the simplest theory of grammar, with dependency locality as the unifying principle behind processing effects and crosslinguistic word-order regularities. Locality has robust corpus support as a processing primitive, and the representational case for dependency formalisms over phrase structure plus transformations has real force. But the broader title claim reaches beyond what the locality literature itself supports. Three dissociations press against a single-factor story. English I have 57 years has the same dependency skeleton on a duration reading (licensed) and an age reading (not licensed in contemporary Standard English); the difference …

records.title: Eliminating Agree
records.abstract: I argue for eliminating the operation of Agree. Agreement in natural language is instead analyzed in terms of external Merge of agreement morphemes and the theory of copies and repetitions developed in Chomsky 2024.

records.title: Sisterhood as a licensing configuration
records.abstract: The paper argues that Sisterhood needs to be admitted as a feature-licensing configuration, which is implemented through prominent feature sharing involved in labeling. The account proposed in the paper explains and unifies a number of phenomena, like indeterminate licensing, wh-movement in languages like English, the EPP, clitic-strong pronoun (and more generally strong/weak element) alternations, ordering of agreement effects, and certain Case effects. Traditional Spec-Head agreement is quite generally recast as licensing under Sisterhood (though not all relevant Sisterhood licensing involves traditional Spec-Head agreement). It is also shown that Sisterhood licensing and Agree licensing …

records.title: Standalone Sentence-final Particles: A Cross-linguistic Study of Japanese ne and Sichuan Mandarin ga
keywords: sfp; pf-deletion; japanese; sichuan mandarin; phase domain
records.abstract: This paper develops a phase-based analysis of so-called Standalone SFP constructions in Japanese and Sichuan Mandarin, arguing that they are derived via PF deletion of the complement of sentence-final particles within a restricted transfer domain. I propose a no-interphasal string deletion condition, according to which deletion must be confined within a single transfer domain; cross-phase deletion is therefore ruled out due to computational inefficiency at the SM interface. Under this approach, particles such as Japanese ne and Sichuan Mandarin ga are analyzed as heads of AddrP, a phase head, allowing their complements to be fully elided and yielding Standalone Response and Standalone Gap …

records.title: Smiles can be conveyed to listeners via speech signals:  A case study with Japanese labiodentalization
records.abstract: One long-standing question in speech communication research concerns the extent to which an emotional state is encoded in the acoustic signal and conveyed to the listeners. To address this question, we deployed a recent finding in Japanese, in which speakers replace bilabial sounds (e.g. [b]) with labiodental sounds (e.g. [v]) when speaking with a smile. Experiment 1 used stimuli recorded by two professional voice actors under four conditions crossing two factors, Voice Quality (Smile vs. Non-Smile) and Articulation (Labiodental vs. Bilabial). The results confirm that labiodentals function as a reliable cue for smiling, even in the absence of visual information. Experiment 2 controlled for …

records.title: Syntax and Pragmatics of Adversativity: Towards a grammar of co-speech gestures
records.abstract: In this article, we examine adversative special questions in Italian expressing disapproval. Our goal is to explore, through an experimental setup, the syntactic triggers involved in the characteristic gestuality associated with these sentences. We argue, building on our previous work, that gestures, particularly non-lexical co-speech gestures, are not just an additional communication channel. Instead, they are a crucial part of the language system, generated and coordinated by the same syntactic principles that govern word order and sentence structure. We will show that expressive language not only triggers a significantly larger number of gestures compared to non-expressive language but …

records.title: (Not) Anything Goes: The syntax and diachrony of the German gehen-middle
records.abstract: This paper offers a syntactic and diachronic analysis of the German [gehen+zu-infinitive] ('go+to-infinitive') construction. Previously misclassified as a periphrastic anticausative or conflated with canonical modal passives, the configuration represents a structurally distinct periphrastic realization of the middle voice. Synchronically, modal gehen operates as a functional raising head that strictly selects a voiceless, eventive vP and a resultative configuration — a selectional restriction that directly accounts for the construction’s rigid lexical-semantic preference for Accomplishments. The raising head carries a formal edge feature forcing internal argument raising, which feeds …

records.title: Decomposition Grammar: A Unified Mechanistic Account of Language Production, Aphasia, Acquisition Order, and Typological Word Order
records.abstract: We propose a novel model for speech production and reception termed Decomposition Grammar. This model presents an alternative mechanistic account of language production, reception, and acquisition, replacing Merge with its inverse, Split, as the core operation of fluent grammar production, and deriving the result that there are two distinct grammatical systems running in parallel in unimpaired individuals. We label these two systems the “Tree System”, which is the primary system of spontaneous speech, and the “Linear System”, which is the primary system of speech reception and monitoring. We argue that the grammatical sentences admitted by the Linear System form a strict superset of those …

records.title: Clausal parentheticals in disguise:  the borrowing of which in code-mixing speech in Hong Kong Cantonese
records.abstract: This paper discusses an understudied construction in code-mixing speech in Hong Kong Cantonese, whose signature feature is the use of the English relative pronoun which (which-constructions). These constructions apparently constitute a relative construction that introduces an atypical, post-nominal modification of the antecedent in Cantonese. While they have been characterized as an instance of lexico-syntactic transference or structural borrowing of post-nominal modification, I argue against such a modification account, and propose that which-constructions are best regarded as clausal parentheticals. I suggest that (i) they involve no syntactic borrowing of modification structures, and …

records.title: Machine yearning: LLMs do not capture formal linguistic structure and obscure neuroscientific inquiry
records.abstract: Futrell and Mahowald (2025) argue that neural networks have learned non-trivial aspects of language. We argue that these systems have not in fact demonstrated “mastery” (2025: 10) of syntax, marshalling recent evidence, and that they further serve to obscure explanatory insights with respect to topics in the cognitive neuroscience of language.

records.title: Diminutives in Spanish: Cyclicity, allomorphy, prosody
records.abstract: This short paper assesses the data on Peninsular Spanish diminutives against an articulated theory of nominal classes in Spanish within Stratal Phonology (Bermúdez-Otero 2013). As opposed to many previous monostratal approaches (see Smith 2011:§2), the analysis developed in this short paper upholds a high standard of modularity. First, no morphological (e.g., nominal class) or syntactic property (e.g., dim), is named in the statement of the phonological constraints, except for ‘stem’ in alignment constraints (Indirect Reference Hypothesis, Bermúdez-Otero 2012:77). Secondly, the high standard of modularity is also grounded in cyclicity: morphosyntactic structure determines the cyclic domains …

records.title: From Demonstrative to Discourse: the cartographic footprint of gam2 in Cantonese
records.abstract: The current study examines two less discussed usages of the demonstrative gam2 in Cantonese. In addition to its adverbial and clausal usages, I argue that gam2 can be used as an event-type SFP for kind establishment, and gam2joeng2 can be used as a tag statement for self-confirmation. I also depict the grammaticalization path of gam2 and gam2joeng2. I show that the two differs in terms of the directionality of grammaticalization.

records.title: Schwa Density as a Phonological Stylistic Classifier: Primary Stylistic,  Secondary Modality
records.abstract: We test whether schwa density, the proportion of vowel phones in a text that are unstressed schwa (CMUdict AH0), can serve as a phonologically motivated single-feature register classifier in English text. A pre-registered confirmatory plan locking three hypothesis tests (minimum effect, non-inferiority versus Flesch– Kincaid grade level, and correlation replication) was applied to two pre-registered corpora and two additional sensitivity corpora: NLTK multi-source ( ), the Standardized Project Gutenberg Corpus ( ), the Brown corpus ( qualifying), and the Open American National Corpus ( ). Both pre- registered confirmatory tests passed: schwa density discriminated registers above the crud …

records.title: On the syntactic autonomy of theme vowels
records.abstract: Some of the most fundamental questions in linguistic theory concern grammatical architecture. Focusing on morphosyntax specifically, how many components are ‘morphosyntactic’ phenomena distributed over, and how do they divide up their labor? Answers differ: some versions of Distributed Morphology posit a rich postsyntactic morphological component, whereas Morphology-as-Syntax approaches sharply reduce its role. Against that backdrop, this article investigates theme vowels, which are often analyzed as purely morphological (nonsyntactic). A diagnostic is introduced for their derivational origin, based on the narrow-syntactic phenomenon of lexical selection (L-selection): if a theme vowel is …

records.title: Events and Argument Structure
records.abstract: The inference from *Jones buttered the toast in the kitchen* to *Jones buttered the toast* is intuitively compelling, and Davidsonian event semantics explains why: action sentences express descriptions of events, about which indefinitely many things can be said. I trace the logical form tradition from this founding observation through thematic separation, definite reference to events, and plural event quantification; show the resulting format extending, unchanged, to aspect, measurement, and the attitudes; and present three contemporary advances—Schein’s supermonadic event layers, Schwarzschild’s elimination of individual variables, and Pietroski’s minimal monadic combinatorics. In the end, …

records.title: You Can't be Neutral on a Moving Train (Comment on Futrell & Mahowald's BBS article)
records.abstract: This is a Commentary on Futrell & Mahowald's BBS target piece "How Linguistics Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Language Models". The commentary argues the authors employ misdirection and strawmanning to cast others as polarized extremes and themselves as the reasonable centrists. We argue that these patterns of misrepresentation ultimately damage any consensus and middle ground they claim to hope to reach.

records.title: Grammaticality as Kind: Ontology, Epistemology, and Empirical Pay-off
records.abstract: This paper argues that grammaticality is best understood as a homeostatic property-cluster (HPC) kind anchored in morphosyntactic form–meaning pairings and regimented by community practice. The framework distinguishes objective grammatical status – whether the community licenses a form–meaning pairing – from the subjective feeling of ungrammaticality, which integrates grammaticality with processing costs, social evaluation, and prescriptive norms. Drawing on contemporary metaphysics of science, we show how grammaticality exhibits the key features of HPC kinds: a cluster of co-occurring properties (morphosyntactic well-formedness, semantic compatibility, community entrenchment), homeostatic …

records.title: Intransitive verbs: unergatives, unaccusatives, middles (part of: Syntax of Hungarian: Verbs and Verb Phrases)
records.abstract: This chapter covers the syntactic, semantic and morphological patterns displayed by intransitive verbs in Hungarian. The discussion will be theory-neutral but informed by various theoretical approaches. No new theoretical claims will be made: rather, the aim is to provide a survey of the facts and to provide pointers to the existing theoretical literature. Our focus is on intransitive verbs: one-argument verbs which lack any arguments in addition to the the syntactic subject (since in Hungarian, nominals are overtly case-marked, and there is subject agreement, identifying the subject of a sentence is straightforward). We will broaden this definition to consider verbs which are arguable …

records.title: Does the Williams Cycle apply to Mandarin Chinese?
records.abstract: This paper addresses a theoretical tension in accounting for the correlation between the landing site and the locality domain of movement—whether to reduce it to the A/A'-distinction (Ban on Improper Movement) or to hard-wire it to the grammar as the Williams Cycle (WC), which has recently been claimed to apply to Mandarin Chinese by Yan & Meadows (2025). By refuting their arguments, we argue that the WC does not apply to Mandarin and therefore cannot be universal. Specifically, we show that the apparent WC effects in Mandarin either follow from independently attested A/A'-distinction in the language, or simply do not hold due to incomplete generalization. The Mandarin case highlights the …

records.title: Gli universali fraseologici nelle lingue naturali
records.abstract: This article examines the concept of phraseological universals, understood as shared features of phraseological units (PUs) that reoccur across different languages. The analysis foregrounds the structural and functional similarities among PUs, supported by examples drawn from Italian, French, English, Polish, Turkish, and Korean. The phraseological universals addressed in this study encompass several phenomena: the coexistence of transparency and opacity within PUs, the systematic classification of PUs, the capacity for modification of otherwise fixed expressions, the notably high frequency of phraseological components within certain semantic fields, the occurrence of mono-collocational …

records.title: Rethinking the model of grammar: PF after LF
records.abstract: The interface levels PF and LF of the Government and Binding theory (GB) have been redefined in Minimalism as a ‘sensory-motor’ component (for PF) and a conceptual-intentional’ component (for LF). The main point of this article is that this redefinition of the interface levels should lead to an adjustment of the model of grammar, such that Narrow Syntax feeds LF, and LF feeds PF. We propose that LF is the component of the model of grammar in which conceptualizations and intentions of the speaker become relevant and that Narrow Syntax (Merge) should be blind to these speaker-sensitive aspects. The argument is based, among others, on case/agreement phenomena that cannot be analyzed as a …

records.title: The domain of phonological processes
records.abstract: In Optimality Theory (Prince & Smolensky 1993), phonological constraints are evaluated with respect to a domain corresponding to the usual notion of grammatical word. I argue here that some common phonological patterns are better analysed by relaxing this restriction. In particular, while a notion of 'phonological' or 'prosodic' word has previously been shown to provide the relevant domain for phonological processes, I argue that productive morphemes can also provide such a domain. The hypothesis is tested with respect to data from Australian and other languages. I show that a model allowing for both intra-and inter-word domains of evaluation provides a more unified analysis of …

records.title: Current AI systems can detect ambiguities in a pre-registration but can offer misleading design-specific advice about random-effects structure
records.abstract: This study tests whether AI systems can identify underspecification in a pre-registration and provide appropriate design-specific methodological advice. In a pre-registered experiment, three AI systems (ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini) were presented with a deliberately ambiguous statistical analysis plan for a Bayesian mixed effects model, and asked for feedback. Each system was tested in two modes (fast/thinking or default/extended), with 10 trials per condition, yielding 60 total trials. The results reveal both a strength and a weakness of current AI systems. On the positive side, all three systems detected all four embedded ambiguities---i.e. unspecified random effects structure, vague …

records.title: Locality Conditions on Wh-Movement in the Miracle Creed Framework
records.abstract: This article aims to unify island conditions on wh-movement in English based on the latest minimalist framework, the Miracle Creed framework proposed by Chomsky (2024) and extended by Kitahara and Seely (2025), according to which A'-movement is reinterpreted as phase-level access from C at the Conceptual-Intentional interface and externalization. This article argues that the Subject Condition, the Adjunct Condition, the Wh-Island Condition, and the Complex NP Condition in English is unified under two locality conditions on phase-level access, the Box-over-Box Condition and the Minimality Condition on Access. Informally speaking, the former states that once search initiated by C has located …

records.title: The Structure of Pronouns and Allomorphy (HU Berlin Dissertation)
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates the following central question: What is the internal structure of pronouns? I propose and investigate the hypothesis that contextual allomorphy is a key tool for (a) accessing the inventory of morphemes that make up a pronoun across languages and (b) tracking the patterns of their interactions. Namely, allomorphic alternations involve an interaction of two morphemes, the trigger and the target of allomorphy. Identifying the trigger and the target in pronominal forms yields an immediate result - pronouns involve two morphemes that occupy distinct structural positions in their internal representation in the narrow syntax. The dissertation presents the idea that …

records.title: The diachrony of iterativity: Evidence from Germanic r-verbs
records.abstract: This article examines the diachrony of Germanic iterative “(V)r-verbs” (e.g., German flattern, English flutter) and related deverbal suffixes (as in, e.g., German folgern ‘to infer’). While these verbs form a distinct class in North-West Germanic—evidenced by cognates like Old High German flogarōn and Old Norse flǫgra—their origin and the development of their iterative semantics remain poorly understood. To clarify the origin of this class, we present a systematic corpus study of four early Germanic languages: Gothic, Old High German, Old English, and Old Norse. We analyze the derivational bases, Aktionsart, and argument structures of early Germanic (V)r-verbs, identifying distinct …

records.title: Raddoppiamento Sintattico in Logical Phonology
records.abstract: I offer an account of Italian raddoppiamento sintattico (RS) within the Substance-Free Logical Phonology (LP) framework. By relying on set-theoretic formalisms, RS is analyzed as an instance of compound unification, wherein a lexically-specified but phonologically-underspecified (empty) segment (X[∅]) is filled by the features of a following consonant. It moves RS away from moraic or morphological accounts and back to the domain of phonology, including in cases of blocking (e.g., phonetic pausing, glottal stop insertion, and vowel lengthening). I show that both the application and non-application of RS emerge merely from evaluating whether the empty segment is available for unification and …

records.title: TINA: A Hybrid Model of Brazilian Portuguese Pronunciation Structure
records.abstract: Automated phonetic transcription for Brazilian Portuguese is not well modeled as a flat grapheme-to-phoneme task, because usable outputs must encode syllabification, lexical stress, and dialect-sensitive realizations. This paper presents TINA, a compact hybrid system that predicts a structured, archiphonemic representation with neural components for syllables, phoneme content, and stress, and then expands that representation into surface-oriented variants through explicit phonological rules. TINA is evaluated against native-speaker pseudoword behavior, with qualitative output inspection on familiar lexical material confirming that the system produces well-formed structured transcriptions. …

records.title: Quasi-names in Akan: A further piece of the definiteness puzzle
records.abstract: This paper provides an analysis of definite bare nouns in Akan as quasi-names – nouns which, like "Mum" in English, can be used as names but are associated with descriptive content (Yip et al., 2023). The paper also provides further evidence that the Akan definite "no" is used in typical uniqueness contexts. Taken together, the data are consistent with an analysis of "no" as a uniqueness definite, whose reduced distribution can be explained by competition with the (quasi-name) bare noun (Bombi, 2018; Bombi et al., 2019).

records.title: synkit: a toolkit to create syntactic representations
records.abstract: synkit is a Typst package for drawing syntax trees from bracket notation. It supports a wide range of features, including triangles, arrows, movement traces, multidominance, semantic annotation, cross-tree equivalence lines, and formatting options for quick adjustments. Trees can be drawn in four directions (down, up, left, right), and multiple trees can be stacked with shared arrow connections. Besides trees, the package also offers functions for numbered examples and glosses. This document serves as the official documentation for synkit, providing examples and explanations for all available parameters and features.

records.title: Formalizing Events and Situations in Language: A Linguistic Analysis of Event Calculus and Situation Calculus
records.abstract: Human language allows speakers to describe actions, events, situations, and change in a flexible and often minimally specified manner. The same sentence can give rise to different interpretations, often due to certain information being left unstated. Human discourse furthermore frequently requires the revision of previously drawn conclusions when new information becomes available. Linguistic expressions encoding phenomena such as aspectual distinctions, causal relations, or temporal sequencing typically rely on shared assumptions and implicit inferences to determine how what is described unfolds over time and affects the state of the world. A central concern of linguistic semantics is how …

records.title: When “passives” involve no A-movement: Rethinking Indonesian-type passives via East Javanese
records.abstract: A passive-like construction in Javanese (Austronesian) highlights how an object topicalization construction can be formally indistinguishable from a passive in languages lacking morphological case. While the so-called passive construction in East Javanese is morphologically identical to the true passive in Indonesian, it involves neither agent demotion nor promotion of the theme to subject position, but instead features A'-movement of an accusative object or adjunct to a left-peripheral topic position. East Javanese therefore contrasts with many other Indonesian-type Austronesian languages in lacking a true passive and in exhibiting an A'-oriented, two-way voice alternation that indexes …

records.title: Not on the same page: negotiating not-at-issue content with bərə (Marathi)
records.abstract: This case study of Marathi discourse particle 'bərə' in medial position makes two contributions: 1. 'bərə' is used to question (how come p?) or reject (as if p) the prejacent p. Importantly, p is necessarily part of not-at-issue content of the preceding context update proposal 2. Hence, not-at-issue updates should be represented as proposals too. In advancing these points, a unified account of the two readings is offered. Formally, the proposalhood of not-at-issue updates is represented in the waiting room model (Biezma & Rawlins 2017) of discourse. The resulting outlook therefore shows that being at-issue ̸= being a proposal. Instead, at-issueness should only be relativized to the current …

records.title: Context Update with Cantonese Sentence-Final Particle "me1" and the Role of the Final Low Tone
Obligatory Speaker-Oriented Rhetoricality: the Case of Cantonese Me↓-Utterances
Structured Partial Predictability in Non-Concatenative Morphology: The Case of Tashlhiyt Berber
records.abstract: Non-concatenative morphology poses a persistent challenge for NLP, yet structured quantitative resources for Amazigh (Berber) languages remain scarce. We present the first large-scale computational study of Tashlhiyt Berber plural formation, drawing on a richly annotated dataset of 1,185 noun paradigms with phonological, morphological and semantic features. We decompose the plural system into macro-level word-formation strategies and micro-level stem mutations, and evaluate predictability across ten target domains using linguistic feature models, N-gram baselines, and Bi-LSTM neural models. Results reveal a structured split: linguistic features decisively outperform neural models on …

records.title: The Acquisition of Pointing Signs and Pronominal Systems in Sign Languages
records.abstract: In American Sign Language (ASL), pronominal functions are carried out by pointing signs: points to self for first-person, points to addressee or non-addressed persons or things as second- and third-person. This picture is complicated by the fact that pointing signs are also used in other ways in ASL: as one example, a signer can point to an abstract locus to refer to a non- present referent associated with that locus. Analysis of these pointing signs has been controversial, starting with arguments that points are not really linguistic elements, just deictics (Johnston 2013). Even when considered as linguistic, there are numerous debates over which analysis is the most appropriate. For …

records.title: Against Proto-Algonquian-Blackfoot: How synchronic analysis informs subgrouping
records.abstract: This paper focuses on subgrouping within families, which is known to be a difficult problem (Clackson 2022, Harrison 2003, Ringe & Eska 2013a). The empirical question is whether Blackfoot is a sister to Proto-Algonquian, such that the remaining “Core Algonquian” languages form a subgroup. These languages share a phonotactic restriction to the exclusion of Blackfoot: outside of a handful of roots, no words in “Core Algonquian” begin in initial *i. Goddard (2018) argues that this is the result of a shared innovation (the loss of initial *i) in Proto-Algonquian. Based on a synchronic analysis of root alternations, I argue instead that Blackfoot innovated stem-initial *i- in several contexts. …

records.title: Evidentiality in Kurmanji
Iconicity and expressiveness of grammatical tones targeting ideophones in Mwaghavul
records.abstract: All tonally derived verbs in Mwaghavul have ideophonic bases and are derived through one of two lexically determined alternations. In the first alternation, every tone-bearing unit (TBU) of the ideophone surfaces with a mid tone. In the second alternation, every nonfinal TBU of ideophones surfaces with a mid tone, while the final TBU surfaces with a high tone. To express pluractionality, both types of ideophones are reduplicated and follow the second pattern: every TBU of the reduplicant bears a mid tone, and every TBU of the base bears a high tone. While verbs derived through mid-tone overwrite share a tonal melody with underived verbs, only derived verbs have a mid–high melody. Beyond …

records.title: Conditions on wh-the-hell licensing: Evidence from Colloquial Singapore English
records.abstract: The unacceptability of in-situ wh-the-hell has been observed since Pesetsky (1987). We investigate the acceptability of in-situ and partially-moved wh-the-hell in Colloquial Singapore English through an acceptability judgment experiment. The results reveal that in-situ wh-the-hell in single wh-questions is unacceptable, but partial wh-movement is able to host the-hell. We argue that this pattern follows from two independently supported components: 1. wh-the-hell needs to move to the Spec-CP so that the negative attitude bearer can be identified (see Chou (2012)); 2. Partial wh-movement in Singlish involves covert movement to Spec-CP while wh-in-situ is interpreted via unselective binding …

records.title: Switch reference as a connectivity effect in Wá·šiw predicate ellipsis
records.abstract: Wá·šiw (Washoe; isolate/Hokan, USA) displays a typologically unusual type of predicate ellipsis – in the form of the so-called sentence connective – whose remnant is comprised solely of inflectional suffixes appearing without their usual verbal host. Crucially, this remnant requires the expression of switch reference marking, which in Wá·šiw has been argued to be the result of agreement, in particular with the clausemate subject (Arregi & Hanink 2022b). In the sentence connective, this clausemate subject is included in the ellipsis site, yet switch reference is still active. Given that an agreement relation with this subject is required for switch reference, we take this as evidence for the …

records.title: Violations for Continuous Candidates in Constraint-based Phonology
records.abstract: Constraint-based phonology normally assigns violations to discrete candidates. At the phonetics-phonology interface, however, many observables are continuous, so pre-evaluative discretization can impose arbitrary boundaries and false local homogeneity. This article argues that continuous candidate spaces therefore require an explicit theory of violation computation. I propose a model in which candidate availability is represented by an empirical density over acoustic space, perceptual and articulatory constraints are defined as continuous functions, and violations are derived by linking constraint values to empirical density. Among several transparent link functions, an exponentialized …

records.title: The morphology/syntax interface
records.abstract: In this Element, we ask, what are today's prominent approaches to the study of the relationship between morphology and syntax? What are the linguistic phenomena that are most relevant at the morphology/syntax interface, and how are these handled in different types of theories? We make a core division between lexicalist approaches, which posit an interface between morphology and syntax at the level of the word, and non-lexicalist approaches, encompassing all other sorts of interfaces. Through the lens of different types of theories, we then examine the status of words and word-formation as well as six types of form-meaning mappings: allomorphy, syncretism, portmanteaux, multiple exponence, …

records.title: Not on the same page: negotiating not-at-issue content with bərə (Marathi)
records.abstract: This case study of Marathi discourse particle 'bərə' in medial position makes two contributions: 1. 'bərə' is used to question (how come p?) or reject (as if p) the prejacent p.
