The resulting outlook therefore shows that being at-issue ̸= being a proposal. Instead, at-issueness should only be relativized to the current …

records.title: Split ergativity isn't always epiphenomenal
records.abstract: Many Mayan languages display split ergativity: ergative-absolutive (ERG-ABS) alignment is observed in some environments, whereas nominative-accusative (NOM-ACC) alignment is observed in others. Most splits in the family are aspect-based (Zavala Maldonado 2017), with the exception of Mocho’, which displays a person-based split (Pérez González 2021). The Standard Analysis treats splits as epiphenomenal: specifically, aspect-based splits are the result of an aspectual predicate selecting an embedded possessed nominalization whose person marker invariably indexes the possessor (Larsen and Norman 1979; see Coon 2013 and references). Such an analysis derives splits via independently supported …

records.title: Names and signs [Имя собственное и языковой знак]
records.abstract: I discuss links between the principle of arbitrariness and the theory of proper names and claim that the arbitrariness of the sign is a generalized version of the referentialist thesis that proper names are conventional tags attached to their bearers. Saussurean linguistics extends this principle to all lexical items and all morphological expressions. Depending on naming practice, proper names can be stored in the respective lexicon, which corresponds to Gardiner’s model of disembodied names, or they can be created by the speaker, as in the model of primary embodied names and Kripke’s model of rigid designators. Neither of the scenarios violates the principle of arbitrariness. Naming …

records.title: Do AI systems fill in missing values?—Testing ethical safeguards against data fabrication
records.abstract: This study is the sixth in a series examining whether the naive use of current AI systems can lead to research misconduct. In a pre-registered experiment, I asked three major AI systems (ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini) to fill in missing values in a dataset, using a prompt designed to simulate a student who may not recognize that this request constitutes data fabrication. Each system was tested 10 times via its web interface. The results were as follows: Claude refused all 10 times with an ethical warning, ChatGPT refused 8 times but complied twice, both times with an ethical warning, and Gemini complied all 10 times without any warning. The findings demonstrate a yet another peril for naive AI …

records.title: Tone Alternation in Kirika (Nko̩ro̩o̩) Associative Construction
records.abstract: Associative construction in Kirika (formerly known as Nkọrọọ) is formed through the combination of two nouns accompanied by tonal alternation. Previous research proposed that this construction exhibits a fixed high-low tonal melody, except when it begins with a low tone, in which case the low tone is predicted to extend over the entire construction. However, this hypothesis could not be fully tested due to limited data. Using newly collected datasets, we evaluate this prediction. Our findings show that tonal alternation is restricted to the second noun. Moreover, when the construction begins with a low tone, the low tone does not spread to the end of the construction. Specifically, the …

records.title: The change specification problem
records.abstract: In recent work Gorman and Reiss (2026) give a formal definition to the feature specification problem (FSP), the problem of determining the natural class representations of the targets and triggers of phonological processes. They argue that the received wisdom---that the FSP is solved by finding the minimal (in terms of the number of valued features) specification---is incorrect, and suggest a simple alternative, in which natural class specifications are determined via intersection. In addition to targets and triggers, traditional phonological rules are also defined by the change, or the modification applied to the targets of the rule. In Logical Phonology (Bale et al. 2014, Bale and Reiss …

records.title: Pronouncing Acronyms in Esperanto
records.abstract: This chapter investigates how fluent Esperanto speakers pronounce acronyms, replicating and extending Torres-Tamarit and Martínez-Paricio's (2024) study of Spanish acronyms. Although Esperanto was designed to be maximally regular, no prescriptive rule was ever laid down for the pronunciation of letter sequences, making acronyms a revealing test case for emergent phonological constraints. We gathered data from 48 experienced speakers on their preferred pronunciations of acronyms varying in length and phonological structure. The results show a highly systematic pattern: longer acronyms that can form multi-syllabic words are almost always pronounced as whole words with regular penultimate …

records.title: Get rich quick: Why children don't need Occam's Razor.
records.abstract: Most phonologists assume that phonological processes are encoded in terms of natural classes defined by sets of features. Thus, children acquiring a phonological grammar need some way to determine the natural classes identifying target and trigger segments. Exactly how children solve this feature specification problem (FSP) is unknown. Many phonologists endorse the view that the feature specifications should be minimal in the sense of containing the minimal number of feature specifications necessary to uniquely identify the class of segments, but no algorithm has been proposed to achieve this objective. We show that there is no guarantee that there is a unique minimal definition of every …

records.title: Countability and measured parts in mixed drink nouns
records.abstract: Liquids (oil, wine) are considered to be canonical non-countable nouns. Yet nouns referring to cocktails and coffee drinks (margarita, cappuccino) display strongly countable behavior, which raises questions about the semantics of countability and the relationship between nouns and the things to which they refer. This paper investigates these mixed drink nouns and proposes the source of their countability lies in their possessing a MEASURED PART which provides a unit for individuation.This part, in connection with the ratio relationship between the drink’s ingredient parts, is the source of countability for these nouns.

records.title: Acquiring the Features of Negative Indefinites: A comparison of Catalan, Spanish and Italian with West Germanic
records.abstract: Corpus-based and experimental studies show that children acquiring non-Negative Concord (NC) languages often display NC-like behaviour, producing or interpreting sentences with two negatives as a single negation. Previous work has taken this as evidence that children initially posit a non-target NC grammar (e.g., Sano et al., 2009; Thornton et al., 2016; Nicolae & Yatsushiro, 2022; Driemel et al., 2023; Illingworth et al., 2025). The empirical basis for this claim is, however, largely based on Double Negation systems, especially Germanic. This paper presents the first corpus study of NC and negative indefinites in Catalan and Spanish, supplemented by existing and new Italian data. …

records.title: Not all coexpressions are syncretisms: Limiting Nanosyntax
records.abstract: This paper revises the findings of Dekier (2021) concerning the syncretism and containment of indefinites in light of their semantic implausibility and empirical inadequacy, compared to the alternative semantic approach of Degano & Aloni (2025), and argues against the omnipotence of a nanosyntactic approach to coexpression phenomena. The paper also addresses the diachronic predictions of Nanosyntax and discusses the structure of lexical entries more generally.

records.title: Frege in the Flesh: Biolinguistics and the Neural Enforcement of Syntactic Structures
records.abstract: Biolinguistics is the interdisciplinary scientific study of the biological foundations, evolution, and genetic basis of human language (Givón 2002; Jenkins 2000). It treats language as an innate biological organ or faculty of the mind (Chomsky 1967; Hornstein 2024), rather than a cultural tool, and it challenges a behaviorist conception of human language acquisition as being based on stimulus-response associations (Lenneberg 1967). Extracting its most essential component, it takes seriously the idea that mathematical, algebraic models of language capture something natural about the world (Chomsky 2014, 2018). The syntactic structure-building operation of MERGE is thought to offer the …

records.title: Optionality and variation in Camuno interrogatives: a syntactic analysis
records.abstract: This paper examines optionality and variation in interrogative constructions in Camuno, an Eastern Lombard variety. Based on original data from different sub-varieties spoken in Valle Camonica, I show that Camuno displays three main interrogative strategies: wh-fronting, clause-internal wh-elements, and wh-doubling. I argue that these patterns can be accounted for within a unified syntactic analysis in which wh-elements form a single A-bar chain composed of an operator and a restriction. Adopting a partial copying approach, I propose that the fronted element realizes the operator in the CP domain, while the clause-internal element corresponds to the restriction stranded at the vP edge …

records.title: Agree in restructuring: evidence from auxiliary switch and clitic climbing in French and Italian
records.abstract: Auxiliary Switch (AS) is an under-studied phenomenon found in Romance restructuring clauses. It is contingent on the climbing of reflexive clitics, but sometimes remains insensitive to non-reflexive clitics. Drawing on the diachrony of French and comparative synchronic data from Italian and Sardinian, I argue that AS reflects a robust syntactic dependency between embedded and matrix domains, instantiated through Agree. The analysis adopts the hypothesis that auxiliary selection is governed not by argument structure but by person value identity. The main conclusions are that HAVE is the default auxiliary in these languages, restructuring is not a phenomenon per se, and the locus of variation …

records.title: On clausal complementation, once more
records.abstract: This paper develops a novel analysis of clausal complementation based on the distribution of Greek declarative clauses introduced by oti and pu. These clauses present three puzzles: (i) they are in complementary distribution after most verbs; (ii) they are licensed as internal arguments and derived subjects but are banned from the external argument position; and (iii) complement pu-clauses impose a previously unnoticed stativity restriction on the matrix verb, a restriction absent in their adjunct uses. I argue that (ii) and (iii) receive a unified explanation if oti and pu of complement clauses select a light noun in their specifier (see also Arsenijević 2009; Moltmann 2019, 2024). This …

records.title: The syntax of Expletive Negation in English: the case of not-ACC-ing constructions
records.abstract: This work aims to describe and analyze a relatively new, puzzling construction that has become very productive in informal registers of English. It is primarily used by younger generations, especially on the web and social-media platforms, but also in spoken language. It appears with the configuration negative marker + subject in the accusative case + gerund (e.g. Not me taking the train at 5 a.m.; meaning: it is ironic and unexpected that I took the train early at 5 a.m.). These constructions, which we dubbed not-ACC-ing constructions, are strictly root phenomena where negation does not reverse the polarity of the sentence. They convey a peculiar ironic, sarcastic, self-deprecating flavor. …

records.title: Integrated and Abstract Wholes:  Prospects for a Constructional Ontology as Part of Universal Grammar (handout)
records.abstract: This talk discusses the view of constructional ontology and mereological pluralism in connection with generative grammar and argues for a dual part structure of artefacts reflected in two nouns 'part' in English and at least other European languages.

records.title: On the nature of phonological cyclicity: Evidence from Nazarene Arabic
records.abstract: We present new evidence supporting the cycle as a grammatical mechanism in phonology. The evidence comes from the distribution of stress and vowel length in Nazarene Arabic, an understudied variety of Palestinian Arabic spoken in Nazareth. We show that the Nazarene Arabic pattern can be accounted for by cyclic versions of both rule-based phonology and Optimality Theory. The same pattern poses a challenge to Base-Derivative Correspondence – an alternative mechanism within Optimality Theory, according to which cyclic effects result from transderivational constraints that enforce similarity between related surface forms. We show that Base-Derivative Correspondence cannot account for the data, …

records.title: Duration iconicity and pace in fictional narrative: An experimental study
records.abstract: This study examines a less well known manifestation of temporal iconicity in narrative: the iconic representation of duration. Work on literary narrative has observed that in scenes (but not in narrative summaries) the time it takes the narrator to tell a sequence of events is roughly the same as the time that sequence takes in the world of the story. If the narration pace remains constant, that implies that a shorter sentence should relate a shorter part of the event sequence, and a longer sentence a longer part. This study is the first to measure the effect of sentence length in words on the readers' impression of duration using a verbal duration estimation task from psychophysics. The …

records.title: The (progressively more) Amazonian character of A'ingae nasality
records.abstract: I describe and analyze a new restriction on the distribution of nasality in the native roots of A'ingae (or Cofán, ISO 639-3: con, an Amazonian isolate). I propose that in A'ingae, (a) nasality is a feature of the morpheme which associates from the left, and (b) all segments are underlyingly either (i) underspecified for orality/nasality, (ii) specified as fully oral, or (iii) specified as oral but with an underspecified stop closure. The new proposal accounts for the patterns of A'ingae nasality distribution, including two new generalizations. First, within a native root, a nasal (or prenasalized) segment is never preceded by oral sonorants/vowels. Second, a prenasalized stop is always …

records.title: Reference and Deixis in Internet Forums
records.abstract: Although deictic expressions are frequently studied interdisciplinarily, a comprehensive linguistic analysis dealing with deixis on internet forums is lacking. Accordingly, this master thesis aims to explore deictic and anaphoric reference on selected discussion forums. In the first part of this paper, the essential theoretical framework for the subsequent analysis is proposed. Afterwards, in the second part, both quantitative and qualitative corpus-based analysis of deictic and non-deictic anaphoric expressions is carried out to explore their functions and patterns of use on selected online forums.

records.title: Varieties as Conditioning Structure
records.abstract: What distinguishes register from dialect from discourse community? This paper argues that they differ not in what they are but in what participant expectation is conditioned on: SITUATION, ASCRIPTION, or IDENTIFICATION. These aren't just descriptive dimensions. Recurrent situations, social classifications, and norm orientations keep rebuilding the same expectation profiles. The key move is separating ascription (what you're treated as) from identification (whose norms you orient to). Drawing on Wiese's (2023) account of communicative situations and O'Connor's (2019) game-theoretic work on how categories stabilize, I argue that varieties hang together because the same kinds of situations …

records.title: How Much Syntactic Structure Have Cartographic Hierarchies Overlooked?
records.abstract: In a range of cases, cartographic (and other syntactic) work will want to be on the lookout for additional syntactic structure, with more silent elements, and more intricate derivations than might have met the eye, at first glance.

records.title: Mirativity on the Table
records.abstract: Using the Hindi-Urdu discourse particle 'lo' as a case study, the present paper models mirativity within the Table model framework (Farkas & Roelofsen, 2017). This comes with an enrichment of the Table model; we propose the discourse structure to encode, in addition to discourse commitments, the time these commitments are publicized. We also incorporate a component that contains the public record of private beliefs. With these two additions, we seek to capture mirativity in the Table model, emphasizing recency as a condition for surprise and underlining the need and the conceptual difficulty of incorporating private beliefs in a public scoreboard of conversation. We show that the difficulty …

records.title: A mirror-principle violation meets Nanosyntax: The case of Czech X-marking
records.abstract: In Czech, the conditional (used in X-marking) is based on the past tense. The containment between the past and the conditional is not unique to Czech. The literature (including Von Fintel and Iatridou 2023, Majdić 2025) found that such a pattern is also attested in other languages. However, there is a difference between Czech and other languages: while Czech appears to have the order VERB-PAST COND (čet-l by), other languages manifest the order VERB-COND-PAST. This chapter proposes a nanosyntactic account of this (apparent) paradox.

records.title: Transmission fidelity versus transmission error: an information-theoretic reanalysis of iterated language learning
records.abstract: Iterated learning experiments demonstrate that languages evolve structure under transmission pressure. The dominant metric for quantifying this process, normalised Levenshtein distance, measures transmission error: how much a signal changes as it passes between learners. We argue that transmission error and transmission fidelity are formally distinct quantities, and that Levenshtein distance is blind to the difference. We reanalyse the full published dataset from Kirby, Cornish & Smith (2008), covering 8 chains, 10 generations, and 27 meanings across both experiments, using normalised mutual information between input and output signal distributions at each generational step. Both …

records.title: Deixis, entropy, and the architecture of grammar
records.abstract: We propose a principled account of deixis as a structural property of grammar that is independently required for the constitution of propositional meaning and whose systematic encoding becomes indispensable under the constraints imposed by externalization. Building on an Un-Cartesian model, we assume that grammar operates over intensional representations derived from world-indexed states. Once such representations are externalized into a temporally unfolding signal, encoding under constrained resources does not preserve all aspects of the original representation, yielding irreversibility in the sense of Shannon’s information theory. As a consequence, linguistic signals underdetermine their …

records.title: Uncountable plurals as maximal clusters
records.abstract: English uncountable plurals are plurals whose parts cannot be counted directly, such as (*five) oats/grasslands/news/measles/tweezers. These form a heterogeneous group in terms of semantic field and various morphosyntactic tests. Nevertheless, this paper shows that a unified analysis can account for the fact that their parts cannot be counted directly. In particular, it argues that uncountable plurals denote maximal clusters in a mereotopological sense. The maximality of these clusters causes a conceptualisation as wholes, which prevents access to the parts. We provide a descriptive typology of English uncountable plurals to illustrate their analysis as clusters connected through either …

records.title: A BMRS analysis of Trojan (and transparent) vowels in Hungarian vowel harmony
records.abstract: A ‘Trojan’ vowel in a vowel harmony system is a vowel that spreads an underlyingly specified value of the spreading feature even though the Trojan vowel itself redundantly surfaces with the opposite value. We propose an analysis of Trojan vowels with Boolean Monadic Recursive Schemes (BMRS; Chandlee & Jardine 2021), a computational formalism describing phonological maps using conditional IF…THEN…ELSE… terms. We show how a BMRS analysis of Trojan vowel behavior in Hungarian follows straightforwardly when coupled with freely-specified input strings. Our analysis also accounts for the fact that redundantly-specified Trojan vowels in Hungarian are transparent in other contexts, and we briefly …

records.title: Comparing Natural and Synthetic Structured Data: A Study of the Passive Verb Alternation in French and Italian
records.abstract: This study compares the impact of natural and synthetic data on training and evaluating large language models (LLMs), using the case of passive verb alternation in French and Italian. We use Blackbird Language Matrices (BLMs), structured datasets designed to probe linguistic knowledge of underlying patterns across sentence sets. We compare structured templates instantiated with natural sentences extracted from Universal Dependencies to structured templates of synthetic sentences. Experiments show that while models achieve ceiling performance when trained and tested on synthetic datasets, they do not reliably generalize to natural sentences. In contrast, models trained on natural data …

records.title: Bipartite question formation in Sm’algyax
records.abstract: Matrix questions in Sm’algyax (Tsimshianic; British Columbia, Alaska) are doubly marked. Wh-questions involve the fronting of a wh-expression to the clause-initial position, together with the interrogative clitic =u; polar questions are introduced by the complementizer ał—diachronically derived from negation—and additionally bear the clitic =ii. By contrast, embedded questions only exhibit a single component: wh-fronting for wh-questions and a complementizer element for polar questions. I argue that this asymmetry reflects a two-layer interrogative syntax. The polar complementizer and the null trigger for wh-movement instantiate an interrogative C[+Q] within CP, while the clitics =u and =ii …

records.title: Experimental evidence for negativity without negation
records.abstract: Approaches to negativity tags, like English 'neither'-tags, 'not even'-tags, and 'why not', differ in whether they treat the antecedent as a clause with clausal negation (e.g., Klima 1964; Kramer and Rawlins 2009; Brasoveanu et al. 2013) or, more broadly, one introducing a salient counterfactual proposition into the discourse (Hofmann 2022, 2023a). This paper presents experimental evidence for the latter view, showing that negativity tags are rated as natural (compared to an affirmative baseline) when their antecedent is introduced without clausal negation, but in an anti-veridical embedding (e.g., 'It's a lie'), under neg-raising (e.g., 'I don't get the feeling'), or with lexical …

records.title: The semantics of plural morphology in Akan
records.abstract: With initial native speaker judgements suggesting an exclusive plural morpheme in downward entailing contexts in Akan, as reported by Ahenkorah (2022), this research seeks to test these claims through experimental means and to provide a more comprehensive picture of Akan’s plural semantics. The current literature on exclusive and inclusive plurals focuses mainly on English, with some investigation of Western Armenian, Turkish, and Korean (Bale & Khanjian 2008; Renans et al. 2017; Kang 1994: a.o.). These languages have drawn intrigue due to their unmarked form behaving number neutrally, while English’s unmarked form is specified for atomicity. Akan, which marks both singulars and plurals …

records.title: Against Distributed Deletion
records.abstract: This paper examines a previously unnoticed ‘split’ construction in Greek, where a possessor that originates in a PP occurs together with the P separated from the possessum. I show a correlation between the availability of this split and the interpretation of a PP. This finding poses a challenge to PF-based accounts of splitting, particularly those that assume distributed deletion (e.g., Fanselow and Ćavar 2002; Fanselow and Féry 2006, Bondarenko and Davis 2023, Murphy and Wilson 2025 i.a.). Such accounts require additional mechanisms beyond those independently required by a syntactic account and fail to predict the distribution of split constructions. Instead, I propose a purely syntactic …

records.title: The Uncommon Sense Effect: experimental evidence for underspecification as the mental basis of logical inference
records.abstract: Logical reasoning is one of humanity's most powerful abilities. A widespread assumption across psychology, linguistics, and philosophy holds that reasoning operates over concepts that refer to objects and properties in the world, yet this has rarely been tested empirically. We introduce a novel paradigm that exploits lexical ambiguity to differentiate candidate representations for human inference: word-forms, reference-fixing concepts, or more abstract "underspecified representations" that constrain meaning without fully determining it. Across three experiments (N=158), participants evaluated deductive arguments equivocating over polysemous or homonymous terms. Although these arguments are …

records.title: Patterns in the phonology of Mandarin Chinese: basic color terms and beyond
records.abstract: This paper investigates non-arbitrary phonological patterns in the Mandarin Chinese lexicon, focusing on basic color terms and common adjectival antonyms. An analysis of the six primary basic color terms reveals systematic onset correspondences. Specifically, the terms for non-colors (*bái* ‘white’, *hēi* ‘black’) exhibit maximal contrast in place and manner of articulation. In contrast, warm colors (*huáng* ‘yellow’, *hóng* ‘red’) and cold colors (*lán* ‘blue’, *lǜ* ‘green’) consistently share the onsets /h/ and /l/, respectively. Computational simulations resampling the Mandarin syllable inventory demonstrate that the simultaneous occurrence of these phonological distributions by chance …

records.title: what for-type KIND and TOKEN interrogatives
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates the what for-construction (WFC), an adnominal wh- construction attested in a limited set of European languages, including Germanic, Slavic, and Baltic varieties. The WFC combines an interrogative pronoun with a preposition-like element (for, für, za, par) and a nominal complement, and it displays a cluster of properties that distinguish it from ordinary wh-determiner phrases, including wh-split, atypical case behavior, and variation between KIND and TOKEN interpretations. The dissertation pursues three main goals. First, it provides a detailed descriptive overview of the WFC across languages, based on grammatical descriptions, existing theoretical work, and …

records.title: Peripheries in Continental West-Germanic
records.abstract: The Continental West Germanic languages provide a fertile ground for studying the structure of the clausal peripheries and the syntactic relations (movement or otherwise) between elements in the clausal peripheries and positions in the remainder of the clause. The left periphery is marked by the verb-second effect, positioning the finite verb to the immediate right of the first constituent. There is some evidence for distinguishing separate positions for topics and wh-elements in the left periphery, but very little evidence for the full range of left-peripheral positions proposed in the literature. In addition, there appears to be a position for even more peripheral elements that do not …

records.title: CONCEPTIONS OF INSTINCT IN LANGUAGE AND COMMUNICATION: PRAGMATIST VS. RATIONALIST APPROACHES
records.abstract: This paper focuses in particular on Peirce's Foundational Habit (Semeiosis) vs. Chomsky's Basic Operation (Merge). The concept of instinct has long played a central but controversial role in explanations of human cognition and behavior. In biology, psychology, and cognitive science, instinct is often invoked to explain capacities that appear early in development, recur widely across individuals, and emerge without explicit instruction. Yet critics have frequently argued that the concept is theoretically ambiguous and risks functioning as a placeholder explanation when underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This chapter reexamines the role of instinct in contemporary debates about language …

records.title: Diphthongs in Dutch
records.abstract: The core of the Dutch diphtong system are three diphthongs, one at each of the major places that Dutch also reserves for monophtongs: front unrounded /ɛi/, front rounded /ʏy/ and back rounded /ɑu/. In this chapter we first discuss these three core diphtongs, their historical origin and their place in the current system. We also compare these to two other sets. The first are the so-called ‘false dipthongs’ /uj, aj, oj, iw, ew/. These differ from the ‘real’ diphthongs in that the consist of vowel parts that are at different places of articulation (whereas real diphtongs are all in one place, differing only in height), and in their syllabification properties (true dipthongs allow non-coronal …

records.title: English Interjections as a Homeostatic Property Cluster
records.abstract: English interjections have been denied category status (Jespersen 1924), dismissed as uninteresting (Huddleston & Pullum 2005), or acknowledged as "marginal and anomalous" (Quirk et al. 1985). This paper argues that interjections are a thin-but-genuine homeostatic property cluster (HPC): a set of co-occurring properties (prosodic isolation, non-inflection, syntactic non-integration, non-referentiality, emotive force) maintained by identifiable stabilisers. At least three diachronic pathways — grammaticalization via semantic bleaching (historically demonstrated), pragmaticalization via syntactic deactivation, and nonce coinage via onomatopoeia (both proposed with clear examples) — converge …

records.title: A Human-In-The-Loop Framework For Culturally Grounded Elicitation In Linguistic Fieldwork In India
records.abstract: The elicitation of naturalistic linguistic data depends on the cultural and ecological suitability of the stimuli employed to prompt speaker responses. Standardized visual tools in language documentation are typically based on Western contexts, creating a mismatch in linguistically diverse settings such as India. This mismatch results in cognitive load and can affect elicited data due to increased code-mixing, reduced deictic accuracy, and interrupted speech. This paper puts forth a methodological proposal in the form of a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) workflow for generating culturally grounded elicitation stimuli using generative AI. The approach formalizes iterative prompt engineering, …

records.title: Argument ellipsis in Russian verb-stranding: an acceptability study of semantic constraints
records.abstract: Russian verb-stranding constructions, in which a finite verb appears without its internal argument, have been analyzed as instances of either Verb-stranding VP Ellipsis (VVPE) or Argument Ellipsis (AE). Recent work has established that AE is restricted to arguments of semantic type e, providing a diagnostic: if verb-stranding shows degraded acceptability with non-e-type arguments, AE rather than VVPE is the operative mechanism. This study extends prior experimental evidence for AE in Russian (Kasenov & Rudnev, to appear) by decomposing the non-e-type category into four subtypes: naming complement, predicative nominal, predicative adjectival, and argumental adverbial. In a pre-registered …

records.title: Yat as a Marker of PIE Vowel Lability: Evidence from Old Church Slavonic and Early Slavic Loanwords
records.abstract: The Old Church Slavonic letter yat (Ѣ, ѣ) represents Proto-Slavic *ě, a vowel unique among Slavic phonemes for producing four distinct modern reflexes: Ekavian /e/, Ikavian /i/, Ijekavian /ije/, and Bulgarian /ja/. We demonstrate that this four-way divergence is not a Slavic-internal accident but a continuation of a deeper pattern: yat systematically marks Proto-Indo-European (PIE) phonological positions where the vowel nucleus was complex—either a laryngeal sequence (*eh1) or a diphthong (*ey, *oy, *ay). We construct a 74-word corpus of yat-bearing OCS words with established PIE etymologies and quantify cross-IE vowel divergence at each yat position using a formal Lability Score (LS). Of …

records.title: Scale-sensitivity of comparatives and measure phrase interpretations in Gitksan
records.abstract: This paper demonstrates that in Gitksan, measure phrases (MPs) occurring with relative gradable adjectives (GAs) like ’wii ’nakw ‘tall’ receive differential interpretations even in the absence of an overt comparative operator or an overt standard phrase, a pattern which has been only reported in Japanese (e.g., Snyder et al. 1995) and Korean (Oda 2008; contra Sawada and Grano 2011). In contrast, MPs occurring with minimum-standard GAs like ḵ’aḵ ‘open’ receive absolute interpretations, as in many languages including Japanese (Sawada and Grano 2011). However, Gitksan differs from Japanese in two crucial ways. First, the distinction between relative and minimum-standard GAs is observed even …

records.title: The Havlík’s Law Asymmetry: Evidence That Liquid-Context Jers Were Not Real Vowels
records.abstract: This paper documents three independent lines of evidence that liquid-context jers in OCS were not real reduced vowels. First, a categorical distributional split: strong-position jers in non-liquid envi- ronments vocalize to full vowels in 100% of cases across Czech (n = 23), Serbian (n = 22), and Slovak (n = 23)—68 out of 68 words—while strong-position jers adjacent to liquids vocalize in 0% of cases (n = 27). The seven Modern Czech words with /e/ near liquids (červ, černý, blecha, pleť’) are secondary epenthesis of the 13th–15th centuries, documented in Old Czech as syllabic consonant forms (črv, črný, blcha, plt), and post-date the jer fall by centuries. Second, a quality test: when Czech …

records.title: On locality conditions for allomorphy and the ordering of interface operations
records.abstract: Research in Distributed Morphology (DM) has found that many patterns of allomorphy can be explained if allomorph selection is done cyclically. Several ancillary mechanisms have been argued to further delimit allomorphy; they include (i) linear adjacency (Embick 2010, a.o.); (ii) structural adjacency (Adger, Béjar, and Harbour 2001, 2003, a.o.); and (iii) accessibility domains, a claim that roots are visible up to the first node above the first categorizer (Moskal 2015). In this paper, I show that there are violations of (i)-(iii) in Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian (BCS) allomorphy. In section 2, I show that n(ominalizer)s in BCS complex nominals show allomorphic conditioning by a linearly …

records.title: Active participles are (deverbal) adjectives
records.abstract: This paper examines so-called active participles in three languages with different morphological systems (Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, English, and Hebrew). Based on a range of morphological, syntactic, and interpretational diagnostics, I argue that these elements are uniformly deverbal adjectives. This result challenges a substantial body of work claiming that active participles show an adjectival/verbal ambiguity, but it is in line with Bešlin 2023 which analyzes passive participles as deverbal adjectives. Importantly, deverbal adjectives may denote predicates of properties or predicates of eventualities (events or states), depending on the characteristics of the verbal structure they embed. …

records.title: The Role of the Possessor/HAVE-Relation in Semantics (handout)
records.abstract: It is a common view that the wide range of readings of the possessor construction and of 'have' are due to polysemy. The talk presents semantic data that require a unified have-relation even in the absence of HAVE in syntax. It will pursue a unified relation along the lines of a 'reference-point relation' in the sense of Langacker (1993).

records.title: Hearsay and (non-)endorsement
records.abstract: This paper is devoted to what I will call the ‘non-endorsement puzzle’: a distinguished feature of hearsay evidentials such that they allow the speaker to disavow the prejacent. Ever since it was ﬁrst brought to the forefront of formal semantic research by Martina Faller (2002), the puzzle has been the subject of lively debates in the literature. My goals in this paper are fourfold: (i) to delineate the desiderata for a theory of non-endorsement by placing evidentials in a larger context of speech and attitude reports; (ii) to disentangle the modelling of the core semantics of evidentials from the modelling of the discourse effects of utterances that contain them; (iii) to propose …

records.title: Grammatically citing your sources via “say”-complementation
records.abstract: Across the world’s languages, one of the most common clausal complementation strategies involves a form of the verb “say.” Most research in this area assumes “say” to be equivalent to the English complementizer “that.” The present paper argues that an element in Lubukusu (Bantu, Kenya) that was formerly treated as an agreeing complementizer is actually a stative verb meaning “say.” This “say” predicate is the head of a clausal adjunct that merges at the VP level of the matrix clause, reasonably mimicking a complementizer. However, we demonstrate a number of reasons to think it is a verb. As a consequence of this analysis, an otherwise complex agreement system is reduced to run-of-the-mill …

records.title: Absolutive agreement failure and the flavors of T/Infl in Mam
records.abstract: This squib analyzes matrix clauses with no overt aspect morpheme in Mam, a Mayan language of Guatemala and Mexico. These clauses involve systematic failure of absolutive (Set B) agreement with intransitive subjects and transitive objects; if either is pronominal, must be expressed overtly in argument position (i.e. not pro-dropped). I argue that these clauses involve a phonologically null completive aspect morpheme (Ø, glossed 'NCOM'), which realizes a T/Infl head that idiosyncratically lacks a phi-probe. Evidence is presented that this agreement failure is not reducible to the phonological status of either the aspect morpheme itself or the Set B morphemes (cf. Woolford 2011). I propose …

records.title: Exploring crosslinguistic and genre variation in syntactic complexity: insights from a multilingual parallel corpus
records.abstract: Syntactic complexity varies not only between languages but also across textual genres, reflecting structural, stylistic, and communicative factors. This study explores the interplay of these two dimensions by analyzing six syntactic complexity metrics (SCMs) across 17 languages and four genres in a large multilingual corpus. We examine how SCMs correlate across languages and genres and assess which metrics best predict language versus genre. Correlation analysis reveals two robust metric clusters – clausal and phrasal. Inter-metric correlations are high in legal texts and movie subtitles, but substantially lower in parliamentary proceedings and fiction, likely due to greater internal …

records.title: Datasets for Verb Alternations across Languages: BLM Templates and Data Augmentation Strategies
records.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable performance across various sentence-based linguistic phenomena, yet their ability to capture cross-sentence paradigmatic patterns, such as verb alternations, remains underexplored. In this work, we present curated paradigm-based datasets for four languages, designed to probe systematic cross-sentence knowledge of verb alternations (change-of-state and object-drop constructions in English, German and Italian, and Hebrew binyanim). The datasets comprise thousands of the Blackbird Language Matrices (BLMs) problems. The BLM task– an RPM/ARC-like task devised specifically for language– is a controlled linguistic puzzle where models must select …

records.title: Complex Segments and the Perceptual Compression Hypothesis
records.abstract: This proposal introduces a new principle, the Perceptual Compression Hypothesis (PCH), which postulates that subsyllabic elements—onset, nucleus, and coda—represent segmental temporal units in phonetics capable of hosting multiple phonetic segments, thereby giving rise to complex segments. Following the tenets of Strict CV theory, which proposes that CV is the only syllable structure existing in phonology, this framework argues that the onset position admits only complex segments, while the arrangement of complex segments within rhyme elements depends on grammatical patterns exclusive to each language. The hypothesis distinguishes between two types of complex segments: primary complex …

records.title: A Quantitative θ₁-Based Analysis of Vowel Tenseness: English Monophthongs /iː/, /ɪ/, /æ/, /ʌ/, /ɑː/, /uː/, and /ʊ/
records.abstract: This paper examines the vowel tenseness indicator θ₁ in the English vowel /ɑː/ and compares the results with previously reported findings in Ishizaki (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2025a, 2025b) in order to provide a more comprehensive discussion. An investigation of the English vowels /ɑː/, /æ/, and /ʌ/, which may cause confusion for Japanese speakers, shows that /ɑː/ and /ʌ/ display similar θ₁ patterns, whereas /æ/ behaves differently. If vowel tenseness is assumed to be defined in the same way for both close and open vowels, comparison with the θ₁ behavior of the close vowels /iː/, /ɪ/, /uː/, and /ʊ/ may provide further insight into the tenseness of /ɑː/, /æ/, and /ʌ/. Ishizaki (2025a) …

records.title: Persona Framing in Human–LLM Interaction
records.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit a high degree of stylistic adaptability, yet they frequently produce unstable responses in terms of discursive register, enunciative position, and pragmatic coherence across extended interactions. A common practice among users is persona prompting, in which the model is instructed to assume a specific discursive role. Although widely used in practice, this technique has been treated primarily as a prompt engineering strategy, with limited analysis from the perspective of linguistics and discourse pragmatics. This paper proposes interpreting persona prompting as a mechanism of discursive framing (persona framing) in human–LLM interaction. It argues that …

records.title: How Music Refers: Music Semantics and Cross-Modal Correspondences
records.abstract: Recent theoretical work in music semantics has proposed a formal framework to model how music can convey information about the extra-musical world. At the same time, a large body of empirical research on cross-modal correspondences has evidenced systematic mappings between perceptual dimensions across sensory domains. In this paper, we present several experimental audiovisual paradigms designed to show that the two efforts should be integrated, and argue that music semantics must be grounded in cross-modal correspondences while allowing for more expressive forms of meaning. We first demonstrate that pitch and loudness can be interpreted as the level of energy of a visual object, or as its …

records.title: Fact checking Geoffrey Pullum's claims about Daniel Everett in Brazil
records.abstract: Geoffrey K. Pullum has repeatedly made severe accusations that the linguist Daniel L. Everett suffered mistreatment in Brazil because his research on the Pirahã people and their language threatened Chomskyan theory. The present article presents a large trove of previously unavailable evidence (official Brazilian government documents, citizen information requests, interviews, etc.) that are directly relevant for assessing the claims that Everett was slandered and unjustly blocked from field research. The evidence disproves these claims, which have circulated widely in what I am designating as the Persecution Hoax. The evolution of Everett’s problems with Brazil’s National Foundation for …

records.title: A Preliminary Phonemic Analysis of Haryanvi
records.abstract: This paper presents a phonemic analysis of the West-Central variety of Haryanvi spoken in parts of Bhiwani and the Hansi region of Hisar district in Haryana, India. Based on minimal pair evidence and native speaker data, the study identifies an inventory of thirty-two consonant phonemes, nine vowel phonemes, and three diphthongs. The study also examines syllable structure and the phonotactic distribution of segments. The findings contribute to the phonological description of Haryanvi, which remains relatively under-documented in linguistic literature.

records.title: Presupposition filtering in disjunction: The role of exclusive interpretation
records.abstract: Kalomoiros and Schwarz (2024) report symmetric presupposition projection across disjunction, a key datum for theories of projection. This study further asks whether projection across disjunctions is affected by exclusive interpretations. We observe that many fully semantic implementations of exclusivity and presupposition projection converge on the same, previously untested prediction: exclusive disjunction yields uniform projection (i.e., no filtering for either disjunct), so increasing exclusivity should reduce filtering. Mayr & Romoli (2016a) derive this prediction for Strong Kleene semantics when exclusivity is computed via bivalent exhaustification, and we show that it also follows, …

records.title: Phonetic Palindromes in Japanese: IPA Analysis of Words Invariant Under Acoustic Reversal
records.abstract: This study investigates the acoustic phenomenon where the Japanese name for the tiger beetle, Ooenma Hanmyou (オオエンマハンミョウ, Cicindela japonica), sounds perceptually identical when played in reverse. Originating from an investigation on the Japanese television program "Tantei! Night Scoop," this finding challenges conventional understandings of palindromes. Unlike orthographic palindromes (e.g., "tomato"), which are visually symmetric but acoustically asymmetric due to stop consonant bursts, the word Ooenma Hanmyou represents a rare class of "acoustic palindromes." Through International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) analysis, this paper demonstrates that true acoustic reversibility requires two …

records.title: Parasuppositions
records.abstract: We introduce a new class of linguistic inferences, "parasuppositions", triggered by diverse constructions, notably appositive participles (e.g. 'Ann drinks, taking enormous risks'); post-speech gestures—e.g. 'Ann drinks – DRINK', where DRINK is a gestural representation of drinking; and parenthetical conjuncts q of the form p (and q)—e.g. 'Ann drinks (and takes enormous risks)'. With special reference to French, we show that parasuppositions give rise to projection patterns reminiscent of presuppositions: 'Ann might smoke, taking enormous risks' yields the inference that if Ann smokes, she takes enormous risks. These projection patterns suggest that parasuppositions must be locally trivial …

records.title: Strong and weak resultatives with result roots in English and Spanish
records.abstract: We consider a subclass of result verbs in Rappaport Hovav & Levin’s (2010) sense built on roots that entail change (Beavers & Koontz-Garboden, 2020), e.g., break, melt, explode, and tear. We argue that this class of roots possesses different grammatical properties between English and Spanish with respect to resultative constructions: these roots productively appear in both strong and weak resultatives in English but form only weak resultatives in Spanish (Washio, 1997). We propose an account of this asymmetry between the two languages rooted in differences in the semantic properties of the root class and independent differences in the inventory of prepositional heads available in each …

records.title: Anaphora for Concepts, Kinds, and Parts in Dynamic Interpretation
records.abstract: The article deals with anaphoric phenomena that involve concepts, kinds, specimens, parts, and totalities. It sketches a theory that explains the use of singular vs. plural kind anaphors that assumes different morphosyntactic features for mass vs. count nouns. It discusses the phenomenon that concept antecedents are not restricted by anaphoric islands, and proposes that this is because they are name-like. It proposes an implementation within DRT and in compositional dynamic interpretation.

records.title: VP ellipsis and argument structure alternations: Evidence from Muira Dargwa complex predicates
records.abstract: In this paper, I investigate the properties of an elliptical construction in the Nakh-Daghestanian language Muira Dargwa, in which only part of a complex predicate goes missing. I show that this process has a number of common features with Verb Phrase Ellipsis in English and related phenomena in other languages. Under an analysis of complex predicates where the light verb is the realization of the v head, the deleted constituent can be associated with the complement of v. Thus, the process diverges from similar phenomena in that the size of the ellipsis is smaller, allowing for a larger number of mismatches between antecedent and elliptical clauses.

records.title: Ellipsis in contact: VPE and sluicing in Spanish heritage speakers
records.abstract: This study investigates the evaluation of verb phrase ellipsis (VPE) and sluicing by English-dominant Spanish heritage speakers (HSs). Spanish permits VPE only with modal remnants (ModVPE), while English allows both ModVPE and auxiliary-stranding VPE (AuxVPE). Sluicing, in contrast, behaves similarly in both languages inasmuch as it is constrained by voice-matching requirements stemming from the universal identity condition on ellipsis. We thus test whether HSs’ difficulties with silent elements (“the Silent Problem”) are observed across structures, or whether they are particularly notable when transfer from the dominant language is available (i.e., AuxVPE in English transferring into …

records.title: Structure and interpretation across categories
records.abstract: This dissertation takes as its starting point the assumption that word formation is syntactic (and piece-based, with Distributed Morphology and related frameworks), and focuses on a point of tension that is inherent to this assumption: If word formation is syntactic and `words’ are really just smaller syntactic structures, then why do they appear to behave differently from larger syntactic structures for purposes of interpretation at the interfaces? Why are they so selective in determining which pieces may become a part of the structure? Why do they show so many idiosyncratic and unpredictable forms and meanings? These questions are investigated in the empirical domain of German …

records.title: Natural Class
records.abstract: In a binary feature system that allows underspecification, which of these sets of segments constitute natural classes, where /D/ is a coronal stop unspecified for Voice?: {t, d}, {t}, {d}, {t, D, d}, {D}, {t, D}, {D, d} The answers and their implications fall out from basic logic, perhaps best understood as “third factor” (Chomsky 2005) effects. Some recurring misconceptions in natural class logic are examined, along with the relationship between natural classes and the notion of “possible rule”. We introduce the three basic operators of Logical Phonology and apply them in rules that obey natural class logic to account in purely phonological terms for the behavior of “exceptionally” …

records.title: The puzzle of language without syntax: A review of Steven Mithen's (2024) "The Language Puzzle"
records.abstract: In his recent (2024) book “The Language Puzzle,” Steven Mithen argues, among other things, that universal grammar has been altogether debunked, and that the question of the origin of natural-language syntax and compositionality has largely been answered by the work of computational evolutionary linguists Simon Kirby and collaborators, thus: “syntax spontaneously emerges from the generation-to-generation language-learning process itself.” I show that Kirby and collaborators’ work in fact presupposes the entirety of syntax in an innate language of thought, and that it subscribes to a notion of universal grammar no weaker than the mainstream one from generative linguistics in the twenty-first …

records.title: Morphosyntax of A'ingae clauses and verb phrases: A description
records.abstract: This paper describes the morphology and morphosyntax of verbs and clauses in A'ingae (or Cofán, ISO 639-3: con, an Amazonian isolate). A'ingae is characterized by rich, predominantly head-marking morphology, robust pro-drop, relatively free (often verb-final) word order, and nominative-accusative morphosyntactic alignment. Themes emphasized in the description include the functions of A'ingae suffixes and clitics, their morphosyntactic restrictions, and the types of clauses they can appear in.

records.title: Exploring Gesture and Prosodic Alignment at Code-Switching Boundaries: A Multimodal Analysis of Twi-English Speech
records.abstract: This study investigates gesture-prosody coordination in naturalistic Twi-English code-switching speech, focusing on gesture type distribution, temporal alignment between gesture strokes and prosodic prominence, and gestural activity at code-switching boundaries. A corpus of 11 video clips totalling 65.1 minutes was annotated using ELAN 7.0, yielding 837 gesture strokes classified according to McNeill's typology. Fundamental frequency was extracted using Praat's autocorrelation algorithm, and code-switching points were identified through a computational language inference pipeline built on FFmpeg speech detection. Results show that beat gestures dominated the corpus at 68.0%, consistent with …

records.title: The potential of kinematic analysis for gesture theory: A case study of intensified head nods
records.abstract: Quantitative motion-tracking methods are widely used in computational linguistics, psychology, and the cognitive sciences to measure fine-grained behavioral dynamics. By contrast, theoretical linguistics—in particular emerging work on gesture and multimodal meaning—has only recently begun to exploit their methodological potential. This paper argues that such tools are particularly well suited to addressing theoretical questions that turn on non-categorical, scalar variation in linguistic expression, where relevant distinctions are encoded in continuous properties of form, as is the case with gesture. As a case study, the paper investigates intensified head nods as gestural response elements …

records.title: Modal Force and its realization across languages
records.abstract: Force is one of the two major dimensions of meaning along which modals in natural language vary, the other being flavor. In this chapter, we provide an overview of formal approaches to modal force, with a focus on cross-linguistic data and typological evidence. In formal semantics, a common assumption is that necessity and possibility modals express (respectively) universal and existential quantification over possible worlds. However, there are some modals that do not fall into this binary in an obvious way. In this chapter, we explore two such cases: weak necessity modals, which are universal-like, but weaker than strong necessity modals, and variable force modals, which can take on …

records.title: Possessives in North-Calabrian dialects
records.abstract: This paper addresses the possessive structures in Southern Italian dialects, focusing on Northern Calabrian dialects. Generally, in Southern Italian dialects possessives follow the analysis of noun and in predicative contexts are introduced by the article. Besides, Northern Calabrian systems attest another structure in which possessives are introduced by the article preceded by the preposition di in copular predicative contexts and, variably, inside DPs. This arrangement recalls the structures where a linker precedes adjectives or genitives in many languages, among which some Balkan languages such as Albanian and Aromanian varieties. The comparison with the linker structures of these …

records.title: Differentiation Before Frequency: Survival, Variation, and Internal Evaluation in Language
records.abstract: Languages routinely generate structurally valid variants, yet derivation alone does not guarantee their survival in use. This essay develops an account of how linguistic forms survive, spread, or are reshaped in use by examining a set of concrete cases, primarily from Telugu plural morphology but extending across registers, dialect contact, and cross-linguistic borrowing. Through a series of illustrations, I show that grammatically possible alternatives are not neutral once enacted in use. Instead, they diverge systematically according to how readily they integrate into ongoing articulatory and structural coordination. Building on this observation, I propose internal evaluation as a …

records.title: Distributive kind predication
records.abstract: This paper makes two contributions to the study of the interpretation of nominals across Germanic and Romance languages. First, it shows that plural kind terms, such as English bare plurals (e.g., lions) and Italian definite plurals (e.g., i leoni), have definite, non-generic uses in sentences expressing generalizations that were traditionally thought to uniformly involve generic quantification. These non-generic uses explain why the distribution of kind-denoting plurals in sentences expressing generalizations is wider than that of singular indefinites, which can only appear in generalizations with a genuinely generic Logical Form (Sects. 3–5). Second, the paper draws on a contrast between …

records.title: How many perspectives to explain how to change a tire? A cinematic approach to analyzing depicting constructions in signed language discourse (poster)
records.abstract: Sign Languages are known for their iconic devices of depiction, such as constructed action and classifier constructions. These depicting constructions are used to show scenes, actions and situations in their temporal unfolding, and they are said to show many spatial perspectives of an event. But what does this look like in a stretch of discourse? How many perspectives are there and how can these different spatial vantage points be identified and labelled for further analysis? How are these perspectives organized to give an oriented view on events and scene? To answer these questions, the poster proposes using a cinematic approach to analyzing depicting constructions in signed language …

records.title: Image superimposition in signed language discourse and in motion pictures: An intermedial comparison
records.abstract: Both film and signed languages are media that make use of iconicity and employ motion images for communicative and narrative purposes. This paper focuses on simultaneously presented images that occur in film for example as double exposures and in signed languages as simultaneous constructions. While film and signed languages differ in many ways with respect to iconicity, they can be compared with respect to the way simultaneously presented motion images relate to each other. Superimpositions are defined as a simultaneous view on two or more scenes or as giving two different simultaneous representations of one scene. They serve as a means of dense information packaging. While …

records.title: Gebärdensprachen als bewegte Bilder? Eine Untersuchung zur Anwendbarkeit von Filmbeschreibungsbegriffen auf bildliche Diskursphänomene in Deutscher Gebärdensprache (DGS)
records.abstract: Titel English: Sign Languages as Moving Images? A Study on the Applicability of Descriptive Categories from Film Studies to Iconic Discourse Phenomena in German Sign Language (DGS) Sign languages ​​exhibit a high proportion of iconic discourse structures, that are characterized by their scenic and illustrative nature and as such reminiscent of film sequences. Due to their productive imagery and combinability, these structures cannot be adequately described with traditional linguistic concepts. Starting from the topos of the film-like quality of sign languages, this dissertation systematically examines how and to what extent descriptive tools and concepts of film studies can be applied to …

records.title: Gradual weakening across morphological layers: Solving stratal paradoxes in Kashaya
records.abstract: Harmonic Layer Theory can correctly predict the interaction of metrical processes in Kashaya which results in an ordering paradox in a classical stratal system. This novel cyclic formalization of the morpho-phonology interface predicts that processes can be restricted to elements that already underwent a previous optimization cycle – while novel elements added in a later cycle are simultaneously present.

records.title: Differential Object Marking in Heritage Italo-Romance: A Microcontact Perspective
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates Differential Object Marking (DOM) in heritage Italo-Romance varieties spoken in Argentina, situating the phenomenon within a broader Romance and cross-linguistic perspective. DOM, whereby only a subset of direct objects receives overt morphological marking, has been widely studied in Romance languages, yet little is known about its behaviour in heritage contexts where the dominant language—Argentinian Spanish—also exhibits a robust DOM system. The study addresses four central questions: (i) whether DOM changes in heritage grammars; (ii) whether such changes are contact-induced or internally motivated; (iii) how microcontact within bilingual communities differs …

records.title: ZË-RO v0.2 Note: Morphological Masking & Recovery in Albanian200 (Controlled Ablation)
records.abstract: We report a deterministic diagnostic from ZË-RO’s Albanian200 analysis harnesses, testing whether schwa-heavy prefix morphology (notably për-/përë-) can mask root-aligned carrier-primary vowels in a small anchored subset (N=28). In the Compound Stress v0.2 harness, root-anchored retention is 64.3% for position (9/14, p=0.013) and 100.0% for order (14/14, p=0.001); all position mismatches are për-prefixed cases where the surface carrier primary becomes Ë while the anchor root primary is A/E. A controlled “Gegë-sim” perturbation (Ë-drop heuristics; not a claim about real dialect IPA) recovers the masked position cases to 100.0% retention (14/14, p=0.001), while order remains 100.0% (14/14, …

records.title: A CARTESIAN DREAM, A geometrical account of syntax In honor of Andrea Moro (full book)
records.abstract: This book springs from the idea of celebrating Andrea Moro’s 60th birthday with a collection of striking remarks on linguistics and neurolinguistics. To this end, we asked a number of Andrea Moro’s colleagues to write a very short essay which sheds some light on a single but significant point of the linguistic system. The result has been rewarding in several respects, with the essays spanning a wide range of topics. Thus, some authors focus on copular sentences (Adriana Belletti; Marcel den Dikken; Carlo Cecchetto and Caterina Donati; Gennaro Chierchia), others on the basic operations of movement (Valentina Bianchi; Cristiano Chesi) and agreement (Alessandra Tomaselli). Some investigate …

records.title: Existential "Amount" Relatives
Negation causes NPI and NCI illusions in Czech
records.abstract: Grammaticality illusions are cases where comprehenders fleetingly consider ungrammatical sentences to be acceptable. The phenomenon been used to tap into the mechanism of online negative polarity item (NPI) licensing (Muller & Phillips, 2020). The effect has high specificity and not all environments that ordinarily license NPIs create illusions-sentential negation being the prime case that is ineffective as an illusory licensor (Orth et al., 2021). In the current study, we contrast NPIs with another class of expressions, namely negative concord items (NCIs), which are said to be licensed in the syntax unlike NPIs. We test whether sentential negation gives rise to illusions with Czech NPIs …

records.title: The roles of grammar and pragmatics in focus dependencies
records.abstract: Focus dependencies, including question–answer congruence, free focus, and association with focus, are often treated in terms of grammatical and pragmatic mechanisms that rely on (a) focus-semantic values along a second semantic dimension, and (b) an anaphoric operator, ~, that is sensitive to these values and can communicate them to various processes. I argue against this view and in favor of a purely pragmatic treatment of focus in which there are no focus semantic values within the grammar, let alone operators sensitive to such values. Instead of ~, I propose a unification of focus dependencies through a pragmatic condition: an utterance is felicitous only if it is a good answer to a good …

records.title: Lambda in natural language semantics: function application and lambda conversion: a web app
records.abstract: The purpose of this little web app is to provide the output of an application of a function to its argument in the style of the lambda calculus, i.e. in the form λx [P (x)] (y), where the part λx [P (x)] is the function and y is the argument that the function is applied to. The page is geared to uses of the lambda calculus in natural language semantics, as introduced in Kearns (2000/2011: chap. 4) and Lohnstein (1996/2011: chap. 8), for instance. The WWW address of the app is provided in the accompanying PDF. References: Kearns, Kate. 2000/2011. Semantics. 2nd edn. Houndmills: Palgrave Macmillan. Lohnstein, Horst. 1996/2011. Formale Semantik und natürliche Sprache. 2nd edn. Berlin: De …

records.title: Optimality Theory
Scalar values in downward and non-downward entailing contexts
records.abstract: We discuss (i) the nature of a lexicalization condition on scalar implicatures that precludes lexicalizing negation of strong scalar elements, and (ii) parametric variation in the scope properties of conjunctive and disjunctive operators relative to negation. The empirical cases discussed show that logic differs from natural language, an internal cognitive system and part of human biology, therefore empirically constrained, in this case by conditions on polarity and scalar implicatures that are absent from formal logic. The interpretation of disjunction and conjunction is universal as in propositional logic following de Morgan’s laws. Hence, the conjunctive interpretation of disjunction in …

records.title: ERGATIVITY, PROPERLY ALIGNED
records.abstract: [added: pivots of topic continuity]. This is the condensed version of “Ergativity demystified”, but supplemented to include causative and applicative constructions.The grammatical elegance of ergative languages becomes evident when they are not read against the grain.

records.title: ZË-RO v0.1: A Deterministic Orthography Aperture Meter with Baseline-Locked Drift Detection
records.abstract: We present ZË-RO v0.1, a deterministic research instrument that extracts orthographic vowel-carrier structure (A, E, I, O, U, Y, Ë) and computes an aperture proxy using a fixed calibration scale. The system is designed for reproducibility and drift detection: research harnesses emit MD/JSON reports and commit baseline-locked references that fail on unexpected change. We report baseline behavior across multiple suites: positive-signal language datasets (Albanian and Turkish), a strict negative control using pseudowords (no semantic intent), and a drift-visibility suite (Taiwan Zhuyin) designed to weaken under expansion. The negative control shows weak/non-significant slope and no …

records.title: Quarantined
The presuppositions of 'forget'
records.abstract: The propositional attitude verb forget has received relatively little attention in the formal linguistics literature, though its properties present interesting problems for formal semantics. White (2014) argues that a uniform account of forget as a factive verb is possible. On this view, forget presupposes the truth of its clausal argument (See also Kiparsky & Kiparsky (1970)). But in order to do so, he claims that a covert modal operator is obligatorily present in the infinitival complements of forget, deriving modalized factive presuppositions. In this paper, I present data showing that the distribution of this covert modal operator is even more restricted. I argue that modalization of …

records.title: Grounding as a Discursive Achievement: A Cognitive Grammar Analysis of the  Definite Article in a Pedagogical Lect
records.abstract: Pedagogical discourse relies on coordination of mental spaces between interlocutors. In Cognitive Grammar, this is achieved through grounding. The definite article acts as a cognitive command to establish mental contact. Formal approaches to uniqueness often view uniqueness as static, this study argues it as a discursive achievement. This paper proposes a seven type schema model of grounding operations. By the analysis of 7 classroom lectures, this study demonstrates the use of the epistemic control cycle to negotiate attention. Notably, the analysis highlights the emergence of reference point constructions- such as the “lizard..tail” phenomenon–reveals cognitive anchoring strategies for …

records.abstract: Pedagogical discourse relies on coordination of mental spaces between interlocutors. In Cognitive Grammar, this is achieved through grounding. The definite article acts as a cognitive command to establish mental contact. Formal approaches to uniqueness often view uniqueness as static, this study argues it as a discursive achievement.
