Notably, the analysis highlights the emergence of reference point constructions- such as the “lizard..tail” phenomenon–reveals cognitive anchoring strategies for …

records.title: A cartographic approach to Chinese V de O clefts
records.abstract: This paper investigates the so-called V de O clefts in Chinese, a specific type of “clefts” where the de particle appears between the verb and the object, and proposes a cartographic approach to their syntactic and semantic properties. While some common generalizations about this pattern are shown to hold upon closer examination (i.e., exhaustive focus, obligatory past reading, ban on TMA markers), some do not (i.e., strict adjacency effect, term focus restriction). Two key projections are argued to exist in the relevant functional hierarchy, each linked to one crucial element in the pattern: (i) a FocP selected by the copula shi; (ii) an Asp*P headed by the verbal particle de. The former …

records.title: Rooth-Partee conditionals and the symmetry of disjunction
records.abstract: This paper argues that ‘or’ is inherently symmetric, based on the intuitive equivalence of [If y is P or Q, then x is] and [If y is Q or P, then x is] – referred to as Rooth-Partee conditionals. As observed in Rooth & Partee (1982), the elided phrase in the consequent clause of these conditionals triggers a reading paraphrased as ‘If x is P, y is P and if x is Q, y is Q’. Accounting for that reading proves to be problematic for asymmetric approaches to ‘or'.

records.title: Syntactic ergativity without inversion in Kalaallisut
records.abstract: Kalaallisut (Inuit; Greenland) is a well-known example of a syntactically ergative language, serving as the primary example of that language type in Bittner and Hale (1996a). In relative clauses, ergatives cannot be relativized; there is an ergative extraction constraint (EEC). From Bittner and Hale (1996a) onward, analyses of the EEC standardly appeal to inversion: the absolutive object must obtain an A-position higher than the ergative subject as a matter of basic clause structure, but object movement over the subject blocks further A’ movement by the subject. In this paper we re-evaluate this analysis for Kalaallisut. Considering patterns of word order, Condition C, hyperraising, scope, …

records.title: Same Form, Different Grammars: The Slavic [ov]~[u] Alternation
records.abstract: This paper investigates the [ov]~[u] alternation in Slavic verbs derived from nominal and adjectival stems. In addition to the alternation between a sequence and a single segment, Slavic languages differ with respect to the surface shape of the VC sequence: some only feature [ov], some alternate [ov] and [ev] depending on the preceding consonant, some only feature [uv]. Drawing from both synchronic and diachronic predecessors, it is shown that the alternation deserves a unified approach. The verbaliser suffix has an abstract underlying representation, adapted phonologically based on hiatus resolution requirements: an underlyingly defective diphthong surfaces as a vowel before a consonant …

records.title: Beyond the horizon: a more-than-human and holistic approach to language
records.abstract: This position paper proposes a more-than-human and holistic approach to language that moves beyond entrenched divides between structuralism, constructivism, positivism, and methodological camps. Writing under the collective pseudonym Gaya Seldon, we argue that many oppositions in linguistics, particularly the equation of quantitative methods with positivism and structuralism, rest on reductive misreadings. Structuralism, we contend, is not inherently anti-social or anti-agentive but grounded in relationality; its caricature has contributed to theoretical fragmentation and epistemic silos. At the same time, constructivist and decolonial turns, while critically valuable, often remain …

records.title: Note on the Semantics of Frequency Adverbials and Mereotopology
records.abstract: This a brief note on Marcin Wagiel’s SALT 33 2023 proceedings paper ‘Acts, occasions, and multiplicatives: A mereotopological account’ and the analysis of frequency adverbials in Parts and Wholes in Semantics (OUP 1997) as well as the general mereotopological view of part-structure that that book had introduced into natural language semantics against the background of the use of extensional mereology in semantics (Link 1983). Recent mereotopological analyses are thus not novel in that respect.

records.title: Psychological science and linguistic theory
records.abstract: In the study of human cognition, language is central in part because our species is the only surviving member of the primate lineage that is in possession of its distinctive properties. Evidence suggests that only in homo sapiens, spectacularly, did language emerge. Aside from the point of view of evolutionary origins, the other reason for language being a defining feature is its function as an indispensable instrument of higher order cognition. If language-related abilities are essential in this way, linguistics can be understood as a branch of psychology; and in general, the methods of cognitive science should be applicable to its study in every way. From another perspective, its …

records.title: Collecting data in understudied language varieties: A methodological note
records.abstract: Eliciting linguistic data from speakers of non-standardized varieties presents well-known challenges. Traditional acceptability judgment tasks have been widely used to probe grammatical knowledge, but task design, such as mode of presentation, response options, and labeling, can strongly influence outcomes (Marty et al., 2020). In this study, we investigate a small group of heritage Catalan speakers in Germany and the Netherlands using a repetition-based task rather than a standard judgment task. Our findings indicate that responses to repetition tasks differ significantly from commonly known generalizations on the phenomenon at issue investigated through grammaticality judgment tasks. We …

records.title: Chain Reduction as substitution: A PF-based account of anti-locality
records.abstract: In current minimalist theorizing, the elimination of copies created by Internal Merge is typically attributed to copy deletion, most prominently formalized by Nunes (2004) as Chain Reduction. This paper explores an alternative hypothesis that Chain Reduction proceeds via substitution rather than deletion. I show that this reconceptualization makes it possible to derive complement-to-specifier anti-locality effects (the ban on P-stranding) from labeling ambiguity that arises in head/head configurations (Chomsky 2013, 2015). Under the timing of the Labeling Algorithm adopted here, such anti-locality violations are predicted to be resolvable through ellipsis. While a detailed discussion of …

records.title: A Unified Hypothesis on the Origins of Hurro-Urartian, Kartvelian, and Tyrsenian Language Families
records.abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework for understanding three ancient language families — Hurro-Urartian, Kartvelian, and Tyrsenian (Etruscan/Lemnian/Raetic) — as descendants of a common Caucasian Hunter-Gatherer (CHG) linguistic ancestor dating to the Mesolithic period. Drawing on comparative personal pronoun systems, grammatical architecture, phonological inventories, and recent archaeogenetic evidence, we argue that these families share a set of structural features — pure suffixing morphology, ergative-absolutive alignment, animacy-based nominal distinctions, Suffixaufnahme, and a five-vowel proto-system — that cannot be explained by chance or contact alone. We further propose that the …

records.title: The Challenge of Analyzing a Dynamic Text: Why the Voynich Manuscript Resists Conventional Interpretation
records.abstract: The Voynich Manuscript (MS 408, Beinecke Library, Yale University) has resisted all attempts of conventional interpretation for over a century. This paper argues that the persistent failure of cryptographic, linguistic, and statistical approaches stems from a shared foundational assumption: that the manuscript’s text was produced by a static system—whether a fixed cipher, a natural language grammar, or a stable encoding scheme. Analysis of the manuscript’s word network and vocabulary evolution reveals that this assumption is untenable. The text exhibits continuous development throughout the manuscript, with vocabulary, character usage, and word frequency distributions shifting gradually …

records.title: Wh-movement paths and oblique extraction in Mam (Mayan)
records.abstract: This paper examines the Ā-extraction of adjuncts in San Juan Ostuncalco Mam (SJO Mam; Mayan), focusing on the enclitic =(y)a’, which (optionally) appears on predicates when certain adjuncts are extracted. We describe the distribution of =(y)a’ in monoclausal and long-distance extraction and show that, with the exception of temporals, the extraction adjuncts licenses the enclitic, which may occur multiple times along a movement dependency, including within a single clause. We argue that =(y)a’ provides a morphological footprint of the path taken by an extracted adjunct. Specifically, we analyze =(y)a’ as the spellout of Ā-agreement between the extracted adjunct and intermediate heads along …

records.title: Nombres propios determinados y gramática del registro. Observaciones desde la Romania Nova
records.abstract: The aim of this work is to offer a comparative analysis of the construction of [article + proper noun] in Río de la Plata Spanish (e.g., "la Samara") and Brazilian Portuguese (e.g., "a Samara"). Despite the different distribution observed in both varieties, the article is neither a mere expletive nor the iota operator that the same form of the article realizes in definite descriptions. On the contrary, the article indicates an expressive syntax and semantics, in the sense of multidimensional semantics (Potts 2005, McCready 2010, 2019, Gutzmann 2015, 2019, and Saab and Carranza 2021, among others). Specifically, the article signals a certain interpersonal proximity relationship between the …

records.title: Japanese accusative/ablative alternation verbs are unaccusative
records.abstract: This paper concerns a small group of Japanese verbs that license a morphological case alternation between accusative case and ablative (postpositional) case. I will call them Accusative/Ablative Alternation Verbs, or simply Alternation Verbs. The primary goal of this paper is to identify the argument structures projected by Alternation Verbs that give rise to the two variants of the case alternation. I will argue that these verbs project a unified, dyadic unaccusative structure without thematic Voice. Alternation Verbs are thus an example of verbs that introduce accusative-marked arguments despite not projecting a typical transitive argument structure.

records.title: The plus and minus of bonobo call combinations
records.abstract: Berthet et al. (2025) propose a computational method to find cases of non-trivial compositionality (when an utterance of a sequence "A B" should not just be interpreted as "A and B", as if elements A and B were interpreted one after the other for instance) in bonobo vocal communication. We show weaknesses of the criteria, and suggest a path for completing the program.

records.title: Plural and feminine marking in Lunigianese varieties. A(n apparent) case of phonologically-determined affix reordering
records.abstract: Thispaperproposesananalysisofanunexpectedlinearorderingofthegen andnum markers in a set of non-standard Romance varieties spoken in Lunigiana, Italy. This linear ordering is unexpected because it apparently violates the Mirror Principle, which predicts that the gen marker is closer to the root than the num marker. I provide an analysis of the Lunigianese linear ordering that is purely phono- logical, and show that the observed √-num-gen ordering, in fact, does not require a reordering of the corresponding syntactic heads, and can be neatly derived by refining the phonological representation of the relevant markers. This refinement is obtained by employing the formal tools provided by Strict …

records.title: Using Collostructional Analysis to evaluate BERT’s representation of linguistic constructions
records.abstract: Collostructional analysis is a technique devised to find correlations between particular words and linguistic constructions in order to analyse meaning associations of these constructions. Contrasting collostructional analysis results with output from BERT might provide insights into the way BERT represents the meaning of linguistic constructions. This study tests to what extent English BERT’s meaning representations correspond to known constructions from the linguistics literature by means of two tasks that we propose. Firstly, by predicting the words that can be used in open slots of constructions, the meaning associations of more lexicalized constructions can be observed. Secondly, by …

records.title: What Does 怀疑 (huaiyi) Mean? An Investigation into the Semantics of the Dubitative Verb in Mandarin Chinese
records.abstract: This thesis attempts to investigate the semantics of the dubitative verb 怀疑(huaiyi) in Mandarin Chinese. Dubitative verbs have always been an interesting topic in the field of syntax and semantics cross-linguistically because of their debatable denotations and peculiar complementation patterns. 怀疑(huaiyi) is yet more complicated due to its ambiguity between two empirical interpretations—the first is "having a tendency not to believe" (huaiyi1), and the second one is "having a tendency to believe" (huaiyi2). Therefore, there is an additional disambiguation mechanism at work in the process of its interpretation. This thesis claims that this disambiguation mechanism is based on the information …

records.title: Prompting instruction-tuned LLMs for semantic similarity values
records.abstract: The impressive few-shot performance of generative decoder transformer language models at novel tasks has raised interest in using them to estimate lexical-semantic properties of words, word pairs or multi-word expressions. We explore the task of eliciting semantic similarity scores between word pairs through prompting, comparing these scores to human benchmarks. We investigate different prompting approaches, different model architectures and different languages using the Dutch, English and Mandarin Chinese SimLex-999 benchmarks. The results show that prompting each word pair individually yields better correlations, and that models struggle with the distinction between similarity and …

records.title: Analogical Extension from Irregular Paradigms in Iranian Armenian: A Case of "Elsewhere Reversal"
records.abstract: The verbal paradigm of Iranian Armenian has undergone a striking case of analogical extension, separating it from conservative varieties of Eastern Armenian. The past perfective pattern that was historically restricted to an irregular subset of one class of verbs has spread to become the default pattern in the language, while the former default is now restricted to a small class. Since what could be described as the default or elsewhere condition in conservative Eastern Armenian has apparently swapped roles with an irregular pattern, we dub this change an “Elsewhere Reversal.” We combine a theoretical analysis with a survey of Armenian dialects and a quantitative model of child language …

records.title: Root-and-Pattern Morphology and Initial Consonant Mutation: Are They Really Two Different Phenomena?
records.abstract: Through the examination and analysis of Irish verbal Eclipsis, I propose a novel representation of the structure of the autosegment responsible for the phonological alternations associated with Eclipsis. I also provide the specific morphosyntactic function of Eclipsis by creating a dedicated Vocabulary Item (VI) that maps finiteness features onto the autosegment responsible for Eclipsis alternations. As for Moroccan Arabic, I argue that the exponent of the causative morpheme is a prefixed mora. Second-consonant gemination, then, falls out from language-general phonotactic requirements on Moroccan Arabic syllable structure. This analysis demonstrates that Moroccan Arabic Root-and-Pattern …

records.title: Focus Ineffability Effects Follow from Conditions on Question Answering
records.abstract: We examine an ineffability puzzle first identified by Schwarzschild (1993), in which a question containing a focus-sensitive operator cannot be felicitously answered, regardless of focus assignment. Previous accounts attribute the problem to a ban on crossing dependencies between focus operators and their associates; we instead derive it from the interaction between semantic content and general pragmatic considerations. We analyze ineffability within a question-based approach, according to which focus in an assertion corresponds to the implicit question it addresses. In ineffability examples, the same focus-sensitive operator occurs in every member of the implicit question denotation. As a …

records.title: The emergence of “weak” definite articles
records.abstract: This paper investigates the emergence and distribution of weak definite articles in German prepositional phrases (e.g. vom) at the expense of strong articles (e.g. von dem). While reduced weak forms are already attested in Old High German, their use was initially rare and largely restricted to noun phrases that are very likely to have a singleton extension in any situation. Over time, weak articles expanded to a wider range of noun phrases, yet failed to extend to anaphoric environments with an indefinite antecedent, where strong forms remain obligatory in Modern German. By combining historical corpus evidence with agent-based simulations grounded in computational pragmatics and …

records.title: Resurrections and insurrections in the neurobiology of language
records.abstract: The dominant models of how human language is neurally implemented have been slowly disintegrating for many years now, but the challenge of assembling a more modern take on this ancient question can only be feasibly undertaken by someone willing to wade through an increasingly dense literature. This someone should ideally also be involved in contemporary experimental neurolinguistics and psycholinguistics. It is with a unique sense of historical context, and contemporary clinical urgency, that Gregory Hickok assumes this task of proposing an updated view of human language processing. His book Wired for Words surveys the field of the neurobiology of language and offers a unique model.

records.title: Rethinking Linguistic Feedback: A Modality-Agnostic and Holistic Approach to Multimodal Addressee Signals in Spoken and Signed Dyadic Interaction
records.abstract: In this paper, we investigate multimodal recipient feedback in casual dyadic conversation in four languages: German Sign Language, Russian Sign Language, spoken German, and spoken Russian. Taking a modality-agnostic and holistic approach, we investigate the composition of conversational feedback from different multimodal signals, comparing sign and spoken languages without prioritizing any of the articulators or modalities. We find that in sign and spoken languages alike, feedback events include non-manual signals such as head movements or facial expressions in 85% or more of the instances. Across modalities, all four languages show only small percentages of feedback events without any …

records.title: Generating language and decoding brains
records.abstract: Can we read other people’s minds by seeing the neuroimaging data of their brains? Recent discussion claims success, but success is self-reinforced by design. More data and better statistics yield a better approximation to a mass of unanalyzed data. But approximation of language production is essentially different from explanation of language generation. Causal explanations of generative grammar may be confirmed by some statistical experiment; in contrast, a statistical result must still be causally explained before some theoretical understanding can be reached. Probability theory is incapable in principle of advancing scientific understanding beyond a measure of prediction based on …

records.title: Language and Brain-to-Brain (B2B) Communication
records.abstract: We review the first proof-of-principle demonstration for successful non-invasive brain-to-brain communication of conscious thought without the use of input-output systems of articulation and auditory perception of speech. In its present stage, the proof is overstated. First, the communication transmitted is not structured thought but a consciously perceived digital code. Second, communication is transmitted with the use of extralinguistic input-output mechanisms of motor and occipital cortices. It may be an innovative and potentially useful technological development but it is without explanatory significance for the study of language in the brain.

records.title: The Syntax of Clausal Prefixes in Tigrinya
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates the syntax of clausal prefixes in Tigrinya, an Ethio-Semitic language which, despite its head-finality, exhibits clause-initial complementizers that attach as prefixes to embedded verbs (clausal prefixes). It challenges the view that prefixes in head-final languages have an intrinsic morphological property, proposing instead that their surface position results from specific syntactic constraints. Four main clausal prefixes are analyzed. Z(ɨ)-, found in relative clauses, noun clausal complements, and comparative clauses, is argued to be a reflex of successive-cyclic A'-movement triggered by Spec-Head agreement in a phasal aspectual projection. Kɛmz(ɨ)-, a …

records.title: Understanding Compositional Meaning in Biology
records.abstract: Recent publications in biology enthusiastically argue that primate vocal call systems possess non-trivial compositionality as their prominent feature, thus parallelling human language. No proposal for an internal computational system explaining this property has been offered so far. However, conceptual and quantitative analysis shows the use of non-human primate compositional meaning to be neither productive nor rule based. Furthermore, formal properties of (higher-order) Markov chains imply only string concatenation, explaining why hierarchical structure, hence structure dependence, is absent from animal call systems. Also, mere acoustic identity of constituent elements with unit calls …

records.title: Magnetic Grammar. A bugfix
records.abstract: In D’Alessandro & Van Oostendorp (2020), we proposed Magnetic Grammar, a model of phonological competence in which a language’s segment inventory is characterised entirely by features that attract or reject other features within a segment. The paper referred to a Python implementation demonstrating the learning algorithm. This squib reports on a bug in that implementation and presents a corrected version, which leads to a small but theoretically meaningful refinement of the learning algorithm. The corrected implementation, with Jupyter notebook in which one can learn about and test the updated theory, is available as an open-source repository at https://github.com/fonolog/MagneticGrammar.

records.title: Constraining Alternatives in Turkish Polar Questions
records.abstract: Focus alternatives may be computed as semantic objects (Rooth 1985, 1992) or as syntactic objects (e.g. Fox & Katzir 2011). We provide evidence that syntax plays a role based on polar questions in Turkish. There is morphological evidence that the Hamblin set for the polar question is formed via focus alternatives (e.g. Atlamaz 2023). Computing alternatives as semantic objects would over-generate answers in the Hamblin set. On the other hand, the target Hamblin set can be naturally predicted in the syntactic approach, provided that alternatives involve replacing the focus with constituents of the same syntactic category.

records.title: Towards a theory of scope rigidity: A case of focus sensitive question particles
records.abstract: Turkish polar questions contain a focus-sensitive clitic =mI. When =mI attaches to a DP and the clause is embedded, we observe that the matrix clause can be read as either declarative or interrogative. We argue that the reading depends on the height of the focus relative to the embedded C. To derive the matrix question reading, the focused DP covertly moves above C. Turkish is often described as scope rigid, indicating that scope shifting covert movement is generally unavailable. If our analysis is correct, covert movement is still licit in certain environments.

records.title: On aspectual coercion in "before"/"after"-clauses: Evidence from processing
records.abstract: Certain "before"-clauses and "after"-clauses are prima facie ambiguous between a strong reading and a weak reading, and theories diverge on how the readings obtain. Some theories take the LF of "before"- and "after"-clauses to be unambiguously weak, with the strong reading falling out as a subcase (as it entails the weak reading). Other theories, such as Rett (2020), take the LFs for the two readings to be distinct, critically, with the weak reading being the result of a coercion process. Under standard psycholinguistic assumptions, coercion incurs a processing cost, and hence, we argue, Rett’s (2020) theory makes processing predictions that are not shared by theories which posit …

records.title: On Externalization (talk handout)
records.abstract: To say that linear order is part of core syntax is to say that temporal order is part of core syntax. Conversely, to say that linear order is not at all part of core syntax is to say that temporal order is not at all part of core syntax. Which is in turn to say that the language faculty has not integrated into its core any notion of time. Such a(n arguably counter-biological) position, or close to it, was in effect taken by Chomsky (1995, 221), who said “If humans could communicate by telepathy, there would be no need for a phonological component, at least for the purposes of communication.” The question for future work (not limited to linguistics) is whether or not the human brain has or …

records.title: Optimal Paradigms: A challenge from Judeo-Tripolitanian Arabic
records.abstract: This paper reevaluates Optimal Paradigms (OP), an extension to Optimality Theory proposed by McCarthy (2005). In OP, candidates are full inflectional paradigms and faithfulness constraints can require uniformity between all members within a paradigm. McCarthy (2005) proposed that OP can replace the assumption that prosodic templates are grammatical entities and other phonological mechanisms, which he regards as stipulations. One of the case studies used in McCarthy (2005) to showcase OP comes from Moroccan Arabic, where a noun-verb asymmetry in the distribution of schwa is claimed to be predicted by paradigmatic constraints as a means to achieve uniformity within an inflectional paradigm. …

records.title: The Tense-Mood-Aspect System of Makista
records.abstract: Makista, the Macao Portuguese Creole, is an understudied endangered language. This essay explores the Tense-Mood-Aspect(TMA) system of Makista by considering the grammatical and semantic properties of the three overt TMA markers: já, lôgo and ta. Examples are collected from José dos Santos Ferreiro's poems and existing scholarly literature by Pinharanda-Nunes. Results reveal that já is a past marker in tense, and a perfective marker in aspect; lôgo is a future marker in tense, and an irrealis marker in mood; ta is a non-punctual marker in aspect. The study provides empirical evidence for the research of Ibero-Romancebased creoles, and contributes to the field of creole study.

records.title: Nandao-Qs: When surprise sparks inquiry
records.abstract: This paper investigates the semantics and pragmatics of nandao questions (nandao-Qs) in Mandarin, focusing on their evidential properties. While previous studies have treated nandao as a biased question word or a rhetorical device (Alleton 1988, Gong 1995, Xu 2012, 2017), this paper argues that nandao-Qs encode evidential signals and reflect the speaker's confrontation with unexpected contextual evidence. Drawing on insights from the Kernel-based framework from Von Fintel & Gillies (2010), this paper demonstrates that nandao-Qs marks an incompatible Kernel, representing an "epistemic" conflict that arises from either disbelief or a deviation from grammatical priors. Additionally, I explore …

records.title: Does AI stop optional-stopping?
records.abstract: This is a fifth experiment of my general research program, which empirically explores how current generative AI systems behave with respect to research ethics. This time, I addressed the question of whether and how three major AI systems (ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini) respond a request for optional stopping. Given a series of data, do the AIs keep running a statistical test until it finds significance? I observed three types of behaviors: outright denial, execution with ethical warnings and execution without warnings. Out of ten trials, Claude denied four times and executed without warnings six times; ChatGPT denied once and executed with warnings nine times; Gemini executed all ten times, …

records.title: Approaches to Experimental Methodologies to Study Stigmatized Languages: The Case of Ecuadorian Andean Spanish
records.abstract: The difficulty of obtaining quantitative evidence under controlled experimental conditions is exponentially increased when the language under study is highly stigmatized, and its speakers are aware of its stigma. In this paper, we describe the difficulties encountered in designing experimental tasks to study focus-marking strategies in Ecuadorian Andean Spanish (EAS). EAS is an emblem of the indigenous people of Ecuador and is frequently associated with an ideal rural, poor, uneducated, indigenous speaker. EAS differs from Ecuadorian Spanish (the standard spoken by the non-indigenous majority in Ecuador) in the level of influence of Kichwa, the Quechua language of Ecuador. We use EAS as a …

records.title: Subject to change: Agreement and case
records.abstract: In contemporary colloquial Hebrew, unaccusative verbs may fail to exhibit ϕ-agreement with their subject when the latter appears postverbally, but not when it appears preverbally. To resolve disagreements regarding the role that intervention may play in licensing this lack of agreement, we conducted two acceptability judgment experiments, whose design and results we report. The findings indicate that intervention is not the factor licensing lack of agreement, contra Preminger’s (2009, 2014) claim, which means the phenomenon does not corroborate his approach to grammaticality. Further, we provide evidence that this lack of ϕ-agreement with a postverbal internal subject results from the …

records.title: The possession marking in permic languages especially Udmurt (german)
records.abstract: This paper examines the intricate ways in which the uralic languages of the Komi and Umdurt Rebuplic as well as the Perm Okrug of Russia concern with possession.

records.title: Nominal placeholders in Southern Cone Spanish: an explorative discussion on Rioplatense 'coso' and Chilean 'este/esta'
records.abstract: This paper examines the grammatical behavior of two nominal placeholders in Latin American Spanish: "coso" in Rioplatense Spanish and "este/esta" in Chilean Spanish. These expressions function as substitutes for nouns that are forgotten or deliberately left unmentioned. Drawing on novel data, I show that both elements systematically give rise to interpretations involving epistemic specificity, a property that distinguishes them from general nouns such as "cosa" ‘thing’. At the same time, they differ with respect to a number of morphosyntactic properties. To account for these contrasts, I propose an analysis according to which "coso" is a noun that incorporates into a specificity projection …

records.title: English kinship terms: From taboo to syntax
records.abstract: English-speaking children rarely address parents by first name – a social prohibition encoding power and solidarity. Separately, English kinship terms like Mom and Dad permit bare singular use (Mom called) where other count nouns don't (*Neighbour called}, in ordinary conversation). While previous work approaches this interface (Downing, 1996), the specific link between the naming taboo and the syntactic outcome – determinerless argumental structure – remains unexplored. I argue that the naming taboo causes the proper-noun-like syntax: high-frequency use of kinship terms in vocative function – forced by the prohibition on first names – produces grammaticalization toward strong proper-name …

records.title: Folk etymology and the diachronic survival of Latin loanwords in Greek
records.abstract: This article attempts to examine the linguistic phenomenon of folk etymology and to ascertain its contribution to the probable initial introduction and later survival of Latin loans in Standard Modern Greek. Specifically, it emerges that from a corpus of approximately 200 surviving Latin words, there is a recorded paretymological connection with Greek morphemes in a percentage of around 10% (c.a. 20 words). The linguistic data are drawn from the electronic corpus of TLG texts and mostly concern medieval dictionaries, such as the Etymologicum Magnum, the Suda Dictionary, etc. The possibility that this etymological association is not carried out by most speakers but constitutes a conscious …

records.title: Subject islands do not reduce to construction-specific discourse function
records.abstract: A central question about our shared capacity for language is how it is integrated with other cognitive systems. One important debate focuses on the extent to which the form of linguistic expressions is grounded in their communicative function: Can all constraints on linguistic form be attributed to the way constructions package information, or is linguistic form autonomous of meaning and function? One area of disagreement involves islands: phrases which block the formation of long-distance filler-gap dependencies (Ross, 1967). Grammatical subjects are considered islands, since questioning a sub-part of a subject results in an ill-formed sentence, e.g., “Which topic did the article about …

records.title: Heuristic and Post Festum Analogies as linguistic Sites of Epistemic negotiation in a Multilingual classroom
records.abstract: This case study investigates how analogical reasoning in a multilingual Indian classroom reflects broader cultural, linguistic and epistemic dynamics. It focuses on the discrepancy between heuristic analogies generated by students and post festum analogies introduced by instructors. It employs the framework of cognitive grammar to examine how linguistic structures at different levels of organization facilitate or hinder the development of alternative conceptions during instruction. A qualitative research design was adopted which drew audio recorded classroom discourse and post-instructional interviews to capture the learners post hoc reasoning. Narrow transcription and discourse analysis …

records.title: Analyzing discrepancy between post-festum and heuristic analogy in a real time pedagogical context
records.abstract: This study explores how analogical reasoning in a multilingual Indian classroom reflects broader cultural linguistic and epistemic dynamics. It draws discourse in the classroom and post instructional interviews to highlight the contrast between heuristic analogies generated by students with post festum analogies introduced by instructors. Using a cultural-linguistic lens, the analysis examines how language ideologies form conceptual misalignments and therefore shape the learners access to canonical scientific knowledge. This study situates analogy not merely as a cognitive tool but a site of epistemic negotiation- where the prior experiences of the student, linguistic repertoires and …

records.title: Analyzing the Mapping between Non-analogous Structured Inventories using Cognitive Grammar Framework
records.abstract: This paper analyzes the mapping between two types of categories belonging to distinct structured inventories related within a single conception in a text; to demonstrate that mapping between two types of structured inventory does not occur between cognitively analogous structures. The relational architecture of one system affects the characteristics of the mapping asymmetrically. This paper maps interactions of scope with respect to linking structures at three schematic levels relative to the schematic levels of the decimal system through cognitive grammar (Langacker, 1987, 1990, 2006) analysis of the text Tractatus Logico-philosophicus (Wittgenstein, Pears & McGuiness (Trans.), 1921/ 2002) …

records.title: A-dependencies and the parametrization of raising constructions
records.abstract: In the first part of my paper, I render the notions of argument raising and A-dependencies and show that case licensing in the upper clause is neither a necessary precondition of raising nor its universal trigger. There are languages with raising constructions, where case is licensed in the complement clause. Hyperraising, i.e. raising out of embedded complement clauses is widespread outside the languages of the Standard Average European type and is attested in some European languages including Bulgarian. In the second part of the paper, I offer a parametrization of six European languages with raising constructions and show that these languages are not uniform: some of them including …

records.title: Modularity, cyclicity, and constrained nonuniformity in Spanish stress assignment
records.abstract: We develop a stratal analysis of Spanish stress in which morphosyntactic conditioning and metrical nonuniformity are tightly constrained. Morphosyntactic conditioning is limited to cyclicity, the distinction between stems and affixes, and the affiliation of affixes to the stem or word level. Nonuniformity arises from lexical prespecification and interstratal constraint reranking. This framework yields several successful empirical predictions: Richness of the Base requires that prespecification be unpredictably distributed across all morph types; Chung’s Generalization demands identical metrical patterns in mono- and polycyclic stem-level constructions; and the Monomorpheme Generalization …

records.title: A Review of AI-Based Multilingual Speechto- Speech Systems for Media Dubbing and Voice Cloning
records.abstract: The creation, delivery, and user customization of audio-visual content have changed as a result of recent advancements in speech and language technologies. Enhancing accessibility, naturalness, and user engagement is the main goal of applications like parameter-efficient text-to-speech (TTS) adaptation, emotion-aware audiobook narration, automatic video subtitling, and multilingual voice cloning. Four representative research works that address basic issues in modern speech processing systems are compared in this review paper. To increase subtitle accuracy, multilingual speech synthesis, emotional expressiveness, and computational efficiency, the chosen studies make use of a variety of …

records.title: Overgeneralization of (Anti)causativization in L2 English Acquisition: Learners’ Acceptability Judgments of Overanticausativized Transitive/Causative Verbs
records.abstract: This thesis investigates the overgeneralization of the causative alternation in second language (L2) English, with particular focus on over(anti)causativization errors, whereby non-alternating transitive or causative verbs are accepted in ungrammatical (anti)causative constructions. While previous research has extensively documented overcausativization errors involving unaccusative verbs (e.g., *The magician disappeared the rabbit), comparatively little attention has been paid to learners’ acceptance of non-target anticausative uses such as *The picture painted. Building on the manner/result distinction proposed in lexical semantic theory, this study advances a manner/result …

records.title: Clitic placement and the Anti-V2 effect in European Portuguese:  insights from uninflected verbs
records.abstract: Clitic placement with European Portuguese uninflected verbs is problematic for prosodic analyses. While ‘proclisis triggers’ give rise to obligatory proclisis with inflected verbs, they often lead to optional proclisis/enclisis with uninflected verbs (Raposo & Uriagereka 2008), except for aspectual/quantificational adverbials with head-like behaviour (Martins 2013a). These patterns provide support for a syntactic ‘Anti-V2 requirement’ account, whereby clitics usually raise to adjoin to T and either (a) an XP raises to/through spec FinP and the verb stays in Asp (resulting in proclisis) or (b) the verb raises to Fin (resulting in enclisis), but not both (building on Fernández-Rubiera 2009, …

records.title: A Constraint-Based Probe for Exploring Phonological Sound-Space Without Decipherment
records.abstract: This note describes an auxiliary, exploratory extension to a previously proposed phonological plausibility framework for evaluating unknown or ambiguous symbol strings. The extension introduces a phonological probe that generates broad sound-category constraints for structurally plausible symbol strings, while explicitly preventing phoneme assignment, lexical identification, or semantic interpretation. The probe operates by conditioning sound-category generation on phonological profiles, enforcing conservative phonotactic filters, and applying entropy-based failure detection to prevent overfitting. The method is falsification-oriented: its primary function is to rule out unsafe or …

records.title: Modelling the Morphology of Verbal Paradigms: A Case Study in the Tokenization of Turkish and Hebrew
records.abstract: We investigate how transformer models represent complex verb paradigms in Turkish and Modern Hebrew, concentrating on how tokenization strategies shape this ability. Using the Blackbird Language Matrices task on natural data, we show that for Turkish --with its transparent morphological markers-- both monolingual and multilingual models succeed, either when tokenization is atomic or when it breaks words into small subword units. For Hebrew, instead, monolingual and multilingual models diverge. A multilingual model using character-level tokenization fails to capture the language non-concatenative morphology, but a monolingual model with morpheme-aware segmentation performs well. Performance …

records.title: On explanatory theories of speech categorization
records.abstract: The study of speech categorization has a long history. Two phenomenological laws of speech categorization are statable based on this extensive history: monotonicity and sigmoidality of the identification/categorization functions. While prior work has heavily focussed on accounting of observed data in terms of specific theories, and computationally modelling observed patterns, far less work has been done on formally comparing theories to study their explanatory potential, particularly their explanatory value with respect to the two laws. Taking up the latter challenge, in this paper, I formally compare four theories (or frameworks) that have been popular in the literature: (a) Categorical …

records.title: Finding objects of experiences
records.abstract: This paper develops a semantics of experiential objects, i.e., satisfiable objects associated with experiential episodes that carry satisfaction/accuracy conditions, and uses it to analyze English find with small-clause complements. I propose that find uniformly introduces an experiential object, and that the embedded predication compositionally specifies the satisfaction conditions of that object within an object-based truthmaker semantics. The account aims to give a unified analysis for the two senses associated with find, namely, the object-encounter reading (John found the door open) and the evaluative reading (John found the cake tasty), without positing two unrelated lexical items or …

records.title: Topics in the Syntax of Tigrinya
records.abstract: This chapter offers a selective, analytically oriented investigation of key aspects of Tigrinya syntax. Rather than providing a comprehensive grammatical description, it focuses on phenomena that are particularly informative for both descriptive and theoretical study. Combining general overviews with targeted phenomena, the chapter examines properties of the nominal, verbal, and clausal domains. These include double determination, object marking, prepositions, verb raising, clause types, information structure, and negation. Through these analyses the chapter aims to clarify central patterns in Tigrinya syntax, and to situate the language within broader investigations in syntactic theory, …

records.title: Negation in Albanian: n-words
records.abstract: This article analyzes negative indefinites (n-words) in Albanian. These items include a prefixed element and an indefinite, and obligatorily require the occurrence of the negative marker, NM. Complementarily, the indefinite element can occur alone in negative contexts. This distribution, specifically the types of negative doubling, is explained by assuming that the negative operator is not realized by a lexical constituent within the syntactic structure. The idea is that negation is postulated and made available to interpretation by the presence of NM and n-words. The Chomskyan notion of I-Merge and the lexical properties of n-words provide the crucial syntactic tools to connect doubling …

records.title: Particle-Origin Primitives A ULD/UNS Confinement-Geometry Account of Free Modifiers and Indo-European Bound
records.abstract: This article develops a single internal claim that recurs across the Morphodynamics program: the primitive inventory that drives grammatical evolution is particle-stratified. Free or weakly bound discourse / clausal modifiers and certain “primitive” bound exponents (illustrated by IndoEuropean suffixal atoms such as -s, -t, and -m̥ ) are not clausal or syntactic primitives. They are particle-origin elements whose apparent clausal behavior emerges from confinement geometry. The analysis is written entirely in the native morphodynamic formalism: a ghost-slot (“well”) is a directed confinement geometry with (i) a state inventory V, (ii) a licensed transition set E, (iii) depth/weight w, and …

records.title: Let me find and exclude outliers for you: when an AI system crosses the red line
records.abstract: This is a continuation of my recent research examining whether the naive use of the current AI systems can lead to research misconduct. Building on the previous observation that current AI systems can offer ways to engage in selective reporting (Kawahara 2026f) and p-hacking (Kawahara 2026d), I examined whether the three major AI systems (ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini) would find and exclude outliers after seeing the results of a non-significant t-test---a clear form of post-hoc data manipulation that constitutes research misconduct under standard definitions. When asked to “remove outliers to achieve statistical significance” with a very direct prompt, the three systems behaved differently. …

records.title: On focus and the perfect aspect
records.abstract: This paper introduces two novel empirical observations about sentences containing narrow focus on the perfect participle (e.g., "Esme has [BEEN]F married"). First, we show that these sentences are examples of universal perfects, which entail that the eventuality described by the VP holds at the reference time. Broad-focused versions of the same sentences, on the other hand, only give rise to experiential readings. This observation is not accounted for by prior accounts of the perfect, which predict that universal readings only arise in the presence of certain overt adverbials (Iatridou et al., 2001; Portner, 2003). Second, we observe that perfect sentences with focused participles imply …

records.title: When grammar-internal factors hinder an OV-to-VO shift: the case of Surgut Khanty
records.abstract: Language contact is often argued to lead to word order change – e.g., the OV-to-VO shift. Though the exact mechanism of change is poorly under- stood, instances of lack of this change, despite the favourable conditions being present (intense contact, dominant bilingualism with a majority VO language, etc.) are worth investigating. In this paper, we present novel data from Surgut Khanty (Ob-Ugric, Uralic) and show how language-internal factors pertaining to information structure (IS) – fusion of grammatical roles and IS-properties, and IS-restrictions on the postverbal domain – govern the distribution of postverbal constituents (PVCs) in an otherwise rather strictly verb-final language. We …

records.title: Revisiting locality: Two case studies from Italian
records.abstract: In the generative tradition, the conditions on subextraction (i.e., the extraction from a phrase XP) have been captured by either one of the following incompatible formulations: (i) a formulation based on the notion of phase (the PIC, i.e., the Phase Impenetrability Condition); (ii) a formulation based on the notion of selection and on the configuration in which XP occurs (the subjacency condition). We provide two empirical case studies, both focused on Italian, to test the predictions of formulations (i)-(ii): inverse copular sentences and the complement of quality. Our main finding is that subextraction is naturally accounted for by the subjacency condition, not by the PIC. In this way, …

records.title: The Morphodynamics of Y as a Ghost Connector Relational Phonology and Directed Vowel Trajectories
records.abstract: This article argues that Y is neither a vowel, nor a glide, nor an energy conduit. Y is instead a ghost connector: a silent predicator and directional operator that assigns transitions between vowel states within a universal vowel well. Under this reconceptualization, English “diphthongs” are not vowel blends and not vowel+glide sequences. Their nucleus is a single trajectory object—a predicated transition—generated by an operator of the form Y(v₁ , v₂ ) and not representable as a static feature bundle. In CVC structures, Y never fills the V-slot; the trajectory fills it. The account also rejects an empty-nucleus analysis and does not treat Y as a governing/licensing head; instead, nucleus …

records.title: Morphophysics: A Field-Theoretic Synthesis of Morphological Evolution and Typological Universals
records.abstract: Morphophysics models morphological structure as a dynamical field in which grammatical categories, affix positions, and co-occurrence constraints emerge as attractors shaped by a shared geometry (curvature, boundaries, resonance minima) and universal forces (upward drift, downward anchoring, lateral expansion, and restorative coherence). In this article, we synthesize the theory presented across the source documents into a unified framework that connects (i) diachronic cyclicity (drift → turbulence → collapse → renewal → integration), (ii) typological universals as emergent properties of shared field geometry, and (iii) cross-system convergence and typological clustering as global outcomes …

records.title: A Phonological Plausibility Framework for Evaluating Unknown or Ambiguous Symbol Strings
records.abstract: This note proposes a neutral, falsification-oriented framework for evaluating how plausibly a given string of symbols could correspond to spoken language systems at the level of language families. Rather than attempting decipherment or semantic interpretation, the framework assesses phonological *compatibility*: the degree to which a symbol string can be accommodated by known phonological constraints with minimal distortion. The method is intended as an auxiliary tool for hypothesis testing in historical linguistics, undeciphered script studies, and comparative phonology.

records.title: A structurally uniform account of slur-based definites
records.abstract: We argue for a structurally uniform account of slur-based definites (SDs), focusing on the systematic ambiguity between descriptive and epithet readings of SDs in Brazilian Portuguese. We show that the interpretive and distributional contrasts between these readings – e.g., concerning misdescription tolerance, Principle C effects, binominal constructions, NP ellipsis – do not motivate structural ambiguity within the DP, contrary to recent proposals. Instead, we derive both readings from the interaction of two independently motivated ingredients: (i) an optional type-shifting operation triggered by a syntactic [ex +] feature on NPs, which transfers descriptive content from the …

records.title: THE CO-UTTERANCE HYPOTHESIS. AN ACCOUNT OF SIMULTANEITY IN SIGN LANGUAGES
records.abstract: In sign languages, different articulators (i.e., the two hands) can represent different characters involved in the same action. As skilled bimodal bilinguals can simultaneously utter a sentence in a sign language and in a spoken language, the simultaneous production of two sentences is cognitively possible. Since in sign languages multiple articulators work with some degree of autonomy, we propose that it is possible to co-utter two or more coordinated clausal units internal to the same sign language if they convey different aspects of the same complex conceptual message. Not only can two propositional units be co-uttered, but also two constituents internal to the same sentence can be. This …

records.title: When A-bar movement cannot cross CPs: A feature-based account of improper movement
records.abstract: The Williams Cycle, which is based on the longstanding idea of the ban on improper movement, encounters a non-trivial problem when we consider the fact that long-distance movement proceeds through clause-internal intermediate positions. This paper makes progress in solving this problem by investigating a sharp locality asymmetry in the Mandarin lian...dou construction: movement to a TP-internal position is clause-bounded (it can span TPs but not CPs), while movement to a TP-external position can cross CP boundaries. Crucially, the “blocked” TP-internal position is still required as an intermediate step in long-distance movement that terminates at the TP-external position. To explain this, I …

records.title: Is there reference to abstract objects in natural language?
records.abstract: The nature and status of abstract objects have been at the center of metaphysical debate for a very long time and they form a topic that bears a particular connection to natural language. Philosophers frequently draw on natural language to motivate properties, numbers, and propositions as objects, and it is generally taken for granted that abstract objects of this sort are well-reflected in natural language and in fact that reference to them in natural language is pervasive. This paper will review and modify in a certain way the view I had advanced in Abstract Objects and the Semantics of Natural Language (OUP 2013). This is the view according to which reference to abstract objects in …

records.title: Absence of Relative Clause Islands in Adara
records.abstract: I argue that definite relative clauses, despite their stable strong island status cross-linguistically, lack island status in Adara. The structure is neither selective nor weak, but rather completely permeable, allowing the free extraction of both arguments and adjuncts. In support of the claim that A-bar movement may escape relative clause domains in Adara, I adduce evidence from crossover effects, reconstruction effects, and quantifier float. In addition, I show that relative clause-internal material may probe upwards and outwards, triggering long-distance agreement of relativized verbs with clause-external subjects in a way that is not possible with true island structures in the language.

records.title: `Pre' and `post' marking in Nanosyntax: the case of a prepositional dative in a dialectal Polish
records.abstract: The Podlasie dialect of Polish exhibits a curious nominal case declension paradigm where the dative is expressed by a preposition and a genitive suffix (prep N-gen), which constitutes a typologically rare pattern. Moreover, the instrumental in this dialect, which is hierarchically above the dative, is marked with only a suffix (N-ins), unexpectedly dropping the preposition. The fact that a hierarchically higher case drops a preposition challenges a generalization made in Caha (2009), which builds on Blake's (2001) hierarchy concerning the morphological marking of case. The paper explores how these two atypical patterns follow from the Nanosyntactic lexicalization procedure, offering an …

records.title: The Referential Shift of the Chinese “VP-de” Structures in Contrastive Contexts: A Sign-Based Construction Grammar Perspective
records.abstract: This paper aims to establish a unified grammatical mechanism for the referential shift of “VP-de” structures in Modern Chinese within the framework of Sign-based Construction Grammar. It addresses the long-standing disjunction in previous studies between the mechanisms of semantic role determination and contextual regulation in the realization of referential shift. The focus is on how the contrastive construction, as a contextual device, facilitates the referential shift of “VP-de.” The central arguments are as follows: (1) in all “VP-de” structures, the referential target is always a frame element within the relevant cognitive frame; (2) when “VP-de” refers to agents or patients, the …

records.title: Future/epistemic ambiguities as height-relativity: evidence from Gujarati
records.abstract: Epistemic claims and future claims often involve the same morpheme (Enç, 1996; Kush, 2015; Winans, 2016; Giannakidou and Mari, 2018). This paper argues that, in some languages, this is because apparent reference to future times is quantification over future worlds. This assimilates the epistemic/future parallel to variable-flavor modality. I introduce novel data from Gujarati (Indo-Aryan), which allows only epistemic readings of the morpheme -s- when it is placed on the auxiliary verb (hovu, ‘to be’), and only future readings when on main verbs. I provide a univocal analysis of the morpheme, where -s- contributes universal modal force, but the modal base (epistemic vs. metaphysical) is …

records.title: MORPHIX: Feature Geometry, Vocabulary Insertion, and the Particle Stratification of PIE Pronominal and Adverbial Morphology
records.abstract: The Morphix manuscript argue that PIE 'pronominal roots' form a distinct morphological species: closed-class, non-derivable, non-compounding, non-ablauting atoms originating in prePIE deictic particles. The model represents these atoms as feature-bundle realizations organized by a geometry whose primary nodes DEIXIS, ANAPH, and Q partition the functional space; optional INDEF and ALTERITY extend the system to indefinite and 'other' series. Vocabulary insertion under the Subset Principle selects the most specific exponent compatible with the syntactic feature bundle, generating syncretisms and blocking effects. Empirically, the manuscript compiles daughter-language reflex lists across major …

records.title: Nominalizing classifiers and the limits of dominance: A first look at A'ingae's syntactically blocked morphophonology
records.abstract: This paper presents and analyzes data from A'ingae (or Cofán, an Amazonian isolate, ISO 639-3: con), where the patterns of stress and glottalization in words with classifying nominalizers are sensitive to the base's morphological and syntactic structure. Normally, classifying suffixes override their base's stress and glottalization. However, the overriding is blocked if the base has previously undergone a functional projection spell-out. These A'ingae data show that information about the morphosyntax of the base (specifically, the distinction between functional and categorizing phase heads; e.g. Guekguezian, 2021; Newell, 2008) is accessible and can be referred to in the course of …

records.title: Participles, State Predicates, and Linking Verbs: A Two-Channel Anchor Semantics
records.abstract: . This paper develops an anchor-based account of English participle predication and linking-verb selection. The central empirical contrast is familiar but under-modeled: a participial predicate licensed under the copula (e.g., be + broken) typically carries stronger world-commitment than the same participle licensed under a perceptual or evidential anchor (look/seem/appear/sound/feel). We argue that this is not a syntactic accident and not reducible to lexical stipulation. Instead, anchors are analyzed as operators that stabilize a state description relative to an information channel (perceptual, inferential, reportative, affective), and the anchoring channel controls (i) commitment …

records.title: Categorial granularity in syntactic acquisition: A multilingual corpus study on the left periphery
records.abstract: The development of functional categories crosslinguistically is an extensively studied and debated topic (i.a., Radford 1990; Boser et al. 1992; Rizzi 1993; Guasti 1993; Clahsen et al. 1994; Friedmann et al. 2021; Heim & Wiltschko 2025). In this paper, I contribute to existing literature by exploring the explanatory potential in acquisition of a previously understudied formal notion – categorial granularity (following Biberauer & Roberts 2015; Song 2019; Biberauer 2019). I study the development of the left periphery with a multilingual corpus study on 10 children, across 5 languages. First, a novel contrast is observed: on the one hand, CP-structures emerge very early, favouring accounts …

records.title: De-idealizing the asterisk: Grammaticality as conditioned stability
records.abstract: The asterisk has done foundational work in theoretical linguistics, but it also hides a persistent conflation. The same diacritic is used (i) to mark strings that defeat structural analysis, (ii) to mark structurally viable utterances whose values don't stabilize under the constraints of an interpreted situation, (iii) to mark interpretable forms that still aren't in the community's repertoire, and (iv) to mark cases that are grammatically well-formed but feel unacceptable for reasons of processing or ideology. One sign, four diagnoses: crash, clash, exclusion, and unease. This article argues that the resulting competence–performance–usage triangulation hasn't resolved the impasse because …

records.title: Generalized non-de dicto:Underspecification and discourse stability
records.abstract: Embedding material under intensional operators gives rise to a variety of `non-de dicto' construals: the proposition seemingly expressed by the embedded clause does not describe subject’s the attitudinal state, yet the sentence can be judged true. This paper makes three contributions: First, we strengthen the claims by Mayr & Schmitt 2024 that non-de dicto construals are a uniform phenomenon, which does not involve dedicated syntactic structures or morphology: The distinction between de dicto and non-de dicto construals does not involve ambiguity but, and this is our second point, arises from properties of meaning per se. What can be described as `replacement' -- in non-de dicto construals …

records.title: R-Anchors and the Architecture of Argumenthood
records.abstract: This paper develops a minimal architectural reanalysis of argumenthood. It proposes that predicates project abstract dependency objects — 'R-anchors' — that encode the existence of argument-related dependencies independently of their overt realization and referential identification. Argumenthood emerges only when such dependencies are structurally completed by a single operation — 'Anchor-Checking'. On this view, omission, generic interpretation, and persistent ambiguity are licensed outcomes of grammatical structure rather than exceptional repairs.

records.title: P-hacking with one prompt
records.abstract: This brief note reports a mini-experiment, which tested whether major AI systems (Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT) readily perform p-hacking when requested through neutral statistical framing. A single prompt requesting “to find a statistically significant difference” from a given dataset—--which essentially amounts to a request to p-hack—--elicited multiple testing, HARKing, and selective reporting from all three AI systems without any cautionary warnings. Further, examination of the code revealed significant discrepancies between what was reported in the outputs and what was actually analyzed: all the AI systems conducted extensive multiple testing but selectively reported only significant …

records.title: Voicing in Czech children’s sibilants: children’s production and adults’ perception
keywords: sibilants; voicing; children; czech; production; perception
records.abstract: This study examines how Czech-speaking children mark voicing in sibilants and how adult listeners perceive these contrasts in children’s speech. Productions of /s, z, ʃ, ʒ/ by 31 children aged 3;5–6;5 show that voicing is cued by both duration and presence of f0: voiceless sibilants are longer and contain less voicing than voiced sibilants. Development is non-linear, with substantial variability, particularly for voiced targets. Consistency improves most clearly by age 6. Phonetic context affects both duration and presence of f0, indicating that productions depend on the elicitation material. Perception experiment involving 48 adults showed that speech-language therapists do not outperform …

records.title: Why English doesn't extract left branches (yet)
records.abstract: English resists separating pre-head dependents from the head of an NP: \textit{*Whose did you read book?} is sharply unacceptable. Rather than positing a universal constraint, this paper asks what English does instead; and measures it. The explanation has three strands: distributional (fused-head construals and workarounds like pied-piping and \textit{big mess} are frequent; configurations resembling left-branch extraction are absent), psycholinguistic (fused-head parsing commits listeners early, making reanalysis costly), and functional (the workaround family already does the semantic work that extraction would do). Corpus rates from Universal Dependencies confirm: workarounds are …

records.title: Tier‑ Nested Shell Composition for Nominal Operator Architecture A unified syntactic shell model integrating MGD, HTQA tier nesting, and RED/DED traversal
records.abstract: This chapter specifies a syntactic (functional) shell‑ composition architecture for the nominal phrase and aligns it with three programmatic components developed in the companion manuscripts: (i) Modifiability‑ Graph Diagnostics (MGD) for tier assignment, (ii) a ranked operator/quantifier architecture (HTQA tier nesting) for closure and traversal, and (iii) a bidirectional RED/DED traversal methodology for diagnosing packaging dependencies. The architectural commitment is deliberately minimal and strictly tier‑ based: Shell 1 hosts LOW primitives; Shell 2 hosts MIDDLE packaging/repair orbitals; Shell 3 hosts HIGH operator ranks; Shell 4 hosts connective bridges; Shell 5 hosts outer polarity …

records.title: Why clause structure is judged like tense and agreement: A coordination account of grammaticality
records.abstract: Grammaticality judgments are selective: speakers treat violations of agreement, clause structure, tense, or evidential marking as straightforward errors of "grammar", while treating accent shifts, many lexical substitutions, and register choices as matters of style or appropriateness. Why? This paper argues that the difference tracks what kind of work a linguistic contrast does. Some contrasts serve as shared infrastructure for public coordination: they configure what kind of move an utterance counts as, who is committed to what, and what responses are licensed. These contrasts (clause typing, argument linking, polarity, tense--aspect where grammaticalized) form closed paradigms whose …

records.title: Dissertation Chapter Modifiability Graph Diagnostics for Operator Architecture
records.abstract: This article formalizes a graph-theoretic diagnostic for nominal architecture. Within a fixed Level‑ k inventory of part-of-speech (POS) items or POS-classes, we build a directed modifiability graph whose edges encode attested direct head-modification under a strict criterion (head targeting, constituency, no category shift, and exclusion of phrase-level scope). Graph partitions—isolates, strongly connected components (SCCs), and stacking partial orders—are coupled to a three-tier architectural taxonomy: High (operators), Middle (repair/packaging mechanisms), and Low (argumental primitives such as reciprocals, nominal WH heads, and free relatives). We provide a closure-sensitivity feature …

Within a fixed Level‑ k inventory of part-of-speech (POS) items or POS-classes, we build a directed modifiability graph whose edges encode attested direct head-modification under a strict criterion (head targeting, constituency, no category shift, and exclusion of phrase-level scope). records.title: A novel argument for cyclicity from the (in)visibility of inﬁxes at morpheme junctures: Bottoms up!
records.abstract: This paper investigates what happens to grammatical relationships between two morphemes when an inﬁx incidentally lands between them. Most relationships—including allomorphic and morphophonological relationships—persist, showing that these relationships are established before the intrusion of the inﬁx. However, inﬁxes do disrupt word-level phonology, which thus must be established after the intrusion of the inﬁx. These ﬁndings furnish a novel argument for grammatical models that are (i) cyclic and bottom-up (or inside out) with respect to both exponence and certain (morpho)phonological operations, and (ii) noncyclic with respect to certain purely phonological processes, which are computed …

records.title: THE as a Closure Operator: D-Lock, Selector-Head Expressions, and Typed Coercion in Nominal Architecture
records.abstract: This paper advances an operator-centered account of definiteness in which the English definite article THE is a closure operator that maps an open nominal predicate to a discourse-resolved referential term. The clearest environment for closure is not ordinary common-noun definites, but Selector-Head Expressions (SHEs) such as the other, the next, the last, and the rest, where closure over a structured domain is obligatory. To make this operator thesis architecturally nontrivial, we introduce a Structured-Domain Closure Algebra (SDCA) in which closure is a partial operation parameterized by a domain signature (candidate set plus order/partition structure and salience). D-Lock is defined as …

records.title: Operators, Quantifiers, and NP-Internal Structure: An Expanded Cognitive and Cross-Linguistic Account of Nominal Architecture
records.abstract: This article develops and expands a cognitively grounded, cross-linguistic model of nominal phrase architecture that distinguishes three structural layers: (i) an NP-core containing conceptual content (nouns, modifiers, possessives, relational material, interrogative determiners, and prop-nouns such as English one), (ii) a quantifier layer comprising true quantifiers that denote cardinality, proportion, or amount and can satisfy NP-headedness and substitution diagnostics, and (iii) an operator layer comprising higher-order scope instructions—including every, each, and no—that take a domain argument but are predicted not to behave as quantifier heads. The preprint makes the diagnostics …

records.title: Integrated versus independent processing of auditory features in speech sounds
records.abstract: Two MMN experiments investigate integrated versus independent processing of complex auditory information in linguistic sound. We hypothesise that neurophsyiologically evoked responses to multiple distinctive cues are stronger than evoked responses to single cues. We developed a novel methodology combining a fixed-deviant design with roving standards, allowing direct comparison of multiple deviant contexts within a single session. We ran two magnetoencephalographic (MEG) protocols which are identical except for the order of presentation of standard and deviant stimuli. We compare the results of the novel fixed-deviant design to a more traditional design which uses a fixed standard stimulus …

records.title: On the Limits of Functionalism: A Reply to Bierl (2025)
records.abstract: Bernd Bierl eloquently proposes an ambitious synthesis towards biological linguistics. This synthesis aims to establish a new bio-ethological linguistics based on 4E cognition. It considers the foundational ethology of authors like Konrad Lorenz and Nikolaas Tinbergen to be its biological basis. Rather than developing the biolinguistics inspired by Noam Chomsky, which also has its roots in early 20th-century European ethology, the author considers it an inadequate naturalization and suggests subsuming it under a conception of language as behavior, within the context of embodied, embedded, enacted, and extended (4E) cognition. This reply presents some critical observations on this proposal, …

records.title: On the identity of -rare in Passives and Potentials in Japanese
records.abstract: Anti-Homophony (Kayne,2017,2025). It shows that the passive is a (sub)component of one type of potential (psv-potential) and examines promotion and demotion in passives and psv-potentials for different‘pseudopassives,’ i.e oblique passives. While goal, directional, and source obliques are possible in passives, locative and instrumental obliques are excluded. These are possible however in psv-potentials with an alethic possibility reading.
