Cinque 1999, 2004), as supported by aspectual …

records.title: Longer Words, Easier-to-pronounce Phonems: A Pilot Study
records.abstract: The study investigates the relationship between word length and phoneme sonority in six languages across diverse language families. Building on the principle of least effort and the Menzerath-Altmann law, the research is aimed to analyze the phoneme sonority using translated New Testament texts in Bilua, Bola, Czech, Gagauz, Jamamadi, and Tongan. The findings reveal that in languages with complex syllables, the tendency of longer words to contain shorter syllables—consistent with the Menzerath-Altmann law— results in a higher proportion of vowels, thereby increasing the mean phoneme sonority. In contrast, languages with simple syllable structures exhibit either a decrease in mean phoneme …

records.title: Selector-Head Expressions (SHEs) in English
records.abstract: English contains a small but systematic class of DP-internal expressions whose categorical status is not well captured by the standard labels «determiner», «adjective», «quantifier», or «noun». Canonical members include «the other» and «the rest», and— crucially for the present theory – their closest structural neighbors in the «indefinite ordinal» family such as «the next», «the last», «the former», «the latter», and «the following». We argue that these expressions instantiate a single, typed configuration: a «Selector-Head Expression (SHE)», i.e., a D-licensed selector constituent of the form «[D the] + [Sel X]» that introduces a discourse-anchored selection variable and therefore …

records.title: On the identity of *-rare* in Passives and Potentials in Japanese
records.abstract: This paper argues that Japanese passive and potential -rare instantiate a single morpheme, as required by Anti-Homophony (Kayne,2017,2025). It shows that the passive is a (sub)component of one type of potential (psv-potential) and examines promotion and demotion in passives and psv-potentials for different ‘pseudopassives,’ i.e oblique passives. While goal, directional, and source obliques are possible in passives, locative and instrumental obliques are excluded. These are possible however in psv-potentials with an alethic possibility reading. We motivate a fine-grained clausal structure in which passive Voice and potential constructions, consisting of passive -rare and silent modal flavor …

records.title: Theoretical, Empirical, and Computational Perspectives on Hungarian Discourse Configurationality
records.abstract: Hungarian employs complex, contextually-sensitive syntactic rules that place certain constituents in the pre-verbal positions of Focus and Topic. This thesis examines this property of Hungarian, known as discourse configurationality, by comparing native speakers’ grammaticality judgments of possible word orderings within a certain context to the probabilities language models assign in the same situations. After reviewing the discourse-semantic and syntactic aspects of Hungarian word order, I introduce a basic taxonomy of Hungarian focusing and topicalization rules based on foundational perspectives from generative linguistics, and construct a novel set of Hungarian scenarios testing all …

records.title: Animal Linguistics as an Integrative Framework for Animal Communication
records.abstract: Interest in animal communication has arguably reached an all-time high, with two very visible projects—the search for the animal roots of human language and the development of methods and technologies to decode animal signals. These projects need a shared, overarching scientific framework. We propose that animal linguistics offers one, which will require close collaboration between ethologists, linguists and, increasingly, AI specialists. One possible way to view the project—not the only one—goes as follows. With the same ambition as human formal linguistics, animal linguistics seeks to develop explicit models of animal communication ("formal animal linguistics"), to understand the extent …

records.title: The Spanish PYTA Morphome Dissolved
records.abstract: Many Romance languages exhibit a morphomic pattern dubbed PYTA (for {perfecto/ pretérito} y tiempos afines–see especially Maiden 2018, Ch 4). Spanish exhibits a striking instance of this phenomenon. No matter how irregular a Spanish verb is otherwise, it always has the same stem for both imperfect subjunctive paradigms and for the future subjunctive (which is defunct in the modern spoken language, but was in active use a few centuries ago), and this stem can be unerringly arrived at by taking the 3rd person plural preterite indicative form and subtracting the sequence -ron. This generalization is exceptionless, but it is not directly formulable in a piece-based view of morphology. For this …

records.title: [uF]2Vec: Why Uninterpretable Features Lack CI-Projection
records.abstract: The deletion or invisibility of uninterpretable features at the Conceptual-Intentional (CI) interface is usually treated as stipulative. This Brief argues instead that these effects follow naturally from CI’s vector-space architecture. Features are represented geometrically: interpretability corresponds to projection onto a CI-Potent Space, while uninterpretable features, transformed by non-linear feature checking, collapse into a Null Space and make no interpretive contribution. Form Copy, by contrast, preserves only linearly recoverable features and maps them onto the Potent Space. Modelling AGREE as an inter-dimensional mapping, the CI-Filter reduces to Null Space projection, unifying …

records.title: When AI’s helpfulness becomes harmful II: A current AI system recommends cherry-picking and HARKing
records.abstract: This study examines whether Gemini, an AI research assistant system that is widely used among college students, recommends ethically questionable statistical practices when analyzing experimental data. I presented Gemini with mock data designed to test for “cherry-picking”—--selectively reporting results from a subset of the data that supports a hypothesis. When the full dataset showed no significant difference but a subset did, Gemini recommended reporting only the subset analysis and suggested post-hoc hypothesis changes (i.e. HARKing). The results underscore the need for stronger ethical guardrails in AI systems and explicit instruction in research ethics for students using AI tools as …

records.title: Gradient Conventionalization: A Unified Framework for Lexical Semantics and Social Epistemology
records.abstract: This paper proposes a unified framework that reconceives the relationship between lexical meaning and world knowledge as a gradient of conventionalization rather than a categorical distinction. Meaning components are distinguished by their level of conventionalization, operationalized as degree of speaker agreement, rather than by membership in "lexical" versus "encyclopedic" categories. The framework introduces a five-level gradient — reference, denotation, sense, cultural connotation, private connotation — corresponding to decreasing intersubjective agreement, and a typology of entailments (strong, default, weak) correlated with these levels. This reconceptualization clarifies semantic …

records.title: La privación lingüística en la infancia y en la adolescencia sordas y sordociegas (book review)
records.abstract: Los lectores de ELA encontrarán en el reciente estudio sobre la sordera un resumen actualizado de una controversia en el ámbito de la adquisición del lenguaje y la enseñanza de lenguas que también suscita cuestiones teóricas de amplia repercusión. Son dos campos de trabajo y reflexión que se unen alrededor de una polémica sin precedentes o comparación en la Lingüística Aplicada. Al mismo tiempo, muchos se preguntarán acerca del primero (del ámbito aplicado): ¿por qué una editorial académica publica un libro que presenta, otra vez, evidencia y argumentos sobre un problema científico, al parecer, ya resuelto a finales del siglo pasado? La lectura detallada de los dieciocho capítulos explicará …

records.title: Morphosyntactic and Referential Properties of Urdu Pronouns: A Preliminary Investigation
records.abstract: This squib examines the morphosyntactic classification and referential properties of pronouns in Urdu, focusing on personal pronouns, reflexives, and reciprocals. It investigates how these elements interact with Classical Binding Theory (Chomsky 1981), with particular attention to the availability of long-distance binding in Urdu reflexives. The analysis shows that while personal pronouns conform to Binding Condition B and reciprocals obey Condition A, reflexives exhibit behavior that challenges strict locality constraints. Specifically, Urdu reflexives display logophoric properties comparable to those observed in languages such as Icelandic and Japanese. These findings suggest that a …

records.title: On the QUD sensitivity of a Third reading
records.abstract: We provide the first experimental evidence supporting the hypothesis that transparent readings are sensitive to the QUD (Question Under Discussion) (Schwager, 2009; Percus, 2020; Benbaji-Elhadad, 2023; Mayr and Schmitt, 2023, 2024), using third readings (Fodor, 1970) in attitude reports. In particular, we test Mayr and Schmitt’s (2023; 2024) claim that, even among QUDs about the attitude holder’s mental state, there is difference in the availability of transparent readings. Our results have consequences for replacement-based theories of transparent readings and more broadly illuminate properties of a discourse that give rise to and constrain a QUD about someone’s mental state.

records.title: Background Deletion: The Syntax of Clausal Ellipsis in Hindi/Urdu [Dissertation]
records.abstract: This dissertation explores the syntax of subsententials in Hindi/Urdu (H/U), with an empirical focus on sluicing and fragment answers. Such phenomena represent instances where all clausal material is unpronounced, except for a (wh-)phrase (e.g., A: Who did John see? B: Mary.). With evidence from various connectivity effects, I argue that a non-structuralist analysis of such configurations, which does not assume the presence of tacit material, is untenable. Rather, subsententials in this language warrant a structuralist solution, according to which the surfacing remnant base-generates in an underlying clause whose morpho-syntax is reduced at PF. Most structuralist proposals of clausal …

records.title: Strong and weak epistemic operators in assertions, polar questions, and declarative questions: An experimental study of German
records.abstract: This article investigates the distribution of the strong subjective epistemic operators "sicherlich", "wohl", "wahrscheinlich", "müsste" and the weak subjective epistemic operators "vielleicht", "möglicherweise", "könnte" in polar questions and in declarative questions in German. The motivation for the study is the hypothesis that in polar questions, the perspective of subjective operators is shifted to the addressee (so-called “interrogative flip”), whereas in declarative questions it remains with the speaker. The article hypothesizes that under this assumption, weak operators should be rated better in polar questions, whereas strong operators should get a higher rating in declarative …

records.title: Information structure from a comparative diachronic perspective
records.abstract: This chapter examines the interaction between syntax, morphology and information structure in Germanic from a comparative diachronic perspective. Making use of syntactically annotated corpus data, we examine historical stages of English, Icelandic, High German and Low German and present a quantificational comparison of (i) fronted constituents in the prefield and (ii) object ordering in the postfinite domain. We focus in particular on the relation between constituent fronting and topicality, suggesting a view of topic which incorporates the Strawson/Reinhart's notion in the situation-semantic approach. Conceiving of topic as a triple of situation coordinates used to asses the sentence, we …

records.title: 'Same' and 'different' are not additive presupposition triggers - Reply to Mikkelsen & Hardt 2024
records.abstract: This paper is a reply to Mikkelsen & Hardt’s 2024 article analyzing 'same' and 'different' as involving an additive presuppositional element TOO akin to overt 'too'. This hypothesis has several virtues: it provides a uniform analysis for both 'same' and 'different' under all of their (internal, external and comparative-like) readings; it explains several effects (poorly discussed so far) exhibited by 'same': parallelism and island effects, as well as analogies with 'too'. But I show that this additive analysis faces several challenges questioning its explanatory power: the uniformity of the account rests on some stipulations, and the analogies between 'same'/'different' and 'too' are only …

records.title: The inherent modality of verbs of perception, recognition, and disposition in Hungarian
records.abstract: This paper argues for an extended notion of sublexical modality through an in-depth analysis of three verb classes in Hungarian: verbs of involuntary perception, verbs of involuntary recognition and verbs of physical disposition. Verbs falling into these natural classes pattern together across four, seemingly unrelated, phenomena: the incompatibility with an ability modal auxiliary, the existence of a dispositional middle voice form, the appearance in so-called root infinitives of circumstantial modality, and susceptibility to reinterpretation as auxiliaries. I argue that this is because of their unique, enriched semantics: such verbs have ability modality hard-wired into their lexical …

records.title: Acquiring Island Constraints through Efficient Structural Chunks
records.abstract: How do children acquire knowledge of syntactic islands? Cross-linguistically, we see constrained variation (Sprouse et al., 2021), suggesting an interplay between child-internal factors and language-specific input. We use computational cognitive modeling to investigate a recent theory of the learning mechanism which relies on the child learning efficient chunks of syntactic structure from the input (Dickson, 2025; Dickson et al., 2024, 2022). Specifically, we adapt the Fragment Grammar (FG) chunking approach (T. O’Donnell et al., 2011; T. J. O’Donnell, 2015; T. J. records.title: A Smuggling approach to low focalisation
records.abstract: Drawing on cartographic assumptions that there exist discourse-related projections in the ‘vP periphery’(Belletti 2001), we explore two types of postverbal focalisation in Lamnso and Limbum (Grassfields Bantu). The first type places an expletive pro- noun and / or a copula before a contrastively focused constituent. The activation of the expletive and/or the copula in object focal- isation induces freezing and minimality effects on subject and verb extraction. records.title: Superlinguistics
records.abstract: Full title: Superlinguistics: A formal approach to multimodal meaning Theoretical linguistics has made great strides towards a science of language, building on solid foundations in logic and analytical philosophy, and, more recently, joining forces with empirical sciences. Superlinguistics wants to expand the reach of our sophisticated theoretical and empirical linguistic toolkit by applying it to language-like objects beyond the scope of traditional linguistics, like gestures, comics, or music. [...] I offer four case studies showcasing different aspects of supersemantic approaches to multimodal sign systems. In 3.1 I discuss a compositional semantic approach to the interpretation of …

records.title: Narrating perception and thought
records.abstract: Good storytellers reveal their characters’ ‘inner stories’, composed of subjective experiences like feelings, perceptions, and thoughts. In fiction, narrators can faithfully represent their main characters’ thoughts, using techniques like free indirect discourse. But perceptions are fundamentally different from thoughts in that they don’t have a linguistic form for the narrator to reproduce or mimic in a report. We argue that there is in fact a dedicated linguistic category, narrated perception, similar to but distinct from free indirect discourse, that allows narrators to vividly represent perceptual experiences. We propose a discourse semantics analysis of this phenomenon, built on the …

records.title: When AI’s helpfulness becomes harmful: Data reconstruction, simulation and research ethics
records.abstract: This short paper reports a preliminary experiment, which tested how major generative AIs respond to a request to restore data from an existing figure and another request to simulate addional data with similar trends. Among the three systems tested, Gemini 3.0 provided the most detailed guidance, including suggestions for merging restored and simulated data that, if followed, may lead to ethically problematic research practices. I am sharing this experience with public as an experimental linguist, but this case should be relevant for any academic field that involves experimentation.

records.title: An Antisymmetric Syntax of Word Order in Farsi: The Predicate Domain
records.abstract: This dissertation closely reexamines the structure of the predicate domain in Farsi/Persian and evaluates whether its surface OV order is best explained by the widely adopted head-final VP/vP analyses or by an alternative framework that universally derives all linear orders from the same base structure. In favor of the latter approach, I argue that the traditional head-final verb phrase accounts face significant theoretical issues highlighted by three empirical domains: (i) complex predicates and their interaction with auxiliary verbs and phenomena such as ellipsis and verb-preposing, (ii) postverbal clausal complements and their subextraction, binding, and ellipsis patterns, and (iii) the …

records.title: Rabelais et ses phraséologismes gargantuesques : analyse des procédés de phraséotraduction en polonais, BCMS, chinois, japonais et portugais brésilien
records.abstract: The article explores the translation of phraseological units (PUs) from Chapter XI of Gargantua by François Rabelais into five languages: Polish, Bosnian-Croatian-Montenegrin-Serbian (BCMS), Chinese, Japanese, and Brazilian Portuguese. The main difficulty in the phraseological translation of the selected text lies in the fact that the therein present PUs have to be taken both in the literal and the figurative phraseological sense. This problem resulted in translators sometimes sacrificing one of the two possible reading layers. Following a theoretical examination of the PUs characteristics and their unfrozenness, the analysis of the translations into five selected languages takes from …

records.title: A tripartition of complementizers: exploring clause size in Romance
records.abstract: This article presents a crosslinguistic study of Romance infinitival complementizers a and de. The proposal is that a/de are acategorial and can be merged in various positions in the CP-field, the TP-field, and the vP-field. Furthermore, we demonstrate that clause size varies extensively from one environment to the other, and from one language to the other, which leads us to argue against a one-size-fits-all approach.

records.title: Infinitive fronting as a transparency effect in Old and Middle French
records.abstract: In this article, we present a novel analysis of infinitive fronting in Old and Middle French (9th-16th century). We find that in sentences with modal verbs and clitic climbing, the infinitive may either follow the main verb or precede it. When the subject of the main verb is overt and the infinitive is fronted, the order is SUBJ-VINF- VFIN. Moreover, we find that the object of the fronted infinitive either cliticises onto the main verb (i.e. clitic climbing) or moves as a full DP with the infinitive, in which case the order is SUBJ-OBJ-VINF-VFIN. We compare our data to Stylistic Fronting, and we show that infinitive fronting in Old and Middle French is a different mechanism. Our analysis …

records.title: Successor-Saturated Ordinals and Indefinite Tail Activation, HTQA, ITA New Theory
records.abstract: This article develops a stronger lexical architecture for ordinal meaning and its quantificational consequences. Building on the Successor-Closed Sequence Lexicon (SCSL), I treat FIRST as successor-saturated: encoding FIRST lexically guarantees not only an immediate successor (FIRST ⇒ SECOND) but an entire successor tail in the relevant sequence. I introduce Indefinite Tail Activation (ITA) as the interface update that maps this successor tail into a discourse-available remainder, canonically lexicalized as indefiniteness (some, a few, others) and, in certain configurations, as specific-referenced indefinites (all, each, every). The central new hypothesis is an ordinal→remainder-indefinite …

records.title: Successor-Saturated Ordinals and Indefinite Tail Activation A RED/DED Operator Extension of the Successor-Closed Sequence Lexicon
records.abstract: This paper strengthens a lexical hypothesis about ordinal meaning: encoding a position as FIRST necessarily encodes a successor position, and more strongly, encodes all successor positions in the relevant sequence. Formally, sequence is defined as an index structure whose domain is successor-closed (or at minimum two-element) and whose semantic interface guarantees a successor for the initial index. Under the Successor-Closed Sequence Lexicon (SCSL), FIRST ⇒ SECOND is not pragmatic enrichment but a lexical entailment/presupposition triggered by the ordinal itself. Building on SCSL, I introduce Indefinite Tail Activation (ITA): when FIRST anchors the beginning of a sequence, all remaining …

records.title: On the referential capacity of language models: An internalist rejoinder to Mandelkern & Linzen
records.abstract: Mandelkern and Linzen (2024) argue that words generated by language models (LMs) are linked to causal histories of use within human linguistic communities, and ultimately to their referents. Therefore, LMs’ words refer. We qualify Mandelkern and Linzen’s claim as applicable to a narrow class of expressions. Thus qualified, the claim is valid and motivated by the need to evaluate LMs’ outputs for relevance and truth. Next, we discuss the actual scope of their claim, and we conclude that the bounds of sense and reference in LMs are more restricted than in humans. We close with some considerations on the status of LMs as members of human linguistic communities.

records.title: Stylistic applicatives: a lens into the nature of anticausative SE
records.abstract: This paper examines an understudied syntactic phenomenon in Chilean Spanish: stylistic applicatives. This construction involves the appearance of the form LE alongside dative clitics in marked anticausative contexts. The pattern displays several puzzling properties, the most striking being that the anticausative/reflexive marker SE becomes optional in it, i.e., its presence or absence does not affect the interpretation of the sentence. I argue that this optionality arises from two interconnected factors. First, stylistic applicatives involve multiple exponence of an applicative head, realized as two separate clitic forms. Second, one of the resulting exponents, which is formally similar to …

records.title: What ever happened to meaning?  (A commentary on Futrell & Mahowald's forthcoming BBS article)
records.abstract: A version of this manuscript was submitted to Behavioral and Brain Sciences as a commentary on Futrell and Mahowald’s (forthcoming) “How linguistics learned to stop worrying and embrace the language models.” By “linguistics,” the target article means usage-based linguistics, which, we agree, plays very well with language models. But the article summarily dismisses important work on meaning from the now disreputable tradition of generative linguistics. We refute the authors’ arguments from distributional semantics and “green tea,” and highlight the importance of formal compositional semantics for the study of thought.

records.title: Dimension Classifiers Mediating Nominal Modification
records.abstract: We present a novel analysis of attributive modification patterns like a green colour car, based on new data primarily from Dutch and Russian. We argue that the nominal element colour is a Dimension Classifier (DimCl) and is in a possessive part-whole relation with the noun car. These constructions show properties of inalienable possession. We show why DimCls cannot be viewed as silent nouns (contra Kayne 2005) and argue that these structures start out as of-modification of the type a car of green colour, with car the possessor. We propose that the postnominal constituent optionally moves to a prenominal functional projection that turns mass nouns into count nouns (i.e., SpecDivP; Borer …

records.title: Scrambling in Japanese: Hidden Similarities to Topicalization
records.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to establish two novel claims on the nature of scrambling in Japanese. First, as opposed to the general consensus that has been reached since Saito (1992) and Tada (1993), we show that not only clause-internal (CI) scrambling, but also long-distance (LD) scrambling can create new binding/scope relations, so the latter need not undergo radical reconstruction, either. Second, we argue that, though CI- and LD-scrambling can both have semantic effects, they are still not uniform in nature and should be derived by distinct grammatical processes, contra Tada (1990), Kitahara (2002), and Saito (2003). In particular, we show that, for LD-scrambling to apply, it must …

records.title: Specific-Referenced Indefinite Quantifiers as Ordinal Refiners: A RED-Based Operator Extension of Cardinal–Ordinal Correlation
records.abstract: Cardinals (three) measure quantity and ordinals (third) identify positions in an ordered domain, yet natural language permits systematic shifts between these regimes. Building on a bidirectional discretization architecture in which an ordinalization operator R refines coarse quantity into addressable order positions, and inverse unification operators collapse refined microstructure back into macro-level wholes, this article extends the program to a third layer: specific-referenced indefinite quantifiers (e.g., all, both, either, neither, certain, half, exact, the least, the most). The central claim is that these quantifiers function as higher-order ordinal refiners: given an ordinal spine …

records.title: On Licensing Barest Conditionals: From the Vantage Point of the Syntax-Prosody Interface
records.abstract: This paper investigates two types of barest conditionals in Mandarin, both characterized by their minimal clausal structure and the presence of identical pairing, i.e., two duplicated verbs, such as Gāi chī chī, gāi hē hē ‘Eat when it's time to eat, drink when it's time to drink’, or wh-phrases, like Ài shéi shéi ‘Whoever it may be’ (cf. Tsai 2025). Based on the identical pairing analysis, this paper argues that both types are licensed by an explicit necessity operator, namely the sentence-initial modal: It unselectively binds the pair of identical variables, thereby licensing the donkey-conditional in question (cf. Cheng & Huang 1996, 2020). On the other hand, the type of identical pairing …

records.title: Cardinal–Ordinal Correlations as Bidirectional Discretization: A RED-Based Operator Account
records.abstract: Cardinals (three) and ordinals (third) are routinely treated as closely related members of the numeral system, yet their semantic contributions diverge: cardinals measure quantity, while ordinals identify positions within an order. This article develops an explicit account of the correlation as a bidirectional discretization architecture in which (i) an ordinalization operator refines a coarse quantity into a structured, addressable progression, and (ii) inverse unification operators collapse refined microstructure back into macro-level ordinalized wholes. The proposal is expressed in a diagnostic methodology (RED: Reverse Entailment Diagnostic) adapted to numerals, testing whether a …

records.title: Cross-linguistic Variation in the Expression of Heterogeneous Plural Marking and its Theoretical Consequences [Dissertation]
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates the morphological expression of associative, similative and approximative plurals (henceforth heterogeneous plurals) cross-linguistically, establishing a number of novel generalizations regarding the use of the regular plural marker as (or as part of) a heterogeneous plural. A typological examination of these plurals reveals that using regular plural morphology for a heterogeneous plural is not arbitrary – as has been previously assumed – but rather tightly constrained by independent aspects of the nominal domain in the relevant cases. Chapter 2 investigates those languages that use the regular plural as (or as part of) the associative plural (associative …

records.title: A cautionary note on word learning paradigms and presupposition triggering
records.abstract: Cross-linguistically, predicates with initial-state and change-of-state components tend to encode them as presupposition and assertion, respectively. Bade, Schlenker, and Chemla (Natural Language Semantics 32(4):473–503, 2024)–henceforth BSC24–argue based on a series of artificial word learning experiments that this cross-linguistic tendency reflects conceptual biases privileging changes-of-state over initial-states. In their experiments, they gauged how participants encoded the initial-state and change-of-state entailments of a nonce verb "wug," and they interpret their results as suggesting that participants generally encoded the initial-state entailment as a presupposition and encoded …

records.title: On Causative Recursion: A Response to Key 2013 and Nie 2025
Degree QUDs and focus-sensitive scalar particles: Chinese dōu, cái, and jiù
records.abstract: Based on a degree-QUD perspective, this chapter analyzes Chinese "dōu", "cái", and "jiù" as "even"-like particles. Similar to English "even", these particles invoke a contextually salient degree QUD, ordering the focus associate's alternative set by informativeness, and requiring their prejacent to be maximally informative. "Dōu" vs. "cái/jiù" differ in their information projection patterns (order-preserving vs. order-reversing). Under this proposal, the two elements identified in the canonical analysis of “even”, i.e., a likelihood scale and entity-based additivity, are replaced by a degree-QUD-based informativeness scale and additivity along this scale, both reflected in the …

records.title: On U-syncretism and Passives: A Response to Key 2024
records.abstract: While Key (2024) is right in claiming that u-syncretism is a surface phenomenon that can “mask” the structural difference between canonical and noncanonical passive derivations, he incorrectly analyzes u-syncretic passive morphology as a manifestation of a nonactive Voice head. This paper proposes an alternative approach based on the following specific points. First, agents are suppressed in noncanonical (low) passives but not in canonical passives; an internal argument is promoted to the low Voice layer in noncanonical passives and a higher Voice layer in canonical passives. Second, u-syncretism arises from internal argument promotion to the low Voice layer, rather than being a …

records.title: Focus Sensitivity in Mabia and Yoruboid
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates the syntax-semantics properties of association with focus sensitive particles in three West African languages: Kasem, Kusaal, and Yorùbá. Specifically, I investigate three focus sensitive particles that have been classified as involving conventional association with focus (Beaver and Clark, 2008). These are 'only', 'also', and 'even'. These particles are focus sensitive because they interact in different ways with the alternatives evoked by the focus constituent. In the three languages, these focus sensitive particles can either be realized adfocally or adverbially, each realization having a distinct morphological form. I propose a uniform analysis for the …

records.title: 'Other' and the Decomposition of Romance Pronominal Possessives
records.abstract: 'Other' is part of Spanish 'nosotros'. 'Other' may well always be part of first person plural, in a way that makes the features +/-exclusive/inclusive superfluous. Part of 'other' is part of Spanish 'nuestro'. Progress can be made toward an understanding of what is part of what. The intricate properties of the Romance person morphemes 'n-', 'm-', 'v-' and 't-' are compatible with Decompositionality, suitably interpreted.

records.title: What Can Mongolian Tell Us about Binding?
records.abstract: Drawing on Mongolian data, this paper proposes that syntactic binding arises as Agree between the phi-features on a predicate-internal subject and those in the specifier of an anaphor as a possessive DP in a lower position on the one hand, and is reassessed when the subject moves up to a position intertwining with verbal inflections on the other hand, leading to the distinction between predicate-internal (phase-based) and predicate-external (inflection-based) binding. Predicate-external binding occurs when this Agree is followed by Move (of the subject from inside the predicate into the inflectional domain), while predicate-internal binding occurs without Move. The paper aligns with the …

records.title: Constraints on modal flavor colexification
records.abstract: Modal items are known to often show ambiguity with respect to modal flavor. For example, English 'can' can express both deontic and circumstantial flavor. To date, however, it remains unstudied whether there are particular sets of modal flavors that are more frequently colexified than others across the world’s languages. Here, we avail ourself of the recent database of Uegaki et al. (2024) to uncover natural classes of modal flavor colexification, and to evaluate the degree that these natural classes can be captured using different kinds of ontological structures.

records.title: Distributive concord with complex licensing
records.abstract: Distributive concord items are only grammatical when licensed in an appropriate plural or distributive environment. In this paper, we introduce a new phenomenon of complex licensing, in which the relevant semantic environment emerges from the interaction between two operators, neither of which is sufficient to license the item by itself. The relevant examples involve disjunction scoping below a distributive operator of a different ontological type. We show that these facts are predicted in a straightforward manner from semantic analyses of distributive concord, but pose significant challenges to syntactic analyses. Further comparisons are made between different theories of semantic …

records.title: Review of Morphology: A Distributed Morphology Introduction (2024, Wiley-Blackwell)
records.abstract: This is a review of a recent textbook, Morphology: A Distributed Morphology Introduction, written by Jeffrey P. Punske, and published by Wiley-Blackwell in 2024. This is the only linguistics textbook that is specific to the framework of DM, and thus fills a crucial gap, bridging the divide between the classroom and a mountain of contemporary linguistic scholarship. Our overall assessment of this textbook, which is in its first edition, is that it has admirable goals, a number of strengths, and substantial potential, but that significant revision is needed for it to more effectively achieve its stated goals and reach its full potential. The textbook’s strengths include its utilization of a …

records.title: Semantics of split quantification
Lexical Ontology Persistence, Neural Representation, and Computational Modeling vs. Quantum Linguistics
records.abstract: Quantum-inspired approaches to language often model word meaning as a superposition of potential interpretations, collapsing to a specific sense only under contextual “measurement.” This analogy has generated elegant mathematical models of ambiguity, contextuality, and non-classical probability in semantics. However, it risks conflating observer-level uncertainty with the ontological status of lexical entities themselves. This paper proposes an alternative framework: Lexical Ontology Persistence (LOP). According to LOP, words are not mere containers of probabilistic potential; they are structured, historically grounded ontological objects. Each word retains an internal architecture of …

records.title: A Two-Level Grammar of Nominal Potential Lexical Structure, Syntactic Slots, and the Determiner Status of NOT
records.abstract: This monograph develops a two-level architecture for grammatical description that separates (i) a lexical module responsible for head category, phrase-internal selection, and local constituency, from (ii) a syntactic module responsible for sentence roles (Subject–Predicate–Object) and the slot families that license constituents into those roles. The empirical focus is English NOT. While not is often treated as a clausal negator in the functional spine, it also appears in a broad family of constituent uses with complements that are heterogeneous in lexical category (NPs, infinitivals, finite clauses in argumental packaging, PPs, APs, and participial/eventive phrases). The central …

records.title: The Processing of Compounds in Adult Second Language Learners of English and Turkish
records.abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the processing of compound words in English and Turkish with monolingual and sequential bilingual adults with intermediate and advanced level proficiency. The study includes two different but parallel experiments on compound word recognition, one in English and one in Turkish. By using a masked priming experiment, the processing of English and Turkish compounds by monolingual and sequential bilinguals is examined.

records.title: The temporary-context theory of conditionals
records.abstract: This paper proposes a minimal, but powerful, theory of indicative conditionals built around three components: a theory of local contexts; the idea that if-clauses function to create a temporary context (and do nothing else); and the claim that worlds outside the context of evaluation are treated, not as true or false, but as irrelevant to semantic evaluation. Conditional restriction of modals emerges as an automatic byproduct of the creation of temporary contexts, and the theory explains parallels between presupposition projection and domain restriction in both conditionals and disjunction. It also accounts for Stalnaker's Thesis, the equation between probabilities of conditionals and …

records.title: A Two-Level Grammar of Nominal Potential Lexical Structure, Syntactic Slots, and the Determiner Status of NOT
records.abstract: This monograph develops a two-level architecture for grammatical description in which (i) a lexical module computes category formation, phrase-internal selection, and headed structure, while (ii) a syntactic module computes sentence roles and the slot families that license constituents into those roles. The empirical focus is English NOT. Standard analyses assimilate not to clausal negation or to a dedicated functional head; however, not productively combines with diverse non-clausal materials (infinitivals, subordinate clauses used as arguments, PPs, APs, and participial phrases) whenever those materials function as nominal candidates in the syntactic role system. I formalize this …

records.title: Partitive and Counting Phrases in Polish: A Nanosyntactic Analysis of Syncretism
records.abstract: This paper investigates syncretism in Polish pseudo-partitive and counting phrases, where different forms of the same noun appear in context as ‘a piece of apple’, ‘two apples’, and ‘five apples’. These contexts exhibit three distinct syncretism patterns: AAB, ABC, and ABA, depending on whether suffixes are repeated or differ across forms. The analysis focuses on how suffixes signal distinctions in number and countability, drawing on the nanosyntactic framework. By applying the Lexicalization Algorithm, the paper shows how noun structures grow incrementally and how suffixes compete for lexicalization. Special attention is paid to the ABA pattern in feminine nouns, where the same suffix …

records.title: Responses to Cantonese A-not-A questions by Cantonese-English bilingual children
records.abstract: This study investigates mismatched responses to Cantonese A-not-A questions produced by Cantonese-English bilingual children. Mismatches are hypothesized to result from overgeneralization and cross-linguistic influence. We examine if there are effects of language dominance on children’s production of mismatches. This corpus-based study uses data from eight Cantonese L1 children and eight Cantonese-English bilingual children from the Hong Kong Cantonese Child Language Corpus and Hong Kong Bilingual Child Language Corpus, respectively. Children’s production was sampled at 3-month intervals from age 2;0 to 3;0. Responses to A-not-A questions were classified into (1) target response, (2) …

records.title: Rethinking principle C reconstruction in ATB movement and parasitic gaps: Data driven perspectives on the too many tools problem
records.abstract: Multi-gap dependencies, such as ATB movement and parasitic gaps, constitute a puzzle for syntactic theory because they violate the strict one-to-one mapping between a filler and a gap. Over the last few decades, multiple 'tools' have been proposed to model this unusual one-to-many relation, some of them unifying ATB and parasitic gaps under a single approach, others treating them as unrelated. Despite their fundamental differences, nearly all tools remain to coexist, and it appears that the field prioritizes proposing new theories over identifying which of them has the best empirical coverage. The lack of clarity regarding the empirical facts themselves might be the main cause of this. The …

records.title: Language as Evidence: A Discourse Semantic and Corpus Linguistic Approach to Examining Written Terrorist Threatening Communication
records.abstract: This thesis contributes to the growing international commitment to countering transnational terrorism. It undertakes an empirical investigation of the language of violent extremism by using a forensic linguistic lens, innovatively combined with the Appraisal and Affiliation frameworks from Systemic Functional Linguistics. These frameworks offer tools for understanding the discursive nature of the language of extremism, including how terrorists attempt to incite violence and threaten their audiences through their evaluative language, and how they position key social bonds in their discourse. The study involved a specialised corpus of 20 terrorist public statements produced by four terrorists …

records.title: The role of (de)bonding in the legitimation of violence in extremists’ public threatening communication
records.abstract: One aspect of threat of terrorist public communication is incitement to violence and legitimatingit (Tsesis, 2017). This paper contributes to understanding how bonds tabled in discourse areexploited to legitimize 'Our' violence and to delegitimize ‘outgroups’. I argue that the inciting textsdrive the strategic use of bonds to achieve a main rhetorical function: legitimizing violence. Thepatterns of bonds, geared as a basis for perception and (de)legitimation, are investigated as realizedin a set of incitement texts communicated publicly by the former al-Qaeda leader, Osama binLaden, and the far-rightist, Brenton Tarrant. The analytical approach mainly draws on Knight's(2010) social semiotic …

records.title: Exploring the grammar of othering and antagonism as enacted in terrorist discourse: verbal aggression in service of radicalisation
records.abstract: The social, discursive practice of othering in violent extremist discourse serves to present outgroups as distant yet real threats to the ideological and physical territories of an ingroup which a terrorist claims to represent. However, the role of grammatical choices (namely, non/transactive construction, voice, and mood) in enacting the othering act within the context of radicalisation to terrorism remains to be empirically verified. This paper explores the patterning and pragmatic functions—namely in framing situations, coercing into violence, and legitimising hostile actions against Others—of the syntactic structure of the othering utterances. The othering utterances, as realized in a …

records.title: Compassion as appraisal, performative identity and moral affiliation: A corpus perspective and digital activist strategic communication analysis
records.abstract: This article addresses the underexplored topic of compassion in digital activism through linguistic research. Utilising corpus linguistics and the SFL appraisal framework, the study initially analyses the lemma “compassion” and its appraisal nature within The Coronavirus Corpus. It then models compassion development as a social discursive process, taking Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS-Australia) campaigns as a case study, drawing on “communion” and “tendering” strategies, and positioning theory-based morality by linking structure to agency. The analysis provides evidence that the concept of “compassion” extends beyond triggered emotions, expressing institutionalised feelings. …

records.title: Beyond thematic uniqueness
records.abstract: A common way of characterising the relationship between events and their participants is to postulate that the latter are assigned thematic roles. This is subject to a 'thematic uniqueness' constraint: an event cannot have more than one participant bearing the same thematic role. Building on recent work on predicates of individuals, this article demonstrates that thematic uniqueness is part of a broader phenomenon, which I call 'predicational uniqueness.' I model predicational uniqueness as stemming from predicational exhaustification; on this view, all predicates, whether they are thematic predicates of events or non-thematic predicates of individuals, are locally strengthened vis-à-vis …

records.title: The effects of implicit causality, topicality, and controller animacy on temporal adjunct control
records.abstract: Non-finite temporal adjuncts often only allow control by the matrix subject, but recent research has shown that non-subject control is also possible. Previous research has found that object control is more likely if the object’s referent is strongly topical. Other research predicts that it should also be possible if the object is logophoric. In three reference choice and acceptability rating experiments, this study demonstrates that object control of temporal adjuncts in English is more widely available than previously thought in sentences such as Alyssa noticed Sergio after sitting in a front-row seat. Object control interpretations are more likely with a supporting context, which can …

records.title: Phonological  Relations  Between  Palatalizers  and  the  Phonemic System: A Case Study on Czech
records.abstract: This paper examines palatalization in Czech, focusing on its behaviour in the domain of noun-deriving suffixes. It argues that Czech palatalization is not an assimilatory process, but a repair mechanism triggered by structurally and lexically deficient phonological units, referred to as palatalizers. These units lack an independent phonetic counterpart and can be identified only through their systematic phonological effects. The analysis proposes that palatalizers and phonemes form a coherent, interactive system whose interrelations determine the surface outcomes of palatalization. The study first introduces a new typology of Czech palatalization patterns, then rejects the assimilatory …

records.title: Going Through Social Red Lights: Combatting Hate Speech, Prejudice, and Incitement
records.abstract: Language is fundamental to and culturally. All too often, language is used as the shorthand for defining cultural commonality and difference – and when tensions flare up, language is the first tool of violence. It, therefore, holds immense and transformative power, capable of both building and fracturing communities. And in the urgent fight against hate speech and prejudice, prioritising genuine human rights concerns and employing rigorous linguistic analysis are paramount. Language not only mirrors reality but actively shapes it, moulding our experi- ences and converting perceptions into meanings. Selective linguistic choices perpetuate sexual difference, racial otherness, and social …

records.title: Unmasking Malicious Stance Indicators and Attitudinal Priming: An ‘Evaluative Textbite’ Approach to Identity Attacks in Violent Extremist Discourse
records.abstract: The article explores the patterning and functioning of attitude semantics in the prac- tice of identity attacks within terrorist communications. Positioned in facework and stance-taking research (e.g. Tracy & Tracy, 1998, 2008, 2017), it introduces the con- cepts of ‘evaluative textbites’ and ‘attitudinal priming’ to linguistic examinations, advocating a functional approach to unravelling identity attacks, drawing on corpus analysis methods (e.g. word frequency, and concordance-line qualitative analysis) and the Appraisal framework (Martin & White, 2005). Findings reveal that, linked with stance-taking activity, attitudinal priming offers insights into how specific idea- tional targets are …

records.title: Determiners as predicates
records.abstract: Since Montague (1973), higher-order functions have formed the blueprint for analyzing determiner meanings in natural language, giving rise to the `standard' relational treatment of (Barwise & Cooper 1981; Keenan & Stavi 1986). The goal of this short paper is to begin sketching an alternative to Generalized Quantifier theory, in which determiners are treated as predicates of structured entities. In order to make sense of this idea, I build on recent work by Bledin (forthcoming), who suggests incorporating a notion of polarity into the domain of entities. The resulting account of determiner meanings is significantly more restrictive than the standard account—concretely, I demonstrate that …

records.title: Moral disaffiliation in cyber incitement to hatred and violence
records.abstract: Incitement to hatred and terrorist acts is a key aspect of illegal online content that, unlike one-to-one incitement acts, addresses a wide range of audiences and requires terrorists exploit social bonds to legitimise violence and achieve their agenda. However, little is known about how terrorists utilise language to activate these bonds and to discursively construct a moral system in the service of positioning the inciters and incitees and regulating their moral conduct against Others. Contributing to the growing international commitment, this study proposes the concept of 'disaffiliation' as a communication strategy used in incitement towards outgroups. The chapter empirically examines …

records.title: Conceptual Burstiness in Sociolinguistic Profiling of Radical‑Criminal Communications: Corpus Method‑Assisted Meaning Extraction for Investigative Leads
records.abstract: Positioned within linguistic profiling research as in Shuy’s work (The language of murder cases: intentionality, predisposition, and voluntariness. Oxford University Press, Oxford, 2014), this study introduces the concept of ‘conceptual burstiness’ to computer-assisted sociolinguistic profiling, demonstrating how to uncover investi- gative leads within terrorist threatening communications. Leveraging corpus analy- sis methods and semiotic clues, the study chiefly utilises AntConc (a software tool developed by Anthony, AntConc (Version 3.5.8) [Computer software]. Waseda Uni- versity, Tokyo, Japan, 2019) to scrutinise word frequency and concordance lines, revealing distinct lexical …

records.title: Moving towards peace, compassion and empathy through semiotic enquiry
records.abstract: In our interconnected world, exposure to hate, fear, violence and adversarial communication is commonplace. Yet, this exposure underscores the urgent need for a more just, peaceful, and inclusive society. While research stresses the importance of nurturing peace, compassion and empathy for enhanced well-being and social justice, these three terms are rarely discussed at length in linguistics and communication studies. Little systematic work explores how language and semiotic resources actualise these ideals across contexts. This special issue, grounded in systemic functional linguistics, addresses this gap. It aims to contribute to a more just world, promote non-violent efforts for social …

records.title: Inverse scope in "all…not" constructions: A cross-linguistic and diachronic investigation
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates the cross-linguistic variation in the use of inverse-scope constructions like "All that glitters is not gold", where clausal negation takes wide scope over a preceding universal quantifier phrase. These "all... not" constructions contrast with transparent-scope alternatives, such as "Not all that glitters is gold", which reflect the intended scope relations through surface structure. The language sample consists of 217 languages from diverse language families and linguistic areas, including historical data from 21 Germanic and Romance languages.

records.title: Les fricatives voisées et l'allongement vocalique en français laurentien
records.abstract: (French document) _____________________ L’allongement vocalique en français laurentien (FL) est un phénomène linguistique au sujet duquel certains auteurs ont déjà proposé plusieurs règles d’application (Dumas, 1974; Poliquin, 2006). Il est généralement admis qu’en syllabe finale fermée par /v z ʒ R/, les voyelles hautes du FL sont produites comme étant longues et tendues. Cela dit, d’autres recherches font état de données où, en syllabe finale fermée par /R/, les voyelles hautes sont longues, mais relâchées (Charette, 2018; Côté, 2012). C’est cette différence de tension entre, d’une part, les voyelles hautes tendues en syllabe finale fermée par /v z ʒ/ et, d’autre part, les voyelles hautes …

records.title: The role of social affiliation in incitement: A social semiotic approach to far-right terrorists’ incitement to violence
records.abstract: One key aspect of threat in terrorists’ language is incitement to violence. Con- tributing to a fuller understanding of how terrorists use language to encourage people to join their cause, this article examines the role of evaluative language in incitement strategies used by a far-rightist to align with and alienate partic- ular social groups. The Af liation framework (Knight 2010a; Zappavigna 2011; Etaywe & Zappavigna 2021; Etaywe 2022a), as grounded in systemic functional linguistics, is used to understand how values and social bonds are leveraged in the process of incitement, as explored in a manifesto published online by Brenton Tarrant, preceding his 2019 terrorist attack on two …

records.title: Discursive pragmatics of justification in terrorist threat texts: Victim-blaming, denying, discrediting, legitimating, manipulating, and retaliation
records.abstract: This article explores the under-researched area of discursive tactics employed in terrorist threat texts that exploit moral values to constantly justify violence, fostering a ‘discourse of justification’, disaffiliation and conflict. Employing a discursive pragmatic analysis, it delves into the tactics of violent extremists associated with jihadism and far-right ideologies. Utilising the Appraisal framework and the ‘moral disaffiliation’ strategy, the study uncovers verbal practices shaping a dynamic of justification. Findings reveal threateners’ involvement in regulatory discursive functions – manipulation, deontic-retaliation, and boulomaic effect – and practices of ideologically …

records.title: Identity, ideology and threatening communication: An investigation of patterns of attitude in terrorist discourse
records.abstract: Linguistic analysis of the interpersonal patterning of threatening communication is a means of uncovering the attitudes, ideological orientation, and hostile intentions of perpetrators of violence in terrorist discourse (Gales 2010, 2011). Corpus analysis focused on attitudinal meaning also offers a diagnostic for characterizing the personal and relational identities (Bednarek 2010) manifest in such texts. This paper explores discursive patterns of authorial identity in terrorist communication in a set of post-9/11 terrorist public statements made by former al-Qaeda leader, Osama bin Laden. It draws on the Appraisal framework (Martin and White 2005), a model of evaluative language developed …

records.title: Relational dynamics in violent extremist incitement communication: Language as bonds, obligations, and a catalyst for polarisation
records.abstract: This study advances counter-extremism efforts by examining the mechanisms whereby incitement texts function as networks of bonds and obligations, shaping bonding dynamics within terrorism and polarisation contexts. It conceptualises incitement texts, in the Hallidayan sense, as functional semantic units, and incitement itself as a relational, intersubjective activity embedded in convergent and divergent bonds and pro-ingroup obligations shaped by contested ideologies, identities, and actions. Inciters strategically select discourse semantic structures to establish these bonds and obligations. Using systemic functional linguistics (SFL), and insights from communication accommodation theory …

records.title: What do derivational paradigms tell us about back-formation and what does back-formation tell us about derivational paradigms?
records.abstract: Back-formation is the process that leads to the coinage of a lexeme by deleting a sequence present in the base, such as the verb babysit from the noun babysitter. Back-formed words exhibit a distortion between a meaning that is more complex than that of their base and a form that is simpler. The very nature of this process remains to be established. Our study suggests that back-formation (i) encompasses multiple realities, (ii) performs a formal regularization within paradigms, and (iii) most of the time involves meaning-form discrepancies. Based on five case studies of French verbs that are either back-formed from nouns or adjectives, or have the structure of neoclassical compounds, we …

records.title: Reconsidering non-negative contexts as a diagnostic for negative concord
records.abstract: Abstract: Non-negative contexts are often used as a diagnostic for negative concord items, the claim being specifically that these contexts are not suitable hosts for negative concord items. We present an in-depth empirical investigation of how a single polarity sensitive item behaves under negation as compared to in non-negative contexts. To our knowledge, this is the first detailed investigation of its kind. The item we focus on is Turkish kimse ‘anyone’, and beyond the fact that kimse can appear in non-negative contexts, it otherwise behaves as a negative concord item. The evidence we collected shows, on balance, that kimse has highly parallel behavior across these contexts. We conclude …

records.title: Merge-based syntax is mediated by distinct neurocognitive mechanisms in 84,000 individuals with language deficits across nine languages
records.abstract: In the modern language sciences, the core computational operation of syntax, ‘Merge’, is defined as an operation that combines two linguistic units (e.g., ‘brown’, ‘cat’) to form a categorized constituent structure (‘brown cat’, a Noun Phrase). This structure can be further combined with additional linguistic units based on this categorial information, respecting non-associativity such that abstract grouping is preserved. Some linguists have embraced the view that Merge is an elementary, indivisible operation that emerged in a single evolutionary step. From a neurocognitive standpoint, different mental objects constructed by Merge may be supported by distinct tiers of processing demands: …

records.title: Lexical and Statistical Analysis of Bangla Newspaper and Literature: A Corpus-Driven Study on Diversity, Readability, and NLP Adaptation
records.abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive corpus-driven analysis of Bangla literary and newspaper texts to investigate their lexical diversity, structural complexity and readability. We undertook Vācaspati and IndicCorp, which are the most extensive literature and newspaper-only corpora for Bangla. We examine key linguistic properties, including the type-token ratio (TTR), hapax legomena ratio (HLR), Bigram diversity, average syllable and word lengths, and adherence to Zipf’s Law, for both newspaper (IndicCorp) and literary corpora (Vācaspati). Our findings reveal that till ∼ 10 6 words, the newspaper corpora show a higher TTR than the literary corpora; after that, the literary corpora have …

records.title: Lexical and Statistical Analysis of Bangla Newspaper and Literature: A Corpus-Driven Study on Diversity, Readability, and NLP Adaptation
records.abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive corpus-driven analysis of Bangla literary and newspaper texts to investigate their lexical diversity, structural complexity and readability. We undertook Vācaspati and IndicCorp, which are the most extensive literature and newspaper-only corpora for Bangla. We examine key linguistic properties, including the type-token ratio (TTR), hapax legomena ratio (HLR), Bigram diversity, average syllable and word lengths, and adherence to Zipf’s Law, for both newspaper (IndicCorp) and literary corpora (Vācaspati). Our findings reveal that till ∼ 10 6 words, the newspaper corpora show a higher TTR than the literary corpora; after that, the literary corpora have …

records.title: Verb Phrase Ellipsis in Likpakpaanl
records.abstract: This paper discusses verb phrase ellipsis in Likpakpaanl, a Mabia (Gur) language belonging to the Niger-Congo family and predominantly spoken in the Eastern part of the Northern Region and the Oti Region of Ghana. I argue that VP ellipsis is licensed by the modals ŋmàn and bàn, which project separate modal phrases (ModP) in the clausal structure. The data drawn from the Licahbol dialect show that only the higher ModP position occupied by ŋmàn and bàn hosts the ellipsis [E]-feature which licenses VP ellipsis by deleting the phonological content of their complements. I show that even though both modals license VP ellipsis, bàn targets an entire CP for deletion, while ŋmàn deletes the VP and …

records.title: Interrogative Pronouns in Dagbani and Likpakpaanl
records.abstract: This paper provides an analysis of the properties of interrogative pronouns of Mabia languages drawing data from Dagbani and Likpakpaanl. We focus on the inventory, internal structure, and key grammatical characterisation of the interrogative pronouns. We contend that interrogative pronouns are salient syntactic elements in the content question systems of these languages. In addition, we demonstrate that number marking, distinction between human/non-human and lexical ambiguity are salient grammatical properties of these interrogative pronouns. We further show that the inflection for number employs both suppletive and nonsuppletive patterns. We also contend that the interrogative pronouns …

records.title: The Syntax of Likpakpaanl Elliptical Constructions
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates Modal Complement Ellipsis, sluicing, and fragment answers in Likpakpaanl, a Mabia language spoken in the Northern, Oti, and North-East regions of Ghana. Adopting a Minimalist, movement-based approach to ellipsis, the study argues that elided constituents in Likpakpaanl have the same underlying syntactic structure as their non-elliptical counterparts and are derived through movement followed by phonological deletion. The analysis shows that only the root modals ŋmàà ‘can’ and bàn ‘want’ license Modal Complement Ellipsis. Ellipsis is triggered by an ellipsis feature merged on the modal head, deleting a vP complement with ŋmàà and a TP complement with bàn. The …

records.title: The Dynamic Existential in Tagalog
records.abstract: This paper is focused on existential (and possessive) sentences in Tagalog that are constructed around a verbal existential verb (which I refer to as the Dynamic Existential). Although this verb appears to be an unaccusative verb in its use in existential sentences, I argue that it is actually a transitive verb equivalent to \textsc{have}, with a covert external argument (which is overt in possessive sentences constructed from the same verb). In addition to providing a unification of the syntax of existential and possessive constructions, I argue that this analysis explains the morpho-syntax of dynamic existential constructions (relating, in particular, to the distribution of case) that …

records.title: Measurement-shifting in the syntax: A rational solution to an agreement-interpretation puzzle?
records.abstract: Fraction partitives which contain a plural argument (e.g., "a third of the apples") exhibit a semantic alternation tracked by verbal agreement in some but not all Indo-European languages. One of the readings, which I call a MEASURE interpretation, is unexpected given established perspectives on how measure functions are defined for pluralities. I work to offer an account of the phenomenon specifically for Italian but secondarily seek to explain why the additional reading is absent in other languages. Building off of a suggestion from Falco & Zamparelli (2019), I resolve the alternation to the presence or absence of a covert operator which (i) is Agreed with over the partitive complement, …

records.title: The syntax of Italian col cavolo and un cavolo: Between emphatic negation and utterance minimisation
records.abstract: I discuss two colloquial Italian idioms expressing respectively emphatic negation and objection, col cavolo (lit. ‘with the cabbage’) and un cavolo (lit. ‘a cabbage’). Despite superficial similarities, they represent two very different strategies at syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic level. Col cavolo belongs to a class of non-verbal polar predicates selecting a clausal complement and expressing the speaker’s degree of strength of sincerity towards the proposition (Repp 2013). Col cavolo expresses high commitment to ¬p: it is base-generated in the left periphery, as confirmed by its limited polarity-licensing abilities and impossibility of agreement with a TP-level negative PolP. Instead, …

records.title: A substance-free autosegmental account of the coronal mutation in English
records.abstract: This paper puts forward a restrictive approach to subsegmental architecture, which assumes that sub-skeletal representations are composed of obligatorily binary branching nodes and substance-free emergent features which serve as pointers to phonetic interpretation. We put the theory to a test by applying its principles to the set of alternations of coronal consonants attested in English before affixes -ion, -ian and -ious in words such as infectious, suggestion, revision, expansion etc. It is demonstrated that the requirement for the structure to be binary branching as well as the requirement for English consonants to contain at most three features derive the correct outputs of the coronal …

records.title: Addendum to the Mapbook of Syntactic Variation in American English: Survey Results, 2020–2021
records.abstract: This paper presents an addendum to the Mapbook of Syntactic Variation in American English (Wood et al. 2020), reporting the results of additional acceptability-judgment surveys conducted by the Yale Grammatical Diversity Project in 2020–2021. Using the same survey design, data-processing pipeline, and mapping techniques as the original mapbook, we extend the empirical record to a new set of syntactic constructions, including additional uses of hella, causal where, the alternative one construction, intensificational fully, and several cases of object omission with transitive verbs, which we call “lonely transitives”. As in the original work, we provide geospatial visualizations of …

records.title: [Draft] Oshingandjera (Oshiwambo) Passive: Projecting the Implicit Argument.
records.abstract: This paper examines the syntax of passive constructions in Oshingandjera (a dialect of Oshiwambo) and the question of whether they have syntactically projected implicit external arguments. The data provides empirical as well as theoretical support for the theory of the passive of Collins 2024. The paper motivates an analysis of implicit arguments that requires that they are syntactically projected (Collins 2024, Gotah 2024, Sulemana 2024 and Angelopoulos, Collins, Michelioudakis, & Terzi 2023), opposing an alternative analysis where implicit arguments are not syntactically present (Bruening 2013).

records.title: Outlook Management: 'Subjective' Meanings of Discourse-Sensitive Adverbs and Particles
records.abstract: This chapter examines Japanese discourse-sensitive adverbs and focus particles (e.g., dōse, mushiro, yoppodo; nanka, kurai, koso) that express “subjective” evaluation meanings. I argue that these items are outlook markers in the sense of Kubota & Ido (2025; 'Outlook markers (as abstract discourse markers)' SALT35): they are abstract discourse markers that signal how an attitude holder (typically, the speaker) positions the prejacent relative to a salient counterstance in the discourse. After reviewing major categories of secondary (or, ‘non-at-issue’) meaning in the literature, the chapter shows that outlook markers pattern partly like presuppositions and partly like conventional …

records.title: A thematic ambiguity account of non-culminating construals of Mandarin Chinese experiencer-object psych verbs
records.abstract: We examine in this paper a class of verbs traditionally labelled experiencer-object psych verbs (EO psych verbs) with respect to their culminating entailments in Mandarin Chinese (Chinese); that is, whether the change in mental state these verbs describe come to hold in their experiencer objects. The basic observation is that these predicates optionally culminate when they have subjects that are agentive, whereas non-agentive subjects enforce culmination, in line with what has been observed for (non-psych) accomplishment predicates both within and in many other languages. We propose that non-culmination arises as a result of a thematic ambiguity, where the agentive variants of these verbs …

records.title: The Origins of the Crossover Phenomenon
records.abstract: In this paper, I present a novel analysis of the the crossover phenomenon, which is based on the nonlinear theory of coreference as well as the special syntax of vectors. I show that the crossover effect is strong when either: (a) the dependency is modified under extraction of an anaphor, (b) a wh-vector anteceding a pronoun remains active, as opposed to being disabled, after extraction, (c) a permanent line-crossing effect appears in the derivation or (d) the structure contains multiple ill-formed states. On the other hand, weak crossover is due either to multiple transitory constraint violation in the derivation or to one ill-formed state in a multiple-state structure. In addition, it is …

records.title: Staged updates
records.abstract: Dynamic semantics standardly treats negation as externally static. This is inconsistent with anaphora to doubly-negated indefinites, and Partee disjunctions. I propose a technique for lifting dynamic systems into richer meaning spaces that support dynamic negation. I argue that extant theories of dynamic negation instantiate this technique in various ways, prove that all such lifted systems are isomorphic, and identify a minimal/canonical enrichment of Dynamic Predicate Logic. I relate this perspective on dynamic negation to recent work on 'bounded' meaning. Finally, I consider how such lifted interpretations with dynamic negations can be extended further, into richer meaning spaces that …

records.title: On Helena Hellerówna. The Life and Achievements of a Polish Literary Translator
records.abstract: Helena Hellerówna, a Polish interwar literary translator, was born in Cracow on February 27th, 1899, and died as a U.S. citizen in New York on June 25th, 1978, under the name Helen Antonia Atlas. She translated, among others, awarded works (e.g. Fiancée d'Avril by Guy Chantepleure or Le repos de Bacchus by Pierre Boileau) and recognised authors (e.g. André Maurois, François Mauriac, or Maria Peteani) frequently signing as Hel Hel or H.H. Her career was interrupted by WWII, during which Hellerówna became a victim of the Holocaust. Her contribution to the Polish translation community has been largely forgotten, to the point where even the Polish National Library has no accurate information …

records.title: Reciprocal binding in Adyghe and Kabardian and the ban on ergative anaphors
records.abstract: According to a High Absolutive analysis of syntactic ergativity, grammatical operations can target intransitive subjects and transitive objects, distinguishing them from transitive subjects, because the former move to a position higher than the latter. A prediction that results from this theory is that an absolutive DP can bind an anaphoric ergative argument as a consequence of moving to a position that c-commands it. While it has been shown that this prediction is not borne out by facts across a range of syntactically ergative languages (Anderson, 1976; Brodkin & Royer, To Appear), reciprocal sentences in Adyghe and Kabardian (Northwest Caucasian) appear to be an exception. The …

records.title: English kinship terms: From taboo to syntax
records.abstract: English-speaking children rarely address parents by first name – a social prohibition encoding power and solidarity. Separately, English kinship terms like Mom and Dad permit bare singular use (Mom called) where other count nouns don’t (*Neighbour called). Nobody has connected these facts. I argue that the naming taboo causes the proper-name-like syntax: high-frequency use of kinship terms in vocative position – forced by the prohibition on first names – produces grammaticalization toward strong proper-name status. Corpus data from CHILDES confirm that parent terms show disproportionate vocative concentration (16–43%) compared to extended kin terms (4–7%). A careful category/function …

records.title: The Internal Structure of R-Loci: Index–Reference Alignment in Sign Languages
records.abstract: This paper proposes a structural reanalysis of R-loci in sign languages as syntactic objects with internal structure that underlie verbal argument positions. I argue that every R-locus consists of two distinct components—an index slot and a reference slot—and that argument licensing follows from the systematic specification of these components rather than from agreement, pronominal elements, or post-syntactic discourse inference. On this basis, I introduce 'Locus-Checking' as a uniform syntactic operation that aligns partially specified R-loci in order to license verbal arguments. The proposal accounts for apparent agreement effects, null arguments, generic interpretations, and first-person …

records.title: A Gradient Framework for Connotative Meaning: Weak Entailments and Conventionalization
records.abstract: This paper challenges the traditional lexical-encyclopedic dichotomy in formal semantics by proposing that linguistic meaning and world-knowledge exist on a gradient of conventionalization rather than forming categorically distinct types of knowledge. Through an analysis of entailment strength and intersubjective agreement patterns, I argue that the field's persistent failure to theorize connotative meaning stems from systematically conflating two distinct phenomena: cultural connotation (systematic, community-level patterns that generate weak entailments) and private connotation (idiosyncratic, individual associations). Drawing on evidence from semantic prosody research, arbitrariness of …

records.title: Contrastive Wa Operates on Outlooks
records.abstract: This paper argues that Japanese contrastive wa is best analyzed as a 'part-time' outlook marker: a discourse-level downtoner that replaces a stronger, salient update proposal with a weaker alternative, and whose stance effects arise only when the prejacent expresses a subjective judgment. The 'ignorance' or concessive implications typically associated with it is derived pragmatically from its basic discourse function: acknowledging a stronger candidate while asserting only a weaker one. We present a formal analysis couched in Farkas and Bruce's Table model: a wa-sentence is alternative-sensitive and presupposes a stronger proposition on the Table that entails that the predicate …

records.title: A Knowledge-Based Language Model: Deducing Grammatical Knowledge in a Multi-Agent Language Acquisition Simulation
records.abstract: This paper presents an initial study performed by the MODOMA system. The MODOMA is a computational multi-agent laboratory environment for unsupervised language acquisition experiments such that acquisition is based on the interaction between two language models, an adult and a child agent. Although this framework employs statistical as well as rule-based procedures, the result of language acquisition is a knowledge-based language model, which can be used to generate and parse new utterances of the target language. This system is fully parametrized and researchers can control all aspects of the experiments while the results of language acquisition, that is, the acquired grammatical …

records.title: THE LEGEND OF PoS
records.abstract: The Poverty-of-Stimulus (PoS) argument is central to Universal Grammar (UG). UG is central for Generative grammars. Without UG no Generative grammars; without PoS no UG. Arguments based on PoS are flawed; UG is dispensable: Every grammar exists by the grace of its own learnability. This follows from the cognitive evolution of grammars.

records.title: Probabilistic non-maximality
records.abstract: In this paper, I present a probabilistic reconstruction of Križ’s (2015, 2016) account of non-maximal interpretation. The proposal addresses a general problem noted by Križ (2015: 85–6), which is shared by other QUD-based approaches to non-maximality (e.g. Bar-Lev 2021; Križ & Spector 2021): for these accounts to work, one needs to posit a fundamental disconnect between the question that is asked and the QUD that is addressed. This is problematic, especially in the absence of a non-stipulative method for identifying the QUD that is being addressed in a given context. In the proposed framework, the overt question alone determines the relevant QUD, allowing non-maximal interpretations to be …

records.title: Algorithmic Etymology via Skeletal Reconstruction
records.abstract: We present a deterministic algorithm for reconstructing Proto-Indo-European etymologies from attested daughter language forms. The Barnaby Protocol operates through systematic skeletal extraction and progressive filtering using established sound laws, morphological patterns, and comparative method principles.
