records.abstract: This paper studies how lexical variation differs across the main dialect zones of the Kazakh language. I use survey data from 40 native speakers in Southern, Western, and Northeastern regions of Kazakhstan, where participants provided word choices for everyday objects. Our results show that the Southern dialect displays the widest variation and frequent Russian borrowings, the Northeastern dialect is the most consistent with limited variation, and the Western dialect stands out as the most distinct with unique lexical items. I also find that 80% of participants report experiencing misunderstandings due to regional vocabulary differences

records.title: Code-Switching Sentence Processing in Bilingual Adults
records.abstract: This study explores how code-switching affects sentence comprehension and reading speed in bilingual adults. Forty participants, fluent in English and Urdu, completed a self-paced reading task with sentences containing code-switched elements and fully monolingual sentences. Results showed that reading code-switched sentences took longer, while comprehension accuracy remained largely unchanged. These findings suggest that bilinguals can manage dual-language activation effectively, maintaining understanding even when cognitive load increases. The study provides insights into bilingual sentence processing and has implications for both theoretical linguistics and applied language studies.

records.title: Converging and diverging variations in metaphorization of light verbs: A corpus study on four Chinese speech communities
records.abstract: [published in Proceedings of PACLIC-39: 200–214, https://aclanthology.org/2025.paclic-1.17/ ] Metaphorization is a robust semantic process that underpins the development of grammatical categories and associated language variation and change. This study adopts a process-based approach to investigate variations in metaphorical extension of five common light verbs from different lexical sources in four Chinese speech communities: jiyu “GIVE”, yu “GIVE”, jia “ADD”, gan “WORK HARD”, and nong “FIDDLE”. Drawing on longitudinal (1995-2016) and latitudinal (Hong Kong, Taiwan, Beijing, Shanghai) data from the Pan-Chinese corpus LIVAC ( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LIVAC_Synchronous_Corpus ), we …

records.title: Ende oration and final /n/-realisation
records.abstract: This paper presents a sociophonetic analysis of word-final /n/-elision in Ende (Pahoturi River; Papuan). An analysis of 73 speakers reveals that tense, phonological context, and most significantly, whether or not the speaker is a kawa practitioner, a prestigious type of public oration, are significantly correlated with /n/-retention. A closer look at just five kawa practitioners reveals that age and genre may also play a role. The present study matches Schokkin’s analysis of /n/-elision in Idi (this issue). Indeed, the findings support her conclusions that this pattern is one of /n/-elision (not /n/-addition) and show similarities in conditioning factors. Analysing sociolinguistic variation …

records.title: Kawa and the variable stopping of obstruents in Ende
records.abstract: This paper details a study investigating sociophonetic variation in Ende, a language spoken in Papua New Guinea. The study examines speech produced by 30 individuals, investigating what social and linguistic factors are linked with the variable alternation between stopped and affricated realizations of Ende retroflex obstruents [ʈ͡ʂ~ʈ] and [ɖ͡ʐ~ɖ]. Our analysis provides evidence that the obstruents in question are more likely to be realized as stops when they are voiced and when the speakers are orators. Orators are people who practice kawa, a long-standing practice whereby select individuals perform regular public orations. Among orators, the speaker’s age also appears to play a role in …

records.title: The Ende way: Short stories and songs from Limol prepared with the Ende Language Committee
records.abstract: This collection of Ende stories and songs contains 20 texts from the Ende Language Corpus, a repository of Ende language and culture. The texts were compiled by the Ende Language Committee and represent a diverse set of authors, illustrators, and translators from the community. Each text is accompanied by a summary, contextual background, and presented in two formats: a running text format in parallel with an English translation, and an interlinearized format with English translations at the morpheme and sentence levels. The texts cover a broad slice of Ende life and are organized into five thematic parts: Animal Tales and Origin Stories, Tales of Hunting and Survival, Heroic or Legendary …

records.title: The Pahoturi River language family, with special reference to its verbal puzzles
records.abstract: This profile of the Pahoturi River language family of southern Papua New Guinea draws from extensive fieldwork on Idi [ISO 639-3: idi] and Ende [kit] – two of six varieties comprising this family – and brief surveying of the other four, which we illustrate in print for the first time. We present the first typological treatment of Pahoturi River in pursuit of shining more light on this understudied corner of the linguistic landscape. This profile is organized into two parts: first, we present sections on the basic structures and systems of Pahoturi River, illustrated with examples from across the family and supplemented with descriptions of Idi and Ende as relevant. From our preliminary data …

records.title: The syntax of adverbial clauses in Persian
Tropes and Events as Truthmakers
records.abstract: This is the appendix of Chapter 2 of my book Abstract Objects and the Semantics of Natural Language, Oxford University Press, Oxford, 2013,p. 89-94. This piece is of particular interest because it discusses the role of events and tropes as potential truthmakers at a time prior to the development of Kit Fine's truthmaker semantics, making use of an older, metaphysical notion of truthmaking (grounding the truth of sentences in things in the world). Chapter 2 itself made use of a Davidsonian view of events and tropes, and thus not as truthmakers. A prepublication version of the book itself can be found on this page: http://www.friederike-moltmann.com/books/

records.title: Differentiating between generic and actualized eventualities in Alashkert Armenian
records.abstract: This paper investigates two structures of imperfective aspect in Alashkert Armenian, where ongoing and habitual events are distinguished from states and dispositions (generic habituals). Alashkert Armenian exhibits two imperfective structures. An aux-containing k-imperfective can describe an ongoing habitual event and an ongoing event, while an aux-less k-imperfective describes states and dispositions (generic habituals that do not need to be actualized). We analyze this distinction as stemming from two different modalities associated with the imperfective aspect: progressive and generic. The paper provides a novel and unified analysis of the k-imperfective and captures the semantic …

records.title: The semantic composition of event counting expressions within nominals in Mandarin Chinese
records.abstract: Event counting expressions like three times are often thought of as adverbial modifiers of a verbal projection. This study establishes and analyzes an apparently related but puzzling phenomenon in Mandarin Chinese whereby an event counting expression consisting of a numeral and an event classifier is introduced within a nominal syntactic argument to a verb, that also contains a thematic nominal. Closely examining the relevant interpretive properties, I show that such constituents are able to express counts of events independently of composition with the verb. Moreover, the phenomenon should be understood to reflect a close syntax-semantic parallelism between event classifiers and individual …

records.title: Phonetic evidence for contextual underspecification of nasality in A’ingae
records.abstract: Vowels are often nasalized in [VN] sequences. Cohn (1993a) argued that contextually nasalized vowels in English are unspecified for nasality, and are phonetically nasalized through coarticulation. In contrast, Solé (1995) argued that contextual nasalization is so extensive in English that nasalized vowels must be phonologically [+NASAL]. This disagreement reflects a broader problem: how do we determine the phonological specification of segments with phonetically intermediate values for nasality (or other properties)? We contribute to this debate with data from A'ingae, a language spoken in the Ecuadorian and Colombian Amazon. A'ingae has a /V Ṽ/ contrast, along with left-to-right, …

records.title: Discourse structure and the reorganisation of the Icelandic aspectual system
records.abstract: Icelandic is commonly considered a conservative language. While this claim holds true for its morphology, especially in the broader Germanic perspective, one area that has undergone considerable changes since the 16th century is the mapping between syntax and discourse structure. In this paper, I will argue that otherwise puzzling facts from the history of the language can be better understood if one takes this shift in discourse structuring as fundamental. While most research to date has focused on a limited set of syntactic phenomena, I bring new data to bear on this question: the emergence of two aspectual markers, the búinn-perfect and the vera að-progressive. I trace the shift in …

records.title: Less is more when more is more than more: A Nanosyntactic analysis of Mandarin duōshǎo
records.abstract: Mandarin duōshǎo ‘how much’ is a question word/phrase with remarkable prop- erties: the degree question marker duō ‘how’ is syncretic with the quantifier duō ‘much’, and the quantifier part shǎo is, elsewhere, equivalent to English little. Adopting a Nanosyntactic approach, we propose a homophone-free structural analysis of duōshǎo ‘how much’ that relates the two properties.

records.title: Revisiting definiteness: Insights from two types of definite articles in Tihami Arabic
records.abstract: Recent studies have examined the semantic typology of definiteness, focusing on languages that have two types of definite articles in typologically unrelated languages (e.g., Schwarz 2009, 2013, 2019; Jenks 2015). Analyses of these languages suggest that one definite article encodes only uniqueness, while the other includes an anaphoric component. This study presents data from Tihami Arabic, which has two definite articles, im- and al-, challenging this conventional dichotomy of definiteness. Instead, the two definites in Tihami align with Löbner’s (1985, 2011) classification of uniqueness, which distinguishes between inherent and context-derived uniqueness. While al- occurs with nouns that …

records.title: A Formal Theory of Definition
records.abstract: This paper presents a formal theory of definition based on the fundamental distinction between a conceptual space ($C$), containing thinkable concepts, and an experiential space ($E$), containing empirical entities. We formalize the notion of a definiendum ($\text{definiendum} \in C$) and its dependency set ($\text{dependencies} \subseteq C \cup E$). Definitions are classified into three types: analytical (precise, linguistic, establishing $C-C$ relations), exemplary (linguistic examples, inductive, establishing $C-C$ relations), and ostensive (empirical pointing, inductive, establishing $C-E$ relations). We introduce the concept of a definition system ($\mathcal{S}$) as a set of …

records.title: Quotative inversion as smuggling: Evidence from Setswana and English
records.abstract: Quotative inversion (QI) clauses in Setswana and English – two SVO languages – show a marked OVS word order in which a quote appears preverbally and the agentive external argument appears postverbally. In this paper, I present empirical evidence from both languages showing that the preverbal quotative subject moves to its landing site via A-movement, while the agentive subject remains in-situ. While moving an internal argument to an A-position above an external argument may seem to pose a minimality problem, I show that QI constructions are best conceived of as smuggling derivations in which the internal argument is moved over the external argument via the movement of a larger constituent …

records.title: Multiple probes and feature deletion in the Tira agreement complex
records.abstract: In this paper we show that the exponents of agreement in Tira are the realization of two separate probes, one on C, which targets DP topics, and another on T, sensitive to just pronouns. Obligatory T-to- C movement results in the realization of both probes on a single complex head. We show that two separate morphological deletion operations conceal the faithful realization of the 𝜑-features copied by these probes. The first deletes the features on T when they are identical to those on C, an instance of Kinyalolo’s Constraint (Kinyalolo 1991, a.o.). The second is characterized by the preferential realization of object features over subject features, an apparent instance of Expone Outermost …

records.title: Subjunctive Mood in Tigrinya
records.abstract: The goal of this squib is to contribute to a better understanding of subjunctive mood by providing novel data on the understudied Ethio-semitic language Tigrinya (SOV, Eritrea and northern Ethiopia). I suggest that the clausal prefix kɨ-, that is selected by many different verb classes and is used to build several different constructions, is a subjunctive marker. I support this idea by presenting a varied amount of data that shows that kɨ- appears (for the most part) in contexts that trigger subjunctive mood in other languages.

records.title: Downstep in Kikuyu
records.abstract: The Bantu language Kikuyu, spoken in Kenya, exhibits the tonal phenomenon known as downstep, which shows several exceptional characteristics. While downstep in other Bantu languages generally lowers high tones, Kikuyu downstep has the rare property of lowering both high and low tones. Moreover, this lowering mechanism serves as an indicator of phrase boundaries, as it appears at the edge of a prosodic constituent. Since, from a typological perspective, downstep usually occurs within a prosodic constituent, its occurrence at the boundary is particularly noteworthy.

records.title: Root Duality: Unifying Indexical Identity and Computational Anchoring
records.abstract: This paper analyzes the study of root properties in constructional morphology, examining the multilingual process of complex word construction. Building on Belder & Craenenbroeck (2015), which characterizes the essence of roots as the “empty position” created by initial Merge-driven displacement, the paper presents a systematic analysis and argues that roots exhibit a dual nature as both indexical units and computational anchors.

records.title: Formality weakening and the underspecified expressive 'yo' in Korean
records.abstract: The repeated use of expressives in general gives rise to a strengthening effect referred to as repeatability (Potts 2007). The notion of repeatability, however, requires further scrutiny. Unlike other formality-denoting expressives, medial 'yo's in Korean show an uncommon pattern of behavior: the more 'yo's you have, the less sense of formality you get. Adopting many of the concepts introduced in Potts (2005, 2007) and McCready (2019), I offer a formal analysis of how a repeated use of an expressive can weaken its expressive content. Further, medial 'yo's can only be realized in the presence of another formality marker, such as '(su)pni.' The findings of this work suggest that there are …

records.title: Where is register? Deriving grammatical free variation within one single grammar
records.abstract: This study offers an analysis of the modal and register dimensions of the analytical/synthetic alternation in the Spanish future/conditional to the effect of showing that grammatical free variation in the register dimension can be modeled within one single grammar as part of the core linguistic knowledge any speaker is competent with. This is particularly reasonable in a multidimensional semantic framework according to which register pertains to the semantic agenda in its own right. In the theory favored in this paper, different meaning dimensions have different derivational paths, with truth-conditional meaning standardly derived in the syntax-LF interface, and register, in the way from …

records.title: The slur-epithet direction: the case of Italian
records.abstract: We offer a new empirical argument from Italian in favor of the thesis that epithets (both in simple and bi-nominal configurations) contain an indexical ingredient. The argument is based on the observation that Italian, unlike other Romance languages like Spanish, forces the use of weak demonstratives with epithets. We show that the use of these demonstratives correlates with the presence of a variety of empty nominal anaphora constructions. Epithets, then, form a natural class with this variety; concretely, they contain an empty noun headed by an index. Slurs, instead, are regular nominal heads in the extended projections of DPs or related nominal phrases. Consequently, they are compatible …

records.title: The impact of interaction on Zinacantec Family Homesign
records.abstract: Emerging sign languages provide the opportunity to observe the process by which signers create and converge on a lexicon. Some studies report that emerging sign languages exhibit more lexical and sub-lexical variation than their longer-established counterparts, which has been interpreted as evidence for a lack of conventionalization. However, a growing body of recent literature takes the view that this variation is not random but rather shaped by the social organization of the signing community. The present study aims to test the hypothesis that variation is conditioned by frequency of interaction, focusing on Zinacantec Family Homesign (‘Z sign’), a sign language developed over the past …

records.title: Listener Driven Sound Change in Exemplar Theory
records.abstract: This paper presents a formal model to derive both gradient and categorical behaviors in listener-driven sound change. As a case study, I model the development of opposing acoustic trajectories of high vowels before labials in SE Bulgarian, where *i > u, and Polabian, where *u > i. By encoding different listener expectations into my model of labial co-articulation, I am able to derive both change, like SE Bulgarian and Polabian, and stability. In order to simulate the observed behaviors, I embed a Harmonic Grammar (Flemming 2001, Katz 2010, Burns 2021) in an Exemplar Theory (Pierrehumbert 2001) framework. My model suggests that while systems where interlocutors are aligned in their …

records.title: Monograph : 'Speaking Brains' (A Summary)
records.abstract: The arguments herein are that a hybrid AI model is needed to replicate human thought, combining local-domain connectionist models (neural nets) with distant-domain symbolic models (rule-based reasoning). His recent research bridges theoretical linguistics and neuroscience to investigate how the brain processes language, with a particular focus on the roles of the basal ganglia and astrocytes. He compares these neural mechanisms to artificial intelligence (AI) models, arguing that biology provides a more complete model for understanding recursive language functions.

records.title: Reconstruction and linearization in wh-movement of DPs
records.abstract: This paper argues that reconstruction for variable binding in wh-movement (e.g., Which picture of herself1 did every girl1 find?) should be analyzed fully on a par with pied-piping (e.g., whose book did John read?), and pied-piping, in turn, should be analyzed as consisting of two separate steps of movement: one semantically consequential step of movement that feeds question semantics, and one semantically vacuous step of movement the purpose of which is to simply pronounce a wh-containing constituent in the left periphery. When such a view of pied-piping is married with a view of movement which makes room for loosening the constraints on it, the result is what is usually described as …

records.title: From Clefts to Definiteness in Bangla and Beyond
records.abstract: I provide empirical support for the claim that the definiteness of a DP can be decomposed into an existential quantifier and a cleft operator attached to the restrictor of this quantifier. As empirical evidence, I provide novel data from Bangla, where exactly the kind of DPs that otherwise do not allow a definite reading suddenly allows a definite reading when a cleft morpheme is put on top of them. I point out how this account is similar to and different from other decompositional accounts of definites and the consequences of this new account for the English data that motivated the other decompositional accounts.

records.title: Belief or Action? Semantic Ambiguity in the Italian Non-finite Domain
records.abstract: This paper examines the belief/intention semantic alternation found in Italian clause-embedding verbs like 'convincere' ('convince'), a phenomenon that is typically attributed to finiteness or mood (Giannakidou & Mari 2021, Grano 2018, 2024). Interestingly, Italian exhibits this alternation within its non-finite domain: di-infinitives convey belief readings, while a-infinitives give rise to intention readings. We argue that this semantic distinction corresponds directly to the structural size of the complement clauses. Syntactic evidence shows that di-infinitives project larger structures, accommodating modal auxiliaries and allowing both subject and object control, consistent with a …

records.title: Nasality and Voicing
records.abstract: Nasality and voicing have traditionally been treated as distinct phonological categories. The Unified Voicing and Nasality Hypothesis (UVNH) posits that both are phonetic manifestations of a single representational unit. Cross-linguistic phonetic and phonological research has shown that nasality and voicing frequently co-occur and interact in processes such as postnasal voicing assimilation, spontaneous prenasalisation, and intervocalic velar nasalization. Such phenomena are observed in diverse languages including Japanese, Greek, Asháninka, and Rotokas. Phonetically, a shared perceptual basis has been suggested in that voicing and nasality both enhance the low-frequency energy in the …

records.title: Theoretical Approaches to Comparative Syntax
records.abstract: Human languages vary in the ways phrases and clauses can be constructed from their building blocks, i.e. their grammatical features, morphemes, and words. The goal of comparative syntax is to discover not only the areas where languages differ, but also where they are the same, i.e. to discover the building blocks and principles that all human languages have in common. Accordingly, a theoretical model of the human language faculty should explain both the range and limits of syntactic variation, as they can be found both across and within languages. The aim of this chapter is to review a selection of closely related generative approaches to this question, with a particular focus on two broad …

records.title: Expletive negation in Italian temporal clauses: an acceptability judgement and a self-paced reading study
records.abstract: This work aims to investigate the role of negation when it fails to reverse the polarity of a sentence, thus becoming“expletive”. An example is o ered by the following Italian sentence: Chiara è rimasta in casa finché Marco non ha chiamato la pizzeria per la cena (literally‘Chiara remained in the house until Marco did not call the pizzeria for dinner’, meaning‘Chiara remained at home until Marco called the pizzeria for dinner’). Although negation occurs, the sentence remains a rmative, and the negative marker fails to trigger all the semantic and syntactic phenomena usually associated with it. Here we implement two experiments, an acceptability judgement task and a self-paced reading …

records.title: Situations, Situation-like Entities, and and their Composition
records.abstract: These are the handouts of my (hybrid) course on situations (and related entities) in fall 2025. Here the course description: In this hybrid course, we will discuss conceptions of situations and similar entities (states, states of affairs, events, tropes, and facts) and their roles in the semantics of natural language. We will discuss the various semantic roles of situations and similar entities in situation-based semantic approaches, in particular truthmaker semantics, and how those roles bear on the ontology of those entities. We will particularly focus on the part-whole structure of entities, taking into account recent research on the metaphysics of relations, ontological dependence, and …

records.title: A structural ambiguity account for non-local allomorphy and *ABA violations using complex affixes
records.abstract: Locality is considered a core condition on application of Vocabulary Insertion rules (Embick 2010; Bobaljik 2012). The evidence comes from adjacency requirements on contextual allomorphy and *ABA generalizations in various morphological domains. Both have been met with counterexamples (Moskal & Smith 2016; Ganenkov 2020; Dolatian & Guekguezian 2023; Ganenkov 2018; Middleton 2021; Davis 2021; Zompì 2023; Caha 2024b among others). The proposal of this paper rests on the idea of complex affix formation (Bobaljik 2012; Matushansky 2025): functional heads forming a constituent in exclusion of the terminal that undergoes allomorphy via base-generation. Based on a novel explicit formalization of a …

records.title: Perfective allomorphy and negative neutralisation in Bambara: a nanosyntactic approach
records.abstract: Bambara (Mande) displays perfective (henceforth PFV) allomorphy conditioned by transitivity properties of the verbal predicate. The allomorphy is neutralised under negation (NEG). I present an analysis of these data in Nanosyntax (Starke 2009, Caha 2009), which relies on the size of lexically stored items (Starke 2014). The PFV allomorphy is accounted for by proposing that the lexical structure of the intransitive PFV marker "-ra" has its bottom feature in VOICE, while the transitive PFV "ye" has a lexical structure with a bottom feature that sits higher in the structure, i.e. in ASP. Negative neutralisation follows naturally from the proposal, if one adopts a low position in syntax for …

records.title: A perfect-like stative: Icelandic 'búinn að' and pragmatic competition in the aspectual domain
records.abstract: Modern Icelandic has two “perfects”: hafa ‘have’ (a canonical HAVE-perfect) and búinn. The latter is younger, gaining an aspectual, perfect-like usage in the 16th century. Prior to this point it is attested as an adjectival participle meaning ‘ready, prepared’, derived from the verb búa ‘reside, prepare, adorn’, subsequently undergoing a meaning shift from ‘ready, prepared’ to ‘finished’ (Thráinsson 2017). In the modern language, búinn has a more restricted distribution than hafa, especially for some predicate classes (Jónsson 1992). The aims of this paper are twofold. Firstly, I provide an account of búinn in modern Icelandic, accounting for these selectional restrictions. Secondly, …

records.title: Specificity and “Non-Derived Environment Blocking” in Logical Phonology
records.abstract: Despite Inkelas' (2000) instinct that such an analysis "would be far-fetched and uninsightful" I show how appeal to underspecification accounts for Turkish velar deletion with a simple, albeit counterintuitive, narrow phonological solution couched in Logical Phonology (LP). Components of the LP approach are introduced via discussion of Finnish assibilation, which, like the Turkish pattern, has also been discussed in terms of "non-derived environment blocking." New version has very minor corrections.

records.title: Alethic modality and dative-infinitive structures
records.abstract: I discuss the meaning of the Russian dative-infinitive construction and argue that it expresses a single kind of modality in indicative sentences, notably — alethic modality. There is no need to split this construction in the indicative mood and ascribe different categorical meanings to its varieties.

records.title: Parasitic Participles in Faroese as Auxiliary Omission
records.abstract: The relationship between auxiliaries and verbal inflection has been a debated issue in syntactic theory since Chomsky (1957) and contemporary theories disagree on whether to analyze the facts through a combination of syntactic selection and merger or head displacement (Halle and Marantz 1993, Lansik 1995, Harwood 2014) or in terms of inflection-as-agreement (Adger 2003, Bjorkman 2011, Wurmbrand 2012). An important argument for inflection-as-agreement comes from parasitic morphology in the Germanic languages. This paper presents a novel case of parasitic morphology in which the auxiliary HAVE itself can take vacuous inflection as predicted by inflectionas-agreement accounts. This kind of …

records.title: Two ways to be non-inertial: frustrativity and event maximality in O'dam
records.abstract: This paper examines two frustrative markers in O'dam, which signal counter-to-expectation effects in different ways. Where existing accounts of frustrativity (e.g., Copley & Harley 2014, Davis & Matthewson 2016, 2022, Kroeger 2017, 2024) treat the phenomenon as purely propositional, we draw on new data from O'dam showing that the non-inertial effects of frustratives can interact with semantic structure both above and below the clause level. We propose that weak frustrativity in O'dam corresponds to a weakly non-inertial commitment by the speaker (i.e., that the evaluation world is in some way atypical), while strong frustrativity combines a weakly non-inertial presupposition with a …

records.title: Reanalyzing frustration: event maximality and inertia in two O'dam frustratives
records.abstract: Frustrative particles modify a clause by conveying the non-realization of an associated expectation. The semantics of frustrativity are relatively understudied, complicated by variation in whether the relationship between the marked clause and the ‘target’ of frustration is lexically or only pragmatically specified. We contribute to the emerging picture by reporting on O’dam, which is typologically unusual in having two contrastive frustratives: t1i and t1ipup. Where most existing analyses treat frustratives as clausal markers of non-inertia, we argue that O’dam frustratives are also sensitive to event-based non-maximality. We propose a unified approach on which the differences are derived …

records.title: Presuppositionless proxies of politeness: An (eventually) Optimality-Theoretic account
records.abstract: TL;DR: Wang (2023) but with Optimality Theory and with a much more comprehensive set of proxies and proxands. Presuppositionlessness, proxies, and politeness are what this dissertation is all about. This dissertation concerns those linguistic forms termed polite pronouns. They convey one particular aspect of social identity: the social distance between language users, where a large social distance mandates the expression of politeness. Most existing work on polite pronouns has modeled polite meaning via dedicated grammatical mechanisms, such as a dedicated feature ([HON], Ackema & Neeleman 2016) or a dedicated dimension of meaning (McCready 2019). This dissertation shows that such dedicated …

records.title: Optimising Daylight for Human Wellbeing: in Appenzell Innerhoden & Ausserhoden
records.abstract: Daylight plays a central role in human health and wellbeing. Beyond allowing us to see, it reg- ulates our circadian rhythm, mood, alertness, and cognitive function. In mountainous regions like Appenzell (Innerhoden and Ausserhoden), traditional tall houses and complex topographies present unique daylight challenges. This project proposes a novel Fuzzy-AI daylight simulation framework to evaluate and optimise daylight penetration into residential spaces under variable seasonal and weather conditions. The study aims to provide window design guidelines that maximise daylight exposure, preserve architectural heritage, and promote occupant wellbeing.

records.title: Derivational Affixes as Heads and Phrases: Evidence from Turkish Diminutives
records.abstract: Recently the Distributed Morphology literature hosted two strands of debates regarding the status of derivational affixes. One main strand has been the root versus functional head status of derivational affixes. While Marantz (1997) and Marvin (2002) (among others) treated derivational affixes as functional heads, Lowenstamm (2014) and De Belder (2011) argued that they are acategorial roots. On the other hand, Creemers, Don, and Fenger (2018) argued that some affixes are roots and others are functional heads. The second strand of discussion has been the head versus modifier status of affixes in general. Wiltschko and Steriopolo (2007) showed that some affixes are heads whereas others are …

records.title: DEMYSTIFYING ERGATIVITY
records.abstract: Facts fall in place and form a coherent picture once myths have been dispelled. Descriptions of ergativity are fraught with grammatical myths. Strikingly, the puzzlement dissolves into nothingness as soon as one is willing to acknowledge the origin of the mystifications, that is, the confusion of subjects and objects (by functionalist typologists as well as by Generativist syntacticians). [v. 1.4: slightly revised].

records.title: A history of prenominal passive participles in English: from resultatives to eventives
records.abstract: This article aims to explain how passive participles used as prenominal modifiers developed their eventive nature throughout the history of English. It is argued that prenominal participles first expressed stative result states in Old English (OE) and came to express perfect result states later on. The locus of required resultativity in participles was the inner aspect head in OE, while in Early Middle English (EME), it shifted to the outer aspect head. This shift was triggered by the loss of OE aspectual prefixes, which generally functioned to perfectivize or transitivize the verb by affecting its (internal) argument and assigning a change-of-state meaning to the verb. This shift rendered …

records.title: Mirror Principle and Split VoiceP: Evidence from Mongolian and Japanese
records.abstract: This paper demonstrates that the layered affixation of passive and causative morphemes in Mongolian and Japanese mirrors the Split VoiceP structure of passive and causative clauses, where the affixation of a voice suffix signals the introduction of an argument by a voice head spelled out by that suffix. This head-argument correlation, ensuring the morpho-syntax mirroring of voice suffixes, entails that the voice domain comprises separate projections that are split out of VoiceP. Clauses are built by introducing arguments as potential subjects (sbjs) through voice heads of the same substance, where a last-introduced sbj is promoted to the nominative position, with others, if any, remaining …

records.title: Passivization by Voice: A Merge-Based Approach
Who am I to (dis)agree? Interpretation Sensitive Agreement: Experimental evidence from French relatives
records.abstract: Agreement morphology is often assumed to realize phi-features uninterpreted at LF. We provide experimental evidence from French relative clauses showing that agreement can in fact have an interpretative effect, adding to the range of `semantic agreement' effects (e.g. Charnavel-Sportiche:2025: https://ling.auf.net/lingbuzz/009362). The choice of variable person agreement turns out to be sensitive to the placement of focus. We provide an analysis that relies on the interaction between focus, binding and the distribution of focus-sensitive operators.

records.title: Meaningful agreement features: evidence from indexical binding
records.abstract: We discuss the semantic import of number and person agreement features (on T, but with wider relevance to other agreeing head probes). We first illustrate that number/person features on T can encode a presupposition about the subject’s denotation. We then discuss the licensing interaction between agreement and indexical binding in French and English (documenting new restrictions on its availability) to support the hypothesis that person agreement can (and perhaps must) have semantic import.

records.title: Gender agreement mismatch in sandwiched coordination
records.abstract: This paper reports on an experimental study on noun-verb agreement in so-called sandwiched configurations, where a coordinated subject (Goal) is situated between two participles (Probes). As reported by Marušič & Nevins (2020), in such configurations, the two conjuncts of a coordinate subject control agreement with different probes, each one with the linearly closest probe – the first conjunct with the probe preceding the subject and the second conjunct with the probe following the subject. This study, in addition, confirms that two participles show agreement with the single, hierarchically highest conjunct, as well as having the first probe reflecting gender features of the closest …

records.title: On the binary format of functional features
records.abstract: In this paper, I argue that the features of functional categories universally conform to a specific equipollent binary format that I will call the Contrary Format, to distinguish it from the more usual Contradictory Format that is usually and implicitly assumed in equipollent binary +/– features or unary features. The term ‘contrary’ adopts Horn’s (1989) distinction between contrary and contradictory negation. To borrow an image, while contradictory values oppose black and white, contrary values oppose white (or black) to every shade of gray. I argue that the Contrary Format functions as a necessary condition for the types of concepts that are expressed as functional categories, and that …

records.title: Reconstructing phonology: A modest proposal
records.abstract: The present work argues that research in the reconstruction of phonologies of the past, particularly that of pre-historical phonologies, is often based more on phantasy than argument from evidence. It offers a compact survey of common sources of argument appealed to, and their frequent misuse, and other abuses. The focus is on the earlier history of English, the language the study of whose history I am most familiar with, but which is not exclusively or, of course, comprehensively addressed here. I am not, unfortunately, an anglo-philologist. The survey highlights successive misinterpretations of the relation between phonology and phonetics and between phonology and writing, involving …

records.title: A′-movement restrictions in Igbo reanalyzed
records.abstract: This paper provides a novel analysis for A'-extraction bans in Igbo clauses which involve a preverbal harmonizing morpheme E/A. We argue that clauses with E/A which ban extraction involve a CP-layer, which is in competition with the layer required in A'-movement. Our analysis of E/A accounts for its co-occurrence with A'-extraction restrictions, and also predicts when its appearance does not correspond with an A'-extraction restriction. We point to several systematic differences between clauses which do and do not permit extraction including their compatibility with subjunctives and the distribution of clitic and non-clitic subjects. Our analysis brings Igbo in line with a broader …

records.title: Reflexes of Proto-Algonquian initial *t in Blackfoot
records.abstract: Blackfoot has long been labelled “divergent” with respect to the rest of the Algonquian family because of its lexical differences (Voegelin 1941: 506) and phonological innovations (Goddard 1994b: 187).1 Even fairly recent studies of Blackfoot historical phonology propose a number of unusual sound changes (Berman 2006; Proulx 1989). This paper focuses on one such sound change in by Berman (2006), who argued that Proto-Algonquian (PA) word-initial *t becomes k in Blackfoot on the basis of three reconstructions. This paper uses multiple methodologies to examine these three reconstructions in detail, including comparative evidence with other Algonquian languages, historical evidence from older …

records.title: Generation Space Size: Understanding and Calibrating Open-Endedness of LLM Generations
records.abstract: Different open-ended generation tasks require different degrees of output diversity. However, current LLMs are often miscalibrated. They collapse to overly homogeneous outputs for creative tasks and hallucinate diverse but incorrect responses for factual tasks. We argue that these two failure modes are unified by, and can both be addressed by, the notion of effective generation space size (GSS) -- the set of semantically distinct outputs a model considers for a prompt. We present GSSBench, a task suite of prompt pairs with ground-truth GSS relationships to assess different metrics and understand where models diverge from desired behavior. We find that hallucination detection metrics, …

records.title: Language as a Stack of Homeostatic Property-Cluster Kinds: From Phonemes to Constructions
records.abstract: This paper develops two operational diagnostics~-- projectibility and homeostasis~-- for deciding when linguistic categories warrant treatment as homeostatic property-cluster (HPC) kinds. Projectibility asks whether a category supports reliable out-of-sample inference; homeostasis asks whether identifiable mechanisms plausibly maintain the cluster over time and across instances. I apply these diagnostics to three structural levels. At the phoneme level I use PHOIBLE inventories to show family-wise concentration of inventory sizes and a scaling relation for the front-rounded vowel /y/; at the lexical level I trace diachronic distributional neighbourhoods to show that some lexemes drift while …

records.title: The Phonological Word: At the interface of lexical insertion, (morpho)syntax, and pronunciation
records.abstract: The phonological word serves as the domain for a variety of phenomena including stress assignment, minimality, phonotactic constraints, and phonological rules. The absence of word-level phenomena or conflicting criteria for the phonological word in certain languages has led some researchers to question its universal validity. An alternative perspective suggests that the phonological word may be understood within an interpretive view of phonology informed by lexical access in speech planning. At certain points in the syntactic derivation, lexical items are retrieved from long term storage and processed in the short-term memory Phonological Output Buffer (POB) preparatory to organisation at …

records.title: Defocus Rephrasing: Right dislocation and syntax-prosody mismatches
records.abstract: This study adopts a rigorous interface approach to investigate the role of defocus, the systematic lack of focus, in syntax-prosody mapping. Despite the abundance of work on focus prosody, how defocus may affect the mapping and whether its effects should be distinguished from those of focus remains relatively unknown. We argue that defocus can, and should in fact, be separated from focus for prosodic phrasing, drawing crucial support from right dislocation (RD) in Cantonese and Mandarin. In RD, elements are displaced or copied to the right of a sentence, a position that resists semantic, alternative-based focus. We show that although RD consists of two syntactic clauses, it only has one …

records.title: Metrical stress and glottal stops in A'ingae: A study of cyclicity and dominance at the interface of phonology and morphology
records.abstract: This dissertation presents a theoretically informed study of A'ingae (or Cofán, iso 639-3: con), an Amazonian language isolate spoken in Ecuador and Colombia. The first part of the dissertation is descriptive. In a chapter on phonology, I touch on the language's phonotactics, laryngeal agreement, diphthongal processes, recent sound changes, nasal spreading, as well as prosody and glottalization. In a chapter on morphosyntax, I describe the structure of A'ingae sentences, including matrix and (co)subordinate clauses, auxiliary verbs, serial verb constructions, WH-movement, and second-position clitics, as well as the morphology of A'ingae verbs, including the meanings of verbal morphemes and …

records.title: Allocutive agreement and indexicals Shift Together, but not always
records.abstract: This paper examines interactions between allocutive agreement and indexical shift, two phenomena that target contextual participants for morphological and semantic purposes in ways that crucially involve mediation by the syntax. This leads us to expect significant interactions between the two that should be instructive for our theoretical accounts of both. Based on a survey of the literature and novel data from Tamil, it is shown that this expectation is fulfilled. Prior work (Alok & Baker 2018, McFadden 2020) has identified a manifestion of the Shift Together constraint holding between shifted indexicals and shifted allocutive agreement in both Tamil and Magahi, supporting the idea that …

records.title: BAVARIAN COMPS – AS PLAIN AS SIMPLE
records.abstract: This is a squib on doubly-filled and on 'inflected' Comps and an exercise in dealing with a tight spot. The wide variety of doubly-filled Comps in Bavarian dialects plus a grammatically multifunctional element confuses analysts. The grammatical resolution is simple, the complication is “decision overload”. [typo-corrected in Fn.11].

records.title: When AI Speaks English: Marginalized Languages in Malaysia
records.abstract: This article investigates the sociolinguistic consequences of English-centric Artificial Intelligence (AI) models in multilingual Malaysia. As AI technologies integrate into daily life, their linguistic biases challenge non-Anglophone populations. Using a mixed-methods approach, this study examines AI performance disparities in English, Bahasa Malaysia, and Tamil. Findings reveal significant inadequacies in the models’ handling of local languages, with higher error rates in key tasks. These technical shortcomings translate into tangible social and economic burdens, creating digital inequality and reinforcing English hegemony. We argue this technological linguistic marginalization functions …

records.title: Notes on Numeral Classifiers
records.abstract: At least some of the properties that we associate with ‘numeral classifiers’ are just spinoffs from the interaction of singular nouns with quantity-related determiners.

records.title: On the Syntactic Reality of Pragmatic Operators: the Case of Non-Redundancy
records.abstract: Considerable progress was made at the semantics/pragmatics interface by postulating covert operators that enrich the meaning of some constituents as part of compositional semantics. Three cases in point are Chierchia, Fox and Spector's exhaustivity operator O, used to compute local implicatures; Bochvar's assertion operator A, used to compute local accommodation of presuppositions; and more recently, Blumberg and Goldstein's non-redundancy operator R, used to capture cases of intrusion of non-redundancy constraints in truth conditions. But are these operators syntactically real? In earlier work, we argued that A isn't, and that O must have such a powerful semantics that one can, in …

records.title: A Guide to Construct Non-canonical Questions: a Cross-linguistic Perspective
records.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of non-canonical wh-questions from a cross-linguistic perspective. This study claims that they are encoded through the interaction of various functional elements, prosodic constraints and pragmatic construals. Our investigation reveals that they combine a wh-expression with a modal element that can be either lexical or silent. Prosodically, they are characterized by distinct pitch and stress patterns. In terms of semantics, these constructions involve negation over modal quantification in conjunction with various not-at-issue contents such as expectations and presuppositions. Pragmatically, they change information-seeking into a …

records.title: Cross-linguistic variation in the lexical semantics of conjunction
records.abstract: A longstanding debate about conjunction concerns so-called ‘asymmetric’ interpretations with additional causal or temporal inferences. Some theories posit a semantic component of conjunction as part of their explanation (e.g. Gómez Txurruka 2003). In this paper, we explore an unstated prediction of such accounts: that the specific semantics of conjunction might vary (i) across languages, and (ii) across conjunction strategies within a language. Drawing on data from A’ingae (an indigenous language of Ecuador) and Gizey (an indigenous language of Cameroon and Chad) respectively, we show that both predictions are met, arguing that such semantic variation is constrained in ways anticipated by …

records.title: Locative phrases as arguments or adjuncts. Existential and locative sentences in Greek
records.abstract: This chapter investigates the status of the locative constituent in Greek locative and existential sentences. Given that several types of sentences qualify as locatives and existentials in the language, this study offers a window into the syntax exploited for these two functions. Specifically, it shows that the locative function requires a structure in which the locative constituent is part of the main predication. In contrast, the existential one is achieved via the same structure with an additional change in the word order or via a second structure in which the locative merges as an adjunct. In this sense, this chapter suggests that the syntax behind locatives and existentials may be …

records.title: Logic and innateness. What is the connection between them?
records.abstract: The article is designed to attract the attention of those who deeply study the meanings of words that are effective in practice and do not mislead readers. The authors of this article call for refining the meaning of the word “logic” and clarifying its meaning to see the relationship of logic to innateness. The same article also describes the meaning of “logical method” as well as “ethics” as the natural opposite of logic. It will also be important in this article to explain that there are only two kinds of logic in nature: abstract logic and concrete logic. Therefore, this article will be useful for the development of science and a better explanation of the meaning of words and tools of …

records.title: No Genuine Copula in Japanese: a reanalysis of 'da' as a conceptual-locative postposition plus a one-argument existential verb
records.abstract: Retitled to "No Genuine Copula in Japanese: the pseudo-copula =da as an existential, conjunctive and locative complex". -------------------- This paper proposes an alternative analysis of the Japanese so-called copula '=da' and its non-contracted form '=de aru'. While '=da / =de aru' has traditionally been treated as a copula equivalent to English 'be', we argue instead that the nature of this pseudo-copula can be better understood in terms of how this language, which lacks the primitive 'be', has employed its most basic linguistic resources — namely, the locative postposition =ni "in", the conjunctive suffix -te "and" and the existential verb ar- "exist-", all of which, still today, …

records.title: Really: syntactics without semiotics?
records.abstract: This paper is the authorized English version of the 2023 paper published in "Baltic accent" 2023/3. The English version was prepared in August 2025 and published at the "Herald of the Russian Academy of Science", 2025. Vol. 95 (1). 34-47. DOI: 10.1134/S1019331625600805 The paper discusses the relation between linguistics and semiotics on the basis of the Old Russian discourse particle ТИ1 ‘indeed’, ‘verily’, ‘truly’ discovered by Andrei A. Zaliznyak in 1993. I treat linguistics and semiotics as different research programs: the former deals with specific features of language structures, while the latter discusses general characteristics of all sign systems. Formal models of language deal …

records.title: Inherent Case Features and Case Assignment in Double Object Constructions in Kazym Khanty
records.abstract: This dissertation contributes to the research on case by addressing questions about default case-marking and the mechanism of case assignment. This study is based on novel fieldwork data from the Kazym dialect of Northern Khanty (Ob-Ugric, Uralic) and makes three central claims. First, it makes an empirical and theoretical generalization that there exist two default cases in the language. I argue that the default case in argument positions is distinct from the default case in adjunct positions, e.g. on hanging topics (cf. Schutze 2001). Apart from the unmarked default, discussed in multiple previous studies (e.g. Schutze 2001; Legate 2008; Caha 2024 etc.), there exists a marked default …

records.title: The notional category of evidentiality
records.abstract: This chapter is a focused discussion of analytical options proposed for evidentiality in recent formal literature as well as the empirical motivation behind those options. Much work has been devoted to the ontological relationship between evidentiality and (epistemic) modality, and the chapter pays special attention to the types of data that motivate the analysis of evidentials as intensional operators. My ultimate goal is to sharpen the dialectic. I reexamine the tests used in existing literature and provide new empirical diagnostics that probe the intensionality of evidential utterances. My hope is for the reader to emerge with a better understanding of evidentiality as a semantic …

records.title: Two is better than one: Subject DPs in Spanish third person plural arbitrary sentences
records.abstract: Spanish has an arbitrary construction with no overt subject and obligatory plural agreement on the verb. When a secondary depictive predicate adjective appears in this construction, the adjectival agreement is optionally singular for some speakers. This number agreement mismatch reveals that this construction involves two distinct subjects: an implicit argument agent as well as an expletive structural subject. I demonstrate that this agreement optionality on secondary predicates is a result of a process known as defective circumvention (Storment 2025b), by which a probe can conditionally Agree past a featurally deficient goal to obtain features from a non-deficient goal. In this …

records.title: A well-formedness condition on alternative generation
records.abstract: Listeners compute inferences by negating alternatives to a given utterance. In this study of the syntax-pragmatics interface, it is argued that a syntactic well-formedness filter acts on structural alternatives, so that an inference that could only be generated by negating the interpretation of an ill-formed syntactic structure does not arise, a claim which is in tension with previous suggestions that grammar does not constrain alternatives. This paper takes as its empirical focus the distribution of temporariness inferences in English. The use of progressive aspect with a stative predicate gives rise to an inference formed by negating a non-progressive alternative, which may contradict …

records.title: An investigation of nominal copular sentences in three reading paradigms: Acceptability judgments, self-paced reading, and eye-tracking
records.abstract: This work aims to investigate the elaboration of (nominal) copular sentences in three different experimental para- digms involving a reading task: an acceptability judgment, a self-paced reading and an eye-tracking experiment. Nom- inal copular sentences (NCs), such as [DP1 The picture of the wall] is [DP2 the cause of the riot], represent a challenging phenomenon for, at least, two reasons: (i) they can be distinguished in two subtypes, namely canonical and inverse NCs, related to the different order of the DPs (respectively, [DPsubject is DPpredicate] in canonical form vs. [DPpredicate is DPsubject] in inverse form); (ii) these two subtypes are associated with one and the same type of …

records.title: Definiteness and Deitality in English: A Homeostatic Property Cluster Account
records.abstract: I separate the semantic category of definiteness from the morphosyntactic category of \textsc{deitality} and treat each as a homeostatic property cluster. On the syntax side, deitality comprises co-tending distributional properties: dispreference as the pivot of existential \textit{there} under neutral prosody, eligibility as the complement of partitive \textit{of}, and suitability as hosts for nonrestrictive modification and identificational constructions. On the semantic side, definiteness comprises identifiability, uniqueness, and anaphoric recoverability. The deital cluster is maintained by five homeostatic mechanisms operating at distinct timescales: grammaticalization creates the …

records.title: The Influence of English and Urdu Loanwords in Hindi
records.abstract: This paper explores the influence of English and Urdu loanwords on the Hindi language, examining how these words have entered everyday speech and cultural expressions. It discusses the linguistic impact at phonological, morphological, syntactic, and semantic levels, as well as the role of these loanwords in translation and communication. The paper highlights the historical and social contexts that facilitated linguistic borrowing, especially cultural interactions and language contact. Through analysis of examples from media, literature, and daily conversation, this study illustrates how loanwords enrich Hindi vocabulary and reflect ongoing language evolution.

records.title: Approaches to Parts and Wholes in Semantics (ESSLLI 2025 handouts)
records.abstract: These are the handouts of my ESSLLI 2025 advanced course together with the initial proposal (which deviates somewhat from the content of the handouts)

records.title: Cartography and Predication: Why we (still) need exocentricity
records.abstract: Predication has been recognized as the fundamental grammatical relation defining clausal structures in all (and only) human languages ever since the canonical model of Ancient Greek linguistics. This notion is by definition compositional, since either component – the subject and the predicate – cannot be defined without referring to the other. The central question addressed here is whether predication is a lexical property or can instead be unambiguously associated to a dedicated configuration, in keeping with the cartographic guidelines. Capitalizing on copular sentences with predicative noun phrases, which allow us to factor out non-essential aspects of this phenomenon, such as the …

records.title: Agree to disagree: additive particles in responses
records.abstract: Most literature on 'too' has focused on its "regular" uses, where, as a first approximation, 'too' triggers a presupposition that one of the focus alternatives to its prejacent, distinct from the prejacent itself, is true (e.g., 'Axel likes cats. BROOK likes cats, too.'). There has also been some discussion of "refutational 'too'", used in positive polarity responses that refute the antecedent utterance (e.g., 'A: It isn't hot. B: It is too!'). Recently, Thomas (2023) proposed that refutational 'too' is a response particle, akin to 'yes' and 'no'—or even more pertinently, to French 'si' and German 'doch'. In this paper, I present novel data on what I will call "confirmatory 'too'", used in …

records.title: A alternative analysis of the morphological structure of Japanese nominal adjectives — NI-adjectives
records.abstract: This paper reanalyses the morphosyntactic–semantic structure of Japanese nominal adjectives (NAs), also referred to as na-adjectives. The core of NAs lies in NA stems ending in '-ni', as in 'jukai-ni' "pleasant" and 'suki-ni' "like". These NA stems are lexical predicates selecting either one argument or two — a theme in 'jukai-ni' and an experiencer–theme pair in 'suki-ni'. However, outside small clauses serving as complements of cognition or perception verbs, as in 'watasi=wa [sore=o jukai-ni] omot-ta/kanzi-ta' "I found/felt [it pleasant]", they cannot function as predicates in their bare '-ni' form. Consequently, an NA stem forms a nominal-adjective phrase containing PRO, as in [PRO …

records.title: A Universal Noun Slot in the Linguistic Mind: Reverse Entailment Across All Parts of Speech with Computational Applications
records.abstract: This article introduces the Reverse Entailment Diagnostic (RED), a bidirectional inference mechanism that demonstrates the universal capacity of all parts of speech—nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, interjections, and articles—to be nominalized into syntactical noun entities occupying noun-slot positions (e.g., subject, object). This capacity suggests a universal noun slot in the linguistic mind, a cognitive mechanism enabling flexible categorization. Using examples—“square/quadrilateral,” “to book carefully,” and “her house”—across English, Mandarin, Tongan, Spanish, and Arabic, we illustrate how derived forms (e.g., possessives, nominalizations) …

records.title: On Semantic Agreement
records.abstract: This latest version is the published version augmented with a few post publication comments (appearing in red in the ms.) We discuss cases in which agreement between a head and a DP seems to drive, or be driven by, interpretive properties of this DP rather than its syntactic properties as for example in: (i) this team are ready; (ii) une moitié de nous six est/sont/ sommes toujours présent(e/s) (one half of us six is/are-3P/are-1P always present). This discussion centers mostly on the case of subject/verb number and person agreement (but its conclusions would extend to other cases of agreement between a head and a DP). In such a configuration, agreement features on T do not seem to match …

records.title: Conjunction Agreement as Semantic Agreement
records.abstract: Version change: Missing bibliography added. We discuss number, and to a lesser extent person, feature value cooccurrence restrictions between a head (Tense here) and a conjoined DP subject. We conclude that these restrictions instantiate semantic agreement, which arises in cases in which the features values on T do not match the features values of this DP. In the case of conjunction, this is because, we conclude, a conjunction of DPs lacks such features as there are no syntactic feature resolution rules. Instead, semantic agreement on T is ad sensum, meaning based, and can trigger presuppositions on the subject's denotation. We also discuss cumulative agreement cases, concluding it is not …

records.title: Anaphora in a four-valued setting
Restrictions on fronting and stress shift in the encoding of Czech focus
records.abstract: This article examines two operations which are used to encode focus in Czech: word order alternation and stress shift. Based on data from a previous production experiment, we ran a rating study where participants rated the authenticity of utterances with manipulated information structure. The results showed that alternating word order to encode focus is free, supporting the claims about the flexibility of Czech word order. Shifting stress is a more costly operation -- it is possible (in terms of competence), but it is not necessarily easy (in terms of performance). Moreover, applying a word order alternation and stress shift at the same time (in object fronting cases) leads to a significant …

records.title: A parametric view on exclusive focus particles
records.abstract: D-quantification and A-quantification are two basic apparatuses of meaning in natural language. There has, however, been a recent attempt to reduce the former to the latter, especially for exclusive focus particles, where adfocal only is claimed to be a "concord" marker, whereas adverbial only functions as an exclusive operator (A-quantifier) (Quek & Hirsch 2017; Branan & Erlewine 2023, among others). This paper argues that such a view is too strong and cannot be upheld universally. Specifically, I argue that both D- and A-quantification are available in the semantic domain of exclusives. Crucial data are drawn from Vietnamese and Yorùbá, where adverbial and adfocal particles are …

records.title: There is more about existentials: agreement and case assignment in Serbian and Lithuanian
records.abstract: This paper examines the properties of existential constructions in Serbian and Lithuanian. Existential constructions share some interpretive properties with locative constructions, in that both express a proposition about the existence or the presence of someone or something in a context. However, Serbian and Lithuanian existentials display a cluster of properties that set them apart from locatives: unmarked verb-subject order (with pivot following copula), lack of agreement between copula and post-copular pivot, genitive case on the pivot and a dedicated form of the copula. The case properties of the pivot in existentials depend on specific interpretive properties related to agentivity, …

records.title: When the syntactic bootstrap breaks: Some children think any means no
records.abstract: Children can use distributional information about where words occur to figure out their meanings. But what happens when two very different words not only have most of their distribution in common, but also compose to form indistinguishable sentential meanings in those common cases? As a negative polarity item (NPI), any is selectively licensed by certain linguistic environments, the most common of which is negation. This is the context in which children hear any in around 80% of their input. However, under negation, the meaning of any looks just like a negative quantifier in concord with the higher negation (a negative concord item; NCI). While studies of children’s production indicate that …

records.title: A Universal Noun Slot in the Linguistic Mind: Reverse Entailment Across All Parts of Speech
records.abstract: This article introduces the Reverse Entailment Diagnostic (RED), a novel bidirectional inference mechanism demonstrating that all parts of speech can be nominalized to occupy nounslot positions (e.g., subject, object) as syntactical noun entities, suggesting a universal noun slot in the linguistic mind. Using examples—“square/quadrilateral,” “to book carefully,” and “her house”— across English, Mandarin, and Tongan, I show how derived forms (e.g., possessives, nominalizations) entail backward to confirm nominal potential. RED challenges lexicalist frameworks like Transformational Generative Grammar, supporting dynamic models such as Distributed Morphology and Construction Grammar. …

records.title: Wh-conditionals are more interrogative than not: An insight from Khorchin Mongolian
records.abstract: The observation that wh-expressions in many languages can be interpreted either interrogatively or non-interrogatively has led to the widely accepted thesis that wh-expressions originate as variables, with their interpretations determined through being bound by a question operator or other non-interrogative operators (Cheng 1991; Li 1992; Tsai 1994; Cheng & Huang 1996; among others). However, recent studies on a specific non-interrogative wh-construction in Mandarin—wh-conditionals—challenge this variable-binding approach (Liu 2016, 2017; Xiang 2016, 2020; Li 2021). In wh-conditionals, two wh-clauses are connected to express a conditional meaning. These studies advocate for a question-based …

records.title: On some putative unaccusativity diagnostics
records.abstract: This paper is concerned with a set of diagnostics – agent-oriented adverbs, instruments and passivization – that are commonly used to detect the presence of a thematic Voice head. It analyzes a hitherto undocumented construction in Turkish, involvee causatives (InvCs). While InvCs surface with standard causative morphosyntax, they do not receive a causative interpretation and also fail the above diagnostics. In previous work, this profile has been taken as evidence for an unaccusative syntax. For InvCs, however, a wide range of evidence contradicts an unaccusative analysis. InvCs do contain a thematic Voice layer, but their argument does not receive an agent interpretation, which accounts …

records.title: Another View of Access by Chomsky (2024): An Analysis of Movement Constraint about Subject
records.abstract: This paper investigates restrictions on subject movement within Chomsky's (2024) MC framework, which replaces successive-cyclic movement with an interpretive operation, Access. We decompose Chomsky's Access into two parts, proposing a phase-level operation, Mark, which determines which syntactic objects are available to the interpretive systems. We argue that restrictions on subject movement are derived from the interaction of Mark with theta-domains, assuming that the CP phase delimits the domain of Mark. Based on this idea, we analyze the that-trace effect, subject island constraints, and the movement of subjects in passives, raising predicates, and copular constructions. We further …

records.title: Roots introduce low internal arguments
records.abstract: This paper argues that Roots introduce their own internal arguments (IAs) as complements. Korean non-derived nominals with argument-licensing capacity (Yoon & Park 2008) and their light verb (LV) predicate counterparts must utilize a √(Root)P (Harley 2014), as both verbal and nominal functional alternatives are empirically inadequate. Comparison across different types of LV constructions reveals that low IAs introduced directly by Roots and higher IAs introduced by verbal functional structure can be empirically differentiated by differential object marking, with low IAs necessarily originating in an acategorical constituent (the √P). Consequently, Roots are fully functioning syntactic heads …

records.title: Reverse Entailment in Nominal Categorization
records.abstract: This position paper introduces the concept of noun reverse entailment, a bidirectional inference mechanism that formalizes how derived noun forms (e.g., plurals, possessives, nominalizations) entail backward to confirm the base form’s nominal properties. I propose the Reverse Entailment Diagnostic (RED), a tool for proving that lexical and syntactic entities (including phrases and parts of speech) can act as syntactical noun entities in dynamic linguistic contexts. Using examples like “square/quadrilateral,” “to book carefully,” and “her house,” I demonstrate how RED reveals category flexibility, challenging rigid lexicalist frameworks and supporting usage-based models. This framework has …

records.title: The ingredients of hyperraising: insights from Tamil
records.abstract: On the strength of novel data from Tamil, which notably lacks hyperraising but optionally allows (classic) raising, this paper argues against two prominent analyses of hyperraising – in terms of the Activity Condition and in terms of CP intervention – which, we will show, overgenerate the possibility of hyperraising in this language. In contrast, we show that proposals that seek to explain the availability of hyperraising in terms of the Williams Cycle (WC, Williams, 2003) acting in conspiracy with the Phase Impenetrability Condition (PIC, Chomsky, 2001, et seq.) accurately predict its absence in Tamil. Further independent empirical support for this line of analysis comes from Spanish, …

records.title: Selective grammatical encoding of emotions in language
records.abstract: In Cinque 2013 I considered one potential argument for Universal Grammar. One stemming from the limited number of functional notions that are grammatically encoded in the languages of the world. What we find is that only a fraction of our cognitive concepts and distinctions seems to receive a grammatical encoding. Here I focus on the specific domain of emotions.

records.title: Conditional backshift and counterfactual illusion: Tense, probability and epistemic stance in backshifted English conditional constructions
records.abstract: Famously, English conditional constructions licence the use of past tense verb forms to refer to present or future time and the use of past perfect structures where we would normally expect to see past simple ones. The occurrence of such verb forms in conditionals is here termed “conditional backshift” in line with scholars such as Dancygier (1998). Across linguistics, philosophy, psychology and related fields the standard view is that conditional backshift conveys that the proposition in the antecedent of the conditional is unlikely to occur, is regarded with doubt by the speaker or is counterfactual. The aim of this paper is to overturn the standard view. To this end, two sets of data are …

records.title: Intra-sentential Code Switching at the Syntax-prosody Interface
records.abstract: Grammatical patterns of intra-sentential code-switching (ICS) provide a testing ground for architectural questions in generative linguistics. ICS shows that bilinguals are able to derive sentences containing material in more than one language. We investigate the nature of a minimal unit for ICS, which must remain unilingual, and propose to derive it from already established properties of grammar, specifically the mapping from syntax to phonology. We report data from three acceptability studies on Hebrew-English bilinguals, investigating ICS patterns at the CP edge, the DP edge, and with pronominal subjects. Our results point to a prosodically-defined minimal unit for ICS, which does not …

records.title: Brief notes on the semantics of copular sentences
Some WISE advice
On the imperialism of the copula: Addressing some puzzling properties of reduced structures in Italian
Was Pierre Marie right? Not really
records.abstract: Pierre Marie, the arch-enemy of Jules Déjerine and Augusta Klumpke-Déjerine, is apparently enjoying a new wave of popular- ity (Coutinho, Caramelli & Teive 2021, Weiller, Glauche & Rijntjes 2022) . While some of his anatomical work may be justly appreciated, a careful reading of his work on aphasia indicates that his theoretical stance was deeply flawed.

records.title: Saussure’s Universal Distinctive Feature Dimensions
records.abstract: This paper revisits Saussure’s scalar analysis of phonemes, offering a modern reinterpretation that replaces binary features with phonological dimensions grounded in measurement theory. By redefining Saussure’s [openness] and [backness] as ordered scales and Chomsky and Halle’s “combination and concatenation” as partially ordered scales, the paper introduces a notion of “[phono]logical simultaneity.” This framework renders the variously-defined phoneme and segment redundant, and shifts the focus of distinctiveness to the linguistic sign, the morpheme. It demonstrates how phonological dimensions link continuous articulations and acoustic signals (e.g., F1 and F2) with discrete linguistic …

records.title: Proto-Mentawai
records.abstract: The term “Mentawai”, which has been haphazardly applied to the languages indigenous to the Mentawai island chain off the coast of West Sumatra, is not an endogenous identifier for any of the language groups which it covers. However, due in large part to a lack of adequate primary data, these languages have hitherto been treated as exemplifying a singular “Mentawai” language, accompanied by either the (baseless) insistence that the island chain is linguistically unified, or an addendum regretting the inadequacy of presuming a single “Mentawai” language, and stating that the true status of these languages requires further investigation. This paper aims to resolve this undesirable situation by …

records.title: LLMs as a synthesis between symbolic and distributed approaches to language
records.abstract: Since the middle of the 20th century, a fierce battle is being fought between symbolic and distributed approaches to language and cognition. The success of deep learning models, and LLMs in particular, has been alternatively taken as showing that the distributed camp has won, or dismissed as an irrelevant engineering development. In this position paper, I argue that deep learning models for language actually represent a synthesis between the two traditions. This is because 1) deep learning architectures allow for both distributed/continuous/fuzzy and symbolic/discrete/categorical-like representations and processing; 2) models trained on language make use of this flexibility. In particular, …

records.title: Romanian Neuter Plural: Both Conservative and Innovative
records.abstract: Romanian stands apart from its Western Romance counterparts in the evolution of the Latin neuter. While most Romance languages resolved neuter nouns into either masculine or feminine classes—often reanalyzing neuter plurals (‑a) as feminine singulars—Romanian preserved the neuter as a distinct morphological and syntactic class in the singular, but innovated by assigning feminine plural agreement to neuter nouns. This development constitutes a mirror-image reanalysis: instead of eliminating the neuter distinction through full assimilation, Romanian maintains the category by reinterpreting its plural behavior. The result is a system that is both morphologically conservative and syntactically …

records.title: The Unaccusative-Unergative Distinction in Mandarin Resultative Constructions
records.abstract: The Unaccusativity Hypothesis (UH) is supported by unaccusative-unergative distinctions in English resultatives, but is challenged by the apparent lack of such distinctions in Mandarin resultatives. This paper shows that, despite appearances to the contrary, Mandarin transitive resultatives do exhibit unaccusative–unergative distinctions, and proposes a non-uniform analysis of Mandarin resultatives with unaccusative abd unergative matrix verbs, in accordance with UH. The proposal not only sheds new light on the Uniformity of Theta-Assignment Hypothesis, but also advances a general theory of resultative argument structure.

records.title: CV Wave Theory: A Unified Model of Connected Speech Simplification
records.abstract: This paper introduces CV Wave Theory, a unified framework for understanding connected speech simplification. Human speech unfolds as a continuous stream shaped by the principle of articulatory economy. The theory formalizes spoken language as oscillations between consonantal closure (C, valleys) and vocalic openness (V, peaks), conceptualizing entire sentences as “one long word.” By modeling speech as a CV waveform, the model explains why phenomena such as linking, elision, reduction, and assimilation naturally occur: consonant clusters collapse into a single valley (e.g., next day → [neks deɪ]), adjacent vowels trigger linking or intrusion (e.g., law(r) and order), and non-prominent vowels …

records.title: The or That? Evaluating language models’ sensitivity to discourse structure in anaphora
records.abstract: We test whether language models (LMs) exhibit sensitivity to fine-grained discourse features that influence referential form choice in human language.
