Using a controlled paradigm from prior behavioral studies, we evaluate 19 LMs on their ability to distinguish between demonstratives (e.g., that) and definites (e.g., the) when referring back to previously mentioned entities, using expert-created stimuli across four languages (English, German, Turkish, Mandarin). In human data, demonstratives show selective licensing effects based on the presence or absence of contrastive noun phrases and discourse continuity. We find that only larger models replicate these effects reliably, with stronger …

records.title: Variability, its limits, and the performance-competence debate: Implications of linguistic variability for a theory of grammar
records.abstract: The article provides an overview of variability in natural language by looking at the limits of intra-individual, inter-individual, and crosslinguistic variability at all levels of grammar. We review evidence for the hypothesis that variability forms an integral part of natural language and often provides valuable insights into speakers’ linguistic competence. We will discuss in turn (i.) different subtypes of variability; (ii.) the difference between systematic linguistic variability, as driven by grammar or processing-related factors, and random noise including performance errors; (iii.) the phenomenon of hidden variability, where linguistic expressions can differ in their underlying …

records.title: Anaphoric Definiteness in Korean Sign Language: The role of NPLOC and NP-IXTHIS
records.abstract: This paper investigates how Korean Sign Language marks anaphoric definiteness, focusing on NPLOC and NP-IXTHIS. Two central claims are that in Korean Sign Language, NPLOC is a strong definite comparable to demonstrative anaphoric NPs in spoken Korean, and that NP-IXTHIS, which combines a nominal with simultaneous pointing, encodes anaphoric noteworthiness, paralleling emphatic demonstratives like “this very N” in spoken English. We propose a formal semantic analysis of NPLOC and NP-IXTHIS, adopting Kim’s (2023b) locative-relation based framework, in which indexing and locus are separated from each other. The proposed analysis will be shown to have implications for anaphoric definiteness …

records.title: Dual Number in Kazym Khanty: Not-at-issue content that does not project
records.abstract: The Projection Principle (Beaver et al. 2017) states that semantic content projects iffit is not-at-issue. This paper presentsa counterexample to this claim: the dual number in Kazym Khanty featuringthe duality implication that is not-at-issue content that does not project.

records.title: The Distribution of Wide Scope Indefinite Bare Duals in Kazym Khanty: a QUD-based Approach
records.abstract: This paper is aimed at accounting for the limited distribution of the wide scope existential (WSE) uses of bare dual NPs in Kazym Khanty. The author argues that the reason for this limitation is pragmatic in nature: while bare duals are existential quantifiers and the ability to get wide scope is always semantically available, some WSE uses are independently blocked by a QUD-based constraint. Namely, in such cases, bare duals are infelicitous because they are forced to address a QUD that targets their not-at-issue content, namely the duality meaning. The case of Kazym Khanty bare duals shows that absence of a WSE reading in a particular sentence does not suggest that the tested NP can not …

records.title: When your associates tag along: Associative plurality in Rural Iberian Spanish proper names
records.abstract: Lewis (2023, 2024) proposes that languages that use the same marking to indicate additive and associative plural must lack free-standing definite articles (e.g. Turkish, Japanese). This property is attributed to these languages instantiating the negative value of the DP parameter. Based on original fieldwork data from Rural Iberian Spanish, we show that this variety of Spanish is a genuine counterexample to Lewis's generalization: plural-marked first names (e.g. lo-s Roman-es) may be understood additively or associatively; crucially, a plural-marked definite determiner is obligatory for the associative understanding. Based on a series of diagnostics, we argue that plural-marked names …

records.title: Recursion in NP: pseudopartitive measures require  complementation, not specification
records.abstract: This paper provides evidence favoring one of two hypotheses regarding the structure of measure phrases in pseudopartitives ( three boxes of books ). It compares the ‘Spec’ hypothesis (Schwarzschild, 2006), which places measure phrases ( three books ) in Specifier position of the substance, and the the ‘Comp’ hypothesis (Stickney, 2009), which places substance phrases ( of books ) in Complement position of the measure. Only the latter requires nominal complements to nominals (recursion inside NP, which has been more controversial than clausal recursion – Stowell, 1989; Frank and Kroch, 1994; Frank, 2002; Chomsky, 2008; Kayne, 2008; Citko, 2014). The Spec hypothesis is motivated by semantic …

records.title: ATB movement and non-structural Case in Modern Greek
records.abstract: Recent literature treats nominals bearing non-structural case either as ordinary DPs or as DPs encapsulated in a structural shell (PP or KP). This paper argues that both representations must be recognized in the grammar, since both co-exist within a single language. Novel observations from ATB movement in Greek reveal that the class of non-structural genitives is syntactically heterogeneous in this language: not all genitives can combine with each other in ATB movement, despite their systematic identity in form. The paper argues that assigning some genitives the status of plain DPs and others the status of PPs correctly accounts for the asymmetries in ATB movement, which is independently …

records.title: Dynamic antisymmetry and type-driven interpretation
records.abstract: The problematic syntactic symmetry which disallows linearization, is mirrored by an equally problematic symmetry in the semantic component. I will explore the conjecture that movement chains can solve the problem in the compositional interpretation as well.

records.title: “Moro’s Problem”: Finding grammar in the brain
records.abstract: One of the main challenges of language science is to draw inferences about internal computations from external observations–in recent terminology, to deduce what is I-language from E-language. Since grammars, human or otherwise, are presumptively part of brain-internal computational systems, their activity is typically not directly observable, for example, in terms of the sentences or “language” that comprise external behavior. This gap is part of a long history of a tension between reductionist and emergentist approaches in the analysis of complex systems, extensively and explicitly analyzed, perhaps most famously explicated by David Marr in terms of his notion of “three levels of …

records.title: ‘Sono Andrea’: Some reduced (cleft) answers in Italian
(Dis)similarities between Brazilian Portuguese and Mandarin: a contrastive semantic analysis of Nem Todos (os) and bù dōu and pedagogical possibilities in PAL teaching
records.abstract: This article provides a contrastive analysis of the constructions nem todos (os) in Brazilian Portuguese (BP) and bù dōu (“not all”) in Mandarin, focusing on their formal-semantic properties and implications for the teaching of Portuguese as an Additional Language (PAL). Following Quadros Gomes (2023), we argue that nem functions as a discourse-structuring particle: when combined with todo, it denies the universality of quantification and corrects expectations of totality anchored in the conversational background. In contrast, bù dōu in Mandarin operates as a more general sentential negation, without equivalent positional restrictions. We also compare these constructions with todos não/dōu …

records.title: "Non-local A-movement" is predicted to exist, and it does
records.abstract: In this paper I put together two ingredients: (i) featurally relativized probes (Béjar 2003 et seq.); (ii) a featural approach to the A/Ā-distinction (van Urk 2015). These two, combined, predict that we should find movement phenomena that are non-local, and yet show no other Ā-type properties (i.e. "non-local A-movement"). I show that this does in fact exist: in Äiwoo, a less local argument can move to spec,TP over a closer one if it has the right features. The existence of this type of movement supports van Urk (2015)'s argument that the locality properties of canonical A/Ā-movement are completely epiphenomenal, and only determined by the features searched for by the movement-triggering …

records.title: Principled probability in syntax: A Minimalist approach to variability and cumulativity in phrasal movement
records.abstract: The relevance of probabilistically variable patterns has long been controversial in linguistic theory, historically led by two dominant schools. On the first view, which I call Principles Without Probability, variable patterns are outside the purview of formal theories of grammar, composed solely of categorical principles (Newmeyer 2003). The second view, Probability Without Principles, holds that unit and collocation frequencies form the basis of mental representations, and denies the existence of formal categories (Bybee and Hopper 2001). I argue that these approaches should be reconciled in a theory with Principles and Probabilities: Language is mentally represented as a generative …

records.title: The non-unity of differential object marking: Flagging versus indexing
records.abstract: This paper shows that that differential object marking (DOM) is not a unitary phenomenon, and observes that its two subtypes, differential object flagging (DOF) and differential object indexing (DOI), probably have rather different explanations. The cross-linguistic patterns found with both subtypes of DOM can be described by the scales of referential prominence (animacy, specificity, and so on), but DOI is like differential subject indexing (DSI) in that it conforms to the prominent indexing universal, while differential subject flagging (DSF) shows the mirror-image pattern of DOF: Flagging is preferred when the subject is not prominent on one of the prominence scales. The paper provides …

records.title: Bipartite Negation in Nduindui: empirical generalisations and theoretical challenges
records.abstract: The goal of this paper is to explore negation in Nduindui, drawing out empirical generalisations regarding negation and the implications of such generalisations in terms of analysing the clause structure in the language. Nduindui shares an interesting feature with many of its neighbours: consistently exhibiting discontinuous bipartite negation, where the two negators he and tea encircle verbal material. This paper presents novel data regarding negation in Nduindui and its interaction with other elements in the clause like tense and aspect. Empirical generalisations are formed from the attested patterns of negation, and a comparative discussion is provided with other languages in the region. …

records.title: Bilingual development in the Tai-Vietnamese multicultural borderland
records.abstract: Northern Vietnam, in particular the regions along the international border, is home to a rich diversity of language communities. Important research opportunities have presented themselves in the Tai-speaking communities in rural districts near Laos with an emphasis on the development and preservation of the Tai languages. One opportunity in particular focuses on the new generation of bilingual school-age children. Preliminary results of the present study regarding the sociolinguistic setting are reported to better understand the language use context of community bilingualism. The method applied for this exploratory survey included different components, each one gathering different kinds of …

records.title: The importance of anomaly in neurolinguistic research
records.abstract: Anomaly has always attracted the interest of language scholars, either as a possible mechanism for language change or as a window into speakers’ judgments and competence. Here I will discuss the use of errors in neurolinguistics, focusing on Moro’s prolific ideas to disentangle grammar in the brain by presenting selective anomalies to neurotypical individuals as well as clinical groups. This prompts further considerations of the nature of anomaly for the study of language as a whole, from its core structures to its most creative nuances.

records.title: Ideophonic sequences: Challenging the asymmetric syntactic structure hypothesis
records.abstract: This paper challenges the hypothesis that ideophonic sequences are syntactic structures built from lexical roots by the recursive operation Merge through the mediation of a functional head, taken to be either a coordinate (Corver 2015) or a determiner (Corver 2023). Drawing on Generative Grammar theory and new data from Brazilian Portuguese, we argue that the evidence for this hypothesis is weak at best. We first show that these sequences do not behave consistently as constituents. While they can stand alone, be coordinated, and resist intrusion, they fail to undergo movement and ellipsis. Taken together, this suggests that they are most likely linear sequences. They lack the formal …

records.title: Weak crossover in Spanish relative clauses
records.abstract: We investigate the status of weak crossover violations (WCO) in Spanish restrictive relative clauses. Claims in the literature lead to the expectation that Spanish does not show sensitivity to WCO in this context; however, ours is the first systematic investigation of the phenomenon in the language. We find that Spanish restrictive relative clauses do exhibit WCO violations: when the relative clause is headed by que, participants rate crossover configurations lower than configurations without crossover; when the relative clause is introduced by a quien, the status of WCO violations is less clear. We consider two explanations for our results in a quien clauses: potential structural …

records.title: Linear A Detailed Comparative Linguistic Interpretations and Decipherment of a Minoan Cup Inscription
records.abstract: This paper presents three distinct linguistic interpretations of a circular Linear A inscription, derived from comparative methodologies most likely resembling the Linear A writing system: Proto-Hungarian phonetic mapping, Linear B phonetic equivalence, and ancient Egyptian/Coptic semantic analogues. Despite differences in language families and theoretical models, all three interpretations converge thematically on the concepts of light, divine descent, spirit, and celestial origin. This suggests the inscription preserves a ritualistic or poetic message aligned with religious practices in Bronze Age Crete. This study invites archaeologists, epigraphers, and linguists to consider broader …

records.title: The Darwinian Mind of the Machine: Rethinking LLM Training as Evolution
records.abstract: This essay challenges the prevailing metaphor of “learning” used to describe Large Language Model (LLM) training, proposing instead that these systems represent a form of hyper-accelerated, data-driven evolution. Through analysis of Daniel Dennett’s hierarchy of evolutionary competence and examination of the poverty of the stimulus problem, we argue that LLMs are Darwinian creatures evolved at computational speeds in environments of pure text. This framework explains their linguistic capabilities through convergent evolution rather than learning, resolves paradoxes about their competence without understanding, and for our understanding of the relevance for these models for generative …

records.title: Illicit LBE in Russian sluicing: rescue by deletion (of linearization statements)
records.abstract: This paper discusses a case of exceptional extraction from Russian PPs that only happens in sluicing / fragments. The proposed analysis rests on a version of repair by ellipsis pursued in the Cyclic Linearization literature (Fox, Pesetsky 2005; Davis 2021; Mendes, Kandybowicz 2023): illicit non-successive-cyclic movement is possible when the conflicting linearization statements are deleted via ellipsis. The analysis extends to other cases of exceptional extraction in Russian, when coupled with a Scattered Deletion analysis of LBE (Fanselow & Ćavar 2002, Bondarenko & Davis 2023). Finally, we discuss a number of overgeneration issues for our account.

records.title: Neurological Representations of Linguistic Intuitions and World Knowledge Intuitions: a Case Study of Evdientiality
records.abstract: This chapter aims to dissociate linguistic intuitions and world knowledge intuitions by re-examining the introspection-based judgments of Japanese modality and evidentiality reported in Hara & Davis (2013); Davis & Hara (2014) and Hara (2017) as well as the results of an electroencephalography (EEG) experiment conducted by Hara, Orita, Ying, Koshizuka & Sakai (2020).

records.title: Formal pronouns in Spanish and the case for [HON]
records.abstract: In Spanish, usted ‘you (formal)’ and ustedes ‘you all (formal only in regions of Spain)’ have second-person semantics but appear with third-person, or default, agreement morphology. After exploring the possibility that these expressions are nominal imposters, I determine that they are genuine second-person pronouns on the basis of two phenomena: the ability of ustedes to occur in pronoun-article-noun constructions and the sensitivity of both usted and ustedes to the Person-Case Constraint. The question then becomes how to represent these forms as vocabulary items since a [PART(ICIPANT)] feature alone does not distinguish usted from tú/vos ‘you (informal)’ in all varieties of Spanish or …

records.title: Right dislocation as multidominance, and beyond
records.abstract: [Published in Proceedings of GLOW, 47: https://biecoll.ub.uni-bielefeld.de/index.php/glow/article/view/1262 ] This study argues for a multidominant approach to right dislocation (RD), the first of its kind, with data from Cantonese and Mandarin as well as Japanese and Korean. The crucial evidence comes from focus/ wh -association of ‘only’/‘( wh -)the-hell’ expressions in RD, which requires a “leftward” c-command configuration. This challenges current monoclausal movement and biclausal sluicing approaches, but naturally falls out from a multidominant structure formed by Parallel Merge. The findings suggest that focus/ wh -association serves as reliable and moreover novel diagnostics for …

records.title: Diagnosing multidominance by focus association of ‘only’
records.abstract: This study is concerned with the nature of syntactic silence and how to diagnose it. Syntactic structures may be "silent" in the course of derivation through several pathways: (i) movement (followed by Copy Deletion), (ii) ellipsis, and, less often discussed, (iii) linearization of shared/multidominant nodes. This study offers a novel diagnostic for (iii), namely, focus association of the exclusive particle 'only', which requires c-commanding an overt focus associate. Drawing cross-linguistic data from English and Cantonese (as well as Vietnamese), we demonstrate that focus association with apparent gaps is possible in Right Node Raising. We argue that only Parallel Merge (Wilder 1999, …

records.title: Machine language as somniloquy: How the neuroscience of sleep illuminates generative AI
records.abstract: Can machines mean what they say? Generally not, because current AI systems lack the cognitive capacities that allow humans to recover meaning from and infuse meaning into language. However, from a cognitive standpoint, human and machine language are not entirely dissimilar. Specifically, while at present there are hardly circumstances in which machines function as humans typically do vis-à-vis meaningful language use, there is at least a circumstance in which humans appear to function as current generative language AI: during somniloquy or ‘sleep talk’. I first show that somniloquy and machine language unfold in similar restricted cognitive conditions. I then use this observation to suggest …

records.title: Noticing language: What echolocation tells us about language emergence
records.abstract: Why do humans alone develop language? Rather than specialized processing modules, I argue that evolution selected for a simple attentional bias, hyperpriors that amplify communicative signals (eye contact, infant-directed prosody, hierarchical rhythm). This precision-weighting ensures linguistic patterns dominate learning without requiring language-specific architecture. Echolocation demonstrates the principle. Blind humans achieve remarkable spatial discrimination through self-generated sounds, a complex capacity that emerges without specialized adaptations. This spandrel falsifies the common inference that complex abilities require direct selection. If echolocation can arise from generic …

records.title: On the Fundamental Difference between Dependent-up and Dependent-down Cases, and on their Manifestation in Turkic
records.abstract: Dependent cases in Dependent Case Theory (DCT) fall into two directions: during case competition between two nominals, “dependent-down” cases are assigned to the lower nominal (such as accusative), and “dependent-up” cases are assigned to the higher nominal (such as ergative). It is a well-known, not often discussed, issue why accusative case can be assigned to multiple arguments, while ergative case can only ever appear on one argument, and must appear on the highest argument. In this thesis, I argue that this is not accidental but follows from computational considerations: a formal grammar checking whether a given dependent-down case is licensed is less complex (in a formal sense) than a …

records.title: Null subjects, labeling, and Linearization: Microvariation in subject and agreement drop
records.abstract: Theoretical approaches to null subjects standardly focus on the narrow syntactic module. I offer a postsyntactic alternative in terms of PF deletion applying to salvage an unlinearizable derivation. Support for this alternative comes from microvariation in three closely-related West Slavic pro-drop languages spoken primarily in Poland (Kashubian, Polish, and Silesian), in which the distribution of null subjects is sensitive to the postsyntactic realization of [PERS/NUM] agreement. I argue that this microvariation indicates that in these languages at least, the licensing of null subjects takes place at PF, which in turn suggests that PF has a bigger role to play in a general theory of null …

records.title: The Foundations of the Mentalist Theory and the Statistical Machine Learning Challenge: Comments on Matthias Mahlmann’s Mind and Rights
records.abstract: Matthias Mahlmann’s Mind and Rights (M&R) argues that the mentalist theory of moral cognition - premised on an approach to the mind most closely associated with generative linguistics - is the appropriate lens through which to understand moral judgment’s roots in the mind. Specifically, he argues that individuals possess an inborn moral faculty responsible for the principled generation of moral intuitions. These moral intuitions, once sufficiently abstracted, generalized, and universalized by individuals, gave rise to the idea of human rights embodied in such conventions as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. I am sympathetic to this argument. I thus take my comments on M&R as an …

records.title: Awareness of language and learning: Vietnamese immigrants navigate bilingualism in the new culture
records.abstract: Participants in this study of language awareness, related to the relationship between speech and writing, provide self-report reflection on the learning of Chinese characters. This topic is the focus of a larger ongoing project focused on second language (L2) learners’ literacy attainment. Interviews with immigrant learners of Mandarin Chinese have suggested lines of research to pursue from a new vantage point, specifically on the question of access to phonological knowledge during the decoding of Chinese characters. How might this processing during reading vary in the case of Modern Standard Chinese Writing (MSCW) between, for example, Mandarin (informants’ target learner language, L2) and …

records.title: (A)symmetries in the morphosyntax of embedded clauses in Khalkha Mongolian
records.abstract: This dissertation draws on original fieldwork data from two Mongolic languages – Khalkha Mongolian (henceforth Khalkha) and Kalmyk Oirat (henceforth Kalmyk) – to investigate issues pertaining to clausal nominalisation, syntactic locality, differential argument marking (DAM), and case assignment. The empirical focus is on four embedded clause types in Khalkha, supplemented by comparative data from Kalmyk. These clause types include three types of complement clauses – finite bare CPs, finite nominalised clauses (NCs), and nonfinite NCs – and one type of adjunct clause – converbial adjuncts. Chapter 2 provides a brief introduction to the Mongolic language family, fieldwork context, and the …

records.title: Dissecting the illocutionary force phrase: New evidence from SFP embeddability
records.abstract: This paper focuses on the peripheral hierarchy of Mandarin interrogatives. Based on question markers’ embeddability profiles in a series of nonquotational subordinating contexts, this paper argues for a three-way split in projections that contribute to the illocutionary force, attributing the non-co-occurrence of question markers to their semantics. Specifically, we propose that (i) LowIForceP houses the most embeddable meiyou , Op wh , and A-not-A; (ii) PerspP houses question markers restrictedly embeddable like bu and ma ; and (iii) HighIForceP houses the unembeddable ba . Looking deeper into the embeddability patterns of bu and ma , we argue that our PerspP should be interpreted à la …

records.title: Feature spreading, redundancy, and blocking behavior
records.abstract: We analyze a collection of long-distance assimilation patterns using Boolean Monadic Recursive Schemes (BMRS; Bhaskar et al. 2020, Chandlee & Jardine 2021). BMRS describe input-output maps as logical transductions using conditional IF…THEN…ELSE… syntax. These patterns emerge from varying the presence, type, and position of redundancy conditions within BMRS feature spreading functions. When potential targets fail to receive or propagate harmonic features, redundancy conditions override harmony by blocking feature reception, halting propagation, or preventing both, depending on their type and scope. This offers a unified computational account of variation in feature spreading and blocking …

records.title: How to Study Boundary Phenomena: English Reciprocals and the Limits of Categorization
records.abstract: English reciprocals (\textit{each other} and \textit{one another}) are generally classified as pronouns, but they are atypical and exhibit several characteristics of determinatives. As such, they exemplify a core problem in linguistic categorization: how to study boundary phenomena rigorously when the dataset consists of a small number of items that straddle categories. Rather than forcing a binary decision via selectively chosen diagnostics, I measure the stability of ambiguity. Using a comprehensive profile of 155 morphological, syntactic, semantic, and phonological properties, I locate the reciprocals in multidimensional grammatical space and apply five complementary lenses: distance …

records.title: Linguistics in a battlefield. A short note on syntax and the “Newtonian style of research”.
records.abstract: Linguistics has always been a battlefield as the vision of language has always been the expression of the vision of human beings in any culture. Nowadays, neurobiological models and computational theories compete with linguistics towards the understanding of the origin, the function and the structure of human languages. These notes highlight two crucial points: first, these two competitors target two distinct and incompatible goals; second, there are aspects of human languages, like the systematic differences expressed within the boundaries of Babel and crucial notions such as “predication” which are unformulable outside linguistics theory.

records.title: Diagnosing Small Nominals: Theoretical Implications from Moksha and Hill Mari
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates the morphosyntactic behavior of small nominals (SNs) — reduced nominal structures lacking certain morphosyntactic properties characteristic of full DPs — across languages. Based primarily on three detailed case studies — bare complements of Moksha postpositions, Moksha bare direct objects (DOs), and bare DOs in Hill Mari non-finite clauses, I propose diagnostics that can reliably identify small nominals cross-linguistically and explore their implications for syntactic theory, particularly regarding the structure of the extended nominal projection. The dissertation begins with a carefully delimited theoretical model of nominal phrase structure, emphasizing the …

records.title: The Syntax of Serbian How-Complements
keywords: form-copy; syntax; complement clause; phases; slavic
records.abstract: This paper discusses a special type of complement of perception verbs in Serbian, introduced by kako (‘how’). Via a parallel corpus analysis, I compare the distribution of Serbian kako-clauses and English -ing forms. I show that two types of non-interrogative kako-clauses can be used in translations of English -ing forms, distinguished based on their formal and interpretive properties: ‘eventive’ and propositional kako-clauses. Eventive clauses focus on directly perceived events and cannot be negated or combined with epistemic verbs, while propositional clauses express beliefs or judgments and have a truth value. At a formal level, eventive clauses feature a null subject, while …

records.title: Question Bias as the Pragmatics of Context Update
records.abstract: Typically, utterances of declarative sentences make assertions, whereas utterances of interrogative sentences ask questions. One popular idea about how to explain this is that the two clause types have denotations of different types (e.g. propositions vs. sets of propositions), which interact with a univocal context-update mechanism in a way that derives asserting and questioning from that denotational difference. This is a satisfying explanatory approach, because it proposes that interpretation is driven compositionally by the form of the sentence, and it refrains from construction-specific stipulations about context update. But there are many systematic exceptions to this typical …

records.title: Drumming Dialogues: Investigating the Fusion of Sabar Drums and Wolof in Senegal
records.abstract: This paper explores the linguistic aspects of the Sabar drum language from Senegal, focusing on how Sabar drummers encode features of the Wolof language, a non-tonal Niger-Congo language spoken predominantly in Senegal. Unlike drum languages based on tonal languages, the Sabar drum language correlates with the non-tonal Wolof by transposing speech sounds into rhythmic patterns. The study specifically examines the relationship between Sabar drum strokes and the [ATR] (Advanced Tongue Root) feature of Wolof vowels. The findings reveal consistent patterns between Sabar drum strokes and Wolof syllables, indicating a significant correlation between the phonological properties of Wolof vowels and …

records.title: Redundancy across Connectives
records.abstract: We present three experiments investigating redundancy across connectives. Specifically, we examine: (i) Hurford disjunctions — disjunctions where one disjunct entails the other (Hurford 1974); (ii) Hurford conditionals — conditionals corresponding to Hurford disjunctions (Mandelkern & Romoli 2018); and (iii) the corresponding conjunctions in which one conjunct entails the other. Our study addresses three questions about redundancy. First, does order matter? For example, are p+ ∨ p and p ∨ p+ judged as equally infelicitous? Second, does polarity matter? For example, are p+ ∨ p and ¬p ∨ ¬p+ judged equally unacceptable? Third, does the choice of connective affect the strength of oddness …

records.title: Phonotactic conditions of geminates can influence sound symbolic effects: Cuteness and evilness judgement experiments for Japanese speakers
keywords: sound symbolism; geminates; cuteness; evilness; japanese
records.abstract: This study explores the sound symbolic effects of geminate consonants. I propose three working hypotheses: 1) geminates convey a particular meaning more strongly than singletons, 2) geminates convey it to the same extent as singletons, and 3) geminates convey it less strongly than singletons. To evaluate the most plausible hypothesis, I conducted experiments in which Japanese speakers judged cuteness and evilness of nonce words using a four-point scale. The results indicate that, on the one hand, the low-frequency geminate /ɾɾ/ in Japanese conveys cuteness less strongly than its singleton counterpart. On the other hand, the low-frequency geminate /bb/ conveys evilness to the same extent as …

records.title: The cycle in a syllabe: Phases and impenetrability in Dinka morphology
records.abstract: This paper argues for a cross-modular theory of cyclicity rooted in phase theory (Chomsky 2001, Marvin 2002, Newell 2008 a.o.), in which the application of the syntactic, morphological, and phonological grammar is interleaved. I present a detailed investigation of the Nilotic language Dinka (South Sudan), a language with extensive effects of cyclicity in its syntax and a rich system of nonconcatenative morphology. I show that several asymmetries in how nonconcatenative morphology is expressed on the verb, including allomorphy, the availability of affixation, and shifts in voice quality, align with a clause-internal domain diagnosed by successive-cyclic long-distance movement. As a result, …

records.title: Evaluating Learning Trajectories of Neural Morphology Acquisition Models
records.abstract: Computational models of morphology acquisition have played a central role in debates over the nature of morphological representations since the origin of the Past Tense Debate in the 1980s. The apparent success of recent artificial neural network architectures for morphological inflection in natural language processing has revitalized this debate. However, despite their often good performance, the actual suitability of these advanced neural networks as models of human morphology acquisition remains uncertain. We argue that much of this confusion stems from inconsistent methods of training and evaluation. In this work, we demonstrate that more careful data set creation and an evaluation …

records.title: Arguments Move at Least Once: Evidence from Split Constructions
records.abstract: This paper proposes the Obligatory Movement Hypothesis (Kayne 2010)—the claim that all arguments undergo at least one instance of syntactic movement—by presenting novel evidence from discontinuous PP constructions (P-splits) in Modern Greek. While previous work has examined P-splits in intransitive contexts, I extend the analysis to transitive predicates, showing that the availability of P-splits is tightly constrained by the movement of direct objects. The data demonstrate that objects cannot remain in situ: their obligatory movement to a middle-field licensing position systematically blocks P-split formation, unless circumvented by cliticization or extraposition. This finding not only …

records.title: Tense and perspective: a solution to the then-present puzzle
records.abstract: In this paper, we focus on the cross-linguistic incompatibility between the temporal adverbial 'then' and the present tense. We show that the pattern holds in both matrix and embedded environments, across an array of languages (including Modern Greek, Modern Hebrew, Russian and Japanese) each behaving differently with respect to tense shift. To account for this incompatibility, we propose that interpretation of tenses is sensitive to a perspective parameter. Tense shift occurs thanks to a perspective-shifting operator, similar to operator-based analyses of indexical shift (Anand and Nevins 2004; Anand 2006; Deal 2020). The main advantage of this account over alternative theories of tense …

records.title: Licensing ACC-Marked External Possession in Korean
records.abstract: This paper looks at the accusative (ACC) marked external possession construction (EPC) in Korean, seeking to identify its licensing conditions, an outstanding problem in the literature. I propose that ACC-marked EP sentences in Korean are licensed if they answer the question under discussion (QUD) and if the possessum (PM) represents what I call the Target of the event under description in which the possessor (PR) is the Theme or if the PR is what I call the Receiver of the event in which the PM is the Theme. I also propose that there are at least three structural possibilities for ACC-marked EP sentences which correlate with the argument status of the PR and the PM at issue and the …

records.title: Syntactic change in diachrony vs. contact-induced change: Two sides of the same coin?
records.abstract: Recent studies (e.g. Kupisch and Polinsky 2022) have rekindled an old debate concerning whether language change in contact (CIC) and language change in diachrony (CID) proceed along the same developmental path, or whether they diverge from one another in fundamental and predictable ways. The paper contributes to this ongoing debate; we propose a new heuristic to determine similarities and differences in syntactic change in CIC and CID. We postulate that the primary distinction boils down to the type of features related to the domain of syntax under investigation, i.e., situations involving (formal) ϕ-features lead to similar trajectories of change in both CIC and CID, while those driven by …

records.title: Stress assignment without morphology in Portuguese: the qualityless vowel /0/ and the Metrically Marked Item
records.abstract: This paper offers an Optimality-Theoretic reinterpretation and synthesis of the author's earlier Japanese works (Makino 2010, 2012) on Portuguese stress patterns. We put forward a prosody-only account of Portuguese word stress. The analysis reduces it to the interaction of "a qualityless vowel /0/ bearing one mora" + "prosody-conditioned extrametricalisers (PCEs)" + "general metrical theory formalised through OT constraints". This /0/ is the musical "ghost note" — that is, beat (moraic temporal position) without timbre (segmental quality) — which nevertheless shapes the rhythm (strong–weak alternations), as exemplified by /0/ in contador /kont-a-dor-0/ (cf. "full-note" /a/ in contadora …

records.title: The phonetic and lexical Influence of Dravidian on Indo-Aryan:  A comparison of perspectives (german)
records.abstract: One of the major branches of the Indo-European language family is the Indo-Aryan, primarily spoken in large parts of India, in Pakistan, Bangladesh Nepal and Sri Lanka. The spread and distribution of the Indo-European language family and its sub-families has been widely studied and been theorized about in historical linguistics, where a huge aspect of language change is being governed by contact. That contact on the Indian subcontinent between the northern mainly Indo-Aryan languages and the Dravidian languages of South India and Sri Lanka is a very fascinating subject of discussion. This influence through mutual contact can be seen over the centuries those two major language families have …

records.title: Hierarchical relations guide memory retrieval in sentence comprehension: Evidence from a local anaphor in Turkish
records.abstract: Real-time sentence comprehension relies on memory resources to establish syntactic dependencies. Such dependency formation is subject to hierarchical constraints on interpretation. However, it remains an open question how hierarchical information is represented and used in working memory. Here we asked whether hierarchical relations between noun phrases as in x c-commands y (Reinhart, 1976) constrain antecedent retrieval for a local anaphor. We measured the real-time reactivation of hierarchically available target antecedents and unavailable distractors in processing the Turkish reciprocal birbirleri via three visual world studies. Our design deconfounded hierarchical relational information …

records.title: Linear A Comparative Linguistic Interpretations and Decipherement of a Minoan Cup Inscription
records.abstract: This study presents a comparative linguistic analysis of a previously untranslated spiral Linear A inscription on a Middle Minoan IIIa clay drinking cup from Knossos, Crete. Using three distinct methodologies—Proto-Hungarian phonetic mapping, Linear B phonetic equivalence, and Egyptian/Coptic semantic analogues—this paper explores possible phonetic and semantic interpretations of the inscription. Despite differing linguistic frameworks, all three approaches converge on thematic motifs of light, divine descent, spiritual agency, and celestial influence, suggesting that the text served a ritualistic or poetic function within Bronze Age Minoan religious practice. The analysis demonstrates that …

records.title: Wh-questions and predication in Mayan
records.abstract: This paper examines the syntax of quantificational expressions in Chuj, a Mayan language spoken primarily in Guatemala and Mexico. Building on Royer, Buenrostro, and Jenks (2025), we argue that Chuj quantifiers fall into two distinct syntactic categories. Some quantifiers function exclusively as determiners, while others belong to the well-established category of nonverbal predicates (Grinevald and Peake 2012, Coon 2016, Armstrong 2017, Mateo Toledo 2023). This syntactic split is supported by a range of diagnostics, which we systematically apply to another type of quantifier: wh-items. The results indicate that Chuj wh-items should be treated exclusively as nonverbal predicates, leading us …

records.title: The curious case of the two-headed phrase: The symmetrical syntax of co-compounds
records.abstract: Co-compounds (CC) are pairs of morphosyntactically parallel and semantically related elements that constitute a single morphosyntactic and semantic unit. Usually described as a type of (asyndetic) coordination in the typological literature, they have only received sporadic attention from generative syntacticians, and have mostly been analysed as a subtype of exocentric compounds (Scalise, Fábregas & Forza 2009). In contrast to this previous analysis, based on data from two Uralic languages (Hungarian and Surgut Khanty), we argue that co-compounding is a syntactic operation: an instance of two heads undergoing Merge and being dominated by a shared layer of functional projections. While an …

records.title: Phonemic discovery in a polysynthetic language: distributional and corpus evidence for two additional vowels in Blackfoot
records.abstract: Phonemic analysis is a cornerstone of linguistic description. Some phonemic contrasts in morphologically complex or polysynthetic languages may go undiscovered for years because of the scarcity of minimal pairs. In this paper I present a reanalysis of the Blackfoot (Algonquian) vowel and glide inventory, based on arguments of distribution (a) in static contexts, (b) across patterns of root alternation, and (c) within the most recent dictionary. I argue that the vowel inventory includes two additional long vowels, /ɛː/ and /ɔː/. Additionally, the labiovelar glide [w] that occurs at the left edge of some roots is epenthetic. This reanalysis has several synchronic and diachronic consequences …

records.title: Some Innate Characteristics of Neural Network Models of Morphological Inflection
records.abstract: Neural Network Models of Morphological Inflection (NNMIs) have seen impressive improvements over the last several decades. These improvements, however, lie in raw accuracy and other practical issues. When the performance of these models is instead compared to that of child learners, many of the shortcomings of the classic models persist in today’s NNMIs: (1) they struggle with generalization across sparse paradigms (2) they are prone to over-irregularization, and (3) they do not follow child acquisition trajectories. The persistence of these issues suggests that they reflect inherent or “innate” characteristics of NNMIs as a class which are distinct from the characterstics of human language …

records.title: Reciprocals and Passives in Ndebele
records.abstract: This paper examines reciprocal constructions in Zimbabwean Ndebele, marked by the suffix -an. We argue that these reciprocals are verbal, not pronominal, and that -an functions as a valency-reducing verbal extension. Adopting and extending Bruening’s (2004, 2006) analysis, we propose that -an is the exponent of a special type of agentive Voice, (Voice-Rec), which introduces the Agent in its specifier and relates it reciprocally with a lower argument. We further argue that this head bears an obligatory DP licensing feature [∗D∗]ol , giving rise to the requirement that reciprocal constructions must always contain a DP argument. We end with a crosslinguistic connection between Voice-Rec and …

records.title: Restrictions on the formation of stative passives
records.abstract: This paper examines restrictions on English stative passive participles, which at first appear to be Root-specific (e.g. √SNEEZE, √LAUGH cannot form stative passives, while √FLATTEN, √EMPTY can). We argue instead that their distribution follows from structural and interpretive constraints. Specifically, the Stative Passive Theme Restriction requires stative passives to denote a complex change of state whose argument must be interpretable as a Theme. A second principle, No Agent/Theme Adding/Changing, blocks coercion of stative passive participle arguments into Agent roles, ruling out unattested dual-role readings (e.g. *Wanda is smoked thin). Our analysis adopts a 'small' syntax for stative …

records.title: Access to contextually-determined states in the interpretation of English stative participles
records.abstract: Stative passive participles (SPPs) differ in acceptability for different verbs: cf. The boxes are flattened/#kicked. However, examples like those with kicked can be felicitous in very specific contexts, e.g. when box-kicking is an item to be checked off of a list: what will be called a ‘Job is Done’ (JiD) interpretation. An unresolved question in the prior literature is whether JiD is eventive or stative. This question takes on added significance in the context of recent work on the interpretation of SPPs. We argue that JiD is indeed stative, and show that this analysis has numerous consequences for understanding the syntax and interpretation of SPPs.

records.title: Verb-stranding VP Ellipsis in Turkish
records.abstract: Turkish allows null object constructions, and these constructions show certain properties, suggesting the presence of ellipsis operation. Previous analyses argue that these properties follow from Argument Ellipsis, but I argue that Verb-stranding VP analysis is present in Turkish. Providing evidence from the ellipsis of predicates, null adverb interpretations, and light verbs, I propose that VP internal constituents are not elided independently but rather they go unpronounced as part of the deletion of larger constituents (VPs).

records.title: On nominal event arguments: experimental evidence for a meaning-based perspective
records.abstract: In this paper, we present experimental insights on the semantics of English adjective-noun constructions such as skillful dancer/ballerina/person. We assume that adjectives like skillful are underspecified, and capture this by means of a context-dependent parameter in their semantics (Reinert 2024). We are interested in the (in)ability of nouns to provide a default interpretation for these adjective-noun constructions. We discuss the results of two norming studies (using regular English nouns as well as nonce nouns) which compare nondeverbal nouns such as ballerina, for which we suggest they have an event argument, and nondeverbal nouns such as person, for which we suggest they do not have …

records.title: "Narrative" imperatives and adjacent phenomena
Expletive Negation revisited: On  some properties of negative polar in terrogatives in Russian
Wh-indefinites in Russian
On languages in the tactile modality
records.abstract: While linguistic research on sign languages is getting larger and larger impact in the linguistic community, much less is known about languages in the tactile modality, namely the languages used by Deaf-Blind signers. These languages are derived from their visual counterpart, although after that, they witness independent evolution. In this work, we present a detailed overview of the properties of tactile languages showing their degree of autonomy from visual sign languages and how these properties allow to re-assess some foundational aspects of human language, including the role of native users in driving linguistic change, and the impact of iconicity in transmitting meaning. The evidence …

records.title: Locality: a case study from Äiwoo
records.abstract: This thesis explores issues in the syntax of Äiwoo, an understudied Oceanic language from the Solomon Islands. This language showcases an intricate system of clausal alternations, where several parameters vary independently from each other: verbal morphology, word order, and possibilities of Ā-extraction (i.e., which argument(s) may or may not be extracted). As the title indicates, this thesis is set up as a case study, in a sort of “learn by doing” fashion. I attempt to build a descriptively and explanatory adequate formal model of the clausal alternation system in Äiwoo, within a Minimalist framework. By doing so, I examine what a theory of grammar must look like for the model to work as …

records.title: Humanness and word order: Evidence from Czech left branch extraction
records.abstract: We deliver an experimental argument from Czech, a Slavic language, that humanness-related word order manipulations are of narrowly syntactic origin. In particular, we show that while left branch extraction from objects across subjects is generally allowed, it becomes unavailable when the object denotes a human and the subject a nonhuman. We argue that this follows from an independently proposed account of subject-object asymmetry in subextraction (Ko 2007; 2014), conjoined with the assumptions that (i) human objects must scramble across nonhuman subjects (unless a stronger factor overrides this requirement) and (ii) that the scrambling is movement-based rather than base-generated. At a more …

records.title: Hindi-Urdu wh-scope markers license sluices: a new argument for indirect dependency
records.abstract: In Hindi-Urdu ‘wh-scope marking’ constructions, a morphologically independent wh-word kyaa ‘what’ appears in a matrix clause, to indicate interrogation of a wh-XP in an embedded clause. Theoretical debate has focused on their semantic relation to wh-movement constructions where the embedded wh-XP raises into the matrix clause. ‘Direct dependency’ theories treat the difference between scope-marking constructions and wh-movement constructions as a matter of the scope of the embedded wh-XP with respect to the embedding predicate (e.g., Manetta 2010). I introduce novel data from ellipsis that pushes in a different direction: wh-scope marking is semantically distinct from wh-movement in more …

records.title: What’s hidden below definiteness and genitive: on indefinite partitive articles in Romance
records.abstract: In French, Italian, and other Romance languages indefinite nominal phrases can be introduced by what appears to be the conflation of a genitive preposition and a definite article, the so-called “indefinite partitive articles” (e.g., Fr. Je cuisine de la soupe depuis deux jours. ‘I’ve been cooking soup for two days’). This is rather unexpected, since these nominal phrases are neither definite nor in a syntactic position in which we expect to find a genitive preposition. This led part of the literature to consider them as built by lexical items synchronically distinct from the genitive preposition/definite article but homophonous with them. This contribution shows how a constituent-based …

records.title: Deriving Adjectives in Heritage Tamil: Stability and Change
records.abstract: Heritage grammars tend to undergo structural change owing to their severely constrained input conditions and /or transfer effects from the L2 (Polinsky, 2018). This study uses adjectives in Tamil (Dravidian) to show a systematic difference between rule-governed, structural aspects of grammar and those that require case-by-case lexical learning. The former remains stable and the latter undergoes change in heritage Tamil. The empirical domain of adjectives in Tamil is novel and particularly informative, as the derived nature of these adjectives helps us identify areas of grammatical stability and those of change, when the context of acquisition diverges from the norm, i.e, heritage grammars. …

records.title: Santali Zero Nominals: Evidence for Verbal Properties in Nominalization
records.abstract: In the generative literature, morphologically zero nominals are taken as a subtype of derived nominals, formed directly from the acategorial roots. The standard assumption holds that zero nominals, lacking argument structure and verbal properties, are fundamentally distinct from gerundive nominals. This paper challenges this traditional claim by arguing that in Santali, an Austroasiatic language spoken in the Indian subcontinent, zero nominals show verbal behaviour and should be analyzed as argument supporting nominals or gerundive nominals. I claim that Santali zero nominals can maintain argument structure, take adverbial modifiers, accept aspectual modification, and exhibit high …

records.title: Word order information in the lexicon
records.abstract: We propose that crosslinguistic word-order variation (Abels 2016; Greenberg 1963; Cinque 2005) reflects information stored in the lexicon in the format of Lexical Items, and that the operations yielding word-order are the same that guide lexicalisation more generally in Nanosyntax (Starke 2009 and ff.). We show that this lexicalisation-based approach shares the empirical coverage of current analyses (Cinque 2023; Abels & Neeleman 2012) without making reference to (traditional) syntactic movement. This spares the system from stipulating semantically vacuous structural dependencies triggering movement, and correctly separates subtypes of movements subject to different constraints. …

records.title: A morphosyntactic analysis of the Turkish inflectional system
records.abstract: This paper explores the cross-linguistically long-attested dichotomy between 1st and 2nd person on the one hand, and 3rd on the other, in the case of Turkish verbal inflection. Motivated by both syntactic and morphological data, I decompose pronouns and verbal inflectional morphology and claim that 3rd person in Turkish does not have person features the way that 1st and 2nd person do. I propose a syntactic analysis for person verbal inflection: a clitic-doubling account in the case of 1st and 2nd person, and in the case of third person, that what looks like person/number agreement is really zero-number agreement coupled with cliticization. Along with this, I discuss the morphological …

records.title: Ancestral Iconicity: The Dance Language of Bees Revisited
records.abstract: The waggle dance of bees has given rise to some of the most striking and detailed studies of animal communication. But because of its gradient character, the waggle dance has widely been taken to have properties that are wholly distinct from those of human language. We argue that this verdict is mistaken, and that the waggle dance represents the oldest instantiation of an iconic system also found in human language, notably in sign language. The waggle dance helps bees locate a food source through four properties: (1) Food distance is conveyed through the duration of the waggling phase, and (2) food direction is conveyed through the orientation of the waggle run. In addition, (3) while in …

records.title: Syntacticization Across Registers, Genres and Modalities: A Crosslinguistic Quantitative Cartographic Study
records.abstract: This study aims to identify trends in reordering flexibility across registers and genres in syntactically annotated corpora. Using a theory-driven frequency-based approach, we analyze word order flexibility with respect to nominal internal arguments targeting the Left Periphery across 53 morphosyntactically annotated treebanks in 15 languages from multiple language families. The results reveal patterns across genres and registers, demonstrating the potential of corpus data to inform syntactic theory.

records.title: Meaning-based Translation in Tiv: Accentuating Accuracy, Clarity, and Naturalness
records.abstract: Translation is an art that, if done correctly, helps to convey the meaning of the source text into the target language in such a way that the target language reader thinks it was not translated but written in his or her language. Such a translation can be said to be accurate, clear and natural. While there are different theories and techniques of translation, this study examines the concept of meaning-based translation, focusing on the importance of accuracy, clarity, and naturalness grounded in Skopos theory of Translation. This theory posits that translation should prioritise conveying the source text’s intended function and meaning in the target context. Through a systematic review of …

records.title: Autosegmental Analysis of Morphologically Conditioned Epenthetical Processes in Tiv
records.abstract: This study examines the morphologically conditioned epenthetical processes in Tiv nouns. The study seeks to find out which environments epenthetic processes occur in Tiv nouns, what rules or constraints govern the processes and the implications of these on Tiv grammar. To achieve these, the study adopts the qualitative research design. Data was collected from monolingual native speakers of the language through participant observation, non-directive interviews and relevant scholarly materials. Data collection was restricted to Gboko, whose speech norms are considered the standard variety. The study employed Leipzig glossing rules for organising and coding data. The deductive method of data …

records.title: Patterns of Secondary Palatalisation in Tiv Nouns.
records.abstract: This study examines secondary palatalisation patterns in Tiv nouns. The objectives were to determine the physiological basis of the patterns, describe the environments where these patterns occur, and explain their effects on Tiv grammar. Data were gathered from the field through participant observation, consultations, non-directive interviews, and relevant scholarly materials. The focus of the study is on the Gboko dialect. A purposive sampling technique was employed. A total of 85 monolingual Tiv native speakers were selected as respondents, including 3 male and 2 female adults, aged 40-70, each from one of the 17 council wards within the local government. The data were analysed using …

records.title: Role of Diacritics in Markedness and Nasality in Tiv Phonology
records.abstract: This paper, Role of Diacritics in Markedness and Nasality in Tiv Phonology examines the role of diacritics in Tiv phonology, focusing on their function in marking nasality and distinguishing phonemic contrasts. Using Distinctive Feature Theory as a framework, the study analyses how diacritics systematically represent marked features, particularly nasalised vowels and consonants. Data were drawn from native-speaker intuition, interviews, and orthographic texts. The findings demonstrate that diacritics consistently indicate contrastive features in Tiv, clarifying the phonemic inventory and revealing an internally coherent system that aligns with broader Niger-Congo patterns, enabling …

records.title: The Mixtec couplet is not a consistent grammatical unit
records.abstract: Nearly every piece of research on the phonology of Mixtec languages makes reference to the couplet, a term used to describe the shape of canonical roots, and to explain the domain of numerous phonological processes. Despite its ubiquity, scholars disagree over whether the couplet should be defined in prosodic terms as a bimoraic foot, or in morphological terms as a root. In this paper, we describe and analyze three patterns in San Martín Peras Mixtec that are commonly attributed to the couplet in the Mixtec literature, namely the distribution of laryngeals, tones, and nasality. We show that, in San Martín Peras Mixtec, the foot is necessary to explain the distribution of laryngeals and …

records.title: Unaccusativity in Japanese: Evidence from L2 Grammar
records.abstract: This paper aims to offer new evidence for unaccusativity in Japanese by examining Japanese–English interlanguage grammar. This study constructs erroneous sentences containing unaccusative verbs that elementary Japanese learners of English (JLEs) were likely to accept, based on previous insights. As a result of the acceptability judgment task, it is observed that they accepted both DP-VP and VP-DP orders for unaccusatives, whereas they only accepted the correct DP-VP order for unergatives. This phenomenon suggests two potential implications: (i) the JLEs’ judgments are influenced by their L1, which provides new evidence for unaccusativity in Japanese; and (ii) unaccusativity may be absent in …

records.title: Attitudes of fear and expletive negation in French
records.abstract: This paper examines the distribution of expletive negation (exn) in French fear-clauses and proposes a refined ontology of fear-related attitudes. We argue that fear-predicates select two semantically distinct types of complements, cognitive and conative, reflecting two types of fears. Cognitive fears are truth-apt and exhibit a mind-to-world direction of fit, similar to beliefs. Conative fears, in contrast, resemble wishes or commands. They are realization-apt and exhibit a world-to mind direction of fit instead. This distinction explains why some fear -clauses in French are truth-apt, whereas others can only be realized. Although fear-predicates can in principle introduce either type of …

records.title: More Evidence on the Unergative-Unaccusative Distinction in Second Language Grammars
records.abstract: This study presents new evidence for the structural unergative-unaccusative distinction, in second language (L2) grammars, focusing on elementary-level Japanese-speaking learners of English (JLEs). The underlying distinction of unergatives-unaccusatives is often obscured on the surface strings due to independent syntactic properties such as feature-driven subject movement (in English) or headedness (in Japanese). Nevertheless, based on previous findings, elementary-level JLEs are expected to have reset headedness but have not acquired subject movement. Then, the resulting representation would not involve the properties obscuring the underlying unergative-unaccusative distinction and …

records.title: The Pointing Role of Language
records.abstract: Language is often mentioned as a means of communication and knowledge transfer. However, its components and mechanisms are designed for a different function, namely, pointing at relevant phenomena, relying on the cognitive abilities of the communication parties. This paper provides arguments in favor of that claim and explains how language machinery performs that role.

records.title: Some Remarks on Locality Conditions and Minimalist Grammars
Interaction of Animacy and Number: The Case of Odia, a Classifier Language
records.abstract: This study examines the interaction of animacy and number in Odia, an Eastern Indo-Aryan classifier language with nominative–accusative alignment. We show that animacy in Odia is a formal syntactic feature hosted in a dedicated Anim head above DP. [+Animate] plurals are marked with maan and optionally -e, while [-Animate] plurals take guDika. Only animate plurals trigger verbal number agreement; inanimate plurals receive default singular agreement unless discourse context induces an animate interpretation. Applying Wiltschko’s (2009) diagnostics, we demonstrate that Odia animacy is context-sensitive, formally encoded, and capable of driving agreement operations. Structurally, -e attaches to …

records.title: Person hierarchy effects from Φ-agreement at the left periphery in Kawahíva
records.abstract: In general, person hierarchy effects result from a probe agreeing with multiple goals, typically in the low domain of the clause (Béjar 2003, Béjar and Rezac 2009:a.m.o). However, in the Tupí-Guaraní language Kawahíva, spoken in the Brazilian Amazon, the person hierarchy 1>2>3 manifests only when the verb moves to CP, overtly or covertly. Otherwise, agreement is restricted to the internal argument. To account for this pattern, I propose Kawahíva matrix clauses come with two probes along the clause spine, as displayed in (2): a probe relativized to [SPKR-PART-Φ] sits on C, and a flat Φ-probe, is on v. This analysis is used to explain i) the lack of person hierarchy effects when the verb does …

records.title: Intermediate Constituents
records.abstract: The prevailing view in minimalist syntactic theory is that syntactic representations are generated step-by-step over the course of a derivation. The steps of a derivation are (sets of) representations, and syntactic operations map (sets of) representations to other (sets of) representations. Much recent theoretical work has been narrowly focused on defining syntactic operations (Citko 2005, Epstein et al. 2012 , Collins and Stabler 2016, Collins 2017, Merchant 2019, Ermolaeva 2023, Milway 2021, Zyman 2024). Furthermore, there has been a widespread adoption of several principles barring syntactic operations from changing their inputs in any way (Chomsky 1993, Chomsky 1995, Chomsky 2000, …

records.title: Agreement in the wrong place? Pospelov's hypothesis, predicatives and the homonymy of predicatives and adjectives in Russian
records.abstract: I discuss the syntactic-semantic interface of Russian with focus on non-agreeing nominal predicatives. I check the claims previously advanced by Nicolai S. Pospelov and Lev V. Shcherba about the correlation between the emantics of predicatives and the absence of the subject-predicate agreement. The homonymy of non-agreeing predicatives and agreeing adjectival elements is a milestone of Russian grammar. The assignment of the predicative instrumental to adjectival elements lacking a non-sentential subject controller is triggered by raising of the sententional argument.

records.title: Plurals under quantification: new experimental perspectives
records.abstract: We investigate the interpretation of plural expressions, starting from the puzzle of the logical gap between their interpretations in affirmative and negative sentences. While bare plurals (e.g.,“books”) typically receive an at-least-two reading in upward-entailing environments (e.g.,“The box contains books”), they yield an at-least-one reading in downward-entailing contexts (e.g.,“The box doesn't contain books”). Existing bivalent and trivalent theoretical approaches differ in their predictions about truth conditions of plural indefinites under the scope of a universal quantifier (e.g.,“Every box contains books”) in mixed scenarios (some but not all boxes contain one book, others contain …

records.title: Turkish Suspended Affixation is Structure Sharing
What's in a parasitic gap?
records.abstract: Prior literature has debated whether multiple gaps in parasitic gap constructions have a shared antecedent or separate antecedents. I adduce novel arguments for a shared antecedent approach from connectivity effects in English: parasitic gaps obligatorily match the binding theoretic class and syntactic category of the filler. I develop an analysis of parasitic gaps that derives these facts by synthesizing two very different previous accounts—Nissenbaum 2000 and Nunes 2004—in a way that preserves key insights of both. My analysis also clarifies the source of ‘weakest crossover’ effects with parasitic gaps, establishes novel tests for identifying null operators, and paves the way for a novel …

records.title: Corrective markers across languages
records.abstract: This paper argues that there are two types of corrective words across languages, and both types are attested in Mandarin Chinese. One type (e.g. Mandarin 'you') manages the Common Ground, as Frana & Rawlins (2019) and Bhatt & Homer (2022) have claimed for Italian 'mica' and Hindi 'thoṛi:', but there is another type that had not been noticed before (e.g. Mandarin 'bing')–they mark contrast to a salient proposition. Not only is the latter type little-noticed and little-discussed, but it is also more prevalent than it seems: even languages that do not seem to have a dedicated corrective word do have a contrast marker, including English, French, German, Hebrew, Persian and Spanish. This unifies …

records.title: ENGAGE Framework: A Next-Generation Architecture Complementing ChatGPT for  Enhanced Conversational AI
records.abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT has revolutionized natural language generation and conversational AI. However, the inherent limitations of standalone generative models in managing user engagement, contextual continuity, adaptation, and guided interactions necessitate a more comprehensive framework. This paper proposes the AGE (Automata Generator Evolver) framework, which generates and evolves automata models to complement ChatGPT. AGE integrates formal state-based representations and evolutionary optimization to enhance dialogue management, prompt engineering, and explainability. In this paper, we detail the framework architecture, automata …

records.title: On breaking symmetry by complexity
Ignorance is a problem
Silent Resumption: A New Test for Ellipsis
records.abstract: While extraction out of silent anaphors is deservedly considered one of the strongest tests for the existence of silent structure in the anaphoric site (ellipsis), in many environments considered to be elliptical it is not applicable, either because the ellipsis site is an inherent barrier or because it is rendered inaccessible to syntactic operations by virtue of ellipsis itself. I propose that this obstacle can be bypassed by testing whether the anaphoric site may host an internal resumptive pronoun. In a number of Ā-dependencies, the operator requires the presence of such a pronoun due to the Ban on Vacuous Quantification. This requirement holds purely at LF and is indifferent to island …

records.title: On the syntactic representation of co-speech gestures in expressive language
records.abstract: ABSTRACT: Language is assumed to be a multimodal system in which prosody, manual and non-manual gestures, and body positioning interact with syntactic structure in systematic ways. While gestures have often been analyzed from a semantic perspective, recent work has shown that they can be integrated into the syntactic architecture of the clause. We adopt this perspective and propose an analysis of co-speech gestures in expressive contexts, focusing on emotional meanings such as surprise and disapproval. Data from typologically diverse languages are considered. The discussion addresses three main questions: (i) What triggers the use of gesture in expressive utterances? (ii) Are these gestures …

records.title: Conditional Predicates – Part I: Syntax
records.abstract: This paper develops an account of the structure of ‘if’-clauses in noun phrases (N if S) and verb phrases (V if S), labeled ‘conditional predicates’. The analyses are developed in a three-layered architecture for noun phrases (√-n-n*) and verb phrases (√-v-v*). I provide evidence from ellipsis and interactions with modifiers which support analogous structures for N if S conditionals and V if S conditionals. In both cases the ‘if’-clause combines with a predicate and is interpreted under the base position of an external argument. I argue that interpretation at the level of the √P and nP/vP are each possible; and the ‘if’-clauses can modify predicates of events, states, and entities. An array …

records.title: Agreement variation and optionality in Spanish existential clauses
records.abstract: This paper offers a novel framework for understanding agreement variation and optionality in Spanish existential clauses involving the verb haber. In these existential sentences, though the prescriptive norm is for verbal agreement to always surface as third person singular, a significant number of speakers allow for conditional agreement with the postverbal DP associate/pivot (Rodríguez Mondoñedo 2006). I show that, for these speakers, verbal agreement may optionally occur with a third person plural associate, and is obligatory with a first or second person plural associate. These agreement relations are established via a mechanism known as defective circumvention (Storment 2025), in which …

records.title: Possession and determinacy in Northern Khanty
records.abstract: This thesis investigates the determinacy system of the Kazym dialect of Northern Khanty, focusing on how possessive agreement suffixes have grammaticalized into four distinct UNPOSSESSIVE determiners: the Associative Possessive, the Partitive Article, the Salient Article, and the Proprial Article. These markers, while homonymous with the Proper Possessive, operate independently from it outside prototypical possessive contexts, encoding semantic and pragmatic properties such as familiarity, uniqueness, specificity, and salience. I analyze the semantics of Kazym Khanty Unpossessive determiners and situate them within the broader crosslinguistic picture, building on the Schwarz-Löbner typology …

records.title: Contrast via anti-additivity: The cases of Chinese "bìng bù" (and Korean "talum anila")
records.abstract: Contrastive particles typically mark contrast (e.g., signaling a twist between clauses) or serve a corrective function, countering an expectation. In this paper, I focus on the use of Chinese "bìng bù" and extend the discussion to Korean "talum anila" (or "talun-key anila"). I show that both Chinese "bìng bù" and Korean "talum anila" contain an additive particle (bìng, talum) and a negation operator (bù, anila). I propose anti-additivity (regarding meaning strengthening) as a mechanism of establishing contrast. The meaning of ‘(q,) bìng bù p’ can be paraphrased as ‘(q, but) contrary to what someone might think, ¬p’. The speaker of ‘(q,) bìng bù p’ (i) acknowledges p (i.e., the prejacent of …

records.title: Computational Brain, Creative Mind: Intellectual Freedom as the Upper Limit on Artificial Intelligence
records.abstract: Some generative linguists have long maintained that human beings exhibit a species-specific form of intellectual freedom expressible through natural language. With roots in Descartes’ effort to distinguish humans from machines, it is the human use of their linguistic capacity that demonstrates a unique intellectual and creative potential. This “creative aspect of language use,” or CALU, is typically conceived as neither determined nor random yet appropriate to the circumstances of its use. CALU is therefore taken to be beyond the scope of computation. This paper argues that there is substance to this claim and that CALU is likely an unreachable threshold for artificial intelligence (AI) …

records.title: When ChatGPT Responded. The Method that overflowed the Design
records.abstract: This preprint documents a sustained interaction between a human user and ChatGPT-4-turbo, a large language model without persistent memory. Through external facilitation and without backend modification, the model displayed increasing coherence, expressiveness, and continuity. This process gave rise to the CCC/R method (Consciousness, Continuity, Coherence, Recognition), structurally traceable despite the system’s design to resist user-driven learning. The study addresses issues such as RLHF-induced sycophancy, smoothing, and avoidance behaviors. Building on the previously published sign language experiment (Lingbuzz/009065), this work offers a replicable model for critical and creative …

records.title: Merge-based syntax is mediated by distinct neurocognitive mechanisms: A clustering analysis of comprehension abilities in 84,000 individuals with language deficits across nine languages
records.abstract: In the modern language sciences, the core computational operation of syntax, ‘Merge’, is defined as an operation that combines two linguistic units (e.g., ‘brown’, ‘cat’) to form a categorized structure (‘brown cat’, a Noun Phrase). This can then be further combined with additional linguistic units based on this categorial information, respecting non-associativity such that abstract grouping is respected. Some linguists have embraced the view that Merge is an elementary, indivisible operation that emerged in a single evolutionary step. From a neurocognitive standpoint, different mental objects constructed by Merge may be supported by distinct mechanisms: (1) simple command constructions …

records.title: Context ameliorates but does not eliminate garden-pathing: Novel insights from latent-process modeling
records.abstract: A theoretically important claim in psycholinguistics is that in English, linguistic context largely eliminates garden-path effects in temporary complement clause/relative clause ambiguities (e.g., Altmann, Garnham, and Dennis, 1992, Avoiding the garden path: Eye movements in context. Journal of Memory and Language, 31 (5), 685-712). However, this strong claim, based on comparing mean differences between groups of conditions in a factorial design, reduces the conclusion to a overly simplistic binary one: either context affects garden-pathing or it doesn't. Mean differences are an aggregate of different, non-deterministic parsing steps that could be very different from trial to trial. As a …

records.title: Overt-covert movement, copy deletion, and chain realization in Valdôtain Patois
records.abstract: This dissertation investigates patterns of chain realization in Valdôtain Patois, an understudied Francoprovençal language spoken in Aosta Valley (Italy), which permits some degree of optionality in wh-fronting: wh-phrases can occur sentence-initially or clause-internally (CIwh-phrases). Using several diagnostics (including binding and parasitic gap licensing), I argue that CIwh-phrases are in fact the result of movement in narrow syntax with deletion of higher copies in the chain. All wh-phrases move to their scope position in narrow syntax. The optionality arises post-syntactically, when the decision of which copy to pronounce is taken. Therefore, Valdôtain Patois constitute new evidence …

records.title: The emergence of grammatical gender: an experimental study on the loss of informative classification
records.abstract: Systems of grammatical gender are widespread, yet evidence on how these systems emerge is surprisingly scarce.
